records.full_text:
We have before us the Havana Diario de la Marina, to 7th instant.

Among its official announcements we find notifications of the departure of troops meant to reinforce the garrison for the Siempre fiel Ysla. The total is between twelve and fifteen hundred.

The English steamer Havana arrived at Havana on the 4th, the schooner Talisman on the 5th, from Nassau. On the 5th, the English bark Th. Thompson and brigantine Sir Robert Peel left Havana for New Orleans. The steamer Creole had cleared for this port.

The Diario has nearly six of its ponderous columns filled with news concerning the late administration of Justice of Spanish colonies. At the late hour at which the article is brought to our notice we deem it unnecessary to say more than that the design of the regulations appears to be that they lead to the assimilation of the forms and administration of justice in the colonies to those of the mother country.

The supplement of the Diario of the 8th inst. announces news from Santo Domingo, that, it will be recollected, commenced active hostilities on November 12th, the date of the latest news.

FROM ST. DOMINGO.—There has been another revolution in Dominica. The papers give the following account of some remarkable occurrences connected with it:

On the 13th of November a party of insurgents entered Azua, and proclaimed Baez as the President. A number of the people of the province of Seibo joined them, and they proceeded towards the capital with cries of "Long live Baez!" and "Death to Cabral!"

They evidently had confederates in the government; for, at the critical moment, a curious scene took place in the Supreme Congress, which was in session, deliberating on the question of the emission of paper money. A mysterious man, armed with a cutlass, entered suddenly, and, despite of all protests, exclaimed: "General Cabral, are you in favor of peace?" "With all my heart," was the reply. "Well, then," said the stranger, "I am an emissary of the revolutionary chief, who will be here to-morrow. You had better make your escape at once." Cabral did not wait for further advice, but fled, and Baez's party took possession of the city without further opposition. A new Government was formed, with Baez as President, and General Pimentel as Minister of War.

records.headline: The Revolution in St. Domingo.
records.summary_en: A mysterious armed man suddenly entered a congressional session and declared himself an emissary of General Baez, causing the ministers to flee in terror while General Cabral agreed to the popular will. The intruder was revealed to be General Pedro Guillermo, who had himself appointed dictator until an election on December 14 unanimously made Baez President of the Dominican Republic. Consequently, Cabral accepted a military position under the new government, of which Guillermo became the practical head.
records.summary_es: Un enigmático hombre armado irrumpió sorpresivamente en el recinto del Congreso proclamándose emisario del general Báez, lo que provocó la huida aterrorizada del gabinete ministerial mientras el general Cabral se plegaba a la voluntad popular. El intruso resultó ser el general Pedro Guillermo, quien se hizo ungir dictador provisional hasta que en las votaciones del 14 de diciembre se designó por unanimidad a Báez presidente de la República Dominicana. A consecuencia de ello, Cabral aceptó una comandancia militar en la nueva administración, cuyo timón efectivo retenía Guillermo.

records.full_text:
Revolutions are sometimes brought about by singular agencies. Seldom is such means as effectual as force of arms. A recent arrival from St. Domingo furnishes the following account of the mode in which a recent revolution was accomplished, and in which Cabral, who had succeeded Pimentel to the presidency of the country, was recently overthrown.

“On the 16th of October a party of insurgents entered Seibo and proclaimed Baez as the President. A regiment sent from Port-au-Prince to Seibo joined them, and they proceeded toward the capital with cries of ‘Long live Baez! and Death to Cabral!’

Baez suddenly appeared at Santo Domingo. Before, at the critical moment, a curious scene took place in the National Council, which was in session, deliberating on the question of paper. A ‘mysterious man,’ armed with a cutlass, entered suddenly, and despite of all protests, exclaimed, ‘General Cabral, are you in favor of peace?’

‘With all my heart;’ was the reply.

‘Well then,’ said the stranger, ‘I am an emissary of the revolutionary chief who will be here in less than two hours;’ and, then raising his voice he exclaimed; ‘Long live General Baez, President of Dominica!’

As these words resounded through the hall, a body of troops was seen advancing towards the palace. Cabral saw that resistance was useless; sought protection in the house of the French Consul; a new executive council was formed; Baez appeared in public, and declared that if the people wished Cabral for President instead of Baez he would gladly give his consent—Cabral replied that he preferred Baez to Cabral, and he retired for several weeks.

The mysterious man who had frightened the Council turned out to be a sergeant in the Dominican army, who took this means to get himself appointed dictator until Baez should arrive. A decree issued on the 14th of December by the Constitutional Assembly, proclaims Buenaventura Baez President of the Dominican Republic.

Cabral has accepted a military position under the new regime. Baez, according to his mysterious man, is the practical head.

records.summary_en: According to *The Evening Telegraph* of January 30, 1866, Mr. Baez attained the presidency through a coup d'état aided by General Cabral's relinquishment of power and Pedro Guillermo's armed force. The article reports that the majority of the nation opposes Baez's administration due to his service as a Spanish Field Marshal during the independence struggle, and notes that his regime is currently jailing and persecuting suspected opponents of a thwarted uprising at Puerto Plata.
records.summary_es: Según *The Evening Telegraph* del 30 de enero de 1866, el Sr. Báez ascendió a la presidencia mediante un golpe de Estado facilitado por la declinación del poder del general Cabral y el respaldo armado de Pedro Guillermo. La crónica refiere que la mayoría de los ciudadanos rechaza el gobierno de Báez en razón de su pasado como mariscal de campo al servicio de España durante la guerra de independencia, señalando asimismo que el régimen persigue y encarcela a presuntos desafectos involucrados en un frustrado alzamiento en Puerto Plata.

records.full_text:
The following is an extract from a letter received from a person holding place in Hayti, and who was present during the late visit of Mr. Seward, Secretary of State, accompanied by Mr. and Mrs. Frederick Seward:—
The De Soto arrived in our harbor so late in the afternoon that the distinguished party on board did not land till the next morning at eight o'clock. Hon. August Ely, Secretary of State for Foreign Relations, and General Ernest Roumain, Haytien Charge at Washington, now on a visit to his family, met the party at the wharf and accompanied it to the residence of Mr. Peck, United States Commissioner to Hayti. We took carriages and went through the city, visiting the Cathedral, Senate House and House of Representatives, and other objects of interest. At ten we returned to Mr. Peck's, where we all took breakfast. Then the President sent his private carriages, two aide-de-camp and a cavalry escort to accompany the party to the palace. Mrs. F. Seward received also an invitation from Madame Geffrard. We all went together, and found a large body guard drawn up in the yard of the palace, with a fine band of music. The Hon. Mr. Seward was received with all the honors due to his rank and position. On the palace steps we were met by Generals Damier and Philippeau, members of the Cabinet, who led us to the reception room, where His Excellency the President, Mme. Geffrard and her daughters gave them a most hearty and sincere welcome. Mr. Seward and the President conversed together about two hours, while Mrs. Seward was entertained by the ladies of the President's family.
I need not say that the interview was most cordial and friendly. Mr. Seward on several occasions expressed his satisfaction at having seen and heard the President. I think the impressions he received were quite favorable to our government and people.
On the return of Mr. Seward to Mr. Peck's he received the diplomatic corps, and then the party returned on board, having remained about six hours with us.
When the Hon. Secretary of State had reached the deck of his ship the Haytien steamer Galatea gave him a salute of seventeen guns, which compliment was immediately responded to by the De Soto.
Thus ended this remarkable visit, which I think an important event in our political history, and which may prove beneficial to our intercourse with the government of the United States.

records.summary_en: According to the *New-York Tribune* on October 4, 1867, the peoples of Hayti and the Dominican Republic recognized that union was necessary to maintain their independence and prosperity, following past experience and Spanish intervention. A treaty—awaiting only the ratification of the Dominican Congress—had its preliminaries signed six days after the arrival of six delegates sent by President Balnave, amidst great enthusiasm from the government and people. The treaty's articles provided for the suppression of frontier brigandage and the extradition of political refugees, a commitment by both parties to preserve the inviolability of their respective territories (ruling out any United States purchase of the Bay of Samaná), and the settlement of claims arising from injuries sustained during the 1844 separation.
records.summary_es: Según el *New-York Tribune* del 4 de octubre de 1867, los pueblos de Haití y de la República Dominicana reconocieron la imperiosa necesidad de la unión para preservar su independencia y prosperidad tras las lecciones del pasado y la intervención española. records.full_text:
HAVANA, Nov. 17—We have the announcement that St. Domingo City has been destroyed, probably by an earthquake. I have telegraphed for details, which I shall forward at once.

The news of the insurrection in Hayti is confirmed. On the 12th of October the scene in the legislative chambers was very violent, and the language used was of the most threatening character. It all arose from a motion made to relieve Montes, who is in a Cape Haytien dungeon. The members all spoke in his defence. It is said Prince Salnave became so audacious as to secretly incite a rabble of women and boys to attack the House of Assembly. This they did with loud vivas for Salnave and cries of “Down with the Assembly,” hurling at the same time bricks, bottles, sticks, &c. The dwellings of many were vigorously stoned. The American consul was fired at, but escaped unhurt. A unanimous protest of the diplomatic corps has been presented against any further repetition of such scenes, and demanding of the government to see to it that the like does not again occur. At last accounts the city of Port au Prince was quieting. The treaty with the United States is as yet in suspense.

records.summary_en: The newspaper reported that a continued outbreak and threatened force created a great panic across Santo Domingo, menacing the white population, while severe earthquakes occurred on the 11th and 12th, with a special report indicating that St. Domingo City was probably destroyed. In Haiti, an insurrection was confirmed, and a violent scene in the Legislative Chambers involved President Salnave inciting a rabble to attack the House of Assembly, during which the American Consul was fired at and the Diplomatic Corps presented a unanimous protest. Additionally, it was noted that Port au Prince was quieting a treaty with the United States, which remained in suspense.

En Haití se confirmó la insurrección y una violenta trifulca en el hemiciclo legislativo donde el presidente Salnave incitó al populacho a asaltar la asamblea, disparándose contra el cónsul estadounidense y elevando el cuerpo diplomático una protesta unánime. Se refirió asimismo que en Puerto Príncipe se aplacaban los ánimos mientras el tratado con los Estados Unidos quedaba en suspenso.

records.headline: The hurricane lasted four hours and destroyed nearly all the shipping
records.summary_en: A Havana press dispatch reported that a tremendous hurricane struck St. Domingo on October 30, lasting four hours, destroying nearly all harbor shipping and Commerce street in St. Domingo city, and causing two hundred deaths, though no American vessels were reported lost. Additionally, a dispatch from Havana stated that the treaty with St. Domingo had been annulled, the Haytian Minister had returned, revolutionary movements were rife with Dominican forces on the Haytian frontier, and an intended issue of $600,000 in bonds was unpopular.

Además, un parte habanero indicó la anulación del tratado con Santo Domingo, el regreso del ministro haitiano, la proliferación de movimientos revolucionarios con destacamentos dominicanos en la frontera con Haití y el unánime repudio hacia una proyectada emisión de bonos de 600.000 pesos.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported on an extraordinary audience where the French Charge d'Affairs presented President Salnave with a friendly letter from Emperor Napoleon regarding a previous assassination attempt, which was met with Salnave's expressions of sympathy for France. The newspaper also noted that President Salnave received an autograph letter from Peruvian President Col. Prado assuring amicable relations, and reported that the Cacos Insurrection had been entirely suppressed, leaving the country quiet.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* dio cuenta de una audiencia extraordinaria en la que el encargado de negocios francés presentó al presidente Salnave una misiva afectuosa del emperador Napoleón relativa a un anterior atentado contra su vida, respondida por Salnave con expresiones de viva simpatía hacia Francia. El diario añadió que Salnave recibió una carta autógrafa del presidente de Perú, el coronel Prado, asegurando fraternales relaciones, y consignó la extinción total de la insurrección de los cacos, recobrando el país entera calma.

While the provinces of St. Domingo, Cibao, Azua, and Samana remained tranquil, General Hungria's Baecist revolution continued to make progress in the northern part of the republic. Por lo demás, se desestimó el empréstito francés, se promulgaron un nuevo código civil y la reforma de los tribunales de justicia y se anunció el próximo viaje a Nueva York del comisionado dominicano Pujol.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that war between St. Domingo and Hayti was imminent and had effectively broken out following the Haytian capture of the Dominican schooner *Copotille*, which was accused of supplying the Cacos rebels. The Haytian government declared a state of war after seizing papers signed by General Cabral that encouraged the rebels, while Cabral's agent failed to secure a loan for firearms from ex-President Geffrard in Kingston. Additionally, it was believed that Salnave was retaliating by assisting the Baez party in St. Domingo with money and arms.

records.summary_en: On April 27, 1868, the *New York Herald* reported that Dominican commissioner Mr. Fabens and Curaçao banker Señor Jesurun arrived in Havana en route to Washington to negotiate the sale of the Bay of Samaná and a loan secured by Dominican customs revenues. Meanwhile, the people of Santo Domingo were reportedly exasperated with the Baez administration—which was imprisoning adversaries and suspected of planning to abscond with state funds—and a revolution expected to elevate General Luperon or ex-President Cabral was imminent. Additionally, reports of specie arriving for the Samaná purchase were contradicted, and it was believed the Baez party was acting in concert with President Salnave of Haiti.

Entretanto, la ciudadanía de Santo Domingo se hallaba indignada con la administración de Báez —la cual encarcelaba adversarios y era sospechosa de preparar el desfalco del tesoro público—, vislumbrándose una inminente revuelta que encumbraría al general Luperón o al expresidente Cabral. Se desmintió por otra parte el rumor sobre la llegada de numerario para la adquisición de Samaná, presumiéndose que los partidarios de Báez obraban de acuerdo con el presidente Salnave de Haití.

records.summary_en: Based on the provided excerpt, Carlos and Valentin Baez recently undertook a confidential mission to Hayti to propose a treaty establishing a liberal, uniform tariff, common frontier port regulations, and the abolition of interior custom houses to free border trade. Additionally, Dominican troops are moving to the "Hunda Frontera" to cooperate with Hayti's forces in suppressing border guerilla outbreaks that are frequently misreported by the foreign press as major revolutions. The Dominican republic is currently reported to be perfectly quiet, with its people tired of civil war and increasingly interested in foreign enterprises.
records.summary_es: A tenor del extracto de prensa, Carlos y Valentín Báez cumplieron recientemente una misión reservada en Haití para proponer un tratado que consagrase un arancel liberal y uniforme, reglamentaciones aduaneras fronterizas comunes y la supresión de las aduanas interiores para franquear el tráfico fronterizo. Asimismo, destacamentos dominicanos marchaban hacia la frontera profunda para cooperar con las fuerzas haitianas en la represión de correrías guerrilleras en la demarcación, a menudo presentadas falsamente por la prensa extranjera como grandes revoluciones. Se informaba que la República Dominicana gozaba de absoluta quietud, hallándose la población fatigada de contiendas intestinas y deseosa de promover iniciativas foráneas.

The newspaper noted that supporters of Baez, including Jesurun's father (who had previously aided him and loaned him money), were regretting their actions or feeling deceived. records.headline: A letter from Santo Domingo City dated July 4, 1868 reports a spreading insurrection against President Baez, with…
records.summary_en: A letter from Santo Domingo City dated July 4, 1868 reports a spreading insurrection against President Baez, with General Polanco in the field in the south under ex-President Cabral and General Luperon, the revolutionists' commander-in-chief, sailing from St. Thomas to take command in the north. Government troops at Azua stay on the defensive while towns desert, prisoners are taken at Higuey, and the capital lives in alarm as money runs out and Baez cannot find men willing to fight.
records.summary_es: Una carta desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo fechada el 4 de julio de 1868 informa de una insurrección creciente contra el presidente Baez, con el general Polanco en campaña en el sur bajo el mando del expresidente Cabral y el general Luperon, comandante en jefe de los revolucionarios, zarpando de Santo Tomás para tomar el mando en el norte. Las tropas del gobierno en Azua se mantienen a la defensiva mientras los pueblos quedan desiertos, se toman prisioneros en Higuey y la capital vive en alarma porque se acaba el dinero y Baez no encuentra hombres dispuestos a luchar.

records.headline: President was on the best of terms with the American Minister

The newspaper also reported on various domestic conflicts and military movements, including the arrest of a senator named Iomean at Aux Cayes for alleged complicity with rebels, and historical background regarding Geffrard, British Consul General Mr. Spencer St. John, and the bombardment of fortifications by the steamer *Bulldog*.

records.headline: A dispatch from St.
records.summary_en: A dispatch from St. Domingo City, dated July 11, 1868, reports that rebel General Timoteo Ogando routed the government forces at Ceiba, killing General Brigman, and that an alarmed President Baez placed two cannons before his house and ordered forty prominent citizens, including men he had held in prison, to leave the country. It also reports aid and money reaching Baez from Curacao, Dominican exiles sailing from there under General Aybar, government troops living off the cattle of private owners, and whole companies deserting on the march.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo, fechado el 11 de julio de 1868, informa que el general rebelde Timoteo Ogando derrotó a las fuerzas del gobierno en Ceiba, dando muerte al general Brigman, y que un alarmado presidente Báez colocó dos cañones ante su casa y ordenó a cuarenta ciudadanos prominentes, incluidos hombres que había tenido presos, que abandonaran el país. También informa de ayuda y dinero que llegaban a Báez desde Curazao, de exiliados dominicanos que zarparon de allí bajo el mando del general Aybar, de tropas gubernamentales que vivían del ganado de propietarios privados y de compañías enteras que desertaban en la marcha.

records.summary_en: Writing from St. Domingo City on August 8, a *New York Times* correspondent reported that President Baez's enemies assembled in Hayti are awaiting the downfall of Salnave to cross the frontier and incite a rebellion, prompting Baez to bolster his border forces and release prisoners to join the army. Baez is also awaiting a delayed European loan and pinning hopes on the sale of a tract of land to the United States for $2,000,000 through his agent, Colonel Fabeus, with the bargain reportedly already closed with Mr. Seward. Meanwhile, General Luperon has been proclaimed Commander-in-Chief of the impending rebellion to overthrow Baez.
records.summary_es: Escribiendo desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo el 8 de agosto, un corresponsal de *The New York Times* comunicó que los adversarios del presidente Báez congregados en Haití aguardaban la caída de Salnave para cruzar la frontera y desatar una rebelión, lo que llevó a Báez a reforzar sus destacamentos fronterizos y excarcelar presidiarios para engrosar el ejército. Báez esperaba asimismo un demorado empréstito europeo y cifraba sus esperanzas en la enajenación de una franja de tierra a los Estados Unidos por 2.000.000 de dólares por mediación de su agente, el coronel Fabens, negocio presuntamente ya concertado con el secretario Seward. Entretanto, el general Luperón había sido proclamado general en jefe del inminente alzamiento armado para deponer a Báez.

records.summary_en: A private letter from Santo Domingo denounces the Baez administration, saying its efforts to obtain gold through the Samana negotiation, a Spanish protectorate and foreign loans have failed, while ruinous contributions are exacted from the people. Describe ganado incautado en la provincia de La Vega y vendido en Santiago, cuyo dinero fue presentado después en La Vega como parte de un préstamo extranjero, y enumera arrestos, contribuciones forzadas, el exilio de 22 presos políticos en la goleta Dos Hermanos y ejecuciones en Azua.

Meanwhile, foreign residents in Havana joined active-service volunteers for the seat of war, prominent individuals denied Mexican involvement in the rebellion, and military battalions prepared to sail for Gibara and take the field in Cuba.

En La Habana, por su parte, los residentes extranjeros se alistaron en los batallones de voluntarios de campaña para el teatro de operaciones, figuras prominentes desmintieron toda injerencia mexicana en la rebelión y varios contingentes militares se aprestaron a zarpar rumbo a Gibara para entrar en combate en Cuba.

records.summary_en: The *Worcester Daily Spy* reported that the island of St. Domingo is divided between the Dominican Republic, where Spaniards and their descendants rule, and Hayti, where negroes hold all governmental power. According to the newspaper's correspondent, the natives of both parts are entirely opposed to the United States obtaining a foothold on the island, and the Dominicans are described as demoralized, heavily armed, and consumed by rapid political revolutions, judicial murders, and private assassinations. Although overtures have been made regarding the sale of Samana to the United States despite local hostility toward foreigners, it is stated that any such treaty would likely be abrogated by the Dominicans if purchased.
records.summary_es: El *Worcester Daily Spy* refirió que la isla de Santo Domingo se halla dividida entre la República Dominicana, donde gobiernan los españoles y sus descendientes, y Haití, donde los negros retienen todo el poder político. Según el corresponsal del rotativo, los naturales de ambas partes se oponen tenazmente a que los Estados Unidos sienten pie en la isla, describiéndose a los dominicanos como desmoralizados, fuertemente pertrechados y consumidos por vertiginosas revoluciones políticas, ajusticiamientos judiciales y homicidios privados. Si bien se habían entablado propuestas para la venta de Samaná a los Estados Unidos a pesar de la hostilidad local hacia los extranjeros, se advertía que cualquier tratado de compra probablemente sería revocado por los dominicanos con posterioridad.

records.headline: A Washington letter attacks Secretary Seward's scheme for St.
records.summary_en: A Washington letter attacks Secretary Seward's scheme for St. Domingo, which shifted within weeks from a protectorate to annexation with no explanation offered for either. The writer argues that President Baez, entrenched in his capital with several civil wars to look after, has no more right to give his country to the United States than Seward would have to give the United States to Great Britain, and warns that the Samana Bay Company and the Alta Vela Guano Company would gain land, mines and guano while the United States took on the Dominican public debt.

El autor sostiene que el presidente Báez, atrincherado en su capital con varias guerras civiles que atender, no tiene más derecho a entregar su país a los Estados Unidos que el que tendría Seward de entregar los Estados Unidos a Gran Bretaña, y advierte que la Samana Bay Company y la Alta Vela Guano Company ganarían tierras, minas y guano mientras los Estados Unidos asumían la deuda pública dominicana.

records.summary_en: *The New York Herald* reported that Dominican envoy Pujol sought to offer Samaná or Manzanillo to the United States as a naval station, even as a free gift without requiring prior formal recognition. However, Secretary of State Seward, reportedly influenced by the Spanish minister, refused to grant Pujol an interview or acknowledge the Dominican Republic. The paper criticized the State Department for repeatedly disregarding strategic American opportunities in Samaná to accommodate Spanish interests.
records.summary_es: *The New York Herald* informó que el comisionado dominicano Pujol intentó ceder Samaná o Manzanillo a los Estados Unidos como estación naval, ofreciéndola incluso a título gratuito sin condicionarla al previo reconocimiento diplomático. No obstante, el secretario de Estado Seward, supuestamente influenciado por el ministro de España, se rehusó a conceder una audiencia a Pujol y a reconocer a la República Dominicana. records.summary_en: Based on the provided excerpt, the newspaper reported that the Dominican Republic's paper currency was overprinted by various chiefs and ultimately repudiated, leaving the masses with a deep aversion to government money. An attempted revolution in January to redeem a currency issue with silver failed to attract even 200 people. Additionally, General Cabral entered the Dominican territory and remained in the border belt without advancing further or being driven out, with conflicting reports claiming minor skirmishes resulting in fewer than a dozen casualties on either side up to May 5.

Una tentativa insurreccional en enero para rescatar una emisión fiduciaria en plata no logró concitar la adhesión ni de 200 hombres. Asimismo, el general Cabral incursionó en territorio dominicano manteniéndose en la franja fronteriza sin conseguir avanzar más ni ser desalojado, con partes contradictorios que reportaban escaramuzas aisladas que no alcanzaban la docena de bajas en ningún bando hasta el 5 de mayo.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported on conditions in Santo Domingo, noting strong popular sentiment in favor of annexation to the United States, favorable reports on mineral wealth by State Geologist Professor Gabb, and a record tobacco crop. The paper also reported that many Dominicans were departing to assist Cuban insurgents against Spain. While initial reports claimed former President Cabral's rebellion had failed, subsequent dispatches indicated Cabral had defeated government forces in several southern towns, prompting President Báez to concentrate his troops at Azua.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó sobre la situación en Santo Domingo, destacando una marcada corriente popular favorable a la anexión a los Estados Unidos, informes elogiosos sobre los yacimientos minerales rendidos por el geólogo del Estado, el profesor Gabb, y una cosecha tabacalera sin precedentes. El diario también dio cuenta de que numerosos dominicanos partían para socorrer a los insurrectos cubanos frente a España. Aunque las primeras noticias aseguraban el fracaso de la revuelta del expresidente Cabral, partes posteriores indicaron que Cabral había batido a las tropas del gobierno en varias poblaciones del sur, lo que constriñó al presidente Báez a reconcentrar sus contingentes en Azua.

records.summary_en: Gen. Luperón, acting with ex-President Cabral to overthrow the Báez government, used his steamer *Telegrafo* to bombard Puerto Plata intermittently for six days starting June 2. Because the vessel maintained a distant position, no damage, property destruction, or loss of life occurred, and the town's forts were unable to return fire before the steamer departed westward on the 8th. Meanwhile, intelligence indicated that Cabral had begun active military operations in the south-western territory as part of a coordinated plan to force Báez to divide his forces.
records.summary_es: El general Luperón, obrando en concierto con el expresidente Cabral para deponer al gobierno de Báez, empleó su vapor *Telégrafo* para cañonear intermitentemente a Puerto Plata durante seis días a partir del 2 de junio. Debido a que el buque conservó una prudente distancia de tiro, no se registraron daños materiales ni pérdidas de vidas, y los fuertes de la plaza no pudieron ripostar el fuego antes de que la nave partiese hacia el oeste el día 8. En tanto, informes confidenciales señalaban que Cabral había iniciado activas operaciones bélicas en el sudoeste como parte de un plan sincronizado para forzar a Báez a fraccionar sus tropas.

records.summary_en: A correspondent of the steamer Tybee, writing from Santo Domingo City on June 22, 1869, describes five lively days loading an assorted cargo of exports and visiting the capital, which he calls the oldest city in the western hemisphere, its site selected by Christopher Columbus. He describes the old walls and fortifications, the chapel built by Columbus and his sundial, the first cathedral with its gilded high altar and silver furnishings, and the many ancient Spanish buildings still in use, in a city whose population is now about half the 20,000 it once held.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal del vapor Tybee, que escribe desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo el 22 de junio de 1869, describe cinco días animados cargando un surtido cargamento de exportaciones y visitando la capital, a la que llama la ciudad más antigua del hemisferio occidental, cuyo sitio fue escogido por Cristóbal Colón. Describe las viejas murallas y fortificaciones, la capilla construida por Colón y su reloj de sol, la primera catedral con su altar mayor dorado y sus enseres de plata, y los muchos edificios españoles antiguos todavía en uso, en una ciudad cuya población es ahora cerca de la mitad de los 20,000 habitantes que tuvo una vez.

records.summary_en: This special report, datelined St. Domingo, July 12, 1869, presents Samana Bay as an American Gibraltar of the Antilles and describes its history, geography and importance to the United States. It recounts a fight in the bay between the Dominican war schooners Capotilla and Alta Gracia and the craft Telegrafo, and then surveys the bay's entrance, headlands, channels and islands, and the Yuna river, which enters the bay at its western end and is one of the largest rivers on the island.

Relata un combate en la bahía entre las goletas de guerra dominicanas Capotilla y Alta Gracia y la embarcación Telégrafo, y luego describe la entrada de la bahía, sus cabos, canales e islas, y el río Yuna, que desemboca en la bahía en su extremo occidental y es uno de los ríos más grandes de la isla.

records.headline: A special report dated July 12, 1869 calls Samana Bay the American Gibraltar of the Antilles and describes it in…
records.summary_en: A special report dated July 12, 1869 calls Samana Bay the American Gibraltar of the Antilles and describes it in detail: a mouth twenty-one miles wide between Cape Samana and Cape Raphael, a reach of thirty miles to the mouth of the Yuna River, and sheltering cays and reefs. records.summary_en: Writing from Porto Plata on September 6, 1869, the correspondent recalls that Columbus founded Isabella, the first European town in the New World, near here, and that only ruins remain where it stood. records.headline: The dispatch gives the case of Mr.
records.summary_en: The dispatch gives the case of Mr. Davis Hatch, a United States citizen who was living at Barahona as agent of a New York company interested in working salt mines. When government troops evacuated the port at the end of August, Hatch was taken with them to Azua and arrested, then brought to the capital and held in close confinement, then taken back to Azua, tried by court martial and sentenced to be shot. A messenger was at once sent back to Azua with a pardon for Hatch, and the dispatch says the anxiety of five days of suspense had a severe effect on his mind and health.
records.summary_es: El despacho expone el caso del señor Davis Hatch, ciudadano de los Estados Unidos que vivía en Barahona como agente de una compañía de Nueva York interesada en explotar minas de sal. Cuando las tropas del gobierno evacuaron el puerto a finales de agosto, Hatch fue llevado con ellos a Azua y arrestado, luego trasladado a la capital y mantenido en estricto confinamiento, y después devuelto a Azua, juzgado por un consejo de guerra y condenado a ser fusilado. De inmediato se envió un mensajero de regreso a Azua con un indulto para Hatch, y el despacho dice que la angustia de cinco días de suspense tuvo un efecto grave en su mente y su salud.

records.headline: Traordinary preparations now going on in the 'navy yards arc not
records.summary_en: According to the *Nashville Union and American*, extraordinary preparations in navy yards were reported to be for guarding the annexation of the Dominican Republic to the United States rather than for war with Spain over Cuba. The article stated that General Babcock, a confidential officer on Grant's staff, had settled the annexation conditions with San Domingo authorities, and the treaty—modeled after the Texas annexation—would be submitted to the Senate. Additionally, warships were sent to West Indies ports at President Baez's request to be present when the U.S. flag was hoisted, with opposition anticipated only from a revolutionary faction aided by Cabral.
records.summary_es: Según el *Nashville Union and American*, los extraordinarios aprestos en los astilleros navales respondían al propósito de asegurar la anexión de la República Dominicana a los Estados Unidos antes que a un conflicto armado con España a causa de Cuba. El artículo exponía que el general Babcock, edecán de confianza en el estado mayor de Grant, había acordado las cláusulas de anexión con las autoridades dominicanas, previéndose remitir al Senado el tratado —calcado del modelo de incorporación de Texas—. Se agregó asimismo que varios buques de guerra zarparon hacia las Antillas a requerimiento del presidente Báez para asistir al acto de izamiento del pabellón estadounidense, aguardándose resistencia tan solo de la facción rebelde auxiliada por Cabral.

records.headline: A United States Navy lieutenant writing from the island reports that he has travelled some two hundred miles since…
records.summary_en: A United States Navy lieutenant writing from the island reports that he has travelled some two hundred miles since leaving Santo Domingo, crossing the mountains and now working on the northern side under his instructions, keeping a full journal of what he has seen. He says that wherever he went he received the kindest attention, even in the mountains, and that he might have travelled with any amount of money without fear of being molested, though he also saw misery and destitution that would make the heart ache; the island's resources, he writes, are inexhaustible and want only population and a more industrious people to develop them.
records.summary_es: Un teniente de la Marina de los Estados Unidos que escribe desde la isla informa que ha viajado unas doscientas millas desde que salió de Santo Domingo, cruzando las montañas y trabajando ahora en el lado norte según sus instrucciones, llevando un diario completo de lo que ha visto. Dice que dondequiera que fue recibió la atención más amable, incluso en las montañas, y que podría haber viajado con cualquier cantidad de dinero sin temor de ser molestado, aunque también vio una miseria y una indigencia que daban dolor al corazón; los recursos de la isla, escribe, son inagotables y solo necesitan población y un pueblo más industrioso para desarrollarlos.

records.summary_en: The *New York Herald* argued that if the United States desires Samaná or any part of St. Domingo, it should simply purchase the territory to avoid future disputes, while criticizing the current government's policy as timid and narrow-minded. The newspaper also questioned whether the administration's sudden emphasis on the importance of the Bay of Samaná was a subterfuge designed to cover up its weak policy regarding Cuba.
records.summary_es: *The New York Herald* sostuvo que, si los Estados Unidos ambicionan la bahía de Samaná o cualquier otra comarca de Santo Domingo, debieran comprar llanamente el territorio para prevenir futuros litigios, fustigando la conducta del actual gabinete estadounidense como pusilánime y estrecha de miras. El diario cuestionó además si el súbito interés de la administración por la bahía de Samaná constituía un subterfugio para encubrir su endeble ejecutoria frente a la cuestión cubana.

records.summary_en: According to the newspaper, the American government made a previous effort to obtain the bay and peninsula of Samana approximately fifteen years prior under President Franklin Pierce and Secretary of State Wm. L. Marcy. In June 1854, then-Captain George B. McClellan was sent on a secret expedition to the West Indies aboard the frigate *Columbia* to select a convenient harbor and coaling station for the U.S. Navy. McClellan returned in September with maps, sketches, and information, resulting in the selection of the bay and peninsula of Samana for the proposed station.
records.summary_es: Según el diario, el gobierno estadounidense realizó una tentativa anterior para adquirir la bahía y la península de Samaná unos quince años atrás, bajo la presidencia de Franklin Pierce y con Wm. L. Marcy como secretario de Estado. En junio de 1854, el entonces capitán George B. McClellan fue comisionado en misión reservada a las Antillas a bordo de la fragata *Columbia* con objeto de localizar una bahía adecuada y estación carbonera para la marina de los Estados Unidos. McClellan regresó en septiembre con planos, croquis e informes periciales, determinando la elección de la bahía y península de Samaná para el proyectado establecimiento naval.

records.headline: Since the acquisition of Samana by the United States government was announced, many have contended it is only the…
records.summary_en: Since the acquisition of Samana by the United States government was announced, many have contended it is only the preliminary move toward possession of the whole island, and the paper's correspondents report that Dominicans themselves favor annexation. Before leaving office Secretary Seward had received President Baez's proposition for an American protectorate, which a House committee majority favored but which was defeated in Congress for lack of information about Dominican affairs, and New York business men are now discussing Samana's commercial value under a fifty years' lease, with a bank, lumber companies and coal and copper mines already being talked of.
records.summary_es: Desde que se anunció la adquisición de Samaná por el gobierno de los Estados Unidos, muchos han sostenido que es solo el paso preliminar hacia la posesión de toda la isla, y los corresponsales del periódico informan que los propios dominicanos favorecen la anexión. Antes de dejar el cargo, el secretario Seward había recibido la proposición del presidente Báez de un protectorado estadounidense, que la mayoría de una comisión de la Cámara favoreció pero que fue derrotada en el Congreso por falta de información sobre los asuntos dominicanos, y los hombres de negocios de Nueva York discuten ahora el valor comercial de Samaná bajo un arrendamiento de cincuenta años, hablándose ya de un banco, compañías madereras y minas de carbón y cobre.

records.headline: WHAT THE DOMINICANS SAY.
records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* warned that using violence against San Domingo would provoke widespread alarm and hatred throughout South America. The article also described the island's history—including its discovery by Columbus, its division between Haiti and San Domingo, Spain's 1861 reannexation and subsequent 1863–1865 defeat, and Dominican independence—while noting that Buenaventura Baez has served as President since 1867 and is one of the negotiators of the annexation treaty.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* advirtió que el empleo de la fuerza contra Santo Domingo concitaría honda alarma y animadversión en toda la América del Sur. El artículo reseñó asimismo la trayectoria histórica de la isla —desde su descubrimiento por Colón y su división entre Haití y Santo Domingo, hasta la reanexión española de 1861, su posterior derrota entre 1863 y 1865 y la reconquista de la soberanía dominicana—, haciendo constar que Buenaventura Báez presidía la nación desde 1867 y figuraba como uno de los negociadores del tratado de anexión.

records.full_text:
WHAT THE DOMINICANS SAY.

At date of St. Domingo, December 6, a Committee of Dominicans write to us as follows:

The world will see with scandal Gen. Grant pursuing his plans with regard to this island. The world, as well as Gen. Grant and his Yankees, ought to know that in the list of Dominican restorers are not to be found the names of Baez, Gautier, Felix Delmonte, nor any of those who form this band of traitors. These men—the Spaniards of yesterday—know that it will not be possible for them to continue in the government of this country, and for that reason they are negotiating it. President Grant does not know—cannot know what is passing here. Daily are being executed honorable Dominicans, in witness of which we refer to the Government’s official gazette, and to any stranger—and even to any honest Yankee—not to such corrupt speculators as Cazneau and Fabens. Gen. Grant intends well to the Dominican Republic, and if the Congress and Senate participate in his intention, why do they not wait for the resolution of the present question by the free act of the Dominicans themselves? A violence done to San Domingo will raise a cry of alarm which will resound in all South America, and with that cry will arise a hatred equal to that which Spain will ever deserve.

The article noted that the U.S. government might encounter competing claims or leases regarding Samana Bay, highlighting a "sharp colored American" mariner who bought land there five years prior and now owns a considerable portion of the available water frontage, coal lands, and valuable property where a naval station would likely be located.

records.headline: News brought by steamer reports that the planned occupation of the Bay of Samana by the United States is stirring…
records.summary_en: News brought by steamer reports that the planned occupation of the Bay of Samana by the United States is stirring strong feeling in Haiti, where the provisional government of Saget, friendly to Cabral, is expected to help him defeat Baez's cession of the bay and where a clash with the United States is feared possible. The item also prints Saget's address to the Haitians, appealing to them to preserve public order, repair their losses under peace, and rebuild their democratic institutions while guarding against tyranny.
records.summary_es: Las noticias traídas por vapor informan que la ocupación planeada de la bahía de Samana por los Estados Unidos está provocando fuertes sentimientos en Haití, donde se espera que el gobierno provisional de Saget, amigo de Cabral, lo ayude a derrotar la cesión de la bahía por parte de Baez y donde se teme un posible enfrentamiento con los Estados Unidos. La nota también reproduce el discurso de Saget a los haitianos, en el que les pide preservar el orden público, reparar sus pérdidas bajo la paz y reconstruir sus instituciones democráticas protegiéndose contra la tiranía.

records.summary_en: Pursuant to a request by the Chairman of Foreign Affairs, Mr. Seward dispatched Mr. Fabens to San Domingo to gather information—specifically regarding the republic's debt—after which Fabens reported the debt was only about $600,000 while lacking information on grants and franchises due to his own suspected interest in them. Following Fabens's return to Washington around April 1, Baez, his Ministers, and the Consulting Committee of the Senate made a loan contract on May 1st, which was printed in the Government journal on September 29, 1869, nearly five months later.
records.summary_es: A solicitud del presidente del Comité de Asuntos Exteriores, el secretario Seward comisionó al Sr. Fabens a Santo Domingo para acopiar datos —en especial sobre la deuda de la república—, tras lo cual Fabens aseguró que la deuda apenas ascendía a unos 600.000 dólares, omitiendo información sobre concesiones y privilegios por sus propios presuntos intereses en los mismos. Al regreso de Fabens a Washington hacia el 1 de abril, Báez, su gabinete y la Comisión Consultiva del Senado convinieron un contrato de empréstito el 1 de mayo, el cual vio la luz en el diario oficial el 29 de septiembre de 1869, casi cinco meses más tarde.

records.headline: This history of the Dominican Republic recounts how Santana negotiated a treaty with General Cazneau, President…
records.summary_en: This history of the Dominican Republic recounts how Santana negotiated a treaty with General Cazneau, President Pierce's agent, on October 6, 1854, whose secret stipulations are believed to have provided for ceding the Bay of Samana to the United States, though it was never ratified. It follows Santana's deposition in 1856, Baez's second term and expulsion in 1858, the Spanish invasion and the two-year war that ended with Spain's defeat and withdrawal, and the rapid succession of Salcedo, Espaillet, Polanco, Pimentel, Cabral and Guillermo that followed.
records.summary_es: Esta historia de la República Dominicana relata cómo Santana negoció un tratado con el general Cazneau, agente del presidente Pierce, el 6 de octubre de 1854, cuyas estipulaciones secretas, según se cree, contemplaban la cesión de la bahía de Samaná a los Estados Unidos, aunque nunca fue ratificado. Sigue con la deposición de Santana en 1856, el segundo gobierno de Báez y su expulsión en 1858, la invasión española y la guerra de dos años que terminó con la derrota y retirada de España, y la rápida sucesión de Salcedo, Espaillat, Polanco, Pimentel, Cabral y Guillermo que vino después.

records.headline: This history of Samana Bay recounts how the natives called the land Samana, how their cacique Cayacoa visited…
records.summary_en: This history of Samana Bay recounts how the natives called the land Samana, how their cacique Cayacoa visited Columbus's ship, and how Columbus christened the bay De las Flechas after a skirmish there. It also tells how the English pirate Jack Banister, at the close of the seventeenth century, placed his guns on one of the cays and with 200 men beat off two English frigates, killing more than 120 of the assailants, an engagement that gave the islets the name Banister's Cays.
records.summary_es: Esta historia de la bahía de Samaná cuenta cómo los naturales llamaban Samaná a la tierra, cómo su cacique Cayacoa visitó la nave de Colón y cómo Colón bautizó la bahía De las Flechas tras una escaramuza en el lugar. Cuenta también cómo el pirata inglés Jack Banister, a fines del siglo XVII, colocó sus cañones en uno de los cayos y con 200 hombres rechazó a dos fragatas inglesas, matando a más de 120 de los asaltantes, un combate que dio a los islotes el nombre de Banister's Cays.

records.summary_en: Article 4 of the November 29, 1869, convention required ratification by both parties—including the advice and consent of the U.S. Senate—within four months in Washington, D.C., with the United States pledging protection against foreign intervention during that period. Meanwhile, the antagonists of President Baez, led by Luperon and Cabral, issued violent protests against the Samana scheme in December 1869. Despite this opposition, the first year's rent of $150,000 for the bay was paid to President Baez in December from a $300,000 fund previously set aside by Secretary Seward.
records.summary_es: El artículo 4 de la convención del 29 de noviembre de 1869 estipulaba que la ratificación por ambas partes —incluyendo el consejo y consentimiento del Senado de los Estados Unidos— debía formalizarse en un plazo de cuatro meses en Washington, D. Entretanto, los opositores al presidente Báez, capitaneados por Luperón y Cabral, emitieron enérgicas protestas contra las maquinaciones sobre Samaná en diciembre de 1869. records.summary_en: In a conversation with senators on Friday, the President urged the ratification of the treaty to acquire San Domingo, warning that otherwise the territory might be offered to a European government, thereby undermining the Monroe Doctrine. He presented evidence that the majority of the people voted for annexation and that insurrectionary leaders, whose rebellion lacked strength after being cut off from Hayti, were not inherently opposed to it. Furthermore, the President expressed his belief that acquiring San Domingo would immediately benefit U.S. commerce and the Darien canal, while potentially leading to broader territorial control of the Gulf islands.
records.summary_es: En conferencia con senadores el viernes, el presidente encareció la pronta ratificación del tratado para incorporar a Santo Domingo, advirtiendo de que, en caso contrario, dicho territorio podría ser brindado a una potencia europea en quebranto de la doctrina Monroe. Exhibió pruebas de que la generalidad de la ciudadanía sufragó a favor de la anexión y de que los caudillos insurrectos, cuyas fuerzas languidecían al quedar desasistidos desde Haití, no repudiaban la medida en esencia. Manifestó asimismo su convicción de que la anexión de Santo Domingo acarrearía inmediatos provechos al tráfico marítimo estadounidense y al proyectado canal del Darién, franquando de paso el control de las islas del Golfo.

records.summary_en: The *Chicago Tribune* reported on the negotiations involving Babcock, Sackett, Fablos, Cazeneau, and Baez, noting that the final treaty closely resembled the one drafted in the U.S. State Department. According to the excerpt, Babcock and Sackett rejected Cazeneau's proposal for a secret treaty, and Babcock declined a land grant at Samana offered to him by Baez, Fablos, and Cazeneau. The report also details Babcock's correspondence with Cazeneau—shared with President Grant—and actions regarding the American flag and coaling station at Samana following the treaty's signing.
records.summary_es: El *Chicago Tribune* dio cuenta de las negociaciones mantenidas entre Babcock, Sackett, Fabens [Fablos], Cazneau [Cazeneau] y Báez, señalando que el texto final del tratado concordaba sustancialmente con el redactado en el Departamento de Estado de los Estados Unidos. Conforme al extracto, Babcock y Sackett desestimaron la propuesta de Cazneau de concertar un tratado secreto, en tanto que Babcock declinó una concesión de tierras en Samaná que le brindaron Báez, Fabens y Cazneau. La relación detalla además la correspondencia sostenida entre Babcock y Cazneau —elevada al presidente Grant— y las resoluciones sobre el izamiento del pabellón estadounidense y la instalación del apostadero de carbón en Samaná tras la firma del convenio.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported on August 4, 1870, that the Dominican government retained ample power to renew annexation negotiations with the United States and propose modifications to address opponents' objections. It noted that the U.S. protectorate had been extended for one year from July 1, 1870, providing the Dominicans with a guaranteed shield against internal revolution, tensions with Hayti, and European intervention. Additionally, the newspaper stated that President Baez and his ministers expressed regret over attacks against President Grant and General Babcock regarding the affair, while dismissing charges made against themselves by unfamiliar critics.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó el 4 de agosto de 1870 que el gobierno dominicano conservaba plenas facultades para reanudar las negociaciones de anexión con los Estados Unidos y proponer modificaciones encaminadas a salvar los reparos de la oposición. Destacó que el protectorado estadounidense había sido prorrogado por un año a partir del 1 de julio de 1870, brindando a los dominicanos un escudo garantizado frente a revoluciones intestinas, desavenencias con Haití e intervenciones europeas. Además, el periódico consignó que el presidente Báez y sus ministros lamentaron los ataques dirigidos contra el presidente Grant y el general Babcock a propósito de este asunto, desestimando los cargos que detractores desconocidos formularon en su contra.

records.headline: In the Senate on December 9, Mr.
records.summary_en: In the Senate on December 9, Mr. Sumner of Massachusetts submitted a resolution asking the President to send the Senate all papers and correspondence relating to the proposed annexation of the Dominican portion of the island of St. Domingo or the purchase of any part of it. The resolution also calls for an account of the Dominican government's debt and liabilities, especially to Haiti, the constitutional provisions on selling the national domain, communications from Haiti, the instructions given to the American naval squadron, and information on President Baez's position and on how far he has been maintained in power by United States vessels of war; on Mr. Conkling's suggestion it was laid over temporarily and ordered printed.
records.summary_es: En el Senado, el 9 de diciembre, el señor Sumner de Massachusetts presentó una resolución pidiendo al Presidente que enviara al Senado todos los documentos y la correspondencia relativos a la anexión propuesta de la parte dominicana de la isla de Santo Domingo o a la compra de cualquier parte de ella. La resolución pide también una relación de la deuda y las obligaciones del gobierno dominicano, especialmente con Haití, las disposiciones constitucionales sobre la venta del dominio nacional, las comunicaciones de Haití, las instrucciones dadas a la escuadra naval estadounidense e información sobre la posición del presidente Báez y sobre hasta qué punto ha sido mantenido en el poder por buques de guerra de los Estados Unidos; a sugerencia del señor Conkling quedó sobre la mesa temporalmente y se ordenó su impresión.

records.headline: A Washington correspondent traces the history of the scheme to annex San Domingo, which the President is pressing…
records.summary_en: A Washington correspondent traces the history of the scheme to annex San Domingo, which the President is pressing again, with General Butler expected to introduce the annexation resolutions in the House. He recounts how General Cazeneau had long promoted annexation, how General Babcock's treaty failed in the Senate, and how Secretary Fish had warned Babcock against Cazeneau because of the vast land concessions Cazeneau was known to have secured in the Bay of Samana and elsewhere.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal en Washington traza la historia del plan de anexionar Santo Domingo, que el presidente está impulsando de nuevo, y se espera que el general Butler presente las resoluciones de anexión en la Cámara. Cuenta cómo el general Cazeneau había promovido la anexión durante mucho tiempo, cómo el tratado del general Babcock fracasó en el Senado, y cómo el secretario Fish había advertido a Babcock contra Cazeneau por las vastas concesiones de tierras que se sabía que Cazeneau había conseguido en la bahía de Samaná y en otros lugares.

records.summary_en: The *Chicago Tribune* reported that the population of Dominica was originally opposed to annexation, and that a subsequent plebiscite revived by General Grant was a "perfect farce" in which Baez's soldiers seized and imprisoned anyone who voted against it. The newspaper noted that the Dominican Republic was engaged in a civil war with insurgents led by former President General Cabral controlling the countryside, and that annexation would saddle the United States with roughly fourteen million dollars in debt, including a 30,000,000-franc gold debt owed to Hayti.

El rotativo hizo notar que la República Dominicana se hallaba inmersa en una guerra civil donde los insurrectos capitaneados por el expresidente general Cabral dominaban las zonas rurales, y que la anexión cargaría a los Estados Unidos con una deuda aproximada de catorce millones de dólares, incluidos 30.000.000 de francos en oro adeudados a Haití.

records.summary_en: A Washington item explains that the Seward-Stevens West India fund is now exhausted: Seward spent most of $100,000 of it on his West Indies trip, and General Babcock took the remaining $150,000 to lease the Bay of Samana. It reports that Mr. Dawes, chairman of the House Committee on Appropriations, refused two senators' request for a bill to pay the rent now due to Envoy Fabens, saying he could only make appropriations authorized by law, and that Senator Sumner calls the whole proceeding without the shadow of law.

records.headline: The report covers a Senate debate on the annexation of St.
records.summary_en: The report covers a Senate debate on the annexation of St. Domingo, in which one speaker denounced the scheme as a private, corrupt job, saying the annexation would be only of husks because the kernels had already gone to private parties. Other senators spoke on both sides: Mr. Hoar of Massachusetts refused to support the measure out of respect for the President, Mr. Stevenson of Ohio favored acquiring Dominica for its minerals, harbors and fertile soil, and a dispatch was read announcing that the Indiana Senate had instructed its senators to vote against annexation.
records.summary_es: El informe cubre un debate en el Senado sobre la anexión de Santo Domingo, en el que un orador denunció el plan como un negocio privado y corrupto, diciendo que la anexión sería solo de cáscaras porque el grano ya había ido a parar a manos privadas. Otros senadores hablaron en ambos sentidos: el Sr. Hoar, de Massachusetts, se negó a apoyar la medida por respeto al Presidente, el Sr. Stevenson, de Ohio, favoreció adquirir Dominica por sus minerales, puertos y suelo fértil, y se leyó un despacho que anunciaba que el Senado de Indiana había instruido a sus senadores a votar contra la anexión.

records.headline: A Washington article traces the money behind the Samana lease to a West India fund obtained by Thaddeus Stevens,…
records.summary_en: A Washington article traces the money behind the Samana lease to a West India fund obtained by Thaddeus Stevens, saying Seward took $100,000 of it on his West Indies trip and General Babcock took the balance of $150,000, with which he leased the Bay of Samana. With that fund now exhausted, the article says, Senators friendly to the administration asked Representative Dawes to bring in a bill appropriating $150,000 for the payment now due to Fabens, but Dawes refused because there is no law for it, and Senator Sumner is quoted as saying the whole proceeding is without a shadow of law.
records.summary_es: Un artículo de Washington atribuye el dinero del arrendamiento de Samaná a un fondo para las Indias Occidentales obtenido por Thaddeus Stevens, y dice que Seward se llevó 100.000 dólares de ese fondo en su viaje a las Indias Occidentales y que el general Babcock se llevó el resto, 150.000 dólares, con los que arrendó la bahía de Samaná. Agotado ya ese fondo, dice el artículo, senadores afines a la administración pidieron al representante Dawes que presentara un proyecto para asignar 150.000 dólares para el pago que ahora se debe a Fabens, pero Dawes se negó porque no existe ley que lo autorice, y se cita al senador Sumner diciendo que todo el procedimiento carece de la menor base legal.

records.headline: The Senate resumed debate on the resolution for a commission to visit San Domingo, with Mr.
records.summary_en: The Senate resumed debate on the resolution for a commission to visit San Domingo, with Mr. Sumner proposing that the commissioners inquire especially into the alleged civil war in Dominica, the territory held by the opposing parties, and the republic's relations with Hayti. Senator Schurz spoke at length in determined hostility to annexation, while Senators Stewart, Morton and Yates argued for expansion, Morton reporting that the leader Cabral favored annexation as an independent question but opposed it under Baez.
records.summary_es: El Senado reanudó el debate sobre la resolución para que una comisión visitara Santo Domingo, y el Sr. Sumner propuso que los comisionados investigaran especialmente la supuesta guerra civil en Dominica, el territorio ocupado por las partes en pugna, y las relaciones de la república con Haití. El senador Schurz habló extensamente con hostilidad decidida hacia la anexión, mientras los senadores Stewart, Morton y Yates argumentaron a favor de la expansión, y Morton informó que el caudillo Cabral favorecía la anexión como cuestión independiente pero se oponía a ella bajo Báez.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* highlighted the rich agricultural potential and natural resources of Santo Domingo, including its fertile soil, fine harbors, and river networks. The article noted that sugar cane, coffee, and especially tobacco thrived, with large amounts of Dominican tobacco exported monthly via Puerto Plata to European markets like Bremen and Hamburg.

El artículo apuntó que la caña de azúcar, el café y muy especialmente el tabaco prosperaban con lozanía, exportándose mensualmente copiosos cargamentos de tabaco dominicano por Puerto Plata hacia plazas europeas como Bremen y Hamburgo.

records.headline: A correspondent who travelled extensively through the island reports that in Santiago, Puerto Plata, La Vega,…
records.summary_en: A correspondent who travelled extensively through the island reports that in Santiago, Puerto Plata, La Vega, Macoris and Moca the universal sentiment was in favour of annexation, with people heartily tired of war and the better class of merchants and property holders enthusiastically endorsing President Baez and his policy. He reports that the election at Azua resulted in an unprecedented majority in favour of annexation, and denies the charge that grants had been given to those sent to negotiate the treaty. A further dispatch adds that news of the appointment of a United States commission was generally favourably received at St. Domingo.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal que viajó extensamente por la isla informa que en Santiago, Puerto Plata, La Vega, Macorís y Moca el sentimiento universal era favorable a la anexión, con un pueblo muy cansado de la guerra y la clase alta de comerciantes y propietarios apoyando con entusiasmo al presidente Báez y su política. Informa que la elección en Azua dio una mayoría sin precedentes a favor de la anexión, y niega la acusación de que se hubieran dado concesiones a los enviados a negociar el tratado. Otro despacho añade que la noticia del nombramiento de una comisión de los Estados Unidos fue recibida en general favorablemente en Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: Andrew D. White, a member of the San Domingo Commission, had a very agreeable interview with President Grant, who told him he was anxious to have everything thoroughly sifted. records.headline: Commander John Irwin reports how, at President Baez's request, he sent Lieutenant Commander McCook and the Nantasket…
records.summary_en: Commander John Irwin reports how, at President Baez's request, he sent Lieutenant Commander McCook and the Nantasket to Azua, where partisans of Cabral, accompanied by Haitians, were causing trouble, and then to Puerto Plata when Baez warned that Luperon's partisans, aided by men from Turks Island, intended to seize that place. He adds that Baez later reported Cabral moving on Azua with a force of Haitians and Dominicans, countenanced by the Haitian government, and asked him to carry dispatches to St. Thomas for the American government.
records.summary_es: El comandante John Irwin relata cómo, a petición del presidente Báez, envió al teniente comandante McCook y al Nantasket a Azua, donde los partidarios de Cabral, acompañados de haitianos, estaban causando problemas, y luego a Puerto Plata cuando Báez advirtió que los partidarios de Luperón, ayudados por hombres de las islas Turcas, pretendían apoderarse de ese lugar. Añade que Báez informó después que Cabral avanzaba sobre Azua con una fuerza de haitianos y dominicanos, con el respaldo del gobierno haitiano, y le pidió llevar despachos a St. Thomas para el gobierno estadounidense.

records.headline: A Herald dispatch from Samana reports local claims that there is no sickness there worth speaking about, while…
records.summary_en: A Herald dispatch from Samana reports local claims that there is no sickness there worth speaking about, while cautioning that the people have every motive to make a favorable impression on the Commission. The writer finds the climate agreeable and the breezes on the bay balmy, the soil rich and the vegetation luxuriant with palms and coconut groves, but notes that little is raised for market except a few oranges and coconuts, and that improving the country is above all a question of labor.
records.summary_es: Un despacho del Herald desde Samaná recoge las afirmaciones locales de que allí no hay enfermedades de las que valga la pena hablar, advirtiendo a la vez que la gente tiene todos los motivos para causar una impresión favorable a la Comisión. El autor encuentra el clima agradable y las brisas de la bahía templadas, el suelo rico y la vegetación exuberante con palmeras y cocotales, pero señala que poco se cultiva para el mercado salvo unas cuantas naranjas y cocos, y que mejorar el país es ante todo una cuestión de mano de obra.

records.summary_en: A Samana dispatch reports that the soil is rich and deep even on the hills, and that the botanists and naturalists have found interesting new specimens, though no reports from them have yet been made up. The writer calls the lease of the bay's privileges to the United States, at a large yearly rent, very much like a 'job,' and reports that Frederick Douglass spoke in the little plaza at Samana to about 130 people, talking of the glory of the United States and of freedom from slavery.

El autor dice que el arrendamiento de los privilegios de la bahía a los Estados Unidos, por una renta anual elevada, se parece mucho a un negocio turbio, e informa que Frederick Douglass habló en la pequeña plaza de Samaná ante unas 130 personas, hablando de la gloria de los Estados Unidos y de la libertad de la esclavitud.

records.headline: The dispatch reports that the officials at Samana pray for annexation, and explains that Colonel Abreu, whom the…
records.summary_en: The dispatch reports that the officials at Samana pray for annexation, and explains that Colonel Abreu, whom the commissioners had honoured as the chief man there, is only the special agent and military commander of the Dominican government, while the governor of this section is General Acosta. The commission, with its geologists, botanists, naturalists and correspondents, has been sending parties out to explore the country bordering the bay and up to the mouths of the Yuna River, and going ashore daily to talk with the people and examine their plantations.
records.summary_es: El despacho informa que los funcionarios de Samaná ruegan por la anexión, y explica que el coronel Abreu, a quien los comisionados habían honrado como el hombre principal del lugar, es solo el agente especial y comandante militar del gobierno dominicano, mientras que el gobernador de esta sección es el general Acosta. La comisión, con sus geólogos, botánicos, naturalistas y corresponsales, ha estado enviando grupos a explorar el país que bordea la bahía y hasta las bocas del río Yuna, y desembarcando a diario para hablar con la gente y examinar sus plantaciones.

records.headline: A Herald correspondent reports arriving at St.
records.summary_en: A Herald correspondent reports arriving at St. Domingo City on February 3 after a thirty-five hours' passage from Samana, and describes the so-called harbor as a poor roadstead the Tennessee could not leave, where vessels roll heavily even in a light land breeze. In the morning the ship fired a salute of twenty-one guns, which the Dominican fort returned, and the correspondent describes St. Domingo as a quaint, ancient and dilapidated town of seven or eight thousand inhabitants, the oldest place built by Europeans in America.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal del Herald informa de su llegada a la ciudad de Santo Domingo el 3 de febrero tras una travesía de treinta y cinco horas desde Samaná, y describe el llamado puerto como una mala rada que la Tennessee no podía abandonar, donde los buques se balancean pesadamente aun con una ligera brisa de tierra. Por la mañana el buque disparó una salva de veintiún cañonazos, que el fuerte dominicano devolvió, y el corresponsal describe Santo Domingo como una ciudad pintoresca, antigua y derruida de siete u ocho mil habitantes, el lugar más antiguo construido por europeos en América.

records.headline: The Tennessee arrived at Santo Domingo from Samana, a few hours after the Nantasket, and the United States…
records.summary_en: The Tennessee arrived at Santo Domingo from Samana, a few hours after the Nantasket, and the United States commissioners came ashore. The dispatch recounts how President Baez's offer of an unoccupied palace for the commissioners was declined by their secretaries, who instead rented a smaller house belonging to Baez and then had to ask him for cots and other necessities, while the correspondents accepted the palace. That day the commission paid a formal visit to Baez, presenting President Grant's autograph letter, and Baez replied that he desired a closer union of the two republics and offered every facility for inquiry, including hearing opponents of annexation.
records.summary_es: El Tennessee llegó a Santo Domingo desde Samaná, pocas horas después del Nantasket, y los comisionados de los Estados Unidos bajaron a tierra. El despacho cuenta cómo el ofrecimiento del presidente Báez de un palacio desocupado para los comisionados fue rechazado por los secretarios de estos, que en su lugar alquilaron una casa más pequeña perteneciente a Báez y luego tuvieron que pedirle catres y otros artículos necesarios, mientras que los corresponsales sí aceptaron el palacio. Ese día la comisión hizo una visita formal a Báez, presentándole la carta autógrafa del presidente Grant, y Báez respondió que deseaba una unión más estrecha de las dos repúblicas y ofreció todas las facilidades para la investigación, incluida la de escuchar a los opositores de la anexión.

records.summary_en: The report presents President Grant's letter of January 15, 1871, introducing Commissioners B. B. Wade, A. D. White and S. G. Howe, with Judge A. A. Burton as secretary, and the Commission's address placing that letter in President Baez's hands in Santo Domingo. Baez replied that he understood the mission, ordered by Congress, to be absolutely one of peace, said his republic desired the pacification of the country, the development of its riches by labor and guarantees for the existence, liberty and property of citizens, and promised the commissioners the most ample and absolute liberty in carrying out their inquiries.

records.summary_en: A Santo Domingo dispatch says President Baez emphatically denies reports that he intended to leave the country, and that because of reported troubles at Azua the United States steamer Nantasket would probably sail for that port. The commission had a long interview with Baez and his cabinet, and Baez offered guides, interpreters and, if needed, a guard, and agreed to grant safe conduct to the city even to Cabral or any of his partisans whom the commission wished to consult.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Santo Domingo dice que el presidente Báez niega enfáticamente los informes de que pensaba abandonar el país, y que, a causa de los disturbios reportados en Azua, el vapor estadounidense Nantasket probablemente zarparía hacia ese puerto. La comisión tuvo una larga entrevista con Báez y su gabinete, y Báez ofreció guías, intérpretes y, si fuera necesario, una guardia, y aceptó conceder salvoconducto hasta la ciudad incluso a Cabral o a cualquiera de sus partidarios a quienes la comisión deseara consultar.

records.headline: President Baez tells the commission he himself held an election with a perfectly free vote to obtain the true…
records.summary_en: President Baez tells the commission he himself held an election with a perfectly free vote to obtain the true sentiment of the people. A Tribune correspondent's account of Santa Barbara de Samana follows, describing a poor village of 80 or 90 bamboo and palm-thatched buildings along half a mile of shore, with about 250 inhabitants in the village and about 3,000 on the whole peninsula, a majority of the villagers speaking English.
records.summary_es: El presidente Báez dice a la comisión que él mismo celebró unas elecciones con voto perfectamente libre para obtener el verdadero sentimiento del pueblo. Sigue el relato de un corresponsal de la Tribune sobre Santa Bárbara de Samaná, que describe un pueblo pobre de 80 o 90 edificios de bambú y techo de palma a lo largo de media milla de costa, con unos 250 habitantes en el pueblo y unos 3.000 en toda la península, hablando inglés la mayoría de los vecinos.

records.headline: A Tribune correspondent describes the San Domingo expedition's voyage to Samana Bay: charming weather for two days,…
records.summary_en: A Tribune correspondent describes the San Domingo expedition's voyage to Samana Bay: charming weather for two days, then stormy seas from the latitude of Hatteras onward, until land was sighted on the morning of January 24. Rounding Cape Cabron and entering the bay, the party saw the roofs of Santa Barbara de Samana, palm tops, green hills and small farm patches, and dropped anchor in the outer harbor at two o'clock that afternoon.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal del Tribune describe el viaje de la expedición a Santo Domingo hasta la bahía de Samaná: tiempo encantador durante dos días y luego mares tormentosos desde la latitud de Hatteras en adelante, hasta que se avistó tierra en la mañana del 24 de enero. Al doblar el Cabo Cabrón y entrar en la bahía, el grupo vio los techos de Santa Bárbara de Samaná, las copas de las palmas, las colinas verdes y pequeños pedazos de tierra cultivada, y echó el ancla en el puerto exterior a las dos de esa tarde.

records.headline: A correspondent describes his ship's arrival at Samana, sighting land on the morning of the 24th, tracing the…
records.summary_en: A correspondent describes his ship's arrival at Samana, sighting land on the morning of the 24th, tracing the mountain range westward from Cape Cabron, and entering the bay past hills, palm groves and small settlements to Santa Barbara de Samana. The ship anchored in the outer harbor about two miles from the village, where the American flag floated over the property leased by the United States and the steamer Nantasket lay, and the commissioners landed to visit the local authorities.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal describe la llegada de su barco a Samaná, el avistamiento de tierra en la mañana del 24, el seguimiento de la cordillera hacia el oeste desde el cabo Cabrón, y la entrada a la bahía pasando colinas, palmerales y pequeños poblados hasta Santa Bárbara de Samaná. El barco ancló en el puerto exterior, a unas dos millas del pueblo, donde la bandera americana ondeaba sobre la propiedad arrendada por los Estados Unidos y se encontraba el vapor Nantasket, y los comisionados desembarcaron para visitar a las autoridades locales.

records.headline: The correspondent describes sailing into Samana Bay on the 24th, rounding Cape Cabron to find Santa Barbara de…
records.summary_en: The correspondent describes sailing into Samana Bay on the 24th, rounding Cape Cabron to find Santa Barbara de Samana coming into view, and anchoring in the outer harbour near the United States steamer Nantasket, with the American flag flying over the property leased by the United States. Ashore the next day, the party inspected the town's few public buildings, its Catholic church, a Methodist church being built, and schools whose pupils include descendants of the coloured colony sent here from Philadelphia, whose textbooks are all in English.
records.summary_es: El corresponsal describe la entrada en la bahía de Samaná el día 24, doblando el cabo Cabrón hasta ver aparecer Santa Bárbara de Samaná, y el fondeo en el puerto exterior cerca del vapor americano Nantasket, con la bandera americana ondeando sobre la propiedad arrendada por los Estados Unidos. Al día siguiente en tierra, el grupo inspeccionó los pocos edificios públicos del pueblo, su iglesia católica, una iglesia metodista en construcción, y escuelas cuyos alumnos incluyen descendientes de la colonia de color enviada aquí desde Filadelfia, cuyos libros de texto están todos en inglés.
