records.summary_en: Based on the provided excerpt, the newspaper reported that while the white and better class of people sympathized with the revolutionary (Moa) party, a plot by young men in Santo Domingo to seize the city was uncovered after a messenger boy was arrested and forced to confess under threat of execution. Consequently, the government arrested about sixty implicated young men from the country's best families who had been meeting at three different locations to plan an imminent rising. The article noted it was supposed only slight punishment or short imprisonment might be inflicted, as the prisons were already crowded to capacity with political prisoners.
records.summary_es: A partir del extracto periodístico provisto, el diario dio cuenta de que, en tanto los elementos blancos y las clases acomodadas simpatizaban con el bando revolucionario (moyerista), se desbarató una conjura de jóvenes capitaleños para adueñarse de Santo Domingo tras el arresto de un ordenanza que confesó los planes bajo amenaza de muerte. En consecuencia, las autoridades aprehendieron a cerca de sesenta jóvenes comprometidos pertenecientes a las familias más distinguidas, quienes celebraban juntas en tres parajes para ultimar el levantamiento. Anotó el texto que se esperaba la imposición de penas leves o breves arrestos, toda vez que las cárceles se hallaban colmadas de reos políticos.

records.summary_en: According to the newspaper report, ongoing revolution and military conscription of laborers in the Dominican Republic have left crops greatly behind, raising the possibility that export taxes will be increased to cover the costs. General Herroux, described as a 40-year-old of obscured early life and reported Haitian origin who rose through the ranks under General Luperon, now holds absolute power as a despot or dictator over the Government at Santo Domingo. Additionally, General Benito Moncion, the former Governor of the province of Monte Cristi and backer of the revolution's leader General Jussimire de Moya, formerly ruled his province more independently than any European king.
records.summary_es: Según la correspondencia periodística, la guerra civil y el reclutamiento forzoso de jornaleros en la República Dominicana ocasionaron un marcado atraso en las labores agrícolas, presagiándose un incremento en los tributos de exportación para costear las operaciones militares. El general Heureaux, descrito como un individuo de unos 40 años, de orígenes oscuros y supuesta ascendencia haitiana que ascendió en la milicia a la sombra del general Luperón, ejerce un poder absoluto y despótico sobre el Gobierno de Santo Domingo. De igual modo, el general Benito Monción, exgobernador de Montecristi y sostén del caudillo insurrecto general Casimiro de Moya, mandaba antaño en su provincia con mayor soberanía que monarca europeo alguno.

records.summary_en: The *Savannah morning news* reported on October 27, 1886, that Americans in Santo Domingo likely favored Gen. Herreux because he had maintained peace on the island for over six years. Although fighting was confined to the interior, the disturbances harmed American-owned sugar estates by halting labor, delaying crops, and threatening increased export taxes to pay for the revolution. Additionally, the article described Gen. Herreux as a 40-year-old negro of reported Haytian origin with a slightly Jewish cast of features, whose early life was obscure until recognized by Gen. Luperon.
records.summary_es: El *Savannah morning news* consignó el 27 de octubre de 1886 que los estadounidenses afincados en Santo Domingo se inclinaban probablemente por el general Heureaux merced a que garantizó la tranquilidad en la isla a lo largo de más de seis años. Aun cuando las refriegas se concentraban en el interior, los disturbios perjudicaban a los ingenios azucareros de propiedad norteamericana al paralizar las faenas, retrasar las zafras y amenazar con mayores arbitrios de salida para sufragar la pacificación. Añadía el artículo una semblanza del general Heureaux como un hombre negro de 40 años, de presumible origen haitiano y fisonomía semítica, cuya juventud transcurrió en la oscuridad hasta ser promovido por el general Luperón.

records.summary_en: General Bunto Moncion, late Governor of the Province of Monte Cristi and backer of revolution leader General Casimiro de Moya, is now an exile in Hayti after pocketing the revenues of the important seaport town. It is probable that President Salomon of Hayti will surrender Moncion and Moza to their alleged countryman, Herreux, to receive no quarter. Although the revolution is over, things remain unsettled and the duration of the current peace is uncertain.
records.summary_es: El general Benito Monción, antiguo gobernador de la provincia de Montecristi y valedor del cabecilla de la insurrección general Casimiro de Moya, se halla asilado en Haití tras haber acaparado las rentas de aquella rada estratégica. Juzgábase factible que el mandatario haitiano Salomon entregara a Monción y a Moya a su presunto compatriota Heureaux para ser castigados sin piedad. Aunque la rebelión ha expirado, los ánimos siguen alterados y resulta impredecible la estabilidad de la concordia actual.

records.summary_en: In a letter dated December 3, 1886, Haytien Consul Mr. Astwood reported to Mr. T. T. Fortune on the Dominican political contest, noting that the color-line made its appearance for the first time as educated young men influenced by foreign association discriminated against the black majority. The election featured General Heureaux representing the masses and General Casimira N. de Moya representing the elite candidate, with the Moya faction making large demonstrations and expected to win by an overwhelming majority through popular vote.
records.summary_es: En una misiva fechada el 3 de diciembre de 1886, el cónsul estadounidense en Santo Domingo, Sr. Astwood, comunicó a T. T. Fortune pormenores de la disputa política dominicana, destacando que el prejuicio de color se manifestaba por primera vez ante la actitud de jóvenes letrados influidos por costumbres foráneas que discriminaban a la masa negra. La contienda enfrentaba al general Heureaux, personero de las clases populares, con el general Casimiro N. de Moya, adalid de las élites, exhibiendo la facción moyerista imponentes alardes y confiando en imponerse por abrumador sufragio popular.

The following morning, General Babcock visited Senator Sumner with a copy of the treaty, but Sumner showed immediate signs of disapproval upon hearing the preamble and the stipulation regarding President Grant's influence to secure congressional popularity for the annexation.

Hedden, claiming an exemption from duty for products imported from the Dominican Republic under a past treaty guaranteeing equality with products from any other country, specifically referencing products admitted free from the Sandwich Islands under an 1876 act. records.full_text:
Suit Against the United States Which May Upset Existing Commercial Treaties.

WASHINGTON, December 14.—An important case involving the treaty relations of the United States with Hawaii and San Domingo was argued to-day in the United States Supreme Court. The case stands on the docket as Hugh Kelly, plaintiff in error, against Edward L. Hedden, collector. The question presented is an alleged exemption from duty under the existing tariff of products of the Dominican Republic which are identical in kind with the products of the Sandwich Islands and admitted free of duty under a special act of Congress, approved August 15, 1876. About twenty years ago the United States entered into a treaty with the Dominican Republic, by the terms of which each country agreed not to charge higher import duties on the products of the other than were imposed on like products from any other country. The importer claims exemption from duty for certain sugars and other products imported by him from San Domingo upon the ground that the articles were of such character that had they been imported from Hawaii they would have been

ADMITTED FREE OF DUTY,

under the treaty between the United States and Hawaii and the treaty of August 15, 1876, enforcing that treaty. The United States Government maintains that the treaty with the Hawaiian Islands was not a mere reciprocity treaty, but was in substance a commercial contract, by virtue of which Hawaii pays valuable consideration for the admission of certain merchandise to ports of the United States. Counsel for the importer say if the United States should be defeated in this case San Domingo might become the Honolulu of the Atlantic coast, while if the United States should succeed, Denmark, Brazil, Central America, Peru, Persia and other foreign governments would be at liberty to shut out American manufactures and products from their ports without giving the United States any cause for complaint for a violation of existing treaties placing the United States on an equality there with all other nations. This, they say, would upset nearly all our existing commercial treaties with foreign powers.

records.summary_en: Based on the provided excerpt, the newspaper reported on a court decision regarding sugar imports from San Domingo compared to those from the Sandwich Islands. The court held that the treaty with San Domingo only pledged against discriminating legislation and did not prevent special concessions like those granted to Hawaii. records.summary_en: The *Burlington weekly free press* reported on December 14, 1888, that the steamer *Haytian Republic* (also referred to as the *Saginaw*) had been seized and held as a prize by the Haytian government for allegedly carrying contraband of war, supplying munitions, and transporting rebel troops to aid insurgents. While the Haytian authorities claimed the vessel aided insurgents who subsequently defeated government troops, the ship's owners denied carrying insurgent supplies, stating the cargo was unloaded at ports under the Dominican government and that their responsibility ended once the goods left the ship.
records.summary_es: El *Burlington weekly free press* informó el 14 de diciembre de 1888 de que el vapor *Haytian Republic* (denominado asimismo *Saginaw*) había sido capturado y declarado presa de guerra por las autoridades haitianas bajo la imputación de transportar contrabando de guerra, proveer pertrechos y trasladar contingentes rebeldes para secundar la insurrección. En tanto el gobierno haitiano aseveraba que la nave prestó auxilio a sediciosos que luego vencieron a tropas oficiales, los armadores negaron haber conducido vituallas revolucionarias, manifestando que los cargamentos se desembarcaron en puertos bajo jurisdicción dominicana y que sus obligaciones fenecían una vez los fardos salían de a bordo.

records.summary_en: The *Richmond dispatch* reported that the steamer *Toussaimt L’Ouvriure* bombarded a city for two hours on December 3, prompting a consular protest and a granted thirty-six-hour period for foreigners to leave. The consul also reported on port traffic between November 2 and December 1, while the State Department received information that incipient rebellions were promptly suppressed at Puerto Plata by San Domingo authorities in early November and at Barcelona by Venezuelan authorities in late November.

El cónsul informó igualmente acerca del movimiento portuario registrado entre el 2 de noviembre y el 1 de diciembre, en tanto el Departamento de Estado recibió noticias de que sendas rebeliones incipientes fueron sofocadas con presteza en Puerto Plata por las autoridades dominicanas a principios de noviembre y en Barcelona por las fuerzas venezolanas a fines del propio mes.

Deering's account that an armed crew of twenty-five men under Captain Henry Williams had been sent to Hayti aboard the *Alene* on December 8 with sealed orders to take possession of the steamer *Haytien Republic*.

Entretanto, persistía la incertidumbre en el consulado haitiano ante la falta de noticias marítimas, consignando un despacho independiente el informe del teniente E. W. records.summary_en: *The Sun* reported on the surrender of the seized American steamship *Haytien Republic* to Admiral Luce following a firm United States naval demonstration. Haitian President Légitime ordered the vessel repaired and returned to its original mooring under formal protest, asserting the ship had aided domestic rebels. The correspondent noted that the assertive American naval posture exerted a salutary moral effect in Port-au-Prince.

El cronista subrayó que la resuelta actitud de la escuadra estadounidense causó un saludable escarmiento moral en Puerto Príncipe.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported on efforts by northern Haitian rebels loyal to General Hyppolite to smuggle arms through Dominican territory during Haiti's civil war. A traveler returning from Santo Domingo City observed a northern Haitian emissary lobbying Dominican authorities to permit the transshipment of weapons across the frontier. Meanwhile, rival Haitian dispatches claimed forces loyal to General Légitime had defeated Hyppolite's troops in several northern locations.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó sobre las tentativas de los rebeldes del norte de Haití adictos al general Hyppolite para introducir armas de contrabando a través de suelo dominicano durante la guerra civil haitiana. Un viajero que retornó de la ciudad de Santo Domingo atestiguó que un delegado del bando norteño gestionaba ante las autoridades dominicanas el tránsito de armamento a través de la frontera. Entretanto, despachos haitianos rivales aseguraban que destacamentos leales al general Légitime habían derrotado a las huestes de Hyppolite en diversas plazas del norte.

records.summary_en: According to the *Pittsburg dispatch* of January 3, 1889, French authorities in Hayti were reportedly divided between Legitime in the south and Hippolyte in the north, while a received cable stated that President Carnot gave an evasive reply to Dr. Auguste's request to recognize Hippolyte. Local merchants dismissed claims that France firmly backed Legitime, that the American squadron would have faced a French warship over the *Haytien Republic*, and that Legitime was imprisoning Americans or threatening to execute foreigners. Additionally, the Dominion Government's purchase of the British steamer *Red Rose* as a national man-of-war was widely reported as a sign of approaching war between San Domingo and Hayti due to vessel seizures, though Consul Julia of San Domingo noted that a $4,000,000 Holland loan had been made long before.

Los hombres de negocios locales desestimaron las versiones de que Francia apoyara decididamente a Légitime, que la flotilla estadounidense se fuera a batir con un buque de guerra francés a causa del *Haytien Republic*, o que Légitime encarcelara a estadounidenses o amenazara con ajusticiar extranjeros. records.summary_en: A small black steamer with her name painted out arrived at Staten Island on Thursday night and was identified as the former fishing steamer Novelty, renamed Mercedes and cleared for Samana. George Bowman told a reporter he had sold her to the Haitian Consul of New York and that she was bound for Samana, in Santo Domingo, to be used as a gunboat under the Dominican flag, while Captain Terry laughed off suggestions of guns aboard or blockade-running; the crew, a motley crowd who were not seamen, had been hired only to take the vessel down and return as passengers.

records.summary_en: According to the *Pittsburg dispatch* on January 27, 1889, Cape Haytien was attacked and shelled for a day while Fort Piccolet replied. Mr. DePendry reported that Hippolyte's forces were preparing an aggressive campaign utilizing a new navy, which reportedly included the purchase of President Hereaux's gunboat *El Presidente* (formerly the *Red Rose*) and the *Mercedes* from Santo Domingo, with armaments brought by the *Ozama* from New York to be handled by American gunners. Additionally, Minister Preston received a cable message reporting a small fire in Port-au-Prince caused by an oil explosion.

records.summary_en: On February 16, 1889, Consul Julia of San Domingo applied to the deputy collector of the port in New York for clearance papers for the steamer *Madrid*, presenting certificates claiming the vessel was owned by the Dominican government and himself. Minister Preston of Hayti opposed the clearance, stating the ship was intended for Hippolyte and would violate the law, prompting the deputy collector to withhold a decision until Collector Magone reviews the matter.
records.summary_es: El 16 de febrero de 1889, el cónsul Julia de Santo Domingo solicitó del segundo recaudador del puerto de Nueva York los despachos de salida para el vapor *Madrid*, aportando certificaciones que acreditaban que el buque era propiedad mancomunada del gobierno dominicano y de su propia persona. El ministro haitiano Preston se opuso al despacho, aduciendo que la nave se destinaba a la facción de Hyppolite en contravención de las leyes, lo que indujo al recaudador adjunto a suspender la providencia en espera de que el administrador Magone examinara el asunto.

records.summary_en: Based on the provided text, an unnamed General born in Spain, who participated in various European conflicts and political movements, organized a revolt against President Hereaux in San Domingo and was subsequently sentenced to death by the Dominican Government. After escaping San Domingo, he was exiled from Hayti by President Salomon, later restored to favor under Legitime, and associated with plans involving dynamite against Hyppolite's warship. Additionally, the newspaper reported on a minor incident in Litchfield, Illinois, where a gas-boring drill caught at a depth of 300 feet, causing excitement.
records.summary_es: A tenor del texto facilitado, un general anónimo nacido en España que intervino en varias contiendas y vicisitudes europeas encabezó una intentona contra el presidente Heureaux en Santo Domingo, siendo condenado a muerte por los tribunales dominicanos. Tras escapar de Santo Domingo, sufrió el destierro de Haití por orden del presidente Salomon, recuperó luego el favor bajo Légitime y apareció comprometido en maquinaciones con dinamita dirigidas contra el buque de guerra de Hyppolite. records.summary_en: The *New York Age* reported on July 27, 1889, that the Dominican Republic features well-preserved Spanish fortifications and gold mine ruins that American tourists find remarkably obscure. The article stated that the Dominican population—descendants of Caribs and Spaniards—is distinct from Hayti, noting that Dominicans are exceptionally hospitable, respect life and property during revolutionary upheavals, and refuse compensation for sheltering strangers.
records.summary_es: El *New York Age* expuso el 27 de julio de 1889 que la República Dominicana atesora vetustas fortificaciones españolas y vestigios de laboreo aurífero que a juicio de los viajeros norteamericanos permanecen singularmente ignorados. Ponderaba el escrito que la masa dominicana —oriunda del cruzamiento de taínos y españoles— se diferencia acusadamente de la de Haití, caracterizándose por su proverbial hospitalidad, el respeto al sosiego civil y a la hacienda durante las convulsiones armadas, y la negativa a admitir retribución alguna por brindar hospedaje al forastero.

records.summary_en: Commander Selfridge reported to the United States Government regarding potential coal depot locations in the West Indies, noting that the port of Mole St. Nicholas at the northwestern extremity of Hayti was strategically superior. Additionally, the Dominican Government previously sent a confidential letter to Secretary Seward requesting a loan of one million dollars and heavy artillery pieces to replace fortifications broken before the Spanish War. JANUARY.

1—The Legislature convenes and nothing occurs to mar the occasion. The Republican slate goes through easily. Governor Beaver’s able message. Successful observations of solar eclipse at Winnemucca, Nev. Emperor William expresses a desire for peace with all nations. President Cleveland’s brilliant reception. National Convention of Colored Catholics at Washington.

records.summary_en: President Ulises Heureaux called a cabinet meeting to consider declaring war against Haiti over a longstanding dispute regarding an 1875-1876 treaty, under which Haiti leased Dominican territory and agreed to pay an annual fee of $150,000 but now owes over $2,600,000. While Haiti wishes to end the agreement while retaining the land due to suffering revenues from duty-free Dominican imports, Dominican consul generals Francisco Ponte Vasquez and Manual De J. Galvan stated they received no official word of an outbreak or invasion, though they acknowledged trouble was brewing.

Aunque Haití desea dar por terminado el acuerdo conservando al mismo tiempo la tierra debido a las pérdidas de ingresos provocadas por las importaciones dominicanas libres de aranceles, los cónsules generales dominicanos Francisco Ponte Vásquez y Manuel de J. Galván declararon que no habían recibido notificación oficial de un estallido armado o invasión, si bien reconocieron que se avecinaban problemas.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Dominican President Heureaux attributed escalating border disputes to Haiti's default on the commercial and boundary treaties of 1874–1875. Under the agreement, Haiti leased Dominican territory for $150,000 annually and granted tariff exemptions to Dominican imports, accumulating over $2,000,000 in unpaid dues while complaining of Dominican rum smuggling. Dominican consular officials in New York acknowledged simmering diplomatic frictions but had received no official confirmation of armed border clashes.

records.headline: This historical article traces Dominican approaches to the United States from the republic's 1840s application for…
records.summary_en: This historical article traces Dominican approaches to the United States from the republic's 1840s application for recognition, through Agent Hogan's 1845 report and Lieutenant D. D. Porter's 1846 survey of the island, to Captain George B. McClellan's 1854 survey of Samana Bay in the flagship Columbus for sites for a naval station and coal depot. It says President Santana was particularly anxious for a general treaty, that in 1856 the American commercial agent was authorized to offer the United States any location in Samana Bay plus its coal mines, that Spain's attempt to restore its power during the American Civil War was abandoned in 1865, and that in January 1867 the United States offered $2,000,000, half in cash and half in arms, for the proposed cession.
records.summary_es: Este artículo histórico recorre los acercamientos dominicanos a los Estados Unidos desde la solicitud de reconocimiento de la república en la década de 1840, pasando por el informe del agente Hogan en 1845 y el reconocimiento de la isla por el teniente D. D. Porter en 1846, hasta el levantamiento de la bahía de Samaná por el capitán George B. McClellan en 1854, en el buque insignia Columbus, en busca de sitios para una estación naval y un depósito de carbón. Dice que el presidente Santana estaba especialmente ansioso por un tratado general, que en 1856 el agente comercial americano fue autorizado a ofrecer a los Estados Unidos cualquier ubicación en la bahía de Samaná además de sus minas de carbón, que el intento de España de restaurar su poder durante la Guerra Civil americana fue abandonado en 1865, y que en enero de 1867 los Estados Unidos ofrecieron 2.000.000 de dólares, la mitad en efectivo y la mitad en armas, por la cesión propuesta.

records.summary_en: The *Pittsburg Dispatch* reported an interview with an observer regarding Dominican-Haitian relations, noting that Haitian political unrest had not disrupted Santo Domingo and that previous bilateral commercial treaties had lapsed. While Dominican officials opposed political annexation to the United States, the interviewee suggested that public sentiment might support leasing Samaná Bay for American use.
records.summary_es: El *Pittsburg Dispatch* informó sobre una entrevista con un observador acerca de las relaciones dominico-haitianas, señalando que los disturbios políticos haitianos no habían perturbado a Santo Domingo y que los tratados comerciales bilaterales previos habían caducado. Aunque los funcionarios dominicanos se oponían a la anexión política a Estados Unidos, el entrevistado sugirió que el sentimiento popular podría apoyar el arrendamiento de la bahía de Samaná para uso estadounidense.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported on specific assurances given by the Dominican government under the new reciprocity arrangement with the United States. Santo Domingo pledged not to raise export duties on free-list goods, to extend any future export duty reductions to American shipments, and to prevent discriminatory municipal taxes on United States products. The treaty permitted reasonable customs regulations to verify the origin of goods while protecting Dominican revenue without imposing undue restrictions on importers.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó sobre las garantías específicas brindadas por el gobierno dominicano bajo el nuevo arreglo de reciprocidad con los Estados Unidos. Santo Domingo se comprometió a no aumentar los aranceles de exportación sobre los artículos de la lista libre, a extender cualquier reducción futura de aranceles de exportación a los envíos estadounidenses y a evitar impuestos municipales discriminatorios sobre los productos de Estados Unidos. El tratado permitía reglamentaciones aduaneras razonables para verificar el origen de las mercancías protegiendo los ingresos fiscales dominicanos, sin imponer restricciones indebidas a los importadores.

records.summary_en: The *Busy Bee* reported that President Ulises Heureaux approved a commercial reciprocity treaty with the United States modeled on the earlier convention with Brazil. In exchange for duty-free access to the American market for Dominican sugar, molasses, coffee, cocoa, and hides, the Dominican Republic established a free list for machinery, tools, and foodstuffs, along with a 25 percent tariff reduction on items like meats, lumber, and cotton textiles. The treaty aimed to expand United States trade, which had lagged behind Dominican exports.
records.summary_es: The *Busy Bee* informó que el presidente Ulises Heureaux aprobó un tratado de reciprocidad comercial con Estados Unidos modelado a partir de la convención previa con Brasil. A cambio del acceso libre de impuestos al mercado estadounidense para el azúcar, la melaza, el café, el cacao y los cueros dominicanos, la República Dominicana estableció una lista libre para maquinaria, herramientas y alimentos, junto con una reducción arancelaria del 25 por ciento sobre artículos como carnes, madera y textiles de algodón. El tratado buscaba ampliar el comercio estadounidense, que se encontraba rezagado respecto a las exportaciones dominicanas.

records.summary_en: The *Macon Beacon* reported the conclusion of a commercial reciprocity treaty between the United States and the Dominican Republic endorsed by President Ulises Heureaux. The treaty granted free entry into Dominican ports for American agricultural and railway equipment and reduced duties by 25 percent on meats, textiles, and iron products. In return, Dominican staples including sugar, molasses, and coffee entered the United States duty-free under the McKinley Tariff Act.

records.full_text:
The United States Buys Samana Bay.

PARIS, June 8.—A dispatch from Kingston, Jamaica, says great excitement was caused in San Domingo by the announcement that the port of Samana bay, in the western part of the island, had been ceded to the United States and the cession confirmed. The Haitian minister is alarmed, owing to the fact that American Minister Durham, of Haiti, who is in charge of affairs at San Domingo, has taken residence in the city of San Domingo. The German consul at Port-au-Prince has received instructions to come to an understanding with the representatives of France and England with regard to taking steps to safeguard the autonomy of San Domingo.

[Samana bay is on the south side of the peninsula of Samana. It is about forty-three miles in length from east to west, by about eight miles broad, and at its west end receives the Yuma, the largest river in the Dominican republic. It forms one of the finest harbors in the world, and may be regarded as a most important maritime position, in reference to the trade of the Gulf of Mexico and the interoceanic routes across Central America, both in a commercial and military point of view.]

records.summary_en: *The Seattle Post-Intelligencer* reported that an armed insurgent force led by General Pablo Reyes and Horacio Vásquez crossed from Haiti into Dajabón on March 10 to invade the Dominican Republic. Dominican government forces commanded by Governor Anderson repulsed the invasion, resulting in twelve deaths during the combat. Haitian President Florvil Hyppolite cooperated by disarming the retreating insurgents and deporting their leaders aboard the steamer *Ozama* to Turks Island.

Las fuerzas gubernamentales dominicanas, comandadas por el gobernador Anderson, repelieron la invasión, con un saldo de doce muertos durante el combate. El presidente haitiano Florvil Hyppolite cooperó desarmando a los insurgentes en retirada y deportando a sus líderes a bordo del vapor *Ozama* hacia las islas Turcas.

records.summary_en: The *Omaha Daily Bee* reported that Haiti and the Dominican Republic settled their diplomatic disputes after Haitian President Hyppolite apologized and offered indemnity for border raids linked to General Luperón. Presidents Heureaux and Hyppolite formed an alliance barring political exiles from organizing in either nation and pledged to coordinate against foreign aggression. The agreement also stipulated that neither republic would cede naval bases like Samaná Bay or Môle Saint-Nicolas to foreign powers without mutual consent.
records.summary_es: El *Omaha Daily Bee* informó que Haití y la República Dominicana resolvieron sus disputas diplomáticas luego de que el presidente haitiano Hyppolite se disculpara y ofreciera una indemnización por las incursiones fronterizas vinculadas al general Luperón. Los presidentes Heureaux y Hyppolite conformaron una alianza que prohibía a los exiliados políticos organizarse en cualquiera de las dos naciones y se comprometieron a coordinar acciones contra agresiones extranjeras. El acuerdo estipulaba además que ninguna de las dos repúblicas cedería bases navales como la bahía de Samaná o Môle Saint-Nicolas a potencias extranjeras sin consentimiento mutuo.

records.summary_en: *The Jersey City News* reported that Dominican soldiers fired upon a landing boat from the American schooner *Henry Crosby* near Azua, critically wounding a sailor and injuring the first officer. The schooner's captain sailed to Azua and filed a formal report with the United States Consul General in Santo Domingo, who forwarded the complaint to Washington. The unprovoked attack was believed to have resulted from soldiers mistaking the crew for insurgents attempting to land and overthrow President Heureaux.

El capitán de la goleta navegó hacia Azua y presentó un informe formal ante el cónsul general de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo, quien remitió la queja a Washington. Se creía que el ataque no provocado se debió a que los soldados confundieron a la tripulación con insurgentes que intentaban desembarcar para derrocar al presidente Heureaux.

records.summary_en: The *Weekly Union* reported that a boat crew from the American schooner *Henry Crosby* was fired upon by Dominican troops while approaching the beach near Azua, resulting in severe wounds to the first officer and the fatal shooting of a sailor. records.headline: General Heureaux's letter is dated from Azua, where the political outrages
records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported on an official communication from Dominican President Ulises Heureaux to Vice President Figuereo announcing the summary execution of several political opponents. Heureaux stated that General Eugenio Generoso Marchena and five associates were executed at La Clavellina for the murder of a government delegate, while three others were shot at Los Jovillos for attempting to assassinate Heureaux. Seven other accused conspirators were spared execution and transferred to prison in the capital.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó sobre una comunicación oficial del presidente dominicano Ulises Heureaux al vicepresidente Figuereo en la que anunciaba la ejecución sumaria de varios opositores políticos. Heureaux declaró que el general Eugenio Generoso Marchena y cinco colaboradores fueron fusilados en La Clavellina por el asesinato de un delegado gubernamental, mientras que otros tres fueron pasados por las armas en Los Jovillos por intentar atentar contra la vida de Heureaux. Otros siete acusados de conspiración se salvaron de la ejecución y fueron trasladados a prisión en la capital.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported on escalating authoritarian measures by President Heureaux, who restricted foreign travel and arrested suspected political opponents across the country. Following Heureaux's armed seizure of $60,000 from a French bank, the bank’s Dominican attorney, Jacinto de Castro Peynado, was imprisoned for his arguments during legal proceedings against the government. Additionally, Dominican troops blocked the son of a former Spanish consul from landing in Santo Domingo, threatening him with rifles until he departed on the steamer.

Además, tropas dominicanas impidieron el desembarco en Santo Domingo del hijo de un excónsul español, amenazándolo con fusiles hasta que abandonó el lugar a bordo del vapor.

records.summary_en: *The Lusk Herald* reported imminent conflict between France and the Dominican Republic after French warships appeared off Santo Domingo City to take soundings. The French government delivered an ultimatum demanding the return of $60,000 seized from a French-backed bank along with a $20,000 indemnity, threatening bombardment if President Heureaux failed to pay. Heureaux reportedly responded that the Dominican treasury lacked the money to meet the demand.

MAY BOMBARD SAN DOMINGO.

France Demands Indemnity for Confiscation of a French Bank.
New York special: A dispatch to the World, dated Puerto Plat, San Domingo, January 18, says:
“Trouble seems imminent between France and the Dominican Republic. A French man of war appeared off San Domingo City a few days ago and began to take soundings. Soon after she departed another appeared. The latter was boarded by a pilot, who was informed that his services were not needed, and when he asked the commander his intention, he was told it was none of his business.”

The San Domingo authorities had a dispute with a bank a few years ago, and eventually took $60,000 from it. The bank was backed by French capitalists, and the bankers laid the case before the French Government. France demanded that the money be returned to the bank, but diplomatic negotiations seem to have resulted in nothing. The World correspondent learns upon trustworthy authority that the French ultimatum has already been sent in and demands the restoration of the $60,000 and $20,000 as indemnity. President Heuraux, it is said, has declared that he has no money to pay it with.

records.summary_en: The *Omaha Daily Bee* reported that France agreed to suspend its demand for immediate payment of the bank indemnity in Santo Domingo following representations from Secretary of State Gresham, leaving the matter to diplomatic negotiations. However, France insisted on immediate compensation for the killing of a French resident, whose convicted murderer had been executed on February 6. In Paris, the French foreign minister received American protests regarding the San Domingo Improvement Company courteously but maintained that private American contracts could not override French sovereign claims.

Sin embargo, Francia insistió en una compensación inmediata por el asesinato de un residente francés, cuyo homicida convicto había sido ejecutado el 6 de febrero. En París, el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores francés recibió con cortesía las protestas estadounidenses relativas a la San Domingo Improvement Company, pero sostuvo que los contratos privados estadounidenses no podían anular las reclamaciones soberanas francesas.

records.summary_en: *The Sun* reviewed President Grant's failed 1870 campaign to annex the Dominican Republic, noting that Grant had personally championed the measure before the Senate rejected it in a tie vote. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the Secretary of State instructed the American consul in Santo Domingo to demand the revocation of a Dominican decree seizing a bridge across the Ozama River owned by American contractor Nat McKay. McKay built the bridge under a twenty-year concession, and the United States intervened after Dominican authorities held him liable for damages caused when a river scow struck the structure.

After verbally briefing Secretary Sherman in Washington, the diplomat decided to disclose the details following the acceptance of his resignation. He explained that Heureaux had requested his visit to Santo Domingo in March to receive the proposed terms and related memoranda.

records.full_text:
REVOLUTION FOR SAN DOMINGO.

It Is Being Brewed in New York by Enemies of President Hereaux.

New York, Oct. 21.—The Journal and Advertiser says: Efforts to crystalize the opposition to President Hereaux of San Domingo, the Spanish speaking republican that shares with the French speaking republic of Hayti the West Indian island of Hayti, into a revolution, are said to be nearing completion in this city.

The leader of the movement in New York is given Moscoso, who arrived here last July and is said to have been constantly busy ever since with secret meetings with the purpose in view. He is one of Hereaux's implacable foes and his friends here declare that he is the most available man to lead a revolt against the Dominican ruler. Moscoso was long ago recognized by Hereaux as a dangerous man and Hereaux was scheming to put him in prison and thus get him where he could not endanger the administration, when Moscoso got wind of his intention and promptly skipped out of the country. He went to the neighboring island of Porto Rica, the usual refuge of Dominican exiles, and was nearly assassinated there shortly after. Moscoso's friends openly declare their belief that the would-be assassins were in the pay of President Hereaux, the desperate method having been resorted to, they claim, because Moscoso was rapidly effecting his plans to return secretly to San Domingo and start an uprising, which Hereaux wanted to prevent by any means. Moscoso's assailants in Pence, Porto Rica, came very near killing him. He was taken unawares and stabbed once before he realized his danger, and then managed to escape only because one of the men thinking a fatal blow had been struck ran away, and the other was too scared and bewildered at the flight of his companion to follow up his attack. Moscoso is barely 35 years of age. He was educated in this country and speaks languages with fluency. His personal bravery is extolled as highly as his mental accomplishments, and his following at home is declared to be large and enthusiastic. He refuses to discuss his plans, but talks readily when President Hereaux's administration is mentioned. He makes no secret of his opposition to the president, whom he freely denounces.

Dominican exiles are not numerous in New York but they make up in determination what they lack in numbers. They declare they mean to stake their all in Mocoso's movement and basing their hopes on recent advices chief seaport, are confident that it will be successful.

Hereaux has been president of Santo Domingo three terms, a much longer period than any of his predecessors. His enemies declare that he has been able to retain the reins of president so long because he has been unscrupulous in carrying out his secret intention of making himself dictator for life by stifling opposition by means of bribery and intimidation. In consequence the best and most influential of the country have either been stultified or banished. It is even charged that a number have been unlawfully put to death at the president's instigation.

records.summary_en: *The Saint Paul Globe* published a letter comparing the proposed annexation of Hawaii to President Grant's unsuccessful effort to annex Santo Domingo in 1869 and 1870. The writer recalled that despite strategic arguments, joint resolution efforts, and a favorable commission report, the annexation treaty failed in the Senate. The author argued that past fears of foreign powers absorbing Santo Domingo proved unfounded and hoped Hawaii would avoid annexation.

El autor sostuvo que los temores pasados de que potencias extranjeras absorbieran a Santo Domingo resultaron infundados y expresó su deseo de que Hawái evitara la anexión.

records.summary_en: *The Indianapolis Journal* reported from Haiti regarding proposed constitutional changes concerning foreign property rights. Haitian Foreign Minister Brutus St. Victor denied claims that the government intended to repeal Article 6 of the constitution, which prohibited alien ownership of real estate, stating the public was not prepared for such reform. St. Victor also declined to disclose specific government plans to address the rising premium on paper currency.
records.summary_es: *The Indianapolis Journal* informó desde Haití sobre las propuestas de reforma constitucional relativas a los derechos de propiedad de los extranjeros. El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores haitiano, Brutus St. Victor, desmintió las versiones de que el gobierno pretendiera derogar el artículo 6 de la constitución, que prohibía a los extranjeros la propiedad de bienes inmuebles, afirmando que la opinión pública no estaba preparada para tal cambio. St. Victor declinó asimismo revelar planes gubernamentales específicos para hacer frente al creciente sobreprecio del papel moneda.

records.summary_en: *The News & Observer* reported that an armed uprising against Dominican President Heureaux had begun at Monte Cristi, near the Haitian border. The Clyde Line steamer *Fanita* reportedly departed Cape Haitien carrying 150 Dominican insurgents concealed in its hold, alongside rebel leaders General Juan Isidro Jimenes and General Villanueva. Observers in Haiti described the revolutionary expedition as well prepared and expressed strong confidence in its potential success.

Observadores en Haití describieron la expedición revolucionaria como bien preparada y manifestaron gran confianza en su posible éxito.

Dominican authorities captured several prisoners, including General Villanueva's son, who were slated for execution.

records.summary_en: The *Waterbury Evening Democrat* reported on the clandestine expedition of the steamer *Fanita*, which picked up exiled General Villanueva and pilot Chris Roberts at Great Inagua while concealing insurgent troops in its hold. Led by General Juan Isidro Jimenes, the expedition aimed to overthrow President Heureaux following extensive preparations. Although early observers expected success, the Dominican consul reported that the insurgent force had been defeated upon landing at Monte Cristi.

Aunque los primeros observadores auguraban el éxito, el cónsul dominicano informó que la fuerza insurgente había sido derrotada al desembarcar en Monte Cristi.

records.summary_en: The *Wichita Daily Eagle* reported conflicting accounts regarding an armed expedition led by General Juan Isidro Jimenes against Dominican President Heureaux. While the Dominican consul claimed the insurgents were defeated at Monte Cristi, other reports stated the rebels had landed munitions from the *Fanita* and were marching toward Puerto Plata and Santiago de los Caballeros. records.summary_en: The Dominican Consul received a dispatch from President Heureaux saying the attempted revolution at Monte Cristi had been defeated, that General Jimenez fled at the first fire of the government troops, taking refuge on board the Fanita, and that all the others who landed, with the exception of three, had been killed. The Haitian General Morales and seven Dominicans were among the killed, and two of the prisoners, Pablo Villanueva and a laborer named Calderon, were to be executed that day. records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that President Heureaux traveled to Great Inagua to lodge piracy charges against General Juan Isidro Jimenes following the failed Monte Cristi invasion. In an interview aboard his gunboat, Heureaux dismissed Jimenes as a skilled merchant but an inept politician whose revolutionary schemes were childish and thoroughly penetrated by government informants. Heureaux also exhibited seized documents and papers taken from insurgent casualties to demonstrate that the conspiracy was completely neutralized.

Heureaux exhibió además documentos y papeles incautados a las bajas insurgentes para demostrar que la conspiración se hallaba totalmente neutralizada.

records.summary_en: The *Waterbury Evening Democrat* reported that Dominican dissidents were organizing a renewed attempt to overthrow President Heureaux using the sloop *Olivia* to recruit men along Haiti's northern coast for attacks on Monte Cristi or Puerto Plata. Revolutionary agents were also reportedly active in southern Dominican provinces enlisting prominent figures. Additionally, Haitian officials, acting upon the Dominican government's request, ordered the son of rebel leader General Jimenes to leave Haiti.
records.summary_es: El *Waterbury Evening Democrat* informó que disidentes dominicanos organizaban una nueva tentativa para derrocar al presidente Heureaux utilizando la balandra *Olivia* para reclutar hombres en la costa norte de Haití con miras a atacar Monte Cristi o Puerto Plata. Según se informó, agentes revolucionarios actuaban asimismo en las provincias del sur dominicano sumando a destacadas personalidades. Además, funcionarios haitianos, a solicitud del gobierno dominicano, conminaron al hijo del líder rebelde general Jimenes a abandonar el territorio de Haití.

records.headline: A report on Dominican politics under President Heureaux describes Emmanuel Jimines as a young man of pleasing…
records.summary_en: A report on Dominican politics under President Heureaux describes Emmanuel Jimines as a young man of pleasing manners who has much sympathy, but calls his Monte Cristi attempt one of the worst planned and feeblest ever known. It recounts how Heureaux employs a large number of spies, many of them women, yet is his own best spy, telling of him disguised as a laborer learning of a conspiracy, confronting conspirators in their own meeting, and pardoning a hired assassin who revealed who sent him, while thousands of dollars have secretly been offered for his assassination and the common people believe he leads a charmed life.
records.summary_es: Un reportaje sobre la política dominicana bajo el presidente Heureaux describe a Emmanuel Jimines como un joven de modales agradables que despierta mucha simpatía, pero califica su intento de Monte Cristi como uno de los peor planeados y más débiles que se hayan conocido. Relata cómo Heureaux emplea un gran número de espías, muchos de ellos mujeres, aunque él mismo es su mejor espía, y cuenta que disfrazado de obrero se enteró de una conspiración, que enfrentó a los conspiradores en su propia reunión y que perdonó a un asesino a sueldo que reveló quién lo había enviado, mientras se han ofrecido en secreto miles de dólares por su asesinato y el pueblo común cree que lleva una vida protegida por un encanto.

records.summary_en: The *Anaconda Standard* published an overview of the Dominican Republic, detailing its geography, population of 610,000, and history from colonial rule through its independence on February 27, 1844. The report described the nation's political structure, public education system, and major agricultural exports, including tobacco, sugar, coffee, and mahogany. It also observed that while rich mineral deposits of gold, copper, and iron existed, the country's mineral resources remained largely undeveloped.
records.summary_es: *The Anaconda Standard* publicó una reseña general de la República Dominicana, detallando su geografía, una población de 610.000 habitantes y su historia desde la época colonial hasta su independencia el 27 de febrero de 1844. El informe describía la estructura política del país, el sistema de educación pública y sus principales exportaciones agrícolas, entre ellas tabaco, azúcar, café y caoba. Observó asimismo que, si bien existían ricos yacimientos minerales de oro, cobre y hierro, los recursos mineros del país permanecían en gran medida inexplotados.

records.headline: This article describes Santo Domingo as long disturbed by dissensions and revolutionary movements, naming Juan…
records.summary_en: This article describes Santo Domingo as long disturbed by dissensions and revolutionary movements, naming Juan Jiminez, a former merchant of Monte Christi and permanent candidate for the presidency, as one of the chief troublemakers. It recounts how Jiminez in June 1898 organised a filibustering expedition against the Heureaux government and landed at Monte Christi, but failed, his men being killed or captured while he escaped, and how another invasion was hourly expected there in July; it also describes the country's recent acute financial crisis, when the rate of exchange on New York rose more than 100 per cent and a commercial panic followed.
records.summary_es: Este artículo describe a Santo Domingo como perturbado durante mucho tiempo por disensiones y movimientos revolucionarios, y señala a Juan Jiménez, antiguo comerciante de Monte Cristi y candidato permanente a la presidencia, como uno de los principales agitadores. Cuenta cómo Jiménez organizó en junio de 1898 una expedición filibustera contra el gobierno de Heureaux y desembarcó en Monte Cristi, pero fracasó, pues sus hombres fueron muertos o capturados mientras él escapaba, y cómo en julio se esperaba allí otra invasión de un momento a otro; también describe la reciente crisis financiera aguda del país, cuando el tipo de cambio sobre Nueva York subió más del 100 por ciento y siguió un pánico comercial.

records.summary_en: After the assassination of President Heureaux, Vice President Figueroa, who assumes the presidential functions, informed the president's widow that the body would be buried at Santiago de los Caballeros rather than taken to Santo Domingo, for fear of hostile manifestations there. Government officials expect an uprising: arms and ammunition have been ordered sent to Santiago, the assassin's party is reported to be gathering to attack the government troops, and the president was shot down at Moca by Ramon Caceres just as he gave alms to an old man who had asked for help.
records.summary_es: Tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux, el vicepresidente Figueroa, que asume las funciones presidenciales, informó a la viuda del presidente que el cuerpo sería enterrado en Santiago de los Caballeros en vez de ser llevado a Santo Domingo, por temor a manifestaciones hostiles allí. Las autoridades del gobierno esperan un levantamiento: se ha ordenado enviar armas y municiones a Santiago, se informa que el partido del asesino se está reuniendo para atacar a las tropas del gobierno, y el presidente fue derribado a tiros en Moca por Ramón Cáceres justo cuando daba limosna a un anciano que le había pedido ayuda.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Times-Republican* reported that Washington officials were prepared to intervene and establish a protectorate over the Dominican Republic if violent conflict erupted over the succession to the assassinated President Heureaux. Cuban newspapers debated remarks by General Maximo Gomez's secretary suggesting foreign intervention would be required to maintain order on the island. Meanwhile, Dominican Vice President Wenceslao Figuereo reportedly accepted the presidency to maintain constitutional continuity.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Times-Republican* informó que las autoridades en Washington estaban preparadas para intervenir y establecer un protectorado sobre la República Dominicana si estallaba un conflicto violento por la sucesión del asesinado presidente Heureaux. Periódicos cubanos debatieron declaraciones del secretario del general Máximo Gómez en las que sugería que se requeriría una intervención extranjera para preservar el orden en la isla. Entretanto, según se informó, el vicepresidente dominicano Wenceslao Figuereo asumió la presidencia para asegurar la continuidad constitucional.

records.headline: A profile of President Heureaux tells how his brother-in-law, the husband of the half sister for whom he had a real…
records.summary_en: A profile of President Heureaux tells how his brother-in-law, the husband of the half sister for whom he had a real affection, was advanced rapidly in the government service, warned once after joining a plot to assassinate the president, and found within six months plotting again. Heureaux gave a state breakfast in the young man's honor, seated him at his side, and as the meal ended told him he was going to be shot in five minutes; the official was then shot in the courtyard while the president's sister screamed from the windows above, and the uncoffined body was quickly buried in a flower garden.
records.summary_es: Un perfil del presidente Heureaux cuenta cómo su cuñado, el esposo de la media hermana por quien sentía un verdadero afecto, fue ascendido rápidamente en el servicio del gobierno, advertido una vez tras unirse a un complot para asesinar al presidente, y descubierto en menos de seis meses conspirando de nuevo. Heureaux ofreció un desayuno de Estado en honor del joven, lo sentó a su lado y, al terminar la comida, le dijo que iba a ser fusilado en cinco minutos; el funcionario fue fusilado entonces en el patio mientras la hermana del presidente gritaba desde las ventanas de arriba, y el cuerpo sin ataúd fue enterrado rápidamente en un jardín de flores.

records.summary_en: A Puerto Plata dispatch dated August 1 calls the situation in Santo Domingo critical after President Heureaux's assassination, with an outbreak expected at any moment and friends of the government under arms to protect property and preserve the peace. It says the assassins, Ramón Cáceres, Manuel Cáceres, Horacio Vásquez and Domingo Pichardo, were in the country about Moca with their followers, that the president was buried with military honors, and that troops were being assembled at Moca and La Vega.

Dice que los asesinos, Ramón Cáceres, Manuel Cáceres, Horacio Vásquez y Domingo Pichardo, estaban en el campo cerca de Moca con sus seguidores, que el presidente fue enterrado con honores militares, y que se estaban reuniendo tropas en Moca y La Vega.

records.headline: A report on President Heureaux's assassination at Moca says his death caused a panic, that Juan Isidoro Jiminez, who…
records.summary_en: A report on President Heureaux's assassination at Moca says his death caused a panic, that Juan Isidoro Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of the previous year, is a candidate for the presidency, and that General Maximo Gomez is also reported to aspire to it. It notes that the father of Caceres, the assassin, was put to death by order of Heureaux in 1884, that Vice President Wenceslao Figuereo at once assumed the direction of affairs, and that President McKinley sent Figuereo a cable of condolences in the name of the American people.
records.summary_es: Un informe sobre el asesinato del presidente Heureaux en Moca dice que su muerte causó pánico, que Juan Isidoro Jiminez, que tomó parte en el intento de insurrección del año anterior, es candidato a la presidencia, y que también se informa que el general Máximo Gómez aspira a ella. Señala que el padre de Cáceres, el asesino, fue ejecutado por orden de Heureaux en 1884, que el vicepresidente Wenceslao Figuereo asumió de inmediato la dirección de los asuntos, y que el presidente McKinley envió a Figuereo un cable de condolencias en nombre del pueblo americano.

records.headline: President Ulises Heureaux of the Dominican Republic was assassinated at Moca on Wednesday afternoon, after several…
records.summary_en: President Ulises Heureaux of the Dominican Republic was assassinated at Moca on Wednesday afternoon, after several earlier attempts on his life, and his murderer, Ramon Caceres, made his escape. Immediately on the announcement of his death, Vice President General Wenceslao Figuereo assumed control of the government, and the paper gives an account of Heureaux's career, from his birth at Puerto Plata and service in the war against Spain to his rise to the presidency.
records.summary_es: El presidente Ulises Heureaux de la República Dominicana fue asesinado en Moca el miércoles por la tarde, tras varios intentos anteriores contra su vida, y su asesino, Ramón Cáceres, logró escapar. Inmediatamente después del anuncio de su muerte, el vicepresidente general Wenceslao Figuereo asumió el control del gobierno, y el periódico ofrece un relato de la carrera de Heureaux, desde su nacimiento en Puerto Plata y su servicio en la guerra contra España hasta su ascenso a la presidencia.

It also describes his polished manner and entertaining conversation, and his palace in Santo Domingo, a three-story building covering a block.

También describe sus modales refinados y su conversación amena, y su palacio en Santo Domingo, un edificio de tres pisos que ocupa una manzana.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported on Dominican fiscal measures requiring a portion of customs duties to be paid in paper currency, which would be publicly burned each month to retire the circulating paper notes. Concurrently, Dominican revolutionary forces crossed from Ouanaminthe, Haiti, and captured the border town of Dajabon, forcing the local garrison to retreat to Fort Belair. The report noted expectations that rebel leader General Jimenes would soon land to take direct command, despite Haitian efforts to prevent his transit.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó sobre las medidas fiscales dominicanas que exigían el pago de una porción de los aranceles aduaneros en papel moneda, el cual se quemaría públicamente cada mes para retirar los billetes en circulación. Al mismo tiempo, fuerzas revolucionarias dominicanas cruzaron desde Ouanaminthe, Haití, y tomaron la localidad fronteriza de Dajabón, obligando a la guarnición local a replegarse hacia Fort Belair. El informe señalaba la expectativa de que el líder rebelde general Jimenes desembarcara en breve para asumir el mando directo, pese a los esfuerzos haitianos por impedir su paso.

Agents Adriano and Maximiliano Grullon worked to mobilize Dominican diaspora communities in New York, Philadelphia, and Boston to back the insurrection. Meanwhile, officials in Santo Domingo reported general tranquillity, though the sixteen conspirators who killed President Heureaux remained at large and the national economy remained paralyzed by currency difficulties.

Entretanto, las autoridades en Santo Domingo informaban de una tranquilidad general, aunque los dieciséis conspiradores que mataron al presidente Heureaux seguían prófugos y la economía nacional permanecía paralizada por dificultades monetarias.

records.headline: A feature on Santo Domingo describes its minerals, including rock salt, petroleum found near Azua, abundant copper…
records.summary_en: A feature on Santo Domingo describes its minerals, including rock salt, petroleum found near Azua, abundant copper and great masses of iron ore in the interior, and explains that the president is chosen by an electoral college for four years with a cabinet of six. It says sugar, tobacco, cacao and coffee are the leading exports, that the United States led all other countries in trade with the republic, that most sugar estates are owned by Americans with the crop estimated at 65,000 tons, and that steamers of the Samana Bay Fruit Company carry fifteen to eighteen thousand bunches of bananas on each trip to the United States.

records.headline: This account describes the Republic of Santo Domingo, which covers 18,045 of the island's 28,240 square miles, its…
records.summary_en: This account describes the Republic of Santo Domingo, which covers 18,045 of the island's 28,240 square miles, its rivers, its gold washings, the rock-salt hills of the Neyba valley, petroleum near Azua and other minerals, and a government headed by a president chosen by an electoral college for four years. Its four leading exports are sugar, tobacco, cacao and coffee; the sugar crop this season is estimated at 65,000 tons and most sugar estates are owned by Americans, tobacco goes chiefly to Germany, and the Samana Bay Fruit Company's steamers carry fifteen to eighteen thousand bunches of bananas on each trip to the United States.
records.summary_es: Esta descripción presenta la República de Santo Domingo, que cubre 18.045 de las 28.240 millas cuadradas de la isla, sus ríos, sus lavaderos de oro, las colinas de sal de roca del valle de Neyba, el petróleo cerca de Azua y otros minerales, y un gobierno encabezado por un presidente elegido por un colegio electoral por cuatro años. Sus cuatro principales productos de exportación son el azúcar, el tabaco, el cacao y el café; la cosecha de azúcar de esta temporada se estima en 65.000 toneladas y la mayoría de las haciendas azucareras son propiedad de americanos, el tabaco va principalmente a Alemania, y los vapores de la Samana Bay Fruit Company llevan de quince a dieciocho mil racimos de plátanos en cada viaje a los Estados Unidos.

records.summary_en: A Puerto Plata dispatch dated September 1 reports that President Figuereo of the Dominican Republic has abdicated, yielding his authority to his council of ministers, and that the revolution in favor of Jiminez is victorious. It describes how Puerto Plata was handed over to the revolutionary generals without a drop of blood being shed, amid flags, music and public celebration, and how the revolutionists had also established a provisional government at Santiago with General Vasquez as president and General Caceres as minister of war.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported the capture of major Dominican northern cities by revolutionary forces, including the surrender of Puerto Plata on August 26. Insurgent troops stormed and took the military fort at Santiago de los Caballeros during the night of August 27 after garrison officials rejected surrender terms. On August 28, civil authorities in Puerto Plata formally transferred power to revolutionary leaders General Imbert and General Garrido in a public ceremony witnessed by foreign consuls and celebratory crowds.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó sobre la toma de las principales ciudades del norte dominicano por fuerzas revolucionarias, incluida la rendición de Puerto Plata el 26 de agosto. Tropas insurgentes asaltaron y capturaron la fortaleza militar de Santiago de los Caballeros durante la noche del 27 de agosto, luego de que los mandos de la guarnición rechazaran las condiciones de capitulación. El 28 de agosto, las autoridades civiles de Puerto Plata transfirieron formalmente el poder a los líderes revolucionarios, el general Imbert y el general Garrido, en una ceremonia pública presenciada por cónsules extranjeros y multitudes en júbilo.

records.summary_en: The *Abbeville Press and Banner* reported that the Dominican government reported general tranquillity despite the assassins of President Heureaux remaining at large, though commerce struggled under an unresolved paper currency crisis. The paper also noted catastrophic hurricane damage and river flooding in San Pedro de Macoris, Samana, and Puerto Plata. Meanwhile, American customs authorities at Baracoa, Cuba, intercepted 25 men and seized 143 rifles with ammunition destined for Dominican insurgents.
records.summary_es: *The Abbeville Press and Banner* informó que el gobierno dominicano reportaba tranquilidad general a pesar de que los asesinos del presidente Heureaux continuaban prófugos, mientras el comercio batallaba contra una crisis monetaria de papel no resuelta. El periódico también dio cuenta de pérdidas catastróficas por huracanes e inundaciones de ríos en San Pedro de Macorís, Samaná y Puerto Plata. Mientras tanto, las autoridades aduaneras estadounidenses en Baracoa, Cuba, interceptaron a 25 hombres e incautaron 143 fusiles con municiones destinados a los insurgentes dominicanos.

records.headline: Writing from San Domingo on September 15, the Herald's correspondent reports that the assassination of President…
records.summary_en: Writing from San Domingo on September 15, the Herald's correspondent reports that the assassination of President Heureaux removed the hand that had for eighteen years preserved a bloody peace, and that Vice President Figuereo's government weakened as he hesitated to dismiss the Heureaux ministry. Late in August a revolutionary proclamation was issued at San Francisco de Macoris in the interest of Jimenez, telegraph communication was cut, and the correspondent reports that Macoris, Moca and La Vega went over to a revolution headed by Horacio Vasquez, Ramon Caceres and Samuel Mayo.
records.summary_es: Escribiendo desde Santo Domingo el 15 de septiembre, el corresponsal del Herald informa que el asesinato del presidente Heureaux quitó la mano que durante dieciocho años había mantenido una paz sangrienta, y que el gobierno del vicepresidente Figuereo se debilitó al vacilar en destituir al ministerio de Heureaux. A fines de agosto se emitió una proclama revolucionaria en San Francisco de Macorís en favor de Jiménez, se cortó la comunicación telegráfica, y el corresponsal informa que Macorís, Moca y La Vega se pasaron a una revolución encabezada por Horacio Vásquez, Ramón Cáceres y Samuel Mayo.

records.headline: This profile of Heureaux, known as Lilis, says his enemies charge him with disposing of political prisoners by…
records.summary_en: This profile of Heureaux, known as Lilis, says his enemies charge him with disposing of political prisoners by poison, by the dagger and by shooting, in the dungeons of Santo Domingo City and elsewhere. It describes how he ran Congress to suit himself, how the supreme court and local tribunals gave verdicts in accordance with his previously expressed wishes, and how as a financier he increased the public debt and fell into the hands of an American syndicate representing the holders of Dominican bonds, which controlled the revenues of the country; of an authorized issue of $1,000,000 in paper money, $3,600,000 was placed in circulation and became waste paper, and the resulting panic, the article says, indirectly took Lilis to Moca, where he met his fate at the hands of Roman Caceres.
records.summary_es: Este perfil de Heureaux, conocido como Lilis, dice que sus enemigos lo acusan de deshacerse de los prisioneros políticos por veneno, por el puñal y por fusilamiento, en las mazmorras de la ciudad de Santo Domingo y en otros lugares. records.summary_en: A Santo Domingo letter says the revolution just ended was comparatively bloodless but filled with terror, after the assassination of President Heureaux removed the hand that had preserved a bloody peace for eighteen years. It describes Vice President Figuereo's government, held together by the Heureaux ministry, losing its chance by hesitating, and the revolt that began at San Francisco de Macoris in the interest of Jimines spreading as Macoris, Moca and La Vega went over, Santiago surrendered, the wires were cut, and the government suppressed the news and doubled the guards in the capital.
records.summary_es: Una carta de Santo Domingo dice que la revolución recién terminada fue comparativamente sin sangre pero llena de terror, después de que el asesinato del presidente Heureaux apartó la mano que había preservado una paz sangrienta durante dieciocho años. Describe cómo el gobierno del vicepresidente Figuereo, sostenido por el ministerio de Heureaux, perdió su oportunidad por vacilar, y cómo la revuelta que comenzó en San Francisco de Macoris a favor de Jimines se extendió cuando Macoris, Moca y La Vega se pasaron a ella, Santiago se rindió, se cortaron los cables y el gobierno suprimió las noticias y duplicó las guardias en la capital.

records.full_text:
MEETS FRENCH ADMIRAL.

Jimenez Confers With Richard—Settlement Expected To-Day.

SPECIAL BY CABLE.
Santo Domingo, Jan. 9.—(Copyright, 1900, by James Gordon Bennett.)—Admiral Richard of the French navy, with his staff, formally called upon President Jimenez this morning. No business was transacted. The French Consul was present. It is rumored on good authority that the French Consul has not been sustained by his Government, and that he has been asked for his resignation.

It is expected that official action will be taken to-morrow. Americans of this place have asked the United States not to allow France to dictate terms to the Dominican Government. An American cruiser is expected to arrive to-day. One is reported to have left Sanchez yesterday.

ORDERS TO THE MACHIAS.
REPUBLIC SPECIAL.
Washington, Jan. 9.—Instructions were to-day cabled to Commander L. C. Logan, commanding the Machias, directing him to promptly return to Santo Domingo.

In compliance with this instruction, it is presumed the Machias has left San Juan bound for the capital of Santo Domingo. Upon his arrival Commander Logan will consult with the American Minister relative to the protection of American interests. It was said at the State Department this evening that no appeal for the intervention of the United States had been received from Santo Domingo and it is hardly likely that this Government will interfere, in view of the fact that the Jimenez Government has collected by popular subscription the money necessary to pay the French claims. It is possible that Minister Powell may act as a mediator between the French fleet and President Jimenez, looking to compliance with the French demand for an apology, but now that the money has been collected [illegible] [illegible] believed that the worst is about over.

records.summary_en: The *Chariton Courier* reported that French Admiral Richard concurred with the Dominican government's position on the Boismare-Caccavelli claims dispute and accepted the terms previously proposed by Dominican authorities. The Dominican government secured a loan to satisfy the financial claim, releasing citizens from the funds collected by popular subscription. Meanwhile, the French warship *Suchet* departed for Haiti to collect 200,000 francs connected to a secret border agreement negotiated with the late President Heureaux.
records.summary_es: El *Chariton Courier* informó que el almirante francés Richard coincidió con la postura del gobierno dominicano respecto a la controversia por las reclamaciones Boismare-Caccavelli y aceptó los términos propuestos con anterioridad por las autoridades dominicanas. El gobierno dominicano obtuvo un préstamo para saldar la reclamación financiera, liberando a los ciudadanos de los fondos reunidos por suscripción popular. Entretanto, el buque de guerra francés *Suchet* zarpó hacia Haití para cobrar 200.000 francos vinculados a un acuerdo fronterizo secreto negociado con el difunto presidente Heureaux.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported on diplomatic friction in Santo Domingo arising from the French consul's abrupt demand on December 5 for immediate installment payments on the Boismare-Caccavelli claims. Dominican citizens held public meetings to protest the consul's haste, while carefully avoiding anti-French hostility. Foreign Minister Henríquez y Carvajal responded to consular complaints on January 4, defending the dignified conduct of the Dominican populace and reaffirming friendship with France.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó sobre las tensiones diplomáticas en Santo Domingo surgidas por la abrupta exigencia del cónsul francés el 5 de diciembre para el pago inmediato de cuotas por las reclamaciones Boismare-Caccavelli. Los ciudadanos dominicanos celebraron asambleas públicas para protestar contra la premura del cónsul, evitando con cautela cualquier hostilidad antifrancesa. El ministro de Relaciones Exteriores Henríquez y Carvajal respondió a las quejas consulares el 4 de enero, defendiendo la digna conducta de la población dominicana y reafirmando la amistad con Francia.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* published an interview with Judge Durham, an American attorney and plantation administrator in San Pedro de Macoris, regarding the Dominican Republic's fiscal crisis. Durham recounted providing $12,000 in gold in exchange for Dominican paper currency under President Heureaux to satisfy earlier French demands, and noted local backlash when the American-owned Bass estate refused to donate to a recent indemnity fund. He warned that excessive export taxes and American import duties were ruining Dominican agriculture, while the Improvement Company's monthly government allocation of $60,000 fell far short of public operating costs.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* publicó una entrevista con el juez Durham, un abogado y administrador de plantaciones estadounidense en San Pedro de Macorís, sobre la crisis fiscal dominicana. Durham relató haber facilitado 12.000 dólares en oro a cambio de papel moneda dominicano durante el gobierno de Heureaux para atender exigencias francesas anteriores, y señaló el rechazo local cuando la hacienda Bass, de propiedad estadounidense, se negó a aportar a un fondo de indemnización reciente. Advirtió que los excesivos impuestos de exportación y los aranceles de importación estadounidenses arruinaban la agricultura dominicana, al tiempo que la asignación gubernamental mensual de 60.000 dólares de la Improvement Company resultaba del todo insuficiente para cubrir los gastos de funcionamiento del Estado.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported further statements by Judge Durham concerning the collapse of the Dominican currency system under late President Heureaux. Durham disclosed that Heureaux systematically evaded agreements with the San Domingo Improvement Company by shifting printing plates between American firms to produce excessive quantities of unauthorized paper money. This unchecked currency inflation created widespread commercial distrust, leaving the Improvement Company with large unusable balances and bringing local commerce to an abrupt standstill upon the president's death.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó sobre declaraciones adicionales del juez Durham relativas al colapso del sistema monetario dominicano bajo el mandato del difunto presidente Heureaux. Durham reveló que Heureaux eludía sistemáticamente los convenios con la San Domingo Improvement Company transfiriendo matrices de impresión entre compañías estadounidenses para fabricar cantidades excesivas de papel moneda sin autorización. Esta inflación monetaria desmedida generó una desconfianza comercial generalizada, dejando a la Improvement Company con abultados saldos inutilizables y paralizando repentinamente el comercio local tras el deceso del mandatario.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that President McKinley received the credentials of the new Dominican Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary at the White House. In his address, the Dominican minister emphasized the historical friendship between both nations and advocated concluding a reciprocal commercial treaty. President McKinley welcomed the envoy and reciprocated the desire to establish closer, mutually beneficial trade relations between the two republics.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el presidente McKinley recibió en la Casa Blanca las cartas credenciales del nuevo enviado extraordinario y ministro plenipotenciario dominicano. En su alocución, el ministro dominicano destacó la histórica amistad entre ambas naciones y abogó por la concertación de un tratado de reciprocidad comercial. El presidente McKinley dio la bienvenida al enviado y correspondió al deseo de entablar relaciones comerciales más estrechas y mutuamente beneficiosas entre ambas repúblicas.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that Belgian bondholders, who held £6,000,000 in Dominican bonds, refused to accept an adjustment contract agreed to with the Dominican Improvement Company. Concurrently, an official notified his government that $350,000 collected from Santo Domingo was being deposited for bondholders following the deduction of Belgian state expenses. The Dominican government simultaneously gave assurances to the American Minister that the interests of American bondholders would be safeguarded.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que los tenedores de bonos belgas, en posesión de 6.000.000 de libras esterlinas en bonos dominicanos, se negaron a aceptar un contrato de ajuste acordado con la San Domingo Improvement Company. Al mismo tiempo, un funcionario notificó a su gobierno que se estaban depositando 350.000 dólares recaudados en Santo Domingo para los tenedores de bonos tras deducir los gastos estatales belgas. Simultáneamente, el gobierno dominicano garantizó al ministro estadounidense que se salvaguardarían los intereses de los tenedores de bonos estadounidenses.

records.summary_en: Under the heading Affairs in Santo Domingo, a November 14 dispatch reports that the Dominican Congress will meet in special session on November 23 to discuss the reciprocity treaty with the United States. It adds that Leovigildo Cuello has been appointed minister of posts and telegraphs, that the sugar crop harvest will begin early in December, and that the country is quiet.

Añade que Leovigildo Cuello ha sido nombrado ministro de Correos y Telégrafos, que la cosecha de azúcar comenzará a principios de diciembre y que el país está tranquilo.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* published a travel account describing the peaceful transition of power following the assassination of President Heureaux and the enthusiastic election of President Juan Isidro Jimenes. The author provided a geographic description of Santo Domingo, noting its fertile soil, moderate tropical climate, and central position among the Greater Antilles. The article observed that despite its rich natural advantages, a century of persistent internal conflict had discouraged foreign capital investment.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* publicó una crónica de viaje que describía la pacífica transición de poder tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux y la entusiasta elección del presidente Juan Isidro Jimenes. El autor ofreció una descripción geográfica de Santo Domingo, destacando su suelo fértil, su clima tropical moderado y su posición central entre las Grandes Antillas. El artículo observaba que, pese a sus ricas ventajas naturales, un siglo de persistentes conflictos internos había desincentivado la inversión de capitales extranjeros.
