records.summary_en: The *Independent* reported that the Dominican government organized a commission to negotiate directly with European bondholders, hoping a financial settlement would dispel talk of United States annexation, which was widely opposed by the Dominican populace. Representatives of the San Domingo Improvement Company in New York acknowledged that while annexation might bring economic benefits, the time was not ripe for such a step. A company spokesman remarked that support for annexation stemmed primarily from prominent foreign and local property holders rather than the general Dominican public.

Representantes de la San Domingo Improvement Company en Nueva York admitieron que, aunque la anexión podría reportar ventajas económicas, no había llegado el momento para dar tal paso. Un portavoz de la compañía señaló que el respaldo a la anexión provenía principalmente de prominentes propietarios locales y extranjeros, más que del pueblo dominicano en general.

records.summary_en: The *Chickasha Daily Express* reported that Dominican President Juan Isidro Jimenes had sent an envoy to the United States to organize a financial syndicate to assume the national debt under an American protectorate, though the attempt proved unsuccessful. The paper highlighted Washington rumors that Santo Domingo might seek territorial status similar to Puerto Rico under Jimenes's leadership. The report also recalled President Grant's failed 1870s annexation campaign and the historical overtures made by Dominican President Buenaventura Báez.
records.summary_es: El *Chickasha Daily Express* informó que el presidente dominicano Juan Isidro Jimenes había enviado un emisario a los Estados Unidos para organizar un consorcio financiero que asumiera la deuda nacional bajo un protectorado estadounidense, si bien la gestión resultó infructuosa. El periódico destacó los rumores en Washington de que Santo Domingo podría solicitar un estatus territorial semejante al de Puerto Rico bajo el liderazgo de Jimenes. El informe recordó asimismo la fallida campaña de anexión del presidente Grant en la década de 1870 y los históricos ofrecimientos efectuados por el presidente dominicano Buenaventura Báez.

records.summary_en: The *Topeka State Journal* reported that the Dominican Congress voted financial compensation for the San Domingo Improvement Company of New York as the government resumed direct control over national customs collection. Under the new arrangement, customs duties were to be received by a mixed commission composed of Dutch, Belgian, American, French, and Dominican representatives. The resumption of national control was greeted with general public satisfaction, and the president received widespread congratulations.
records.summary_es: El *Topeka State Journal* informó que el Congreso dominicano votó una compensación financiera para la San Domingo Improvement Company de Nueva York mientras el gobierno reasumía el control directo de la recaudación aduanera nacional. Conforme al nuevo esquema, los aranceles aduaneros debían ser percibidos por una comisión mixta integrada por representantes holandeses, belgas, estadounidenses, franceses y dominicanos. La recuperación del control nacional fue acogida con general satisfacción pública y el mandatario recibió amplias felicitaciones.

records.summary_en: Washington reported on January 12 that the government would probably take cognizance of the troubles in San Domingo and act as necessary for the protection of American interests, but that the State Department had not yet heard from Consul-General Maxwell on the reports that the Dominican Government had resumed the direction of its own fiscal affairs, terminating the system by which an American syndicate collected the duties and paid the debts of the government. The plan had been adopted some years earlier, and some Belgian bond owners were understood to have objected to it. Representatives of the San Domingo Improvement Company held long conferences with Acting Secretary Hill and Solicitor Penfield concerning the reported repudiation of the companys grant, and a cable message of inquiry was sent to the American representative in San Domingo.
records.summary_es: Washington informó el 12 de enero de que el gobierno probablemente tomaría conocimiento de los problemas en Santo Domingo y actuaría según fuera necesario para proteger los intereses estadounidenses, pero que el Departamento de Estado aún no había recibido noticias del cónsul general Maxwell sobre los informes de que el gobierno dominicano había reasumido la dirección de sus propios asuntos fiscales, poniendo fin al sistema por el que un sindicato estadounidense cobraba los derechos y pagaba las deudas del gobierno. El plan se había adoptado años antes, y se entendía que algunos tenedores de bonos belgas habían objetado a él. Representantes de la San Domingo Improvement Company celebraron largas conferencias con el secretario interino Hill y el procurador Penfield sobre la supuesta rescisión de la concesión de la compañía, y se envió un cable de consulta al representante estadounidense en Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: The *Savannah Morning News* reported that the Santo Domingo Chamber of Commerce passed a resolution repudiating the San Domingo Improvement Company's attempt to declare government customs collections invalid. The commercial body demanded that the American company rescind its provocative notice to merchants. In response to the escalating dispute, the Dominican Minister of Foreign Affairs prepared to travel to Washington to present his government's case directly to the United States.
records.summary_es: El *Savannah Morning News* informó que la Cámara de Comercio de Santo Domingo aprobó una resolución desconociendo la pretensión de la San Domingo Improvement Company de declarar inválida la recaudación aduanera gubernamental. La entidad comercial exigió que la compañía estadounidense revocara su provocador aviso a los comerciantes. Ante la escalada del conflicto, el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores de la República Dominicana se dispuso a viajar a Washington para exponer los argumentos de su gobierno directamente ante los Estados Unidos.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published an interview with Dominican leader Horacio Vásquez, who described the nation's abundant mineral resources, including deposits of copper, precious metals, and vast salt reserves. Vásquez maintained that political stability had been quickly restored after President Heureaux's assassination through the establishment of a provisional government. He sharply criticized the San Domingo Improvement Company, asserting that it had merely constructed a railroad with Dominican state funds, enriching itself, Heureaux, and local financier Cosme Batlle at the country's expense.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* publicó una entrevista con el líder dominicano Horacio Vásquez, quien describió los abundantes recursos minerales de la nación, incluidos yacimientos de cobre, metales preciosos y vastas reservas de sal. Vásquez sostuvo que la estabilidad política se restableció con rapidez tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux mediante la constitución de un gobierno provisional. Criticó duramente a la San Domingo Improvement Company, aseverando que únicamente había construido un ferrocarril con fondos del Estado dominicano, enriqueciéndose a sí misma, a Heureaux y al financista local Cosme Batlle a expensas del país.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that nationalist pressure compelled President Jimenes to confront the San Domingo Improvement Company and threaten its agent with expulsion after the company challenged Dominican customs authority. Meanwhile, Belgian Foreign Minister de Favereau instructed his consul in Santo Domingo to ensure that bondholder funds in the treasury safe remained strictly protected for European creditors. Additionally, the semi-official Dominican press responded defiantly to rumors that the American gunboat *Scorpion* was en route to coerce the government.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que presiones nacionalistas obligaron al presidente Jimenes a confrontar a la San Domingo Improvement Company y a amenazar a su agente con la expulsión después de que la empresa desafiara la autoridad aduanera dominicana. Mientras tanto, el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores belga, De Favereau, instruyó a su cónsul en Santo Domingo para que garantizara que los fondos de los tenedores de bonos en la caja fuerte de la tesorería permanecieran estrictamente resguardados para los acreedores europeos. Asimismo, la prensa semioficial dominicana respondió con desafío a los rumores de que el cañonero estadounidense *Scorpion* se dirigía a coaccionar al gobierno.

records.summary_en: The *San Antonio Daily Light* reported rising tensions along the Haitian-Dominican border following the failure of a joint boundary commission established under the Sam-Heureaux convention. Haitian authorities accused Dominican forces of illegally occupying frontier positions that Haitian troops had evacuated in good faith to facilitate negotiations. Violent skirmishes erupted at Philobert along the Massacre River, where Haitian border posts established to suppress smuggling came under repeated Dominican attack.

records.summary_en: The *Morning Astorian* reported on the breakdown of the joint boundary commission that convened at Anses-à-Pitres to define the Haitian-Dominican border based on 1874 territorial positions. Negotiations collapsed after Dominican delegates insisted on conditional compliance and Dominican troops moved into vacated frontier points, prompting Haitian accusations of bad faith. Tensions escalated sharply following armed confrontations at Philobert near the Massacre River, where Haitian border outposts repelled attacks from Dominican territory.
records.summary_es: El *Morning Astorian* informó sobre la ruptura de la comisión limítrofe conjunta que se reunió en Anses-à-Pitres para definir la frontera domínico-haitiana tomando como base las posiciones territoriales de 1874. Las negociaciones fracasaron luego de que los delegados dominicanos insistieran en un cumplimiento condicional y las tropas dominicanas avanzaran hacia puntos fronterizos desocupados, lo que motivó acusaciones haitianas de mala fe. Las tensiones se intensificaron bruscamente tras choques armados en Philobert, cerca del río Masacre, donde los puestos fronterizos haitianos repelieron ataques procedentes de territorio dominicano.

records.summary_en: The *Phillipsburg Herald* reviewed the military career of General Máximo Gómez, noting his early service with Spanish forces during the Dominican annexation before becoming a leader in Cuba's ten years' war for independence. In 1887, Gómez returned to Santo Domingo to cultivate tobacco in Guayubín near Monte Cristi, where his widespread popularity quickly aroused political suspicion. Fearing that Gómez harbored presidential ambitions and planned an insurrection, President Heureaux secretly arranged for his arrest and execution.
records.summary_es: El *Phillipsburg Herald* repasó la carrera militar del general Máximo Gómez, destacando su servicio inicial en las fuerzas españolas durante la anexión dominicana antes de convertirse en un caudillo de la guerra de los Diez Años por la independencia de Cuba. En 1887, Gómez regresó a Santo Domingo para cultivar tabaco en Guayubín, cerca de Monte Cristi, donde su inmensa popularidad despertó pronto suspicacias políticas. Por temor a que Gómez albergara ambiciones presidenciales y tramara una insurrección, el presidente Heureaux dispuso secretamente su arresto y ejecución.

records.summary_en: The *Arizona Republican* reported that Dominican insurgents captured the southern coastal town of Barahona after heavy fighting that resulted in forty casualties. A government gunboat subsequently bombarded the port and landed forces that successfully recaptured the town, driving the rebels into nearby strongholds. In response to the uprising, the Dominican Congress suspended constitutional guarantees and declared nationwide martial law.
records.summary_es: El *Arizona Republican* informó que insurgentes dominicanos tomaron la localidad costera meridional de Barahona tras intensos combates que causaron cuarenta bajas. Con posterioridad, un cañonero gubernamental bombardeó el puerto y desembarcó tropas que recuperaron con éxito la ciudad, obligando a los rebeldes a replegarse hacia reductos cercanos. En respuesta a la sublevación, el Congreso dominicano suspendió las garantías constitucionales y declaró la ley marcial en todo el territorio nacional.

President Jimenes sought asylum in the French consulate following the city's capitulation, while Governor Deschamps at Puerto Plata refused to yield without direct executive orders. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that foreign diplomats led by United States Minister Powell intervened during General Horacio Vásquez's advance on Santo Domingo to ensure civilian safety under the rules of war. Although Vásquez initially agreed to a temporary truce, insurgent troops occupied positions along the Ozama River to control the harbor. Finding the insurgents in effective control of the city, the diplomatic corps facilitated negotiations between Vásquez and the Jimenes administration for a formal capitulation.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que diplomáticos extranjeros encabezados por el ministro estadounidense Powell intervinieron durante el avance del general Horacio Vásquez sobre Santo Domingo para garantizar la seguridad de los civiles conforme a las leyes de la guerra. Aunque Vásquez aceptó inicialmente una tregua provisional, las tropas insurgentes ocuparon posiciones a lo largo del río Ozama para dominar el puerto. Al constatar que los sublevados tenían el control efectivo de la ciudad, el cuerpo diplomático facilitó las negociaciones entre Vásquez y el gobierno de Jimenes para una capitulación formal.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Times-Republican* reported that United States Minister Powell convened the diplomatic corps in Santo Domingo to safeguard foreign nationals and establish terms of engagement as insurgent forces approached. Despite an agreed temporary pause in hostilities, General Vásquez advanced his troops to command the Ozama River and secure the city. Concurrently, President Jimenes notified foreign ministers that he would agree to capitulate provided that full safety guarantees were granted to government officials and defenders.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Times-Republican* informó que el ministro de los Estados Unidos Powell convocó al cuerpo diplomático en Santo Domingo para salvaguardar a los ciudadanos extranjeros y acordar normas de beligerancia ante la aproximación de las fuerzas insurgentes. A pesar de una suspensión temporal de las hostilidades pactada, el general Vásquez avanzó sus tropas para dominar el río Ozama y asegurar la plaza. Al unísono, el presidente Jimenes comunicó a los ministros extranjeros que aceptaría capitular siempre que se otorgaran plenas garantías de seguridad a los funcionarios y defensores del gobierno.

records.headline: PRESIDENT OF THE DOMINICAN REPUBLIC HAS RETIRED.
records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported that the Dominican capital surrendered to General Horacio Vásquez on May 2 following two days of severe combat outside the city. President Jimenes took refuge in the French consulate, while other officials sought asylum in the American and French legations as rebel troops occupied the capital without public demonstrations. The report added that Puerto Plata, the final stronghold loyal to Jimenes, had also capitulated, leaving Vásquez in full control of the country.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó que la capital dominicana se rindió al general Horacio Vásquez el 2 de mayo tras dos días de encarnizados combates en las afueras de la urbe. El presidente Jimenes se refugió en el consulado francés, mientras otros funcionarios solicitaron asilo en las legaciones estadounidense y francesa cuando las tropas rebeldes ocuparon la capital sin manifestaciones públicas. El informe agregó que Puerto Plata, el último bastión leal a Jimenes, también había capitulado, dejando a Vásquez con el control absoluto del país.

records.full_text:
PRESIDENT OF THE DOMINICAN REPUBLIC HAS RETIRED.

Horacio Vasquez, Leader of the Successful Revolutionary Movement, Now at Head of the Government.

SURRENDER OF PUERTO PLATA

LAST CITY THAT WAS HELD BY THE EX-PRESIDENT'S TROOPS.

New Government Probably Will Be Promptly Recognized by the United States—The Looting of a Town.

WASHINGTON, May 7.—Cable advices received here state that President Jimenez, of the Dominican Republic, has signed a relinquishment of his claims to the presidency and on his part Horacio Vasquez, the late Vice President, has granted amnesty to the adherents of the late government and assumed the presidential office.

Senor Don Foo Leonte Vasquez, the charge of the Dominican Republic, has received cable advices from home announcing the success of the revolution. It is probable that he will now become a resident minister here. Naturally the charge is desirous that the United States shall recognize at once the new government. This is a matter, however, that is by custom left to the United States minister resident, but it is not doubted that Mr. Powell will, as he has heretofore done, soon put himself in communication with the de facto government.

Puerta Plaza, the last place held by the Jimenez adherents, has capitulated.

Advices from San Domingo, under date of May 2, say the Dominican capital capitulated to-day to the revolutionary forces commanded by Gen. Horatio Vasquez, the Vice President of the republic. President Jimenez sought refuge in the French consulate and many government officers obtained shelter in the French and United States legations. The revolutionary troops entered the capital quietly. There was no enthusiasm shown by the population here at the entry of the victorious army. The approach of the revolutionists to the capital was announced after two days of heavy fighting between the government troops and the forces of General Vasquez, during which many were killed or wounded on both sides. When it became known here that General Vasquez threatened to attack Santo Domingo, the United States minister, J. S. Powell, as dean of the diplomatic corps, requested the Dominican government to inform him regarding the arrangements made to protect the lives and property of foreigners here, adding that in case no precautions were taken he would consider it his duty to take measures to provide for their safety as the situation demanded. The reply was satisfactory.

SACKING OF BARAHONA.

Sailors Describe the Capture of the Town by Revolutionists.

NEW YORK, May 7.—Members of the British brigantine Alice, Captain Inness, which has just arrived from the West Indies, report that while the brigantine lay about eighty-five yards from the shore at Barahona, on the southwest coast of San Domingo, a force of revolutionists entered the town and began discharging rifles. Inhabitants of the port ran shrieking from their homes along the beach. “The revolutionists first sacked the principal saloon in the town,” said one of the crew. “They broke all the windows, drank all the liquor in bottles and then smashed the bar. They rolled barrels of rum out into the street, and what they could not drink they turned into the gutters. Next they attacked the jail and took out all the prisoners they wanted. The freed convicts joined the insurrectionists. In the attack eleven guards and one prisoner were killed. Two civilians were killed in the woods, which thickly skirt the town at the base of the mountain. The women and children who fled along the beach sought the protection of Captain Inness, who brought off as many as the gig would hold. A sloop brought off the rest of the refugees. The refugees, 100 in number, remained about three days. Meantime about 100 government soldiers appeared and were driven to retreat by the revolutionists, who then disappeared.”

records.summary_en: The *Age-Herald* reported that General Horacio Vásquez established a provisional government in Santo Domingo after the capital capitulated following two days of intense combat. President Jimenes took refuge in the French consulate, and victorious insurgent troops occupied the capital without public celebration. On the northern coast, the crew of a Dominican war vessel mutinied in support of the revolution, forcing Governor Deschamps at Puerto Plata to negotiate surrender terms.
records.summary_es: El *Age-Herald* informó que el general Horacio Vásquez estableció un gobierno provisional en Santo Domingo después de que la capital capitulara tras dos días de intensos combates. El presidente Jimenes se refugió en el consulado francés y las victoriosas tropas insurgentes ocuparon la capital sin celebraciones públicas. En la costa norte, la tripulación de un buque de guerra dominicano se amotinó en apoyo a la revolución, obligando al gobernador Deschamps en Puerto Plata a negociar las condiciones de capitulación.

records.summary_en: The *Age-Herald* detailed the formal capitulation terms accepted by President Jimenes, which guaranteed the security of state officials, the protection of private property, and the immediate liberation of political prisoners. Insurgent troops took possession of government buildings in Santo Domingo under terms monitored by the foreign diplomatic corps, while the cruiser *Cincinnati* was en route to the island. Meanwhile, Puerto Plata surrendered to the revolutionists, and its deposed governor, General Deschamps, boarded a French steamer for Haiti.
records.summary_es: El *Age-Herald* detalló las condiciones de capitulación formal aceptadas por el presidente Jimenes, las cuales garantizaban la seguridad de los funcionarios del Estado, la protección de la propiedad privada y la liberación inmediata de los presos políticos. Tropas insurgentes tomaron posesión de los edificios gubernamentales en Santo Domingo bajo condiciones supervisadas por el cuerpo diplomático extranjero, mientras el crucero *Cincinnati* navegaba rumbo a la isla. Mientras tanto, Puerto Plata se rindió ante los revolucionarios y su depuesto gobernador, el general Deschamps, abordó un vapor francés con destino a Haití.

United States Minister Powell and representatives from France, Spain, Germany, Italy, and Great Britain met with Vásquez to enforce the rules of war and protect non-combatants. Although Vásquez initially pledged a temporary ceasefire, his forces swiftly encircled the capital, prompting the diplomatic delegation to mediate formal surrender terms.

records.summary_en: A San Juan report quotes a letter received by a native of Santo Domingo living there saying the situation in the Dominican Republic is decidedly critical and the new government in momentary danger of being overthrown. The letter reports President Vasquez as mentally affected, the republic's finances in a deplorable condition with government employees receiving only half pay, the people having lost all confidence and many leaving the country, and declares the present regime cannot last longer than October.
records.summary_es: Un informe de San Juan cita una carta recibida por un natural de Santo Domingo residente allí, según la cual la situación en la República Dominicana es decididamente crítica y el nuevo gobierno corre peligro de ser derrocado en cualquier momento. La carta presenta al presidente Vásquez como mentalmente afectado, las finanzas de la república en una condición deplorable con los empleados del gobierno recibiendo solo la mitad del sueldo, al pueblo sin ninguna confianza y a muchos marchándose del país, y declara que el régimen actual no puede durar más allá de octubre.

In response, Commander Mason of the cruiser *Cincinnati* departed Cape Haitien to investigate the disturbances and protect American interests at the Dominican port. records.summary_en: The *Essex County Herald* emphasized the strategic importance of Samana Bay as the naval key to the Caribbean, recalling President Grant's earlier annexation efforts. It reported that an unexpected revolution had seized the capital of Santo Domingo during the president's absence, complicating recent American diplomatic agreements compensating a U.S. steamship company. With the Dominican president on the run and the foreign minister sheltering in the American consulate, the paper suggested U.S. marine landings or intervention might follow.
records.summary_es: El *Essex County Herald* subrayó la importancia estratégica de la bahía de Samaná como la llave naval del Caribe, recordando los anteriores intentos de anexión del presidente Grant. Informó que una revolución imprevista se había apoderado de la capital de Santo Domingo durante la ausencia del presidente, complicando recientes acuerdos diplomáticos estadounidenses que indemnizaban a una compañía naviera de los Estados Unidos. Con el presidente dominicano en fuga y el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores refugiado en el consulado estadounidense, el periódico sugirió que podrían producirse desembarcos de la infantería de marina de EE. UU. o una intervención militar.

records.headline: This article argues that Samana Bay, on the eastern coast of Santo Domingo, is one of the great maritime positions…
records.summary_en: This article argues that Samana Bay, on the eastern coast of Santo Domingo, is one of the great maritime positions of the Antilles, a harbour from which operations could be conducted by any kind of war vessel and in which a blockaded fleet might lie in safety. It praises the island's fertility, rivalling Cuba's, and its possible products of tobacco, coffee, indigo, sugar, cocoa, fruits and vegetables, noting that millions of acres lie wild for lack of cultivators and transport, and recalls the era of comparative peace under President Heureaux, who was assassinated on July 26, 1899.
records.summary_es: Este artículo sostiene que la bahía de Samaná, en la costa oriental de Santo Domingo, es una de las grandes posiciones marítimas de las Antillas, un puerto desde el cual podrían realizarse operaciones con cualquier clase de buque de guerra y en el que una flota bloqueada podría permanecer a salvo. Elogia la fertilidad de la isla, que rivaliza con la de Cuba, y sus posibles productos de tabaco, café, añil, azúcar, cacao, frutas y vegetales, señalando que millones de acres permanecen incultos por falta de cultivadores y de transporte, y recuerda la era de paz comparativa bajo el presidente Heureaux, asesinado el 26 de julio de 1899.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that the entire northern region of the Dominican Republic had joined an armed insurrection against President Alejandro Wos y Gil. The insurgents published a manifesto at Puerto Plata detailing grievances against the administration, including the imprisonment of dissidents, widespread financial waste, and default on national debt obligations. The document also fiercely denounced new fiscal burdens on cocoa, port fee concessions granted to the Hamburg-American Line, and an unconstitutional proposal to neutralize Dominican harbors during wartime.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que toda la región norte de la República Dominicana se había sumado a una insurrección armada contra el presidente Alejandro Wos y Gil. Los insurgentes publicaron un manifiesto en Puerto Plata detallando sus agravios contra el gobierno, entre ellos el encarcelamiento de disidentes, el despilfarro financiero generalizado y el impago de las obligaciones de la deuda pública. El documento también repudiaba enérgicamente las nuevas cargas fiscales sobre el cacao, las exenciones de derechos portuarios otorgadas a la Hamburg-American Line y una propuesta inconstitucional para neutralizar los puertos dominicanos durante conflictos bélicos.

records.summary_en: The *Willmar Tribune* reported that the steamer *Cherokee* arrived in Santo Domingo after being turned away from northern ports by a government cruiser, bringing word that northern regions had joined the revolution. The paper published an insurgent manifesto from Puerto Plata condemning President Wos y Gil for tyranny, crowded prisons, and extreme financial decay. The document highlighted unpaid public debts, heavy petroleum taxes, an odious $120,000 loan, and irregular four-year port concessions granted to the Hamburg-American Line.
records.summary_es: El *Willmar Tribune* informó que el vapor *Cherokee* arribó a Santo Domingo tras haber sido rechazado en puertos septentrionales por un crucero del gobierno, trayendo noticias de que las regiones del norte se habían sumado a la revolución. El diario publicó un manifiesto insurgente de Puerto Plata que condenaba al presidente Wos y Gil por tiranía, prisiones abarrotadas y una ruina financiera extrema. El documento destacaba las deudas públicas impagas, los elevados tributos al petróleo, un oneroso empréstito de 120.000 dólares y concesiones portuarias irregulares por cuatro años concedidas a la Hamburg-American Line.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that 800 insurgents with artillery laid siege to the capital of Santo Domingo, prompting German warships *Panther* and *Gazelle* to land armed guards and escort the merchant steamer *Athen*. Dominican exiles in New York received reports that insurgent forces had proclaimed General Juan Isidro Jimenes president of the republic. Jimenes had previously resigned as Dominican fiscal agent to organize the armed movement to reclaim the presidency from which he had been ousted.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que 800 insurgentes con artillería sitiaron la capital de Santo Domingo, lo que motivó a los buques de guerra alemanes *Panther* y *Gazelle* a desembarcar destacamentos armados y escoltar al vapor mercante *Athen*. Exiliados dominicanos en Nueva York recibieron informes de que las fuerzas insurgentes habían proclamado presidente de la república al general Juan Isidro Jimenes. Jimenes había renunciado previamente a su cargo de agente fiscal dominicano con el propósito de organizar el movimiento armado para recuperar la presidencia de la cual había sido desalojado.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that Dominican Consul General Galván threatened that government gunboats would sink any vessel, including the Clyde Line steamer *Cherokee*, attempting to enter rebel-controlled ports. New York customs authorities refused to deny clearances to American merchantmen, stating that the United States had not recognized the blockade as effective. The report also noted that President Wos y Gil had agreed to arbitrate the San Domingo Improvement Company's four-million-dollar claim regarding railroad construction.

Las autoridades aduaneras de Nueva York se negaron a denegar el despacho a los mercantes estadounidenses, alegando que los Estados Unidos no habían reconocido el bloqueo como efectivo. records.summary_en: The *Daily Kennebec Journal* reported that the United States government formally refused to recognize the Dominican naval blockade as effective and instructed port collectors to issue clearances for all Dominican harbors. In Dominican waters, insurgents fired unsuccessfully on the American steamer *New York* at Samana, while Minister Powell rejected rebel appeals for diplomatic recognition. In response to American diplomatic pressure, the Dominican government named Foreign Minister Galván and Judge Gray as arbitrators to resolve the San Domingo Improvement Company claim.

records.summary_en: There was a heavy artillery duel between government troops and the insurgents at Santo Domingo City on the night of November 17, and the United States cruiser Baltimore landed a force of marines for the protection of American interests. Minister Powell's despatches to the State Department call the situation desperate: the city is constantly under fire, shells are falling in it, it is surrounded on three sides, an assault is momentarily expected, and it is believed the Dominican government cannot much longer hold out against the revolutionists.

Los despachos del ministro Powell al Departamento de Estado califican la situación de desesperada: la ciudad está constantemente bajo fuego, caen proyectiles en ella, está rodeada por tres lados, se espera un asalto de un momento a otro y se cree que el gobierno dominicano no podrá resistir mucho más contra los revolucionarios.

Maxwell aboard to advise Captain Archibald, after the Dominican government blockaded Sanchez, Samana, Puerto Plata, Macoris and Monte Cristi and threatened to sink the vessel if she entered them. Maxwell said he did not think the Dominican gunboats would fire, and that a blockade is effective only when warships are actually and permanently on the spot to prevent vessels entering.

Maxwell dijo que no creía que las cañoneras dominicanas dispararan, y que un bloqueo solo es efectivo cuando los buques de guerra están real y permanentemente en el lugar para impedir la entrada de barcos.

The same report tells how the Clyde Line steamer New York was fired on by insurgents as she entered Samana Bay at four in the morning on November 1, a shell whistling over Captain Marmion's head from a fort on the bluff above the narrow channel.

El mismo informe cuenta cómo el vapor New York, de la Clyde Line, fue atacado a tiros por los insurgentes cuando entraba en la bahía de Samaná a las cuatro de la mañana del 1 de noviembre, y una granada pasó silbando sobre la cabeza del capitán Marmion desde un fuerte en el risco sobre el estrecho canal.

records.headline: Should the insurgents succeed in effecting an entrance to the city
records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that the besieged Dominican provisional government was unable to raise a $20,000 loan for city defense, leaving the capital vulnerable to insurgent assault and street fighting. With the gunboat *Newport* remaining as the only foreign warship in port, concerns grew over the safety of foreign residents. Meanwhile, insurgent leader Juan Isidro Jimenes scored a decisive victory at Moca against 500 government troops under General Ramón Cáceres, who was wounded, clearing the path for an advance on Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que el asediado gobierno provisional dominicano fue incapaz de obtener un préstamo de 20.000 dólares para la defensa de la ciudad, dejando a la capital expuesta a asaltos insurgentes y combates callejeros. Siendo el cañonero *Newport* el único buque de guerra extranjero en el puerto, creció la inquietud por la seguridad de los residentes extranjeros. Mientras tanto, el caudillo rebelde Juan Isidro Jimenes logró una victoria decisiva en Moca contra 500 soldados gubernamentales al mando del general Ramón Cáceres, quien resultó herido, despejando el camino para avanzar sobre Santo Domingo.

records.headline: Dispatches dated December 29 report three revolutions raging in Santo Domingo, with the forces of Jimenez within…
records.summary_en: Dispatches dated December 29 report three revolutions raging in Santo Domingo, with the forces of Jimenez within four hours of Santo Domingo City and Minister Powell appealing to the State Department for an additional warship because he thinks the situation demands it. The State Department had already arranged for a vessel from Rear Admiral Lamberton's squadron at Trinidad to be sent at full speed to assist the gunboat Newport in protecting American and other interests, while President Morales, back in the capital after finding it impossible to land in the north, had bombarded Puerto Plata, many arrests had been made, and government troops were preparing to attack rebels at San Cristobal.

records.summary_en: The *Montgomery Advertiser* reported that the Dominican gunboat *Independencia* captured two armed insurgent schooners and shelled suburban districts of the capital to dislodge revolutionary fighters. Government forces successfully retook Baní and San Cristóbal and repelled a major assault on Santo Domingo following an engagement at Haina. To isolate the insurrection, the government issued a decree closing six major coastal ports to foreign shipping, supported by naval patrols.
records.summary_es: El *Montgomery Advertiser* informó que el cañonero dominicano *Independencia* capturó dos goletas insurgentes armadas y cañoneó distritos suburbanos de la capital para desalojar a los combatientes revolucionarios. Las fuerzas del gobierno recuperaron con éxito Baní y San Cristóbal y repelieron un asalto de envergadura contra Santo Domingo tras un combate en Haina. Para aislar la insurrección, el gobierno emitió un decreto clausurando seis puertos costeros principales al comercio marítimo exterior, apoyado por patrullajes navales.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported that the State Department withheld diplomatic recognition from Dominican factions despite claims by General Jimenes's followers that they controlled nearly the entire country outside the capital. United States officials observed that three rival governing authorities were contending for power simultaneously, leaving policy implementation to Minister Powell's judgment. To protect American interests, the Navy dispatched the cruiser *Columbia* from Guantanamo to reinforce the warships *Detroit* and *Newport* at Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó que el Departamento de Estado se abstuvo de conceder reconocimiento diplomático a las facciones dominicanas, a pesar de que los partidarios del general Jimenes afirmaban controlar prácticamente todo el país fuera de la capital. Funcionarios de los Estados Unidos observaron que tres autoridades de gobierno rivales se disputaban el poder de forma simultánea, dejando la ejecución de la política al criterio del ministro Powell. Para resguardar los intereses estadounidenses, la Armada envió el crucero *Columbia* desde Guantánamo para reforzar a los buques de guerra *Detroit* y *Newport* en Santo Domingo.

General Deschamps fled and took refuge in the United States consulate, the British cruiser Pallas landed marines to protect the consulate, and the United States cruiser Hartford arrived.

El general Deschamps huyó y se refugió en el consulado de Estados Unidos, el crucero británico Pallas desembarcó infantes de marina para proteger el consulado y llegó el crucero estadounidense Hartford.

records.summary_en: The commander of the United States steamer Detroit reports from Puerto Plata on January 17 that, after a fight outside the city limits, the Jimenez forces occupying Puerto Plata surrendered unconditionally to President Morales's forces. He says perfect order prevails, the port's business will begin the next morning, there were no casualties among non-combatants and no destruction of property, and he calls the surrender a severe blow to Jimenez.

Dice que reina un orden perfecto, que el comercio del puerto comenzará a la mañana siguiente, que no hubo víctimas entre los no combatientes ni destrucción de propiedades, y califica la rendición de un golpe severo para Jiménez.

records.summary_en: Reports from St. Thomas say the Dominican minister of foreign affairs has left San Domingo for Washington to try to arrange a United States protectorate over the republic, while Jiminez's forces continue bombarding the capital. A Puerto Plata report adds that seven hundred government soldiers are marching on San Domingo, the rebel stronghold, in what is expected to be the most important battle of the Jiminez revolution, and gives details of the recent recapture of Puerto Plata, where the commander of an American vessel in the harbor practically managed the battle within a fighting zone fixed by the American and British warship commanders.
records.summary_es: Informes desde St. Thomas dicen que el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores dominicano ha salido de Santo Domingo hacia Washington para tratar de acordar un protectorado de los Estados Unidos sobre la república, mientras las fuerzas de Jiménez continúan bombardeando la capital. Un informe de Puerto Plata añade que setecientos soldados del gobierno marchan sobre Santo Domingo, el bastión rebelde, en lo que se espera sea la batalla más importante de la revolución de Jiménez, y da detalles de la reciente reconquista de Puerto Plata, donde el comandante de una embarcación estadounidense en el puerto dirigió prácticamente la batalla dentro de una zona de combate fijada por los comandantes de los buques de guerra estadounidense y británico.

records.summary_en: The *San Francisco Call* reported that pressure was mounting in Washington for President Roosevelt to establish an American protectorate over the Dominican Republic to end persistent revolutionary instability. While Secretary of State Hay opposed such an intervention, President Roosevelt was considering steps to protect American commercial investments, though final decisions awaited ratification of the Panama Canal treaty. The report highlighted that six American, German, and French warships were guarding foreign interests, with European governments receptive to American measures restoring order.
records.summary_es: El *San Francisco Call* informó que crecía la presión en Washington para que el presidente Roosevelt estableciera un protectorado estadounidense sobre la República Dominicana a fin de terminar con la constante inestabilidad revolucionaria. Aunque el secretario de Estado Hay se oponía a dicha intervención, el presidente Roosevelt consideraba medidas para proteger las inversiones comerciales estadounidenses, si bien las decisiones definitivas aguardaban la ratificación del tratado del Canal de Panamá. El informe subrayó que seis buques de guerra estadounidenses, alemanes y franceses custodiaban los intereses extranjeros, mostrándose los gobiernos europeos receptivos ante medidas estadounidenses que restablecieran el orden.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* recounted political maneuvers during President Buenaventura Báez's historical efforts to annex the Dominican Republic to the United States. The account recalled how Báez jailed political opponents to guarantee passage of the treaty until an American politician persuaded him that a small dissenting vote would look less suspicious. It also detailed an earlier attempt to lease Samana Bay surveyed by Captain George B. McClellan, which collapsed when British and French warships arrived to oppose American acquisition.

records.headline: A special cable from Santo Domingo reports that peace has been concluded with the insurgents, that General Cespedes…
records.summary_en: A special cable from Santo Domingo reports that peace has been concluded with the insurgents, that General Cespedes will take charge of the government and that the rebel leader General Rodriguez promises to leave the country, though members of the Jimenez party express dissatisfaction, believing the American gunboats aided Acting President Morales and forced the rebels to capitulate. Rear Admiral Sigsbee telegraphed the Navy Department from Monte Cristi that the custom house there would resume business that day, that all the ports of the Dominican Republic are now open to commerce and that the revolution has ended.
records.summary_es: Un cable especial de Santo Domingo informa que se ha concluido la paz con los insurgentes, que el general Céspedes se hará cargo del gobierno y que el líder rebelde general Rodríguez promete abandonar el país, aunque miembros del partido de Jiménez expresan su descontento, creyendo que los cañoneros estadounidenses ayudaron al presidente interino Morales y obligaron a los rebeldes a capitular. El contralmirante Sigsbee telegrafió al Departamento de Marina desde Monte Cristi que la aduana de allí reanudaría sus operaciones ese día, que todos los puertos de la República Dominicana están ahora abiertos al comercio y que la revolución ha terminado.

records.headline: Writing from Santiago de los Caballeros on June 17, the correspondent says Santo Domingo has had some two hundred…
records.summary_en: Writing from Santiago de los Caballeros on June 17, the correspondent says Santo Domingo has had some two hundred revolutions within sixty years of independence and that their battles were long fought with little bloodshed, but that this is no longer the rule. He asserts that more people have been killed in the present revolution than in the war with Spain forty years ago, and gives eyewitness accounts of the battle at Puerto Plata last January, where soldiers on both sides fired their guns off as fast as they could load until their ammunition was gone, and then ran.
records.summary_es: Escribiendo desde Santiago de los Caballeros el 17 de junio, el corresponsal dice que Santo Domingo ha tenido unas doscientas revoluciones en sesenta años de independencia y que sus batallas se libraban durante mucho tiempo con poco derramamiento de sangre, pero que eso ya no es la regla. Afirma que en la revolución actual ha muerto más gente que en la guerra con España de hace cuarenta años, y ofrece testimonios de la batalla de Puerto Plata del enero pasado, donde los soldados de ambos bandos dispararon sus armas tan rápido como podían cargarlas hasta agotar las municiones, y luego huyeron.

records.headline: The article describes President Morales arriving at Puerto Plata with five hundred troops aboard his gunboat El…
records.summary_en: The article describes President Morales arriving at Puerto Plata with five hundred troops aboard his gunboat El Presidente, intending to proceed to Monte Cristi, whose authorities had signed a peace compact aboard the American ship Detroit. Those authorities told him by telegraph that he could not land his troops in their territory, and, finding them fully prepared and under arms to resist, he gave up the project and returned to the capital, while the American ship Bancroft sailed away to Porto Rico. The article also charges that Morales broke his amnesty agreements, describing how the surrendered rebel chief Jose Gonzalo was shot in the back by his escort on the road to Santiago, supposedly while trying to escape, and saying such executions have been common under his government.

Esas autoridades le dijeron por telégrafo que no podía desembarcar sus tropas en su territorio y, al encontrarlas plenamente preparadas y en armas para resistir, abandonó el proyecto y regresó a la capital, mientras el buque americano Bancroft zarpaba hacia Porto Rico. El artículo también acusa a Morales de romper sus acuerdos de amnistía, describe cómo el jefe rebelde rendido José Gonzalo fue baleado por la espalda por su escolta en el camino a Santiago, supuestamente mientras intentaba escapar, y afirma que ejecuciones como esa han sido comunes bajo su gobierno.

records.summary_en: This feature portrays President Carlos F. Morales ruling Santo Domingo through a secret black list of citizens to be killed or imprisoned, and recounts how, on the eve of his inauguration, he had General Mansueta and Commander Guillhoux taken out at sunrise and shot at the cemetery after they asked for a pardon. It stresses that the execution deliberately violated an amnesty compact signed three weeks earlier aboard the United States cruiser Detroit, in Commander Dillingham's presence, guaranteeing the lives and liberty of rebels who laid down their arms.

Subraya que la ejecución violó deliberadamente un pacto de amnistía firmado tres semanas antes a bordo del crucero estadounidense Detroit, en presencia del comandante Dillingham, que garantizaba la vida y la libertad de los rebeldes que depusieran las armas.

records.headline: U. S. RECEIVERSHIP FOR SANTO DOMINGO
records.summary_en: The *Spokane Press* reviewed the history of United States annexation attempts in the Dominican Republic, focusing on President Buenaventura Báez's 1869 pact with President Grant. The treaty failed in the Senate after Senator Charles Sumner denounced Báez as a corrupt despot maintained in power solely by American naval force. The article also noted the short-lived 1872 lease of Samana Bay and President Heureaux's subsequent transfer of national custom houses to an American syndicate in 1893.
records.summary_es: El *Spokane Press* repasó la historia de los intentos de anexión de los Estados Unidos en la República Dominicana, centrándose en el pacto de 1869 entre el presidente Buenaventura Báez y el presidente Grant. El tratado fracasó en el Senado después de que el senador Charles Sumner denunciara a Báez como un déspota corrupto sostenido en el poder únicamente por la fuerza naval estadounidense. El artículo también destacó el efímero arrendamiento de la bahía de Samaná en 1872 y la posterior transferencia de las aduanas nacionales que hizo el presidente Heureaux a un sindicato estadounidense en 1893.

records.full_text:
U. S. RECEIVERSHIP FOR SANTO DOMINGO

The Novel Scheme Which Roosevelt Will Probably Put Into Effect—Island Would Have Been Annexed to This Country in 1869 But for the Opposition of Chas. Sumner.

By Jacob Waldeck.
WASHINGTON, Jan. 10.—Santo Domingo, torn by revolution, misgoverned and despoiled, is soon to feel the chastening influence of "the big stick." A century of turmoil, bloodshed, robbery and disorder is to be terminated by the intervention of the United States.

Officials of the highest rank in the administration say that such action is inevitable. President Roosevelt is said, on the best authority, to hold that view of the case. It is a question of time, but of months, rather than years. American officials and American marines will inaugurate a reign of good order and a season of debt-paying in the country.

They don't call it that in diplomatic language, but the proposed order of things in Santo Domingo seems to be nothing more or less than a receivership. It will be

Something Brand New
in American history. The republic will bear a relation to this country unlike Porto Rico, which was annexed; unlike the Philippines, which were hitched on behind, and unlike Cuba, which is the object of a benevolent guardianship. Santo Domingo is to be regulated. It is to be told to pay its debts and be good.

The plan is to place men in the custom houses to collect the revenue of the country. They are to see that a fair share of this money goes to the creditors, and that public officials, instead of looting the public treasury, conduct the government on an economical basis. One custom house, that of Puerto Plata, is now in the hands of an American as a result of arbitration, last summer, over a claim of $5,000,000 owned by New Yorkers. They advanced a lot of money about 10 years ago and took a blanket mortgage on the government. The proceeds at Puerto Plata are being devoted to their claim.

Opinion as to the new deal is divided among the people. Creditors, business men and most of the people of the cities favor it. Those living in the interior are, as a rule, opposed to foreign interference. So are the insurgent chiefs, who fear that a settled order of things may interfere with the revolution industry and keep them from digging their hands into the treasury.

A Land of Chaos.
In the past the order of things has been very much unsettled. The country has been in a chronic state of revolution. There have been nearly a dozen presidents in five years.

From the standpoint of novelty it would seem that the people ought to welcome a receivership. The country has had autocratic, monarchial and republican forms of government. It has also had no government; there having been prolonged seasons of anarchy. Te people have been ruled by despots, emperors and presidents. Mostly despots, though, for whatever the title of the man who happened to be ruling for a short period, he has usually paid no attention to law. Men whom he hasn't liked he has caused to be shot. Any money lying around that he fancied he has appropriated. If money was scarce he negotiated loans at extravagant rates from foreigners. The lenders got Chadwick rates in the way of interest and bonuses, and could rest serene in the fact that when the day for settlement came their governments would force San Domingo to pay.

Another class of men who may embarrass the administration, when intervention takes place, are now flocking to Santo Domingo. They are "investors." A lot of them, Americans, are going over to the republic from Porto Rico. They

Scent Rich Profits
and are eager to be early on the ground. Tehir option is to pick up property at anarchy rates and sell at prices incident to American rule. Santo Domingo, in its climate and resources, has been described by all travelers who have visited the country as one of the most attractive and richest spots in the world. It has not been developed because for 100 years there has been little or no respect for personal or property rights. As a result of this condition it has been possible for years to buy the best of sugar land and land covered with magnificent forests at a nominal price. A good many Americans have taken advantage of the opportunity. They have made no attempt to develop their holdings, but have patiently awaited the day when order should be restored in the country. Others are now crowding in to get the benefit of the bargains offered. They are confident that this country will, in some form, soon enforce order, and they are equally confident that when the United States finally withdraws it will exact guarantees for the protection of their interests.

Came Close to Annexation.
The question of adding the territory of the republic to the United States has been raised at intervals for half a century. It confronted Lincoln in the closing days of the civil war, but he was busy with bigger problems, and consigned it to a pigeonhole. Grant took it up in 1869. Men contended in those days that Santo Domingo would be a more valuable acquisition than Cuba, Haiti or Porto Rico. The fine climate, valuable forests, rich soil, sparse population and small public debt were all said to be in its favor. At that time the debt to be assumed by this country would have been only $1,500,000. Now it would be $32,000,000, secured by Dominican bonds, while Spain would put in a claim for other millions that, the dons say, they were to receive if the republic should ever, by consent of its people, become annexed to another country.

De B. Randolph Keim, a Pennsylvania editor who is also an official of the bureau of insular affairs, brought the first proposition of annexation to this country. He went to the island in 1869 as the correspondent of a New York newspaper.

records.headline: A feature on Santo Domingo under President Morales says the government pays out money daily at Santiago, La Vega,…
records.summary_en: A feature on Santo Domingo under President Morales says the government pays out money daily at Santiago, La Vega, Moca, Puerto Plata and other towns to maintain peace, while recalcitrant citizens and even suspects are imprisoned, banished or summarily shot. It argues that export duties ruin the sugar planter and discourage production, even though tobacco from the Cibao is shipped to Germany and cocoa, coffee, wax, honey and gold washed from mountain streams all leave the country.

Sostiene que los derechos de exportación arruinan al productor de azúcar y desaniman la producción, aun cuando el tabaco del Cibao se envía a Alemania y el cacao, el café, la cera, la miel y el oro lavado de los arroyos de las montañas salen del país.

records.headline: The Domin ican planters and all the foreign capitalists concerned in
records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* argued that foreign capitalists and commercial planters in the Dominican Republic actively encouraged political unrest to terminate indigenous rule. It cited State Department admissions that American firms had supplied money and weapons to opposing Dominican factions while simultaneously petitioning Washington for naval protection. The editorial noted that President Morales, having secured power through United States naval support, signed the customs receivership agreement to align with foreign property interests.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* sostuvo que los capitalistas y hacendados comerciales extranjeros en la República Dominicana fomentaban activamente la inestabilidad política para poner fin al gobierno autóctono. Citó admisiones del Departamento de Estado respecto a que firmas estadounidenses habían suministrado dinero y armas a facciones dominicanas rivales mientras pedían simultáneamente protección naval a Washington. El editorial señaló que el presidente Morales, habiendo asegurado el poder mediante el apoyo naval estadounidense, firmó el acuerdo de administración aduanera para alinearse con los intereses de los propietarios extranjeros.

Secretary of State Hay prepared to submit the protocol negotiated with President Morales, who had previously sought American protection by offering a coaling station at Samana Bay. records.headline: The article prints and discusses an arrangement under which a financial agent, at the Dominican government's…
records.summary_en: The article prints and discusses an arrangement under which a financial agent, at the Dominican government's request, may exercise customs authority at Sanchez, Samana, Monte Cristi and other ports of entry, as is already done at Puerto Plata, where an American agent has run the custom house for several months. It notes that officials expected trouble when the United States took charge of those custom houses, and lists the American marines within reach, at Guantanamo, San Juan and Culebra, while senators questioned whether the text of the protocol printed in The Sun was correct.
records.summary_es: El artículo reproduce y comenta un acuerdo según el cual un agente financiero, a petición del gobierno dominicano, puede ejercer autoridad aduanera en Sánchez, Samaná, Monte Cristi y otros puertos de entrada, como ya se hace en Puerto Plata, donde un agente estadounidense dirige la aduana desde hace varios meses. Señala que los funcionarios esperaban problemas cuando los Estados Unidos se hicieran cargo de esas aduanas, y enumera a los infantes de marina estadounidenses al alcance, en Guantánamo, San Juan y Culebra, mientras los senadores cuestionaban si el texto del protocolo publicado en The Sun era correcto.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* detailed the finalized protocol providing for American administration of Dominican customs until foreign creditor claims were settled. The modified convention affirmed the Monroe Doctrine, guaranteed Dominican territorial integrity, and allotted 45 percent of gross customs revenues directly to the Dominican government for its operating budget. The agreement stipulated that future tariff modifications required approval from the President of the United States and prohibited increases in the national public debt.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* detalló el protocolo definitivo que establecía la administración estadounidense de las aduanas dominicanas hasta que se saldaran las reclamaciones de los acreedores extranjeros. La convención modificada reafirmaba la Doctrina Monroe, garantizaba la integridad territorial dominicana y asignaba el 45 por ciento de los ingresos aduaneros brutos directamente al gobierno dominicano para su presupuesto operativo. El acuerdo estipulaba que las futuras modificaciones arancelarias requerían la aprobación del presidente de los Estados Unidos y prohibía cualquier incremento de la deuda pública nacional.

records.headline: This editorial examines the legal basis claimed for American customs operations in Santo Domingo, centered on the…
records.summary_en: This editorial examines the legal basis claimed for American customs operations in Santo Domingo, centered on the arbitration award of July 14, 1904, which authorized the United States Financial Agent to extend his control to Monte Cristi, Sanchez and Samana if the collections at Puerto Plata proved insufficient to meet the monthly installment of $37,500 payable under the award. It reports that Judge Abbott, the Financial Agent, unexpectedly returned to New York saying it had not been necessary to go beyond Puerto Plata for the revenue needed, while Admiral Sigsbee was negotiating with the people of Monte Cristi for their independent adoption of the protocol.
records.summary_es: Este editorial examina la base legal invocada para las operaciones aduaneras americanas en Santo Domingo, centrada en el laudo arbitral del 14 de julio de 1904, que autorizó al Agente Financiero de los Estados Unidos a extender su control a Monte Cristi, Sánchez y Samaná si las recaudaciones en Puerto Plata resultaban insuficientes para cubrir la cuota mensual de 37.500 dólares pagadera según el laudo. Informa que el juez Abbott, el Agente Financiero, regresó inesperadamente a Nueva York diciendo que no había sido necesario ir más allá de Puerto Plata para obtener los ingresos necesarios, mientras el almirante Sigsbee negociaba con la población de Monte Cristi la adopción independiente del protocolo por su parte.

records.summary_en: The *Wisconsin Weekly Advocate* published the terms of the treaty signed between United States Minister Thomas C. Dawson and Dominican ministers Juan Francisco Sánchez and Federico Velásquez. Invoking the Monroe Doctrine, the preamble pledged United States assistance in resolving foreign debts while respecting the territorial integrity of the Dominican Republic. Under the first article, the United States agreed to arbitrate all domestic and foreign financial claims and establish joint commissions to determine debt validity and payment schedules.
records.summary_es: El *Wisconsin Weekly Advocate* publicó los términos del tratado firmado entre el ministro de los Estados Unidos Thomas C. Dawson y los ministros dominicanos Juan Francisco Sánchez y Federico Velásquez. Invocando la Doctrina Monroe, el preámbulo prometía la asistencia de los Estados Unidos para saldar las deudas externas respetando al mismo tiempo la integridad territorial de la República Dominicana. Conforme al primer artículo, los Estados Unidos acordaron arbitrar todas las reclamaciones financieras nacionales y extranjeras y establecer comisiones mixtas para determinar la validez de las deudas y los calendarios de pago.

records.headline: An Associated Press report from Washington, dated March 17, says Senator Morgan used practically the entire…
records.summary_en: An Associated Press report from Washington, dated March 17, says Senator Morgan used practically the entire executive-session discussion of the Santo Domingo treaty to charge that William Nelson Cromwell of New York was the prime mover in a scheme to influence the United States in the financial affairs of the Dominican government. Morgan said Cromwell acted to frustrate the Reader syndicate's plan for Dominican concessions and to promote a syndicate holding a mass of claims against Latin-American republics, including a large part of the Dominican debt; the Senate was divided over whether he made his case, and the treaty was expected to be recommitted without a vote.

records.headline: With the customs-houses in,the control of the United States, the resources
records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported statements from President Morales warning that the Dominican government was powerless to resist European debt enforcement unless the United States intervened to delay creditor demands. Following the United States Senate's failure to ratify the customs treaty, fears spread in Santo Domingo that European nations would seize ports to satisfy unpaid claims. The report noted that while multiple American warships patrolled the coast, local observers argued that European seizures would effectively undermine the Monroe Doctrine.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* informó sobre declaraciones del presidente Morales en las que advertía que el gobierno dominicano era incapaz de resistir la ejecución forzosa de la deuda por parte de Europa a menos que los Estados Unidos intervinieran para aplazar las exigencias de los acreedores. Tras la falta de ratificación del tratado aduanero por el Senado de los Estados Unidos, se extendió en Santo Domingo el temor de que las naciones europeas incautaran puertos para saldar las reclamaciones pendientes. El informe señalaba que, mientras varios buques de guerra estadounidenses patrullaban la costa, observadores locales sostenían que las incautaciones europeas socavarían de hecho la Doctrina Monroe.

records.summary_en: The *San Francisco Call* reported that European investors held approximately $21,000,000 in Dominican bonds, with major portions distributed across Belgium, France, Holland, and Germany. French authorities announced they would not immediately enforce debt claims by force, though French bondholders expressed deep disappointment over the United States Senate's delay in ratifying the customs treaty. The report highlighted that interest payments on the 1897 unified debt had been in default since April 1899.

El informe subrayó que el pago de intereses de la deuda unificada de 1897 se encontraba en mora desde abril de 1899.

records.summary_en: The *Washington Times* reported on the private negotiations conducted by Mr. Reader, whose wife had sought to act as Dominican fiscal agent to negotiate the sale of Samana Bay and settle foreign debts. Although President Morales initially favored the private proposals, United States Minister Dawson instructed Dominican authorities on January 9 to terminate talks with Reader and deal exclusively with Washington. Following the arrival of Commander Dillingham on an American gunboat, official state negotiations commenced, prompting Reader to abandon his mission and return to New York.

Aunque el presidente Morales favoreció en un principio las propuestas privadas, el ministro estadounidense Dawson instruyó a las autoridades dominicanas el 9 de enero para que cesaran las conversaciones con Reader y trataran exclusivamente con Washington. Tras la llegada del comandante Dillingham en un cañonero estadounidense, comenzaron las negociaciones oficiales entre estados, lo que motivó a Reader a abandonar su misión y regresar a Nueva York.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Times-Republican* published President Roosevelt's directive instructing Minister Dawson to implement an interim modus vivendi for collecting Dominican customs revenues while the treaty awaited Senate approval. Under the executive plan, the Secretary of War would nominate port collectors, with unexpended revenues deposited in New York banks pending final legislative action. Concurrently, American warships monitored political movements in Monte Cristi, including the departure of General Barba from Puerto Rico, to prevent revolutionary disruption.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Times-Republican* publicó la directiva del presidente Roosevelt en la que instruía al ministro Dawson a implementar un modus vivendi provisional para recaudar los ingresos aduaneros dominicanos mientras el tratado esperaba la aprobación del Senado. Según el plan ejecutivo, el secretario de Guerra designaría a los recaudadores de los puertos, y los ingresos no devengados se depositarían en bancos de Nueva York a la espera de la resolución legislativa definitiva. Al mismo tiempo, buques de guerra estadounidenses vigilaban los movimientos políticos en Monte Cristi, incluida la salida del general Barba desde Puerto Rico, para evitar disturbios revolucionarios.

records.headline: Advices from Monte Cristi announce that General Barba and a number of Dominican exiles have landed there and that…
records.summary_en: Advices from Monte Cristi announce that General Barba and a number of Dominican exiles have landed there and that the inhabitants have risen against President Morales, blaming him for the present difficulties with foreign countries, with the district ready to begin a revolution in favour of Jiminez. The same report sets out the State Department's plan for Santo Domingo's finances, under which American commissioners would collect the customs, with forty-five per cent of the receipts going to the Dominican government and fifty-five per cent deposited in New York for the foreign creditors, pending the Senate's action on the treaty.

El mismo informe expone el plan del Departamento de Estado para las finanzas de Santo Domingo, según el cual comisionados americanos recaudarían las aduanas, con el cuarenta y cinco por ciento de los ingresos para el gobierno dominicano y el cincuenta y cinco por ciento depositado en Nueva York para los acreedores extranjeros, en espera de la decisión del Senado sobre el tratado.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that the implementation of the Dominican customs receivership awaited President Morales concluding agreements with European creditor nations. The Secretary of War prepared to nominate customs collectors, with President Roosevelt recommending William E. Gould of Baltimore, a linguist and financial editor, for a collectorship. It was also anticipated that George R. Colton, formerly an American revenue collector in the Philippines, would be appointed to assist in administering the Dominican customs service.

records.headline: A travel narrative follows the old Camino Real, the royal road running 150 miles north from Santo Domingo City to…
records.summary_en: A travel narrative follows the old Camino Real, the royal road running 150 miles north from Santo Domingo City to Cotui, La Vega and Moca, describing the ancient Spanish roads as broad paths cut a hundred feet wide through the forest, with no ditching, drainage, macadam or bridges, and the Isabella River crossed in native dugout canoes while the horses swim. It describes the savanna country of red clay loam and an inland town, Savanna Grande, as a row of one-story palm-wood huts thatched with palm leaves around a green central square, and the travelers' night stop at the home of Don Emiliano Tejera, a wealthy power in Dominican politics housed in thatched native houses with dirt floors.
records.summary_es: Una crónica de viaje sigue el viejo Camino Real, la vía real que corre 150 millas al norte desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo hasta Cotuí, La Vega y Moca, describiendo los antiguos caminos españoles como senderos anchos abiertos de cien pies a través del bosque, sin zanjas, drenaje, macadán ni puentes, y el río Isabela cruzado en canoas nativas de un solo tronco mientras los caballos nadan. Describe la región de sabana de arcilla roja y un pueblo del interior, Sabana Grande, como una fila de chozas de un piso de madera de palma techadas con hojas de palma alrededor de una plaza central verde, y la parada nocturna de los viajeros en la casa de don Emiliano Tejera, un hombre rico y poderoso en la política dominicana alojado en casas nativas de techo de palma y piso de tierra.

records.headline: A feature calls Santo Domingo the garden of the western tropics, with soil for cocoa, tobacco, tropical fruits,…
records.summary_en: A feature calls Santo Domingo the garden of the western tropics, with soil for cocoa, tobacco, tropical fruits, sugar cane, coffee, vanilla and rubber, mahogany forests in its mountainous interior, and constant verdure, and says that freed from its financial incubus it need not lag behind its sister republics. It then traces the career of President Carlos F. Morales, born at Puerto Plata to a prosperous merchant's family, ordained a priest after seminary study, who renounced the priesthood after eight years, edited an opposition newspaper, was arrested and narrowly escaped being shot, lived through revolt and exile, served in Congress and as governor of Puerto Plata, and last year headed the movement that drove out Jiminez and Wos y Gil and assumed control, proclaiming an election for next June.
records.summary_es: Un reportaje llama a Santo Domingo el jardín de los trópicos occidentales, con suelo para cacao, tabaco, frutas tropicales, caña de azúcar, café, vainilla y caucho, bosques de caoba en su interior montañoso y verdor constante, y dice que libre de su peso financiero no tiene por qué quedarse atrás de sus repúblicas hermanas. Después recorre la carrera del presidente Carlos F. Morales, nacido en Puerto Plata en la familia de un comerciante próspero, ordenado sacerdote tras estudiar en un seminario, quien renunció al sacerdocio después de ocho años, editó un periódico de oposición, fue arrestado y escapó por poco de ser fusilado, vivió entre revueltas y exilios, sirvió en el Congreso y como gobernador de Puerto Plata, y el año pasado encabezó el movimiento que expulsó a Jiminez y a Wos y Gil y asumió el control, proclamando una elección para el próximo junio.

records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch reports that, to thwart a revolutionary movement at Macoris against President Morales of Santo Domingo, the State Department has asked the Navy Department to send a warship to that port, and instructions were telegraphed to Rear Admiral Bradford at Guantanamo. It describes Bradford as the American policeman delegated to see that Morales's rule is not disturbed while the Senate acts on the proposed protectorate, and says the department believes the disturbance is fomented by New York interests opposed to the Dominican treaty.

Describe a Bradford como el policía estadounidense delegado para velar por que el gobierno de Morales no sea perturbado mientras el Senado decide sobre el protectorado propuesto, y dice que el departamento cree que la alteración es fomentada por intereses de Nueva York opuestos al tratado dominicano.

records.summary_en: The *Birmingham Age-Herald* criticized President Roosevelt for enforcing the unratified Dominican customs treaty through executive action, using warships to protect Customs Receiver George R. Colton. The editorial argued that neither Roosevelt nor President Morales held constitutional authority to bind their nations without legislative approval, and warned the policy risked committing the United States to guaranteeing debts throughout Spanish America. The article predicted that Senate Democrats would firmly oppose ratification, noting rumors that the administration might seek a congressional joint resolution to validate the receivership.
records.summary_es: El *Birmingham Age-Herald* criticó al presidente Roosevelt por aplicar el tratado aduanero dominicano no ratificado mediante una acción ejecutiva, empleando buques de guerra para proteger al receptor de aduanas George R. Colton. El editorial sostenía que ni Roosevelt ni el presidente Morales tenían autoridad constitucional para comprometer a sus naciones sin aprobación legislativa, y advertía del riesgo de que esta política comprometiera a los Estados Unidos a garantizar deudas en toda Hispanoamérica. El artículo vaticinaba que los demócratas en el Senado se opondrían con firmeza a la ratificación, señalando rumores de que el gobierno intentaría obtener una resolución conjunta del Congreso para validar la administración aduanera.

records.summary_en: The *Free Lance* reported on the repressive governance of Dominican President Morales, stating he had executed approximately 200 political opponents and maintained a coded blacklist of prominent citizens. Meanwhile, the State Department in Washington announced a policy of non-intervention in internal Dominican strife, regarding the conflict as domestic as long as foreign interests remained safe. Officials cautioned, however, that the United States would intervene militarily if violence threatened American lives or interfered with customs collections.
records.summary_es: El *Free Lance* informó sobre la gobernanza represiva del presidente dominicano Morales, afirmando que había ejecutado a cerca de 200 opositores políticos y mantenía una lista negra cifrada de ciudadanos prominentes. Entretanto, el Departamento de Estado en Washington anunció una política de no intervención en las disputas internas dominicanas, considerando el conflicto como doméstico mientras los intereses extranjeros estuvieran a salvo. No obstante, los funcionarios advirtieron que los Estados Unidos intervendrían militarmente si la violencia amenazaba vidas estadounidenses o interfería con la recaudación de aduanas.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that revolutionary forces under General Guellito united outside Puerto Plata to attack Santiago, where provisional President Ramón Cáceres was concentrating government forces. A cable from Customs Receiver Colonel George R. Colton confirmed that President Morales had fled the capital to join the Monte Cristi insurrection, prompting the Dominican Congress to initiate impeachment proceedings. Colton reported that despite the acute political crisis, the customs receivership continued to operate without interference from any faction.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que las fuerzas revolucionarias bajo el mando del general Güellito se unieron en las afueras de Puerto Plata para atacar Santiago, donde el presidente provisional Ramón Cáceres concentraba las fuerzas gubernamentales. Un cable del receptor de aduanas, coronel George R. Colton, confirmó que el presidente Morales había huido de la capital para sumarse a la insurrección de Monte Cristi, lo que llevó al Congreso dominicano a iniciar un juicio político en su contra. Colton comunicó que, a pesar de la agudeza de la crisis política, la administración de aduanas continuaba operando sin interferencias de ninguna facción.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported on impending military clashes at Santiago between forces loyal to provisional President Ramón Cáceres and rebel units allied with former President Jimenes and fugitive President Morales. An American observer arriving from Monte Cristi, Hugh M. Creighton, asserted that the United States should sustain Morales, arguing the conflict erupted because Morales refused financial demands from Cáceres's political faction. Creighton noted that the 45 percent customs revenue allocated by the American receivership adequately met lawful state expenses but left no funds for political patronage.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó sobre inminentes enfrentamientos bélicos en Santiago entre fuerzas leales al presidente provisional Ramón Cáceres y unidades rebeldes aliadas con el expresidente Jimenes y el presidente prófugo Morales. Un observador estadounidense recién llegado de Monte Cristi, Hugh M. Creighton, afirmó que los Estados Unidos debían respaldar a Morales, argumentando que el conflicto estalló porque este rechazó las demandas financieras de la facción política de Cáceres. Creighton señaló que el 45 por ciento de los ingresos de aduanas asignado por la administración estadounidense cubría adecuadamente los gastos legítimos del Estado, pero no dejaba fondos para el clientelismo político.
