records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that former President Juan Isidro Jimenes traveled to Monte Cristi to seek the presidency with the backing of fugitive President Morales and broad northern support. The paper profiled insurgent leader General Demetrio Rodríguez, an American-educated commander who had previously controlled customs revenues in Monte Cristi before being defeated by General Céspedes. It noted that Céspedes, originally a key supporter of Morales, had turned against the president in fierce opposition to the fiscal convention with the United States.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* informó que el expresidente Juan Isidro Jimenes viajó a Monte Cristi para aspirar a la presidencia con el respaldo del presidente prófugo Morales y un amplio apoyo en el norte. El periódico reseñó al líder insurgente, general Demetrio Rodríguez, un militar educado en los Estados Unidos que anteriormente había controlado los ingresos de aduanas en Monte Cristi antes de ser derrotado por el general Céspedes. Señaló además que Céspedes, quien en un principio fue un firme partidario de Morales, se volvió contra el mandatario en feroz oposición a la convención fiscal con los Estados Unidos.

records.summary_en: The *Paducah Sun* reported that Dominican government forces defeated insurgent troops in major combat, prompting the rebel-held gunboat *Independencia* and Monte Cristi officials to seek surrender terms under safety guarantees. In San Juan, Puerto Rico, injured former President Carlos F. Morales arrived aboard the gunboat *Dubuque* and expressed deep appreciation for President Roosevelt's assistance. Morales stated from his hospital bed that the salvation of the Dominican Republic depended entirely on the ratification of the customs convention to prevent continual national ruination.
records.summary_es: El *Paducah Sun* informó que las fuerzas gubernamentales dominicanas vencieron a las tropas insurgentes en un gran combate, lo que llevó al cañonero en poder rebelde *Independencia* y a las autoridades de Monte Cristi a solicitar condiciones de rendición bajo garantías de seguridad. En San Juan, Puerto Rico, el herido expresidente Carlos F. Morales llegó a bordo del cañonero *Dubuque* y expresó su profundo agradecimiento por la asistencia del presidente Roosevelt. Morales manifestó desde su cama de hospital que la salvación de la República Dominicana dependía por entero de la ratificación de la convención de aduanas para evitar la constante ruina nacional.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* published an interview from San Juan with ousted Dominican President Carlos F. Morales, who affirmed that national salvation depended on the ratification of the pending customs convention by both nations. Morales noted that while provisional President Cáceres and various rebel factions had come to endorse the convention, political stability remained precarious under Cáceres's minority government. Morales recounted suffering a fractured ankle when a vine rope broke while scaling a cliff during his escape from the Dominican capital.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* publicó una entrevista desde San Juan con el depuesto presidente dominicano Carlos F. Morales, quien afirmó que la salvación nacional dependía de la ratificación de la convención aduanera pendiente por ambas naciones. Morales señaló que, si bien el presidente provisional Cáceres y varias facciones rebeldes habían llegado a respaldar la convención, la estabilidad política continuaba siendo precaria bajo el gobierno minoritario de Cáceres. Morales relató que sufrió una fractura de tobillo al romperse una cuerda vegetal mientras escalaba un risco durante su huida de la capital dominicana.

records.summary_en: A dispatch from Cape Haitien on January 16 reports a bloody and probably final battle near Guayubin, where the troops of General Caceres, temporary president of San Domingo, defeated the insurgents, with several generals on both sides killed or wounded. Former president Morales, interviewed at San Juan, said the future salvation of Santo Domingo depends entirely on ratification of the pending convention by the United States Senate and the Dominican congress.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Cabo Haitiano del 16 de enero informa de una batalla sangrienta y probablemente final cerca de Guayubín, donde las tropas del general Cáceres, presidente temporal de Santo Domingo, derrotaron a los insurgentes, con varios generales de ambos bandos muertos o heridos. El expresidente Morales, entrevistado en San Juan, dijo que la salvación futura de Santo Domingo depende enteramente de la ratificación de la convención pendiente por el Senado de los Estados Unidos y el congreso dominicano.

records.summary_en: The *Stark County Democrat* reported on a Senate speech by Senator Benjamin Tillman condemning President Roosevelt's Dominican policy and the enforcement of the unratified customs treaty. Tillman criticized the administration for prioritizing European bondholders and ridiculed the executive *modus vivendi* as an unconstitutional usurpation of Senate authority. Warning against imperial expansion, Tillman asserted that unless the Senate firmly rejected the administration's actions, the United States would permanently dominate and occupy Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: El *Stark County Democrat* informó sobre un discurso en el Senado del senador Benjamin Tillman, en el que condenó la política dominicana del presidente Roosevelt y la aplicación del tratado aduanero no ratificado. Tillman criticó al gobierno por priorizar a los tenedores de bonos europeos y ridiculizó el *modus vivendi* ejecutivo como una usurpación inconstitucional de la autoridad del Senado. Al advertir contra la expansión imperialista, Tillman aseveró que, a menos que el Senado rechazara firmemente las acciones del gobierno, los Estados Unidos dominarían y ocuparían de forma permanente a Santo Domingo.

records.headline: A treaty of peace between the insur gent generals at Monte
records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that a peace treaty ending the Dominican insurrection was signed aboard the United States cruiser *Yankee* at Monte Cristi. Foreign Minister Emiliano Tejera stated that the rapid restoration of peace was made possible by decisive military action and the American financial *modus vivendi*, which deprived the insurgents of customs revenues. Under the capitulation terms, Monte Cristi returned to government control, rebel General Desiderio Arias was permitted to go into exile in Puerto Rico, and remaining insurgents were granted amnesty.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* informó que se firmó a bordo del crucero estadounidense *Yankee*, en Monte Cristi, un tratado de paz que puso fin a la insurrección dominicana. El ministro de Relaciones Exteriores Emiliano Tejera declaró que el rápido restablecimiento de la paz fue posible gracias a la enérgica acción militar y al *modus vivendi* financiero estadounidense, que privó a los insurgentes de las rentas aduaneras. Bajo los términos de la capitulación, Monte Cristi volvió al control del gobierno, se le permitió al general rebelde Desiderio Arias exiliarse en Puerto Rico y se concedió amnistía a los insurgentes restantes.

records.headline: Herald correspondence from Santo Domingo, dated March 3, reports that General Ramon Caceres will not resign the…
records.summary_en: Herald correspondence from Santo Domingo, dated March 3, reports that General Ramon Caceres will not resign the presidency, because a change of administration would involve internal disturbances, and that the demand for him to remain was almost universal. His cousin Horacio Valdez, head of the Horacist party and the man in whose favor Caceres wished to withdraw, was the first to urge him to reconsider, and after petitions and a mass meeting in Columbus plaza a crowd marched to Caceres's house, where he told them he would postpone his resignation until the danger to the republic ceased, later issuing a public address accepting what he called the new sacrifice.
records.summary_es: Una correspondencia del Herald desde Santo Domingo, fechada el 3 de marzo, informa que el general Ramón Cáceres no renunciará a la presidencia, porque un cambio de administración implicaría disturbios internos, y que la demanda de que permaneciera fue casi universal. Su primo Horacio Valdez, jefe del partido horacista y la persona en cuyo favor Cáceres deseaba retirarse, fue el primero en instarlo a reconsiderarlo, y tras las peticiones y una reunión masiva en la plaza Colón una multitud marchó a la casa de Cáceres, donde les dijo que pospondría su renuncia hasta que cesara el peligro para la república, y después emitió un mensaje público aceptando lo que llamó el nuevo sacrificio.

records.headline: A former high official of Santo Domingo, now residing in San Juan and close to former President Morales, says that…
records.summary_en: A former high official of Santo Domingo, now residing in San Juan and close to former President Morales, says that judging from the attitude of Congress there is every possibility the Santo Domingo convention will not be approved by the United States government, at least not this year, and that this would be the death blow to the present administration headed by President Ramon Caceres. He explains that Caceres forced Morales to resign in the belief the convention would pass and sustain his party in power, partly through the article providing for the landing of American troops at the President's request, the very article Caceres had used against Morales, and that Caceres made promises he will never be able to keep.
records.summary_es: Un ex alto funcionario de Santo Domingo, que ahora reside en San Juan y es cercano al expresidente Morales, dice que, a juzgar por la actitud del Congreso, hay todas las posibilidades de que la convención de Santo Domingo no sea aprobada por el gobierno de los Estados Unidos, al menos no este año, y que eso sería el golpe mortal para el gobierno actual encabezado por el presidente Ramón Cáceres. Explica que Cáceres obligó a Morales a renunciar creyendo que la convención sería aprobada y mantendría a su partido en el poder, en parte por el artículo que prevé el desembarco de tropas estadounidenses a petición del Presidente, el mismo artículo que Cáceres había usado contra Morales, y que Cáceres hizo promesas que nunca podrá cumplir.

records.summary_en: Former President Morales is at the head of a formidable revolutionary movement being organized among Dominican refugees in Porto Rico, preparing to sweep into the northern part of Santo Domingo with a large force, aided by Sanchez, his former minister of foreign affairs. Advices received at the State Department indicate a revolution brewing that could be greater than any disturbance since the American customs receivership was first inaugurated, and the Navy will take precautions to protect American interests.

Informes recibidos en el Departamento de Estado indican que se gesta una revolución que podría ser mayor que cualquier disturbio desde que se inauguró la receptoría aduanera estadounidense, y la Armada tomará precauciones para proteger los intereses estadounidenses.

records.summary_en: The Evening Times published a statement from Dominican revolutionists detailing their aims to reform land taxes, modify tariffs, eliminate export duties, and establish habeas corpus protections. The statement asserted that Generals Morales and Jimenez had reached an understanding, while former President Horacio Vasquez had deserted President Caceres. It also alleged that Dominican Minister of Finance Federico Velasquez was seeking to secure half of the $1,300,000 deposited for foreign creditors to fund government war expenses.
records.summary_es: The Evening Times publicó una declaración de revolucionarios dominicanos en la que detallaban sus objetivos de reformar los impuestos sobre la tierra, modificar los aranceles, suprimir los derechos de exportación y establecer garantías de habeas corpus. El manifiesto aseguraba que los generales Morales y Jimenes habían alcanzado un entendimiento, mientras que el expresidente Horacio Vásquez había abandonado al presidente Cáceres. Alegaba además que el ministro de Hacienda dominicano Federico Velásquez procuraba asegurarse la mitad de los 1.300.000 dólares depositados para los acreedores extranjeros con el propósito de costear los gastos bélicos del gobierno.

records.headline: Exiles arriving at San Juan from Santo Domingo, a couple of them wounded in encounters with government troops, said…
records.summary_en: Exiles arriving at San Juan from Santo Domingo, a couple of them wounded in encounters with government troops, said the revolution was in full blast along the northwest line and that towns including Barahona, Azua, Puerto Plata and Monte Cristi were constantly harassed by insurgent bands. A letter from the country printed with the report says public opinion wants ex-President Morales to lead the movement, hopes Morales and Jimenez will unite to retake the government, and reports that Minister of Finances Velasquez had set out hastily for Washington to seek support for his tottering government.
records.summary_es: Exiliados que llegaron a San Juan desde Santo Domingo, un par de ellos heridos en encuentros con tropas del gobierno, dijeron que la revolución estaba en pleno auge a lo largo de la línea del noroeste y que pueblos como Barahona, Azua, Puerto Plata y Monte Cristi eran hostigados constantemente por bandas insurgentes. Una carta del país publicada con el informe dice que la opinión pública quiere que el expresidente Morales encabece el movimiento, espera que Morales y Jiménez se unan para retomar el gobierno, e informa que el ministro de Hacienda Velásquez había salido a toda prisa hacia Washington en busca de apoyo para su tambaleante gobierno.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dominican representative Mr. Joubert conferred in Washington with Dr. Hollander and other U.S. officials regarding the situation in Santo Domingo. Joubert dismissed reports of a major revolutionary uprising at Monte Cristi as rumors from enemies of President Caceres and denied claims that customs funds held by the United States would be divided before treaty ratification. Joubert and Dominican Finance Minister Velasquez planned to travel to New York, where Velasquez would study American institutions.
records.summary_es: The Evening Star informó que el representante dominicano, el señor Joubert, conferenció en Washington con el Dr. Hollander y otros funcionarios estadounidenses sobre la situación en Santo Domingo. Joubert y el ministro de Hacienda dominicano Velásquez planeaban viajar a Nueva York, donde Velásquez estudiaría las instituciones estadounidenses.

records.headline: This profile presents Ramon Caceres, the present dictator-president of the Dominican Republic, as a big man of fully…
records.summary_en: This profile presents Ramon Caceres, the present dictator-president of the Dominican Republic, as a big man of fully six feet and over 250 pounds whose word is law but who rules with a laugh, even, the writer says, when he shot down his predecessor, Ulysses Heureaux, and who is known throughout the land simply as Mon. It relates that Caceres put Morales in the presidential chair because he did not want the job himself, kept him there against his will, and that Morales, feeling himself virtually a prisoner in his own capital, negotiated with the revolutionists and precipitated a revolution against his own government.

records.summary_en: The article reports a Dominican government proclamation for Monte Cristi province, countersigned by President Caceres, declaring that peace negotiations having failed, the government will end the war however violent and severe the means, placing the district under siege and threatening summary shooting even for women found carrying cartridges. Exiled revolutionist General Berroa, speaking in New York alongside ex-President Jiminez, called the decree simply despotic, said 700 to 1,000 well-armed revolutionists were in the field, and said the revolution would stop only when constitutional rights, political prisoners and the exiles were dealt with justly.
records.summary_es: El artículo informa de una proclama del gobierno dominicano para la provincia de Monte Cristi, refrendada por el presidente Cáceres, que declara que, habiendo fracasado las negociaciones de paz, el gobierno terminará la guerra por violentos y severos que sean los medios, pone el distrito en estado de sitio y amenaza con fusilamiento sumario incluso para las mujeres a las que se encuentren cartuchos. El general revolucionario exiliado Berroa, hablando en Nueva York junto al expresidente Jiménez, calificó el decreto de simplemente despótico, dijo que había entre 700 y 1,000 revolucionarios bien armados en campaña, y afirmó que la revolución solo cesaría cuando los derechos constitucionales, los presos políticos y los exiliados fueran tratados con justicia.

records.summary_en: The Morning Tribune reported that Dominican government forces under President Caceres had completely defeated revolutionists near Monte Cristi, leading most rebels to surrender and accept pardons. Several rebel leaders fled across the frontier into Haiti to join General Navarro at Cape Haitien, where they were required to depart for a foreign country because the Haitian government prohibited their stay. The excerpt noted that the uprising had been motivated by border smugglers and that the Monte Cristi district had returned to quiet.
records.summary_es: The Morning Tribune informó que las fuerzas gubernamentales dominicanas al mando del presidente Cáceres habían derrotado por completo a los revolucionarios cerca de Monte Cristi, llevando a la mayoría de los rebeldes a rendirse y aceptar el indulto. Varios cabecillas rebeldes huyeron cruzando la frontera hacia Haití para unirse al general Navarro en Cabo Haitiano, donde se les exigió partir hacia un país extranjero debido a que el gobierno haitiano prohibió su permanencia. La nota señaló que el levantamiento había sido impulsado por contrabandistas fronterizos y que el distrito de Monte Cristi había recobrado la tranquilidad.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the U.S. naval fleet had been withdrawn from Dominican waters, leaving only the *Marietta* and *Don Juan de Austria* to protect American citizens if needed. Future American involvement was described as limited to nominating customs collectors, who would transmit 55 percent of customs receipts to Kuhn, Loeb & Co. for bond service and 45 percent to the Dominican treasury. Collector Colonel Colton had already deposited more than $2,600,000 in New York banks and paid the Dominican government regular shares that funded soldiers, police, and civil employees.

La futura participación estadounidense se describió como limitada al nombramiento de recaudadores de aduanas, quienes remitirían el 55 por ciento de los ingresos aduaneros a Kuhn, Loeb & Co. para el servicio de los bonos y el 45 por ciento a la tesorería dominicana. records.summary_en: The Courier-Journal reported that President Roosevelt transmitted a new treaty with the Dominican Republic to the U.S. Senate concerning the administration of Dominican revenues. Under the agreement, contingent on debt arrangements with creditors, the U.S. President would appoint a receiver general to collect Dominican customs funds. Senate leaders aimed for action before congressional adjournment, and while several Democratic senators signaled support, Senator Bacon of Georgia had not yet fully assented.
records.summary_es: The Courier-Journal informó que el presidente Roosevelt remitió al Senado de los Estados Unidos un nuevo tratado con la República Dominicana relativo a la administración de las rentas dominicanas. En virtud del acuerdo, supeditado a los arreglos de deuda con los acreedores, el presidente estadounidense nombraría a un receptor general para recaudar los fondos aduaneros dominicanos. Los líderes del Senado procuraban actuar antes del receso del Congreso, y si bien varios senadores demócratas manifestaron su respaldo, el senador Bacon de Georgia aún no había dado su total consentimiento.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star detailed the financial provisions of the proposed Dominican treaty, outlining how customs revenues would cover receivership expenses, interest, bond amortization, and payments to the Dominican government. Collection costs were capped at five percent, with $100,000 monthly allocated to the loan's fiscal agent and annual collections over $3,000,000 applied to the sinking fund. The terms also prohibited the Dominican Republic from increasing its public debt or modifying import duties without the consent of the U.S. President.
records.summary_es: The Evening Star detalló las disposiciones financieras del propuesto tratado dominicano, explicando cómo los ingresos aduaneros cubrirían los gastos de la receptoría, los intereses, la amortización de los bonos y los pagos al gobierno dominicano. Los costos de recaudación quedaron limitados a un tope del cinco por ciento, con 100.000 dólares mensuales destinados al agente fiscal del empréstito y la aplicación al fondo de amortización de las recaudaciones anuales que superaran los 3.000.000 de dólares. Los términos prohibían asimismo a la República Dominicana incrementar su deuda pública o modificar los derechos de importación sin el consentimiento del presidente de los Estados Unidos.

records.summary_en: The Morning Tribune reported that ratification of the treaty in the Dominican Republic remained uncertain despite support from President Caceres and his cabinet. Severe opposition had arisen in the Dominican Congress and among the public, with opponents threatening lawmakers and alleging the treaty would give the United States an unshakable grip on the nation. The article argued that the treaty would protect Dominican independence and curb revolutionists, hoping the Dominican Congress would ultimately approve it.
records.summary_es: The Morning Tribune informó que la ratificación del tratado en la República Dominicana continuaba siendo incierta a pesar del respaldo del presidente Cáceres y su gabinete. Una severa oposición se había desatado en el Congreso dominicano y entre la ciudadanía, amenazando los opositores a los legisladores y alegando que el tratado otorgaría a los Estados Unidos un dominio inquebrantable sobre la nación. El artículo argumentaba que el tratado protegería la independencia dominicana y frenaría a los revolucionarios, manifestando la esperanza de que el Congreso dominicano terminara por aprobarlo.

records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune reported on Caribbean and Central American developments, noting U.S. naval patrols in Honduras and widespread Dominican discontent over the newly approved U.S. treaty. Dominican citizens reportedly feared the United States was turning their debt-burdened republic into a fief, preferring multiple foreign creditors over a single American power. Due to this popular backlash, expectations grew that the Dominican Congress might reject the treaty.
records.summary_es: The New-York Tribune informó sobre los acontecimientos en el Caribe y Centroamérica, señalando los patrullajes navales estadounidenses en Honduras y el descontento generalizado de los dominicanos ante el tratado recién aprobado por los Estados Unidos. Según se comunicó, los ciudadanos dominicanos temían que los Estados Unidos estuvieran convirtiendo su endeudada república en un feudo, prefiriendo múltiples acreedores extranjeros a un único poder estadounidense. Debido a este rechazo popular, crecieron las expectativas de que el Congreso dominicano pudiera rechazar el tratado.

records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune reported that the Dominican modus vivendi proved financially beneficial, resulting in $3,000,000 deposited in New York, increased revenues, four U.S.-built coastguard cutters, and reduced smuggling. Following Secretary Root's revision of the pending treaty, an agreement was reached between Finance Minister Federico Velasquez and foreign creditors to reduce claims by 50 percent for cash settlement. A New York banking house agreed to advance funds against $20,000,000 in fifty-year 5 percent bonds to consolidate Dominican debts.
records.summary_es: The New-York Tribune informó que el modus vivendi dominicano resultó económicamente provechoso, acumulando 3.000.000 de dólares depositados en Nueva York, un alza en los ingresos, cuatro guardacostas construidos en los Estados Unidos y la reducción del contrabando. Tras la revisión del tratado pendiente por el secretario Root, el ministro de Hacienda Federico Velásquez y los acreedores extranjeros alcanzaron un acuerdo para reducir las reclamaciones en un 50 por ciento mediante pago al contado. Una casa bancaria de Nueva York acordó adelantar fondos contra 20.000.000 de dólares en bonos a cincuenta años con un interés del 5 por ciento para consolidar las deudas dominicanas.

records.full_text:
TREATY RATIFIED BY SAN DOMINGO

Departure in United States' Relations to Small Republics

CONTROLS CUSTOM HOUSE

United States Now Becomes Legally a Trustee In a Financial Sense.

Will Discourage Revolutions.

Santo Domingo, May 3.—The new treaty between the United States and Santo Domingo intended to replace the treaty which has been pending before the United States Senate for the last two years was ratified by the Dominican congress today.

The Dominican treaty marks a new departure from the relations of the United States to the smaller republics of the western hemisphere, for in the case of Santo Domingo the United States now becomes legally a trustee in a financial sense, and must go so far in the preservation of order and the accompanying discouragement of revolutions as is incident to the control of the custom house.

The treaty really had its birth in a revolution. While the American government was pressing for a settlement of the claims of its citizens against Santo Domingo in December, 1904, President Morales being beset by revolutionists in the hope of securing the moral support of the United States, entered into an agreement with Captain Dillingham of the American navy by which the Dominican custom houses were to be occupied by the Americans and the foreign indebtedness of the country discharged from the receipts. Rejected at Washington, this agreement gave place March 31, 1905, to a modus vivendi which has operated up to this time. This placed an American collector in charge and provided for the deposit in New York of 55 per cent of the customs receipts for the benefit of the Dominican creditors. The modus vivendi did not save Morales from political destruction, as he was deported by the revolutionists and his vice president, General Caceres, installed as president. But the modus vivendi did lead to the deposit in New York of $3,000,000 which will now be placed to the credit of the Dominican government. That government has had more available money since the modus vivendi was established than any other time in its history. The Dominican government also finds itself in possession of four coast guard cutters built in the United States.

The modus vivendi was formed after a treaty pending before the United States Senate when Secretary Root assumed office. He recast the document, and February 19, last, the treaty which has just been ratified was submitted to the Senate. The way had been paved by an agreement between Federico Velasquez, the Dominican minister of finance, and the creditors of the republic whereby the latter agreed to a 50 per cent reduction in their claims if these were settled in cash.

A New York banking house undertook to advance the money for this purpose, accepting $20,000,000 5 per cent fifty-year bonds, which will now be promptly issued. Thus all of the creditors of Santo Domingo will be embodied in this New York firm.

The new treaty provides in its first article for the appointment by the President of a receiver of customs to collect the Dominican revenues as long as the bonds are outstanding, a period estimated at twenty to forty years. This collector is to pay the expenses of receivership, the interest on the bonds and the annual sums required for a mortization of the bonds, and then turn the balance over to the Dominican government. On the first day of each month he is to pay $100,000 to the fixed agent of the loan. When the customs receipts exceed $3,000,000 annually, then one-half of the surplus shall be applied to the sinking fund.

records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune reported on an interview with the former Dominican president, who described being detained in a palace during a visit to Port-au-Prince. He asserted that the era of Dominican revolutions had ended, praised President Caceres and the American customs receivership, but expressed firm opposition to annexation by the United States. He also stated his desire to return to Santo Domingo once a general amnesty was granted and recounted how political betrayal had forced his past flight.

Afirmó que la era de las revoluciones dominicanas había concluido, elogió al presidente Cáceres y a la receptoría de aduanas estadounidense, pero manifestó su firme oposición a una anexión por parte de los Estados Unidos. Declaró además su deseo de regresar a Santo Domingo tan pronto se concediera una amnistía general y relató cómo la traición política había forzado su huida en el pasado.

Medina asserted that American revenue administration had restored national credit, enabling debt payments and attracting American capital into central pine forestry and railroad construction. He maintained that the government was fully prepared to counter any revolutionary efforts from Dominican exiles in Puerto Rico.

records.headline: A Washington report describes a new plan to settle the Dominican Republic's debt after the original bond sale to a…
records.summary_en: A Washington report describes a new plan to settle the Dominican Republic's debt after the original bond sale to a New York firm fell through because of the money market. Foreign creditors recognized in the original project would receive an immediate pro rata cash payment from the $3,500,000 accumulated in the National City Bank from 55 per cent of the republic's customs revenues over two years, with the bond sale postponed or bonds issued directly by the Dominican government for the remainder, in a settlement to be discussed with Senor Velasquez at the State Department.
records.summary_es: Un informe de Washington describe un nuevo plan para saldar la deuda de la República Dominicana después de que la venta original de bonos a una firma de Nueva York fracasara por la situación del mercado monetario. Los acreedores extranjeros reconocidos en el proyecto original recibirían un pago inmediato en efectivo, a prorrata, del fondo de $3,500,000 acumulado en el National City Bank procedente del 55 por ciento de las rentas aduaneras de la república durante dos años, y la venta de bonos se pospondría o los bonos serían emitidos directamente por el gobierno dominicano por el resto, en un acuerdo que se discutiría con el señor Velásquez en el Departamento de Estado.

records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune reported on a debt settlement plan proposed by Dominican Finance Minister Velasquez to distribute cash deposited in the National City Bank pro rata and issue $16,000,000 in forty-year 5 percent bonds to foreign creditors. With no New York banking syndicate willing to underwrite the liquidation directly, Velasquez hoped European and American claimants—including the Santo Domingo Improvement Company—would accept the arrangement. The report noted that the United States would continue collecting Dominican customs duties to service the bonds and maintain a sinking fund.
records.summary_es: The New-York Tribune informó sobre un plan de liquidación de deuda propuesto por el ministro de Hacienda dominicano Velásquez para prorratear los fondos en efectivo depositados en el National City Bank y emitir 16.000.000 de dólares en bonos a cuarenta años al 5 por ciento para los acreedores extranjeros. Al no hallarse ningún sindicato bancario neoyorquino dispuesto a suscribir la liquidación directamente, Velásquez esperaba que los acreedores europeos y estadounidenses —incluida la Santo Domingo Improvement Company— aceptaran el arreglo. El informe señaló que los Estados Unidos continuarían recaudando los derechos aduaneros dominicanos para atender el servicio de los bonos y mantener un fondo de amortización.

records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune reported that the U.S. Secret Service arrested Giordani in New York, uncovering his role as the financial agent of a Haitian revolutionary movement under General Fermin. Giordani had previously contracted the printing of 1,500,000 "Deux Gourdes" banknotes, half of which had been stored in a New York warehouse after an earlier failed uprising. Federal authorities intervened to prevent the remaining currency from being shipped to finance active insurgent forces in Haiti.
records.summary_es: The New-York Tribune informó que el Servicio Secreto de los EE. UU. arrestó a Giordani en Nueva York, descubriendo su papel como agente financiero de un movimiento revolucionario haitiano encabezado por el general Fermin. Giordani había contratado previamente la impresión de 1.500.000 billetes de «Deux Gourdes», la mitad de los cuales se hallaban almacenados en un depósito neoyorquino tras un fracasado levantamiento anterior. Las autoridades federales intervinieron para impedir que el resto del papel moneda fuera despachado para financiar a fuerzas insurgentes activas en Haití.

records.summary_en: The Semi-Weekly Herald reviewed the outcome of the 1905 Dominican customs arrangement instituted by President Roosevelt to avert foreign military intervention over unpaid debts. Despite initial domestic controversy and Senate delays over Roosevelt's executive authority, the system transferred 45 percent of collections to the Dominican government and 55 percent to debt liquidation. The paper noted that the policy achieved a total transformation in the country, stabilizing public finances and virtually eliminating civil insurrections.
records.summary_es: The Semi-Weekly Herald analizó los resultados del arreglo aduanero dominicano de 1905 instituido por el presidente Roosevelt para eludir una intervención militar extranjera por deudas impagas. Pese a la controversia nacional inicial y las demoras en el Senado en torno a las atribuciones ejecutivas de Roosevelt, el sistema transfirió el 45 por ciento de la recaudación al gobierno dominicano y el 55 por ciento a la liquidación de la deuda. El periódico destacó que esta política logró una transformación total en el país, estabilizando las finanzas públicas y eliminando prácticamente las insurrecciones civiles.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star detailed extensive public works and infrastructure projects advancing in the Dominican Republic, including the purchase and expansion of the Puerto Plata-Santiago railroad and new branch lines. The Dominican government reduced port fees, dredged the Ozama River, surveyed irrigation systems in Monte Cristi and Azua, and initiated macadamized highway construction between the capital and San Cristobal. The report lauded the country's economic potential, civic improvements, and the hospitality of its citizens.
records.summary_es: The Evening Star detalló los amplios proyectos de obras públicas e infraestructura que avanzaban en la República Dominicana, incluyendo la adquisición y ampliación del ferrocarril de Puerto Plata a Santiago y nuevos ramales. El gobierno dominicano redujo las tasas portuarias, dragó el río Ozama, realizó estudios para sistemas de irrigación en Monte Cristi y Azua, e inició la construcción de una carretera macadamizada entre la capital y San Cristóbal. El informe alabó el potencial económico del país, sus mejoras urbanas y la hospitalidad de sus habitantes.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star published excerpts from President Taft's message to Congress, reporting that the Dominican customs receivership was operating satisfactorily under the 1907 convention. Taft noted that despite lower customs revenues caused by economic conditions and anticipated tariff revisions, debt service payments were maintained and burdensome private concessions were retired. The message also reviewed U.S. diplomatic interventions regarding corporate claims in Nicaragua and Chile.

El mensaje examinó además las intervenciones diplomáticas estadounidenses relativas a reclamaciones corporativas en Nicaragua y Chile.

records.full_text:
WIPING OUT A REPUBLIC'S DEBT

Honest Administration is Saving Santo Domingo. Honduras Asks for Help

NEW TARIFF LAWS HAVE HELPED COUNTRY

WASHINGTON, Aug. 11—The recent suggestion that this government assume a protectorate over Honduras and enter into a joint protectorate with Great Britian, France and Germany over Liberia, makes a review of this country's protectorate of Santo Domingo of timely interest. It will be recalled that the United States in March, 1905, entered into a treaty with the Dominican Republic to arrange its financial difficulties. The republic owed about $20,000,000, and its foreign creditors were pressing hard. Under a treaty, which the Senate reluctantly ratified, an American collector of customs was appointed for the republic, who received all customs receipts and divided them in the proportion of 45 per cent. for the republic and 55 per cent. for the creditors. Under the old Spanish law, which the Dominican republic never repealed, all expenses of the government are paid them for revenues derived from, imports and exports, property paying no taxes whatever.

In the five years that this government has assumed control of the Dominican custom-houses, the republic's debt has been reduced by $7,000,000 and the government, although receiving only 45 per cent. of the revenues has had more money to expend on administration and on public improvements than ever before when all the receipts went into the national treasury. The reason is not far to seek, for the American administration of the customs is honest. There have been naturally several abortive attempts at revolutions from hungry patriots whose souls shudder at the thought that the country's revenues are going into the country's treasury, but behind the American collector of customs, Mr. W. E. Pulliam, stands the American navy, and the net result of these revolutons has been only a decrease in the population of Santo Domingo, for those revolutionists who are not buried where they fall are safely tucked away in Dominican dungeons.

Result of New Tariff.
So well has Mr. Pulliam administered the revenues of the republic that a year ago last month he submitted a new tariff downward by about 15 per cent. Up to that time the Spanish principal of revenue taxation prevailed—namely, placing the heaviest possible duties on the necessities of life and permitting the luxuries to come in with the lightest possible duty. Mr. Pulliam introduced the American idea of letting the necessities of life come in free of duty, or nearly free, while the burden of taxation rested upon the luxuries. It was stipulated that an annual collection of $2,000,000 must be shown if the new tariff should remain in effect for more than a year. The tariff has now been adopted, and after a few months of a transition period, during which the business men of Santo Domingo adgusted themselves to new conditions, the receipts more than surpassed Mr. Pulliam's expectations. For the past three months the custom receipts have passed each month the quarter-million mark. At this rate the revenues for the current year will be at least $3,000,000, or one million more than the stipulated amount.

With this splended display of what American tariff and honesty will accomplish, it is small wonder that Honduras,, whose foreign creditors are pressing her hard for their money, and that Liberia, which faces dissolution as a republic, have appealed to this country for a similar protectorate. Although the State Department is strongly inclined to accede to both requests, it would be premature to say that the request will be granted. The Senate is bitterly opposed to any more such arrangements, although the example of Santo Domingo is encouraging. In the case of Liberia this country has only a sentimental interest, for Liberia owes its inception to American philanthropists.. It was the legislature of Maryland, whose generous appropriations nearly a century ago founded the Province of Maryland and peopled it with freed men from Maryland. The present republic if Liberia is a development of that settlement, but it is acknowledged on every hand that the republic is a failure. If this country enters into a joint protectorate with Great Britain, France and Germany, it will only mean a postponement of the fatal day.

No more Protectorates.
As for Honduras, a protectorate over that little republic would seem to be a logical corollary of the Monroe Doctrine, but the Senate, as already stated, is so bitterly opposed to any more of these treaties that Secretary Knox is at this moment unable to see his way clear to establishing a protectorate there. The Senate holds that if, following the example in Santo Domingo, this country takes up Honduras, it is only a question of time when an American receiver will be in charge of the customs of every petty republic in Central and South America, a condition not to be regarded with toleration.

records.summary_en: After a border clash near Comendador, the Dominican government is hurrying troops and reinforcements on the American steamer Cherokee, while the Haitian minister has advised his government to withdraw its defeated troops. At San Domingo on December 27, President Ramón Cáceres said his latest advices looked more favorable for a friendly settlement of the boundary dispute with Haiti: he did not wish a conflict, but demanded that his country's rights be respected, and work continued on the government railway intended ultimately to connect the two capitals.

records.summary_en: An unconfirmed report of border trouble led Dominican officials to hold a hasty Cabinet meeting and begin negotiations with the resident Haitian minister in Santo Domingo, while Dominican troops were ordered from various parts of the country to the border; the trouble was attributed to a long-standing dispute over the boundary between the two republics. At Santo Domingo on December 27, President Caceres said his latest advices looked more favorable for a friendly settlement, that he did not wish a conflict, but demanded that his countrys rights be respected, and work continued at the border on the government railway intended ultimately to connect the capitals of Santo Domingo and Haiti.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the Dominican government accused Haitian forces under General Ferdinand of firing on frontier guards at Pedernales, demanding their immediate withdrawal while both nations sent troops to the border. Rumors that American customs collector Marion E. Beale had been killed in the conflict were officially disproved by recent reports received from him by the War Department. Meanwhile, the U.S. naval cruiser *Yankton* arrived at Samana Bay to prepare torpedo practice courses for the Atlantic fleet.

Beale había muerto en el enfrentamiento quedaron desmentidos oficialmente por informes recientes remitidos por él al Departamento de Guerra. records.summary_en: The Yorkville Enquirer commented on Dominican political instability and former President Morales's campaign to regain the presidency by force, arguing that the country needed a strong leader comparable to Mexico's Porfirio Diaz. The article questioned whether Morales could improve upon the incumbent administration or justify plunging the nation into civil war. It noted that if threatened, the Dominican government could invoke a treaty clause originally drafted by Morales himself to request American intervention to protect debt obligations.
records.summary_es: The Yorkville Enquirer comentó sobre la inestabilidad política dominicana y la campaña del expresidente Morales para reconquistar la presidencia por la fuerza, argumentando que el país precisaba de un líder fuerte semejante al mexicano Porfirio Díaz. El artículo cuestionaba si Morales podría mejorar la gestión del gobierno en funciones o justificar que se sumiera a la nación en una guerra civil. Señalaba que, de verse amenazado, el gobierno dominicano podría recurrir a una cláusula del tratado redactada en su momento por el propio Morales para solicitar la intervención estadounidense en salvaguarda de los compromisos de la deuda.

records.summary_en: The Topeka State Journal reported on President Taft's speech defending his foreign policy against critics of "Dollar Diplomacy," advocating pending treaties with Nicaragua and Honduras modeled on the Dominican arrangement. Taft emphasized that American customs collection in Santo Domingo had ensured debt repayments and fostered national reconstruction. He countered Senate objections that such treaties created entangling alliances for American banking interests rather than promoting regional stability.
records.summary_es: The Topeka State Journal informó sobre el discurso del presidente Taft en defensa de su política exterior frente a las críticas a la «diplomacia del dólar», promoviendo los tratados pendientes con Nicaragua y Honduras diseñados bajo el modelo del arreglo dominicano. Taft destacó que la recaudación aduanera estadounidense en Santo Domingo había asegurado la amortización de la deuda y favorecido la reconstrucción nacional. Replicó a las objeciones del Senado que sostenían que tales tratados forjaban alianzas comprometedoras para los intereses de la banca estadounidense en lugar de afianzar la estabilidad regional.

Taft highlighted that 55 percent of customs collections provided unprecedented domestic revenues while 45 percent went toward debt extinction, reducing costly American naval patrols to a minimum. He urged applying the Dominican model to resolve chronic revolutions and financial distress in Honduras and Nicaragua.
records.summary_es: The Topeka State Journal prosiguió con el discurso del presidente Taft, destacando que cinco años de vigencia del tratado en Santo Domingo habían desterrado las insurrecciones al colocar las aduanas bajo amparo estadounidense. Taft subrayó que el 55 por ciento de la recaudación aduanera proveía rentas internas sin precedentes, mientras que el 45 por ciento se destinaba a la cancelación de la deuda, reduciendo al mínimo los costosos patrullajes navales de los EE. UU. Instó a aplicar el modelo dominicano para poner término a las revoluciones crónicas y la angustia fiscal en Honduras y Nicaragua.

records.summary_en: The Daily Kennebec Journal published President Taft's remarks highlighting the financial and political successes of the Dominican customs receivership. Taft reported that honest customs administration ended insurrections, attracted foreign investment, and eliminated the need for costly American naval patrols. He pointed to this Dominican precedent as a proven remedy for neighboring republics suffering from chronic debt and civil strife, specifically Honduras and Nicaragua.

Señaló este precedente dominicano como un remedio comprobado para repúblicas vecinas aquejadas de deudas crónicas y guerras civiles, en particular Honduras y Nicaragua.

Taft underscored that safeguarding customs revenue deprived revolutionists of funding, brought unprecedented revenues to the Dominican treasury, and curtailed U.S. naval spending. Abogó por extender esta estructura administrativa a Honduras y Nicaragua para promover la estabilidad y el crecimiento económico.

records.summary_en: The Salt Lake Tribune reviewed the origin of the 1905 Dominican modus vivendi, crediting former American Minister Thomas C. Dawson with devising the administrative revenue plan. Put into effect on April 1, 1905, the agreement placed customs collection under American officials who distributed funds between the government and foreign creditors. The article observed that civil conflicts ceased almost immediately once revolutionists were unable to seize customs houses and revenues.
records.summary_es: The Salt Lake Tribune examinó el origen del modus vivendi dominicano de 1905, reconociendo al exministro estadounidense Thomas C. Dawson la concepción del plan administrativo de recaudación. Puesto en vigor el 1 de abril de 1905, el acuerdo confió el cobro aduanero a funcionarios estadounidenses que distribuían los fondos entre el gobierno y los acreedores extranjeros. El artículo observó que las guerras civiles cesaron casi de inmediato una vez que los revolucionarios se vieron impedidos de apoderarse de las aduanas y de sus caudales.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star recounted the December 1904 Dominican debt crisis, which culminated in threats of force from European creditors, including the dispatch of an Italian warship. Following the U.S. Senate's failure to ratify an initial 1905 treaty, American Minister Thomas C. Dawson formulated an interim plan to manage customs and reassure foreign powers. The resulting arrangement allowed the Dominican government to dedicate revenue percentages to creditors while guaranteeing impartial financial oversight.
records.summary_es: The Evening Star relató la crisis de la deuda dominicana de diciembre de 1904, la cual culminó con amenazas de uso de la fuerza por parte de acreedores europeos, incluido el envío de un buque de guerra italiano. Tras la falta de ratificación de un tratado inicial por el Senado de los EE. UU. en 1905, el ministro estadounidense Thomas C. Dawson formuló un plan interino para administrar las aduanas y dar garantías a las potencias extranjeras. El acuerdo resultante permitió al gobierno dominicano destinar porcentajes de ingresos a los acreedores garantizando al mismo tiempo una fiscalización financiera imparcial.

records.summary_en: The Salt Lake Tribune discussed political reactions following the assassination of Dominican President Ramon Caceres, noting his past role in killing dictator Ulises Heureaux in 1899. Officials recalled Caceres's rise through cabinet and vice-presidential posts to the presidency in 1905, expressing concern that rival politicians might seize on his death to provoke unrest. The War Department noted that the assassination disrupted an exceptional four-year period of peace in a nation previously plagued by annual revolutions.
records.summary_es: The Salt Lake Tribune analizó las reacciones políticas tras el magnicidio del presidente dominicano Ramón Cáceres, recordando su participación en la muerte del dictador Ulises Heureaux en 1899. Los funcionarios rememoraron el ascenso de Cáceres a través de carteras ministeriales y la vicepresidencia hasta alcanzar la presidencia en 1905, expresando inquietud de que políticos rivales aprovecharan su deceso para provocar alteraciones. El Departamento de Guerra advirtió que el magnicidio truncó un excepcional período de cuatro años de paz en una nación anteriormente asolada por revoluciones anuales.

records.summary_en: The Washington Times reported that the presence of U.S. gunboats *Petrel* and *Nashville* served to deter war between the Dominican Republic and Haiti, with U.S. officials prepared to land marines to protect foreign interests if conflict erupted. Concurrently, customs receivership reports showed robust fiscal health, with June collections reaching $334,791.27 and eleven-month receipts totaling $3,317,973.17. Both import and export duties posted significant annual increases under American supervision.

Al mismo tiempo, los informes de la receptoría aduanera mostraron una sólida salud fiscal, alcanzando la recaudación de junio 334.791,27 dólares y los ingresos de once meses un total de 3.317.973,17 dólares. Tanto los derechos de importación como de exportación registraron considerables aumentos anuales bajo la supervisión estadounidense.

records.summary_en: The Richmond Virginian reported that war appeared imminent between Haiti and the Dominican Republic amid revolutions in both countries, following the assassination of Haiti's President Leconte and rebel capture of the border town Dajabon. Santo Domingo prepared to declare war after hundreds of Haitians allegedly assisted Dominican insurgents, massing 4,000 troops along the border. The region also faced severe agricultural drought and famine, while civil strife escalated concurrently in Nicaragua.
records.summary_es: The Richmond Virginian informó que la guerra parecía inminente entre Haití y la República Dominicana en medio de revoluciones en ambos países, tras la muerte del presidente haitiano Leconte y la toma por los rebeldes de la localidad fronteriza de Dajabón. Santo Domingo se preparaba para declarar la guerra luego de que cientos de haitianos presuntamente auxiliaran a los insurgentes dominicanos, concentrando 4.000 soldados a lo largo de la frontera. La región padecía además una severa sequía agrícola y hambruna, mientras la guerra civil se intensificaba a la par en Nicaragua.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the United States prepared naval assets to safeguard Dominican customs houses against rebel capture, maintaining the gunboat *Petrel* in Santo Domingo harbor with other vessels positioned nearby. A new rebellion broke out in the interior between Puerto Plata and Sanchez, where government forces claimed victory in a recent engagement despite rebel forces remaining intact. Officials anticipated further fighting and prepared to deploy additional warships if necessary.
records.summary_es: The Evening Star informó que los Estados Unidos alistaron medios navales para impedir que los rebeldes tomaran las aduanas dominicanas, manteniendo el cañonero *Petrel* en el puerto de Santo Domingo y otros buques emplazados en las proximidades. Una nueva rebelión estalló en el interior entre Puerto Plata y Sánchez, donde las tropas del gobierno se atribuyeron la victoria en un combate reciente a pesar de que las fuerzas rebeldes permanecían intactas. Las autoridades preveían nuevos enfrentamientos y se preparaban para desplegar buques de guerra adicionales si fuere necesario.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the seizure of Dominican border custom houses by rebels operating near Haiti prompted U.S. officials to consider establishing a formal protectorate. records.full_text:
Mexico, Santo Domingo, Nicaragua.

It appears that the criticism of Senor Didapp, the representative of the Mexican revolutionists in Washington, and former Mexican Consul General to Spain, Turkey, and later at Norfolk, Va., is pretty well founded when, in his public utterances, he criticises Secretary Knox’s “dollar diplomacy,” which he maintains is making a mess of it in all Pan-American affairs, especially so in Mexico and Nicaragua.

As regards the former, Senor Didapp says that, unable to protect American lives and property by showing a firm attitude toward Madero, the department has been forced to the expedient of assisting the Mexican government by allowing Mexican troops to cross American territory in their attempt to get closer to the revolutionists. This, adds the senor, under the rules of international law, is equivalent to a declaration of war against the revolutionists on the part of the United States.

While The Herald believes that he is wrong in this contention, because the Mexican revolutionists are not yet recognized as belligerents by the Powers, yet it is a queer way of upholding the laws of neutrality. If this is considered fair on the part of the United States, then it would hardly be a greater violation of neutrality to throw a few brigades of United States regulars across the Rio Grande for the purpose of re-enforcing the Madero armies.

It would seem, therefore, that there is some ground for the contention of Senor Didapp that our government already has “intervened” when it allowed Mexican troops to cross American soil on their way to attack the revolutionists.

Secretary Knox, while away on a mission which an Assistant Secretary could well have fulfilled, leaves Pan-American affairs in a badly muddled condition, and the question may be permitted what good his recent trip to Central America has accomplished. His peace efforts have made a dismal failure of preserving the peace in Nicaragua.

The object of our proposed treaty with that country has been to authorize the executive branch of the United States government, with the consent of Congress, to intervene in Nicaragua, as it did in Santo Domingo in the alleged interest of the protection of American lives and property and the maintenance of public order. We know what that has meant to the Dominicans. Neither was property protected nor order maintained. The natives were overawed by the aid of the American forces. All debts of that republic, since the year one of its existence, were combined into bonds, and these exchanged for pieces of paper called Dominican-American “guaranteed national bonds.” These bonds have the interest guaranteed by the United States, but not the principal, by the collection of customs moneys.

If seriously looked into it will be found that Americans hold large blocks of the old debts of Nicaragua. The State Department had such an easy time in the Senate in the Dominican intervention deal that it also may have given assurances to Nicaraguan professional patriots with bundles of old scrip. But the Senate balked, because, were the United States to side with one faction against another, it would make it quite uncomfortable for American industrial expansionists.

It looks to The Herald that, when the smoke has cleared away, the United States will be found collecting Nicaraguan customs duties in the interest of American pioneers. This is known as “Dawsonizing the Monroe Doctrine,” for it avoids annexing the republics, while it obliterates them from the map as international factors of discord. Despite the fact that the Senate has refused to sanction the grabbing of a neighboring republic's custom-house, it would seem that those interested in the possibilities of spoil possess sufficient power to have the State Department spread United States marines over Nicaragua interior towns. This is apparently evidenced by the fact, quite palpable, that a battalion of American marines had been dispatched to Granada, which is not on the line of communication between Washington and Minister Weitzel, in order to rescue some girls alleged to be held in a French college.

What we should like to know is what these girls, this purely domestic affair, have to do with the Nicaraguan question?

records.summary_en: The Washington Herald reported that U.S. Commissioners Doyle and McIntyre were sent with marines to re-establish Dominican border custom houses and protect personnel under the 1907 treaty. The report reviewed the convention's financial terms, which scaled public debt to $17,000,000 and issued $20,000,000 in bonds through New York trusts. Increased customs revenues under American administration had enabled annual principal payments to reach $400,000, well above required minimums.

El incremento de las rentas aduaneras bajo la gestión estadounidense había permitido que las amortizaciones anuales de capital alcanzaran los 400.000 dólares, muy por encima de los mínimos requeridos.

records.summary_en: The Birmingham Age-Herald reported that Insular Bureau Chief Frank McIntyre and William Doyle sailed on the transport *Prairie* with marines to inspect the Dominican frontier and reopen four customs stations closed by insurgents. Authorities declared that military force would be utilized if necessary to uphold customs obligations under the 1907 Dawson treaty, with troops prepared to march inland from coastal landings. U.S. officials expressed hope that the show of force would compel rebels to abandon the posts without bloodshed.

Las autoridades declararon que se recurriría a la fuerza armada si resultaba indispensable para hacer cumplir los compromisos aduaneros del tratado Dawson de 1907, con efectivos listos para avanzar tierra adentro tras los desembarcos costeros. Los funcionarios estadounidenses manifestaron su confianza en que la demostración de fuerza obligaría a los rebeldes a desalojar los puestos sin derramamiento de sangre.

records.summary_en: The Sun reported that American commissioners investigating Santo Domingo found widespread corruption and treaty violations under the unpopular Victoria administration. The commissioners reported that public funds had been misappropriated, illicit debts incurred, and government employees left unpaid while border custom houses were forced shut. The United States demanded an immediate administrative cleanup and the reopening of frontier customs posts, holding marines in readiness to provide protection.
records.summary_es: The Sun informó que los comisionados estadounidenses que investigaban en Santo Domingo constataron una corrupción generalizada y violaciones de los tratados bajo la impopular administración de Victoria. Los comisionados denunciaron que se habían malversado caudales públicos, contraído deudas ilícitas y dejado sin salario a los empleados públicos, al tiempo que se clausuraban a la fuerza las aduanas de la frontera. Los Estados Unidos exigieron un saneamiento administrativo inmediato y la reapertura de las receptorías fronterizas, manteniendo a los infantes de marina en alerta para brindar protección.

records.summary_en: The Sun reported on the appointment of Walter W. Vick as general receiver of Dominican customs, emphasizing the requirement that he maintain strict political neutrality. The article credited the American receivership with securing revenues from aspiring revolutionists and providing seven years of uninterrupted domestic peace until disturbances resumed in 1912. Vick's mandate was to preserve the integrity and security of customs collections across all contending political factions.

La misión de Vick consistía en preservar la integridad y seguridad de la recaudación de aduanas frente a todas las facciones políticas en pugna.

records.headline: Colonel Harry Betancourt, who served under the anti-government banner, recounts the machete cavalry charge at the…
records.summary_en: Colonel Harry Betancourt, who served under the anti-government banner, recounts the machete cavalry charge at the battle of La Vega, where about a hundred men on each side, half-clad rebels with spurs strapped to naked ankles, fought hand to hand with cane knives in place of sabres. He says seventy-five per cent of the combatants on either side were killed or disabled, that he was the only United States citizen holding a command, and that three battles were fought that day around La Vega, with an interval of two hours between each.
records.summary_es: El coronel Harry Betancourt, que sirvió bajo la bandera antigubernamental, relata la carga de caballería con machetes en la batalla de La Vega, donde unos cien hombres de cada bando, rebeldes semidesnudos con espuelas atadas a los tobillos descalzos, lucharon cuerpo a cuerpo con cuchillos de caña en lugar de sables. Dice que el setenta y cinco por ciento de los combatientes de cada bando resultaron muertos o incapacitados, que él fue el único ciudadano de los Estados Unidos con un mando, y que ese día se libraron tres batallas alrededor de La Vega, con un intervalo de dos horas entre cada una.

Sullivan recibió instrucciones de proteger las aduanas bajo control estadounidense, respaldado por el crucero *Des Moines*, que llegó a Puerto Plata preparado para desembarcar infantes de marina. records.summary_en: The Sun reported that President Wilson adopted a firm policy against Dominican revolutionists in Puerto Plata, viewing their rebellion against President Bordas as driven merely by a quest for government offices and revenue. Backed by the cruiser Des Moines, Minister Sullivan warned insurgent leaders that Washington would refuse to recognize insurgent regimes or disburse customs funds to them. U.S. officials believed that withholding customs revenue served as a decisive weapon to end Caribbean insurrections.

Con el respaldo del crucero *Des Moines*, el ministro Sullivan advirtió a los jefes insurgentes que Washington se negaría a reconocer regímenes rebeldes o a entregarles caudales de las aduanas. Los diplomáticos estadounidenses consideraban que la retención de los ingresos aduaneros constituía un arma decisiva para sofocar las rebeliones en el Caribe.

Sullivan has induced the warring factions to sign a pact, ending the revolution led by General Horacio Vasquez against Provisional President Jose Bordas Valdes. Sullivan announced that in future any uprising will be stamped out as criminal, with the United States Government supporting the constitutional authority, and that the remedy for future grievances lies in the free ballot.

records.summary_en: American minister Mr. Sullivan announced that force of arms could never again settle a question in the Dominican Republic, that future uprisings would be stamped out as criminal, that the United States would support the constitutional authority, and that grievances should be remedied by the free ballot at a future election, a policy the paper says was accepted joyously by all parties. After the last battle on October 2, when government forces near Puerto Plata attacked the rebels, Commander Louis M. Nulton of the Nashville and customs receiver Walter W. Vick helped bring the deadlocked peace commissions to Santo Domingo City, where a final agreement was reached on Tuesday evening at a conference Sullivan attended.
records.summary_es: El ministro estadounidense Sullivan anunció que la fuerza de las armas nunca más podría resolver una cuestión en la República Dominicana, que los futuros levantamientos serían reprimidos como criminales, que los Estados Unidos apoyarían a la autoridad constitucional y que las quejas deberían remediarse con el voto libre en una elección futura, una política que, según el diario, fue aceptada con júbilo por todos los partidos. Tras la última batalla, el 2 de octubre, cuando fuerzas del gobierno cerca de Puerto Plata atacaron a los rebeldes, el comandante Louis M. Nulton, del Nashville, y el receptor general de aduanas Walter W. Vick ayudaron a traer a la ciudad de Santo Domingo a las comisiones de paz estancadas, donde el martes por la noche se alcanzó un acuerdo final en una conferencia a la que asistió Sullivan.

records.summary_en: The Daily Missoulian reported that U.S. Minister Sullivan brokered a peace settlement between the Dominican government and northern insurgents, proclaiming that armed rebellion would no longer be tolerated and constitutional changes must occur via the ballot. After initial talks deadlocked at Puerto Plata following an October 2 clash, Commander Nulton of the Nashville and Customs Receiver Vick transported negotiating teams to Santo Domingo City. The ensuing conference produced a final peace agreement that averted further bloodshed.
records.summary_es: The Daily Missoulian informó que el ministro de los EE. UU. Sullivan concertó un acuerdo de paz entre el gobierno dominicano y los insurgentes del norte, proclamando que las sublevaciones armadas no se tolerarían más y que los cambios constitucionales debían efectuarse a través de las urnas. Luego de que las conversaciones iniciales se empantanaran en Puerto Plata a raíz de un combate el 2 de octubre, el comandante Nulton del *Nashville* y el receptor aduanero Vick trasladaron a las comisiones negociadoras a la ciudad de Santo Domingo. La conferencia subsiguiente culminó en un acuerdo definitivo de paz que impidió mayores derramamientos de sangre.

records.summary_en: The Raymer Enterprise reviewed the history of the Dominican customs receivership, noting that removing customs revenues from political grasp had ended chronic revolutions and established domestic peace between 1905 and 1912. The article recalled that President Roosevelt intervened in 1905 to prevent European creditor nations from seizing Dominican customs to collect $20,000,000 in defaulted debts. Newly appointed Receiver Walter W. Vick was charged with maintaining strict administrative neutrality and safeguarding revenue security.
records.summary_es: The Raymer Enterprise repasó la trayectoria de la receptoría de aduanas dominicana, destacando que sustraer los caudales aduaneros de la codicia política había suprimido las revoluciones crónicas e instaurado la paz interna entre 1905 y 1912. El artículo recordó que el presidente Roosevelt intervino en 1905 para evitar que las potencias acreedoras europeas se apoderaran de las aduanas dominicanas para cobrar 20.000.000 de dólares en deudas morosas. El recién designado receptor Walter W. Vick tenía por misión preservar una rigurosa neutralidad administrativa y resguardar los fondos fiscales.

Following a battle on October 2, Commander Nulton of the Nashville and Receiver Walter W. Vick transported deadlocked peace envoys from Puerto Plata to Santo Domingo City. Negotiations at the capital concluded with a comprehensive peace accord accepted by all factions.

Vick trasladaron desde Puerto Plata a la ciudad de Santo Domingo a los delegados de paz cuyas gestiones se hallaban trabadas. records.headline: This article explains that the United States government is the custodian of the Dominican revenues under a treaty,…
records.summary_en: This article explains that the United States government is the custodian of the Dominican revenues under a treaty, standing sponsor for the conservation of the public funds and the settlement of the republic's debts, and that President Wilson appointed Mr. Vick to administer the receivership, his salary of $6,500 a year being paid by the Dominican government. It says the removal of the customs revenues to neutral hands gave Santo Domingo its first long period of freedom from revolution, from 1905 to 1912, and recounts how European creditors in 1904 demanded settlement of a debt of about $30,000,000, leading to the modus vivendi, the treaty that took effect on July 8, 1907, and a $20,000,000 bond issue.
records.summary_es: Este artículo explica que el gobierno de los Estados Unidos es el custodio de los ingresos dominicanos en virtud de un tratado, garante de la conservación de los fondos públicos y del arreglo de las deudas de la república, y que el presidente Wilson nombró al señor Vick para administrar la receptoría, con un sueldo de 6.500 dólares al año pagado por el gobierno dominicano. Dice que el traslado de los ingresos aduaneros a manos neutrales dio a Santo Domingo su primer largo período sin revoluciones, de 1905 a 1912, y cuenta cómo los acreedores europeos exigieron en 1904 el arreglo de una deuda de unos 30.000.000 de dólares, lo que llevó al modus vivendi, al tratado que entró en vigor el 8 de julio de 1907 y a una emisión de bonos de 20.000.000 de dólares.

Sullivan facilitated the end of civil conflict and secured commitments for free elections and civil liberties. A forthcoming constitutional convention planned to enact reforms and select a new president through the ballot. The article also provided a cultural and historical overview of the Dominican Republic, noting its Spanish heritage and multiracial population.

Una próxima asamblea constituyente contemplaba sancionar reformas y designar un nuevo mandatario por sufragio. El artículo ofreció además un compendio cultural e histórico de la República Dominicana, aludiendo a su legado hispánico y su población mestiza.

records.summary_en: The U.S. gunboat had lately used her main battery of four-inch guns to silence President Bordas's batteries, which were bombarding the rebel garrison holding the city in violation of the agreement that the lives of foreigners and other non-combatants would not be endangered by artillery fire. A junta commission of legalistas, representing the revolutionists, boarded the vessel and gave assurances of their desire to avoid endangering the safety of Americans, after scattering rebel rifle fire had passed over the ship and some shots struck her. A cable report said Santo Domingo City was still besieged by rebels and that other towns had joined the revolutionist cause, with four separate revolutions raging in the country.

Una comisión de la junta de los legalistas, en representación de los revolucionarios, abordó el buque y dio garantías de su deseo de no poner en peligro la seguridad de los estadounidenses, después de que disparos dispersos de fusilería rebelde pasaron sobre el barco y algunos lo alcanzaron. Un informe por cable decía que la ciudad de Santo Domingo seguía sitiada por los rebeldes y que otras poblaciones se habían sumado a la causa revolucionaria, con cuatro revoluciones distintas en el país.

records.summary_en: The Sentinel-Record reported that the Dominican Republic was descending into chaos with four concurrent revolutions, leaving President Bordas unable to suppress insurgents despite maintaining power through extra-constitutional decrees. Fighting disrupted multiple regions, including Azua, where the national navy destroyed the custom house, and La Romana, where American sugar estates requested protection. With Customs Collector Vick resigned and Minister Sullivan returning to the United States, Washington faced mounting pressure to intervene directly.

Los combates desestabilizaban numerosas zonas, entre ellas Azua, donde la marina de guerra nacional destruyó la aduana, y La Romana, donde centrales azucareros estadounidenses demandaban resguardo. Con la renuncia del recaudador aduanero Vick y el regreso del ministro Sullivan a los Estados Unidos, Washington afrontaba una creciente presión para intervenir en forma directa.

records.summary_en: The Arizona Republican reported that four simultaneous insurrections had paralyzed Santo Domingo, where President Bordas remained entrenched via American customs distributions but could not defeat widespread rebel forces. American Collector Vick resigned and Minister Sullivan departed for the United States, leaving the legation under a secretary while the State Department weighed appointing a special mediator rather than intervening by force. Meanwhile, a substantial U.S. naval squadron—including the South Carolina, Machias, Marietta, and Castine—patrolled Dominican harbors.

El recaudador estadounidense Vick renunció y el ministro Sullivan partió rumbo a los Estados Unidos, quedando la legación a cargo de un secretario mientras el Departamento de Estado consideraba designar un mediador especial en vez de intervenir militarmente. Entretanto, una importante escuadra naval de los EE. UU. —que integraba al *South Carolina*, *Machias*, *Marietta* y *Castine*— patrullaba las bahías dominicanas.

records.summary_en: The Montgomery Advertiser reported widespread insurrections across the Dominican Republic, including uprisings at Azua, Monte Cristi, and La Romana, where American plantation owners requested State Department protection. President Bordas remained gridlocked against insurgent forces despite ruling through decree and receiving customs funding. With Minister Sullivan and Collector Vick stepping down, the U.S. government remained hesitant to deploy force, considering instead sending a prominent mediator to reconcile the factions.

El presidente Bordas se mantenía empantanado contra las fuerzas insurgentes no obstante gobernar por decreto y recibir caudales de aduana. Con la renuncia del ministro Sullivan y del recaudador Vick, el gobierno de los EE. UU. vacilaba en recurrir a las armas, evaluando en su lugar el envío de un destacado mediador para aproximar a las facciones.

records.summary_en: The New Hampshire Farmer and Weekly Union contrasted unrest in the Caribbean, noting that while Dominican disturbances were likely to prompt U.S. armed intervention, the country presented fewer military and diplomatic difficulties than neighboring Haiti. European nations maintained smaller financial interests in Santo Domingo, whereas Haitian instability threatened foreign defaults. The Wilson administration sought guarantees that Haitian customs revenues would be managed to satisfy foreign debts in a manner analogous to the Dominican receivership.
records.summary_es: The New Hampshire Farmer and Weekly Union contrastó las revueltas en el Caribe, observando que, si bien era probable que las perturbaciones dominicanas provocaran una intervención militar estadounidense, dicho país planteaba menores dificultades bélicas y diplomáticas que el vecino Haití. Las naciones europeas conservaban intereses financieros más reducidos en Santo Domingo, al tiempo que la inestabilidad haitiana ponía en riesgo moratorias con el exterior. La administración Wilson demandaba garantías de que los ingresos de las aduanas de Haití fueran administrados para cancelar deudas foráneas de modo análogo a la receptoría dominicana.
