records.full_text:
'INSIDE INFORMATION' AT SULLIVAN PROBE

Revelations Made by Harry J. Overman, Brother of Senator From South Carolina.

Inside information as to the influences at work on the appointment of American representatives in the Dominican government was brought out yesterday at the first session of the Sullivan hearing here.

Harry J. Overman, file clerk in the office of the Secretary of the Senate and a brother of Senator Lea S. Overman of North Carolina, testified concerning his efforts to obtain appointment as deputy receiver of customs at Santo Domingo under the treaty relations between the Dominican republic and the United States. He declared that he had been urged to apply for the place by a man named Gold, who, he said, suggested that William C. Beer would be a good person to support him for the place. Beer, he said he was told by Gold, could influence Secretary of State Bryan through John H. Grey, of Wilmington, Del.

Md. Overman testified that inasmuch as his own brother was unwilling to use his position to further his candidacy he was compelled to do much of the work himself. He said that he had met Mr. Beer at a hotel in Washington in company with Minister Sullivan.

John E. Osborne, First Assistant Secretary of State, stated that prior to the appointment of Mr. Sullivan, he had gone to Haiti and Santo Domingo on a secret mission for the Government. While there, he stated, he had warned the Dominican government against increasing its indebtedness.

Regarding the Sullivan case, Secretary Osborne said that he knew practically nothing except that he had received personal letters from Mr. Vick, criticising the conduct of the minister.

Others who were present were Joseph P. Tumulty, Secretary to the President; Assistant Secretary of State, Philips; Assistant Secretary of War Breckenridge, and Brigadier General McIntyre, chief of the Bureau of Insular Affairs, War Department.

At the outset of today's session Charles H. Strong, attorney, conducting the examination for Comimssioner Phelan, announced that the entire scope of the investigation was to inquire into the fitness, competence, and conduct of Minister Sullivan.

“The Commissioner intends,” he said, “to run down any legitimate clue bearing on this case without fear or favor for anybody in or out of public office. He means to sift the case to the bottom. Necessarily, inasmuch as the lines upon which this investigation is being conducted are wholly different from court procedure, much hearsay testimony, or even gossip, must creep into the evidence. But as a result of this hearsay evidence we have already been able to unearth things of the utmost importance.”

records.summary_en: The Daily Kennebec Journal reported that former Customs Receiver Walter W. Vick testified that Minister James M. Sullivan improperly attempted to negotiate an unauthorized $500,000 bank loan for the Dominican government. Vick presented a letter from Sullivan to Dominican banks proposing the loan without the sanction of the State Department or the Dominican Congress. The proposed borrowing provoked protests from Dominican legislative leaders until an outbreak of revolution halted the negotiations.

Vick exhibió una carta dirigida por Sullivan a instituciones bancarias dominicanas en la que planteaba el empréstito sin la aprobación del Departamento de Estado ni del Congreso dominicano. El proyectado crédito suscitó reclamos de los dirigentes legislativos dominicanos hasta que el estallido de la revolución frenó las negociaciones.

Sullivan secretly solicited a $500,000 loan from Dominican banks, falsely claiming U.S. approval to raise the republic's debt limit. Vick produced correspondence indicating Sullivan offered Dominican bonds as security without authorization from Washington or the Dominican Congress. Vick also defended his own record against personal countercharges raised during the official inquiry into Sullivan's diplomatic fitness.

Vick defendió además su propia gestión frente a imputaciones personales formuladas en la investigación oficial sobre la idoneidad diplomática de Sullivan.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported testimony from presidential secretary Joseph P. Tumulty regarding the inquiry into Dominican Minister James M. Sullivan. Tumulty stated he had instructed Customs Receiver Vick to monitor Sullivan following allegations concerning the Banco Nacional and commercial interests, denying that the White House had ever whitewashed the diplomat. While describing Dominican politics as filled with recrimination, Tumulty defended the administration's scrutiny and dismissed personal criticisms between Vick and Sullivan.

Sullivan solicited an unauthorized $500,000 loan from local banks for the Dominican government. La iniciativa de endeudamiento fracasó ante la enérgica oposición de los líderes del Congreso dominicano y el estallido de la insurrección armada.

records.summary_en: The Springfield Weekly Republican reported on ongoing proceedings in the Phelan investigation into Minister James M. Sullivan, reviewing personal debts and legal judgments submitted into the record alongside testimonials on his behalf. State Department investigator Harry S. Dickey and former Vice Consul Charles H. Albrecht praised Sullivan's diplomatic rapport, attributing the controversy to personal hostility from former Receiver Walter W. Vick. Representative Hamill also testified, denying any connection to commercial interests in advocating for Sullivan's appointment.

Dickey y el exvicecónsul Charles H. Albrecht elogiaron el trato diplomático de Sullivan, atribuyendo la polémica a la hostilidad personal del exreceptor Walter W. Vick. El representante Hamill también prestó declaración, negando todo vínculo con intereses comerciales al promover la designación de Sullivan.

records.summary_en: The Bridgeport Evening Farmer reported that a violent mob stormed the Dominican consulate in Port-au-Prince, dragging out Haitian General Oscar—who had sought refuge there following palace clashes and the execution of political prisoners—and shooting him dead. The crowd also besieged the French legation, where Haitian President Guillaume had fled after rebels damaged the executive mansion. In response to the breakdown of order, the U.S. cruiser *Washington*, carrying Rear Admiral Caperton and an expeditionary marine force, sailed to intervene.

La multitud sitió también la legación francesa, donde se había refugiado el presidente haitiano Guillaume tras los destrozos causados por los rebeldes en la mansión ejecutiva. Ante el quebranto del orden, el crucero de los EE. UU. *Washington*, con el contralmirante Caperton y una fuerza expedicionaria de infantería de marina a bordo, zarpó para intervenir.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that a mob breached the Dominican legation in Port-au-Prince and executed General Oscar in retribution for his mass killings of political prisoners during a rebel assault on the presidential palace. His corpse remained outside the Dominican mission while demonstrators threatened to storm the French legation to capture fleeing President Guillaume. U.S. Rear Admiral Caperton sailed aboard the cruiser *Washington* with an expeditionary force of marines and sailors to restore security in the Haitian capital.
records.summary_es: The Evening Star informó que una turba asaltó la legación dominicana en Puerto Príncipe y ejecutó al general Oscar en represalia por la matanza indiscriminada de prisioneros políticos durante un asalto rebelde al palacio presidencial. Su cadáver quedó tendido frente a la misión dominicana mientras los manifestantes amenazaban con irrumpir en la delegación de Francia para apresar al presidente en fuga Guillaume. El contralmirante de los EE. UU. Caperton zarpó a bordo del crucero *Washington* con un contingente expedicionario de infantes de marina y marineros para restablecer la seguridad en la capital haitiana.

records.summary_en: The Barre Daily Times reported that American marines established guards in Port-au-Prince following the mob murder of President Guillaume after his removal from the French legation. Prior to the uprising, special commissioner Paul Fuller Jr. reported to President Wilson that Guillaume refused to sign a treaty establishing an American customs receivership out of fear of public revolt. The article noted that the United States had sought to establish financial control in Haiti modeled directly on its Dominican customs administration.

El artículo hizo notar que los Estados Unidos habían pretendido instituir un control financiero sobre Haití calcado del modelo de su administración aduanera en la República Dominicana.

records.summary_en: The Sun commented on chronic instability in Haiti and Santo Domingo, asserting that recurring revolutions over twenty years had cost the United States more in naval patrols and interventions than direct administrative control would have required. The article stated that constant strife had depressed population numbers and blocked foreign capital from developing the island's fertile resources. It noted that the Monroe Doctrine had repeatedly blocked European powers from intervening to impose order, leaving the island underdeveloped.

El artículo sostenía que la pugna ininterrumpida había mermado el crecimiento demográfico e impedido la afluencia de capital extranjero para el aprovechamiento de los fértiles recursos insulares. Hizo notar que la Doctrina Monroe había impedido repetidamente a las potencias europeas intervenir para imponer el orden, sumiendo a la isla en el atraso.

records.summary_en: The Washington Herald reported that a Haitian rebel commander fled toward Monte Cristi in the Dominican Republic to recruit men and procure arms, raising concerns of renewed destabilization along the border. Officials noted rising unrest and riots within Santo Domingo, where a compromise coalition government instituted under U.S. auspices was widely regarded as failing. American naval forces faced strain, having withdrawn the cruiser *Nashville* from Dominican waters to handle military operations and disarmament efforts in Haiti.
records.summary_es: The Washington Herald informó que un jefe insurgente haitiano huyó en dirección a Monte Cristi, en la República Dominicana, para reclutar partidarios y obtener armamento, desatando la alarma ante una nueva alteración en la línea fronteriza. Los funcionarios observaron una creciente conmoción y disturbios en Santo Domingo, donde se consideraba un fracaso el gobierno de concertación auspiciado por los Estados Unidos. La fuerza naval estadounidense se veía exigida tras haber retirado el crucero *Nashville* de aguas dominicanas para atender las operaciones castrenses y de desarme en Haití.

records.headline: A feature on the Dominican Republic describes the capital's social life, with its clubs, Club Union and Casino de la…
records.summary_en: A feature on the Dominican Republic describes the capital's social life, with its clubs, Club Union and Casino de la Juventud, and frequent entertainments, and says automobiles are plentiful, with the ride from the capital to San Cristobal along the new macadam boulevard most attractive at four dollars an hour. It notes several hotels, of which the Hotel Francis is the best known, a large foreign colony at the capital and in Macoris and Puerto Plata, a trip of about eight or nine days from New York, and a healthy climate with no serious epidemic since the cholera outbreak of the early sixties.
records.summary_es: Un reportaje sobre la República Dominicana describe la vida social de la capital, con sus clubes, el Club Union y el Casino de la Juventud, y sus frecuentes entretenimientos, y dice que los automóviles son abundantes, y que el paseo desde la capital hasta San Cristobal por el nuevo bulevar de macadán es muy atractivo a cuatro dólares la hora. Menciona varios hoteles, de los cuales el Hotel Francis es el más conocido, una numerosa colonia extranjera en la capital y en Macoris y Puerto Plata, un viaje de unos ocho o nueve días desde Nueva York, y un clima saludable sin ninguna epidemia grave desde el brote de cólera de principios de los años sesenta.

records.headline: This descriptive feature presents Santo Domingo City, the capital, seventy miles from La Romana and forty from…
records.summary_en: This descriptive feature presents Santo Domingo City, the capital, seventy miles from La Romana and forty from Macoris, as a place of modern life amid relics of the fifteenth century, including the ruins of the first church, San Nicolas, the bones Dominicans claim are those of Christopher Columbus in the cathedral, and the ruins of the house of Diego Colon, his son. It describes the city on the west bank of the Ozama river, its macadam boulevard, the ruins of Fort San Geronimo, its two clubs, hotels and plentiful automobiles, its large foreign colony, and argues that, contrary to a common impression, the climate of Santo Domingo is healthy.

Describe la ciudad en la orilla occidental del río Ozama, su bulevar de macadán, las ruinas del fuerte San Gerónimo, sus dos clubes, hoteles y abundantes automóviles, su numerosa colonia extranjera, y sostiene que, contra una impresión común, el clima de Santo Domingo es saludable.

records.summary_en: The Evening Public Ledger reported that Rear Admiral Caperton was authorized to use military force, including landing marines and bluejackets, to maintain the constitutional government of Dominican President Juan Isidro Jimenes. Washington warned Dominican officials that it viewed congressional impeachment proceedings against Jimenes as a veiled revolutionary plot, granting him an eight-day respite to reply. The excerpt also detailed a concurrent constitutional clash in Haiti, where Caperton backed President Dartiguenave against a rebellious parliament.

Washington advirtió a las autoridades dominicanas que consideraba el juicio político iniciado en el Congreso contra Jimenes como una conjura revolucionaria encubierta, otorgándole un plazo de ocho días para responder. El pasaje dio cuenta también del coetáneo choque constitucional en Haití, donde Caperton respaldaba al presidente Dartiguenave frente a un parlamento díscolo.

records.summary_en: American marines, fully equipped, were landed on the outskirts of Santo Domingo City, first from the cruiser Prairie to protect the American legation after disorders in which several persons were killed or wounded. Advices said the serious situation caused by hostilities between the factions of President Jimenes and General Arias had become quiet after Jimenes resigned, a step he took to prevent threatened armed intervention by the United States. Five additional destroyers and the supply ship Panther were to sail for the Dominican Republic, and the French armored cruiser Marseillaise had arrived in port.
records.summary_es: Infantes de marina estadounidenses, con equipo completo, desembarcaron en las afueras de la ciudad de Santo Domingo, primero desde el crucero Prairie para proteger la legación estadounidense tras desórdenes en los que varias personas murieron o resultaron heridas. Los informes decían que la grave situación causada por las hostilidades entre las facciones del presidente Jimenes y el general Arias se había calmado después de que Jimenes dimitiera, paso que dio para evitar la amenazada intervención armada de Estados Unidos. Cinco destructores adicionales y el buque de abastecimiento Panther debían zarpar hacia la República Dominicana, y el crucero acorazado francés Marseillaise había llegado a puerto.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield weekly Republican* reported that American forces under Rear Admiral Caperton occupied Santo Domingo and were being distributed across the republic to maintain order. The marine patrol was intended as a preliminary step toward establishing an American-led native constabulary, similar to arrangements under the Haitian treaty. The State Department also announced that it would refuse to recognize the election of Federico H. Carvajal as valid.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield weekly Republican* informó que las tropas estadounidenses al mando del contralmirante Caperton ocuparon Santo Domingo y estaban siendo distribuidas por toda la república para preservar el orden. Las patrullas de infantería de marina representaban el paso previo al establecimiento de una guardia nacional nativa comandada por oficiales estadounidenses, a semejanza de lo dispuesto en el tratado suscrito con Haití. El Departamento de Estado anunció además su negativa a otorgar validez a la elección de Francisco Henríquez y Carvajal (citado como Federico H. Carvajal).

records.summary_en: In a letter to The Sun, a writer signing himself as one who was at Vera Cruz protests that the American press gave only a few lines to the death of a Marine captain killed while landing with his company near Puerto Plata. He contrasts that neglect with the space British papers give their fallen officers, and notes that a regiment of marines is now on its way from the Pacific coast to Santo Domingo.

records.headline: This feature calls the Dominican Republic, and indeed the whole island, naturally one of the richest spots in the…
records.summary_en: This feature calls the Dominican Republic, and indeed the whole island, naturally one of the richest spots in the world, with remarkably fertile soil: cotton near Monte Cristi backed by American and English capital, Puerto Plata linked by railway to the cacao and tobacco towns of the Cibao, Samana Bay with the town of Samana and the port of Sanchez, and San Pedro de Macoris as the sugar port, where thousands of acres of cane and millions of dollars of American capital are worked with modern machinery. It also tours the capital's relics, including the ruins of the first church of San Nicolas, the bones Dominicans claim are those of Christopher Columbus, and the ruins of the house of Diego Colon.
records.summary_es: Esta crónica califica a la República Dominicana, y en verdad a toda la isla, como naturalmente uno de los lugares más ricos del mundo, con un suelo notablemente fértil: algodón cerca de Monte Cristi respaldado por capital estadounidense e inglés, Puerto Plata unida por ferrocarril a las ciudades del Cibao productoras de cacao y tabaco, la bahía de Samaná con la ciudad de Samaná y el puerto de Sánchez, y San Pedro de Macorís como puerto azucarero, donde se trabajan miles de acres de caña y millones de dólares de capital estadounidense con maquinaria moderna. Recorre también las reliquias de la capital, incluidas las ruinas de la primera iglesia de San Nicolás, los huesos que los dominicanos afirman que son los de Cristóbal Colón y las ruinas de la casa de Diego Colón.

records.headline: But after six or seven years of peace trouble broke out
records.summary_en: The *Perth Amboy evening news* reported on U.S. intervention in Santo Domingo, stating that severe unrest in 1914 and 1915 forced the United States to deploy marines and warships to restore quiet. The article asserted that Dominicans reluctantly accepted external peace enforced under the Monroe Doctrine after customs administration alone failed to prevent renewed revolutions. It characterized the military interventions in Santo Domingo, Haiti, and Nicaragua as costly, altruistic sacrifices made for regional security rather than territorial gain.
records.summary_es: El *Perth Amboy evening news* informó sobre la intervención de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo, indicando que los graves disturbios acaecidos en 1914 y 1915 obligaron a Washington a movilizar infantes de marina y escuadras navales para restaurar la calma. El artículo aseveraba que la población dominicana aceptaba a regañadientes una paz exterior impuesta al amparo de la Doctrina Monroe, luego de que la sola administración aduanera resultara ineficaz para evitar la reaparición de revueltas. Calificaba los desembarcos militares en Santo Domingo, Haití y Nicaragua como sacrificios onerosos y altruistas en favor de la seguridad continental antes que en búsqueda de engrandecimiento territorial.

records.summary_en: The *Ogden standard* reported that Captain Knapp was dispatched to Dominican waters with instructions to institute military rule following the overthrow of President Jiminez by General Arias. Because the United States refused to recognize the administration of Frederico Henriquez, customs revenues had been withheld, leaving native officials unpaid until American officers began disbursing $600,000 in accumulated export duties on December 2. Secretary Daniels emphasized that the military administration would not infringe on civil rights and that Dominican courts would continue to administer municipal laws.
records.summary_es: El *Ogden standard* informó que el capitán Knapp fue despachado a aguas dominicanas con instrucciones de instaurar un régimen militar tras el derrocamiento del presidente Jimenes a manos del general Arias. Debido a que los Estados Unidos no reconocieron el gobierno de Francisco Henríquez y Carvajal (mencionado como Frederico Henriquez), los caudales aduaneros fueron retenidos, quedando sin sueldo los funcionarios del país hasta que los oficiales estadounidenses comenzaron a desembolsar el 2 de diciembre 600.000 dólares en derechos de exportación retenidos. El secretario Daniels enfatizó que el régimen castrense no conculcaría las libertades cívicas y que los tribunales dominicanos seguirían aplicando las leyes locales.

records.headline: Under the military government put into effect by Captain Knapp's proclamation
records.summary_en: The *Presbyterian of the South* reported that Captain Knapp established a military government in Santo Domingo following the overthrow of President Jiminez and Washington's refusal to recognize Frederico Enriquez. Under Knapp's proclamation, the military administration guaranteed monthly loan payments to the Guaranty Trust Company of New York and the payment of salaries for Dominican officials. Secretary Daniels noted that the 1,800 marines would enforce order without infringing upon Dominican civil rights or regular judicial processes.
records.summary_es: El *Presbyterian of the South* informó que el capitán Knapp constituyó un gobierno militar en Santo Domingo tras la deposición del presidente Jimenes y el desconocimiento de Washington hacia Francisco Henríquez y Carvajal (citado como Frederico Enriquez). Mediante la proclama de Knapp, la administración castrense garantizaba los abonos mensuales del empréstito a la Guaranty Trust Company de Nueva York y la cancelación de sueldos a los servidores públicos dominicanos. El secretario Daniels indicó que los 1.800 soldados de infantería de marina mantendrían el orden sin quebrantar las garantías cívicas dominicanas ni el curso procesal ordinario.

records.summary_en: The *New Hampshire farmer and weekly union* reported that Captain Knapp assumed control of the Dominican government under instructions formulated with Minister Russell following the overthrow of President Jiminez by General Arias. Because the United States refused to recognize Frederico Enriquez, customs revenues were withheld until American officers began disbursing $600,000 in accumulated export duties on December 2. records.summary_en: The *Pinedale roundup* reported that the U.S. Navy proclaimed military rule in Santo Domingo to quell political chaos and establish a financial and police protectorate similar to that in Haiti. records.summary_en: The *Norwich bulletin* recounted the chronic political instability and recurring civil wars in Santo Domingo that left the republic heavily indebted to foreign creditors. When foreign warships threatened bombardment to enforce debt claims, Dominican authorities entered into an agreement with the United States in 1905 to take over the collection of customs. Under this treaty, American authorities restructured the nation's tariffs to tax luxuries and guaranteed payments to satisfy European claims.
records.summary_es: El *Norwich bulletin* rememoró la crónica inestabilidad política y las constantes guerras civiles en Santo Domingo que abocaron a la república a un pesado endeudamiento con acreedores extranjeros. Al amenazar cañoneros extranjeros con bombardear los puertos para hacer efectivas sus reclamaciones, las autoridades dominicanas celebraron un acuerdo con los Estados Unidos en 1905 para confiarles la recaudación aduanera. Bajo este convenio, los funcionarios estadounidenses modificaron los aranceles nacionales gravando los artículos de lujo y aseguraron pagos para saldar los reclamos europeos.

U. S. MARINE DIES IN FIGHT

One American Is Killed and One Severely Wounded by Santo Domingo Bandits.

Washington, Jan. 24.—A night fight between native bandits and American marines in the Dominican republic, resulting in the death of one marine and the severe injury of another, was reported to the navy department.

Captain Knapp, commanding the American cruiser forces, reported the fight occurred Saturday night in the vicinity of the Porvenir sugar plantation, near Macoris, the scene of two similar encounters recently. Private J. R. Olson of the Fiftieth company was killed and Corporal George Wilson of the Fifty-second company was shot in the neck.

records.summary_en: An Associated Press correspondent writing from Santo Domingo on February 13 reports that peace, expected by everyone to be permanent, has at last been established through the intervention of the United States in a country that has had approximately fifty presidents in seventy years, not one chosen without revolution. Captain Knapp, head of the temporary military government, faces the work of establishing good government, a sound educational system, agriculture and transportation, with an education commission headed by Archbishop Adolfo Nouel already appointed and a great highway of more than 200 miles planned across the Cibao to Monte Cristi.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Puerto Plata reports that extensive repairs have begun on the Dominican Central…
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Puerto Plata reports that extensive repairs have begun on the Dominican Central railroad between Puerto Plata and Santiago, in line with the wishes of the United States military government, including new deviations that will reduce the grade from twelve percent to a maximum of three percent. Tons of tobacco, coffee and cacao have accumulated unmoved at Santiago, and other work described includes a new wharf and customs house at Puerto Plata, a hydro-electric project to serve Santiago, Moca, La Vega and Puerto Plata, rebuilding the bridges on the Santiago to Monte Cristi road that revolutionists burned last spring to check the advance of United States Marines, and a macadam road from Macoris to Santo Domingo City.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Associated Press desde Puerto Plata informa que han comenzado extensas reparaciones en el ferrocarril Central Dominicano entre Puerto Plata y Santiago, de acuerdo con los deseos del gobierno militar de los Estados Unidos, incluidas nuevas desviaciones que reducirán la pendiente del doce por ciento a un máximo del tres por ciento. Toneladas de tabaco, café y cacao se han acumulado sin mover en Santiago, y otras obras descritas incluyen un nuevo muelle y una aduana en Puerto Plata, un proyecto hidroeléctrico para servir a Santiago, Moca, La Vega y Puerto Plata, la reconstrucción de los puentes del camino de Santiago a Monte Cristi que los revolucionarios quemaron la primavera pasada para frenar el avance de los marines de los Estados Unidos, y un camino de macadán de Macorís a la ciudad de Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: The *Omaha daily bee* detailed the natural and mineral wealth of the Dominican Republic, highlighting the gold placers worked in the Cibao range and San Cristobal region. It also pointed to extensive unused forests of valuable timber and mountains of pure rock salt located in Barahona province. The report concluded that the country's lack of coal and poor overland transit routes posed the greatest obstacles to its industrial development.
records.summary_es: El *Omaha daily bee* detalló las riquezas naturales y minerales de la República Dominicana, destacando los placeres auríferos explotados en la cordillera del Cibao y la región de San Cristóbal. Hizo notar asimismo los extensos bosques vírgenes de maderas preciosas y las montañas de sal gema pura ubicadas en la provincia de Barahona. El informe concluía que la escasez de carbón y las deficientes vías de transporte terrestre representaban las principales trabas para el desarrollo fabril del país.

records.summary_en: The *Omaha daily bee* reported that many Dominicans accepted American intervention to re-establish law and order, though they remained firmly opposed to annexation. The article analyzed the country's social structure, explaining that approximately twenty elite families controlled virtually all political offices and land while avoiding property taxes. It observed that pervasive political corruption and sinecures had long characterized native governance prior to the American occupation.
records.summary_es: El *Omaha daily bee* informó que numerosos dominicanos aceptaban la intervención estadounidense para restaurar el orden y la ley, aun oponiéndose resueltamente a una anexión. El artículo examinó la estructura social dominicana, señalando que una veintena de familias pudientes acaparaba prácticamente las tierras y los destinos públicos mientras eludía el pago de impuestos prediales. Subrayó que la corrupción inveterada y las prebendas políticas habían sido el rasgo distintivo de la gobernación local con anterioridad a la ocupación estadounidense.

records.summary_en: The *Omaha daily bee* reported that the government of President Jimenez collapsed after its revenues were withheld by American authorities, and Admiral Knapp refused Jimenez's request for a month's salary. Jimenez subsequently departed the country to lecture in Latin America against American despotism in Santo Domingo. The article noted that Knapp's proclamation established a military government intended as a temporary measure, keeping native courts and municipal administrations intact while imposing press censorship.
records.summary_es: El *Omaha daily bee* informó que la administración del presidente Jimenes se desmoronó luego de que las autoridades estadounidenses retuvieran sus fondos fiscales, habiéndose negado el almirante Knapp a pagar a Jimenes un mes de sueldo solicitado. Acto seguido, Jimenes abandonó la nación para dictar conferencias por Hispanoamérica denunciando la opresión estadounidense en Santo Domingo. El artículo apuntaba que la proclama de Knapp fundaba un gobierno militar con carácter provisional, manteniendo operando a los tribunales del país y los cabildos locales pero implantando la censura de prensa.

records.summary_en: The *Albuquerque morning journal* reported on rising tensions following the landing of U.S. marines in Santo Domingo, including native outrage when marines hung laundry on the historic Conde gate. Snipers frequently fired on marine patrols, prompting street skirmishes and armed retaliation by American forces. The article also reviewed earlier U.S. policy, including the 1914 Wilson plan and the 1915 demand that the Dominican Republic sign a new treaty granting rights similar to those in Haiti.

Francotiradores tiroteaban con frecuencia las patrullas invasoras, desatando choques callejeros y represalias armadas de las tropas de los Estados Unidos. El artículo repasó además la política previa de Washington, abarcando el plan Wilson de 1914 y la exigencia formulada en 1915 para que la República Dominicana suscribiera un nuevo tratado otorgando atribuciones análogas a las impuestas a Haití.

records.summary_en: The *Evening star* reported that the U.S. military government in Santo Domingo collected customs and internal revenues, holding them in trust for administrative expenses. Government outlays were reduced by eliminating salaries for the president and congress and disbanding the native army, allowing surplus funds to accrue for return to the republic upon the occupation's end. The administration also generated new income through the strict enforcement of alcohol tax laws, which forced non-compliant distilleries to close.
records.summary_es: El *Evening star* informó que el gobierno militar estadounidense en Santo Domingo recaudaba las aduanas y rentas internas, manteniéndolas en custodia para gastos de administración. Los desembolsos públicos se redujeron suprimiendo los sueldos del presidente y de los legisladores y disolviendo el ejército nativo, permitiendo así que se acumularan excedentes que serían devueltos a la república una vez concluida la ocupación. La administración allegó asimismo nuevos ingresos mediante la rigurosa aplicación del impuesto al alcohol, obligando a cerrar a las destilerías infractoras.

records.summary_en: A feature describes Higuey as one of the principal inland cities of the Dominican Republic, a city of some 2,000 souls in the least settled eastern half of the country, center of a considerable primitive trade. It is the site of the most famous shrine on the island, the shrine of the Virgin of Alta Gracia, visited by devotees from every part of the country and housed in a church built in the old Spanish architecture.

records.summary_en: The *Richmond times-dispatch* reviewed a book on the history, geography, and administration of Santo Domingo and Haiti written by an author who served with the U.S. financial investigation commission and the Dominican Minister of Finance. The publication traced the republic's development from the Spanish conquest through modern times, detailing its topography, flora, fauna, and population. Additional chapters analyzed Dominican commerce, transportation, national finances, and political prospects.
records.summary_es: El *Richmond times-dispatch* reseñó una obra acerca de la historia, geografía y administración de Santo Domingo y Haití, escrita por un autor que formó parte de la comisión investigadora financiera estadounidense y prestó servicios al ministro de Hacienda dominicano. La obra reconstruía la evolución de la república desde la conquista española hasta la época contemporánea, detallando su topografía, flora, fauna y habitantes. Capítulos complementarios examinaban el comercio dominicano, el transporte, las finanzas públicas y el horizonte político.

records.summary_en: The *Washington herald* reported on the service of Marine Sergeant Corbett, who landed in Santo Domingo City in May 1916 from the *Prairie* to guard foreign legations during battles between federal and rebel forces. Corbett later sailed on the *Memphis* to Puerto Plata and joined the marine expedition advancing toward the rebel stronghold at Santiago. The marine force faced frequent ambushes and heavy fighting at Lajas, Alta Mira, and El Tunnel before successfully securing Santiago on July 6.

Posteriormente, Corbett navegó en el *Memphis* hacia Puerto Plata e integró la expedición militar que avanzó hacia el reducto rebelde de Santiago. La fuerza de infantería de marina resistió reiteradas emboscadas y recios combates en Las Lajas, Altamira y El Túnel antes de tomar con éxito Santiago el 6 de julio.

Schoenrich concluded from 1877 cathedral excavations that Spain had mistakenly removed the remains of Diego Columbus, leaving Christopher Columbus's body in Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: The *mirror* recounted that Pedro Santana proclaimed the annexation of the Dominican Republic to Spain in 1861 while the United States was engaged in the Civil War. A Dominican rebellion broke out two years later, forcing Spain to recognize the republic's independence in 1865. President Grant subsequently attempted to annex the country to the United States, but the treaty was rejected by the U.S. Senate on a tie vote after winning approval from the Dominican public.
records.summary_es: El *mirror* narró cómo Pedro Santana consumó la anexión de la República Dominicana a España en 1861 mientras los Estados Unidos libraban la Guerra de Secesión. Dos años después estalló la rebelión dominicana, obligando a España a reconocer la independencia de la república en 1865. El presidente Grant pretendió más adelante anexionar el país a los Estados Unidos, pero el pacto resultó desaprobado en el Senado estadounidense por un empate de votos luego de ser respaldado por la opinión pública dominicana.

records.summary_en: The *Americus times-recorder* reported on the U.S. occupation of Haiti under the 1915 treaty, which intervened to prevent European powers from seizing autonomy over unpaid bonds. The treaty placed U.S. officials in charge of Haitian finances, public works, and sanitation, alongside a naval general of gendarmerie directing the native constabulary. Brigadier General A. W. Catlin was appointed to command the U.S. marine detachment stationed in Haiti.

records.summary_en: The *Americus times-recorder* reported on Protestant Episcopal Church efforts to assist public health and youth education in Haiti alongside the U.S. military presence. Haitian President Dartiguenave and education officials requested the establishment of trade schools to address the nation's severe educational shortages. Church advocates emphasized that cooperating with the marines would help develop a self-sustaining Haitian nation and enable the eventual withdrawal of American troops.

Los delegados religiosos puntualizaron que el auxilio a las tropas expedicionarias contribuiría a estructurar una nación haitiana autosuficiente y propiciaría la futura retirada militar estadounidense.

records.summary_en: The *Yorkville enquirer* examined constitutional precedents for submitting treaties to the U.S. Senate, citing President Grant's transmission of a draft convention with the Dominican Republic. Grant requested the Senate's advice and consent to the transfer according to terms negotiated by American and Dominican representatives. The article noted that the convention was already agreed upon between the governments and was formally presented to the Senate awaiting ratification.
records.summary_es: El *Yorkville enquirer* examinó los precedentes constitucionales relativos a la presentación de tratados ante el Senado de los EE. UU., citando la remisión efectuada por el presidente Grant de una convención preliminar con la República Dominicana. Grant solicitó el consejo y consentimiento del Senado para la cesión con arreglo a las bases concertadas entre los plenipotenciarios estadounidenses y dominicanos. El artículo subrayó que la convención ya se encontraba acordada entre ambos gobiernos y fue sometida en debida forma al Senado para su ratificación.

records.summary_en: The *sun* discussed Dominican efforts to enlist Spanish diplomatic support to secure the withdrawal of U.S. marines, noting historic cultural affinities between the two nations. The piece recalled that Pedro Santana annexed the Dominican Republic to Spain in 1861, which was overturned by a popular revolt that led Spain to recognize Dominican independence in 1865. It added that an 1869 annexation treaty with the United States was ratified by Dominicans but defeated by a tie vote in the U.S. Senate.
records.summary_es: El *sun* trató sobre las gestiones dominicanas dirigidas a concitar el respaldo diplomático de España para lograr la evacuación de las tropas de marina estadounidenses, resaltando los seculares vínculos culturales que unían a ambos pueblos. La nota recordó que Pedro Santana reincorporó la República Dominicana a España en 1861, medida revocada por un alzamiento patriótico que forzó a España a reconocer la emancipación dominicana en 1865. Añadió que el tratado de anexión de 1869 con los Estados Unidos fue respaldado por la población dominicana pero desestimado en el Senado de los EE. UU. por votación empatada.

records.summary_en: This narrative tells how a Puerto Plata senator chosen as president, on trial for one year after the previous president was killed, announced after some ten months that he intended to hold onto the job, sparking a general uprising against him as a usurper and tyrant. As his forces prepared to shell Puerto Plata unless the city surrendered by two o'clock, and Washington had sent two contingents of Marines to Puerto Plata and Monte Cristi to stand by, the American commander warned him that the first gun fired would result in the landing of Marines and a general cleaning out of the belligerents.
records.summary_es: Este relato cuenta cómo un senador de Puerto Plata escogido como presidente, a prueba por un año tras la muerte del presidente anterior, anunció después de unos diez meses que pretendía quedarse en el puesto, lo que desató un levantamiento general contra él como usurpador y tirano. Mientras sus fuerzas se preparaban para bombardear Puerto Plata si la ciudad no se rendía a las dos en punto, y Washington había enviado dos contingentes de marines a Puerto Plata y Monte Cristi para estar listos, el comandante americano le advirtió que el primer cañonazo disparado provocaría el desembarco de los marines y una limpieza general de los beligerantes.

records.summary_en: The *Richmond planet* reported that many U.S. marines in Santo Domingo did not understand why they were stationed there beyond vague rumors about collecting a $20,000,000 debt while running customs. The article criticized the strict military censorship that destroyed letters written by enlisted men and suppressed news from reaching the islands. It highlighted efforts to conceal former President Theodore Roosevelt's public denunciations of President Wilson's military operations in Santo Domingo and Haiti.
records.summary_es: El *Richmond planet* informó que muchos infantes de marina estadounidenses en Santo Domingo desconocían la razón de su permanencia en el lugar más allá de confusos rumores sobre el cobro de una deuda de 20.000.000 de dólares mientras administraban las aduanas. El periódico censuró la estricta vigilancia militar que destruía la correspondencia de los soldados e impedía que las noticias arribasen a las islas. Resaltó el empeño puesto en silenciar las condenas públicas formuladas por el expresidente Theodore Roosevelt contra las incursiones militares del mandatario Wilson en Santo Domingo y Haití.

records.headline: One year was the limit if he failed to "make good
records.summary_en: The *Richmond planet* recounted the outbreak of civil war in Santo Domingo after a provisional president, appointed for a one-year trial term, issued a manifesto ten months later refusing to relinquish office. The declaration provoked widespread public outrage, prompting citizens to take up arms under the banner of liberty to remove the administration. While the president armed supporters with government artillery, fighters in Puerto Plata organized resistance, plunging the country into open conflict.
records.summary_es: El *Richmond planet* relató el estallido de la guerra civil en Santo Domingo después de que un presidente provisional, designado para un período de prueba de un año, emitiera un manifiesto diez meses después negándose a dejar el cargo. La declaración provocó una indignación pública generalizada, lo que llevó a los ciudadanos a alzarse en armas bajo el estandarte de la libertad para deponer a la administración. Mientras el presidente armaba a sus partidarios con artillería gubernamental, combatientes en Puerto Plata organizaron la resistencia, sumiendo al país en un conflicto abierto.

records.summary_en: A feature on the American occupation reports that 2,600 additional United States Marines, armed with hand grenades and the latest machine guns, are to be sent to San Domingo to cooperate with the 3,000 Marines already there, where Marines have been stationed for three years under a strict censorship that keeps news of the fighting from the United States. It says Dominicans hate the Americans and take shots at the uniform when they can do so safely, that officers would tell of leathernecks driven insane searching the brush for bandits, and that few of the Marines know why they are there beyond a vague idea of a debt of some $20,000,000 and the United States being in charge of the customs.

records.summary_en: The *Evening star* reported that Dr. Francisco Henriquez y Carvajal rejected assertions that the United States exercised a protectorate over the Dominican Republic, declaring that no treaty akin to the Platt Amendment existed. Henriquez explained that the 1907 convention was limited strictly to customs administration for debt repayment and, as President Roosevelt affirmed, conferred no authority for military intervention. He maintained that the agreement was temporary and would naturally expire once the foreign debt was fully discharged.
records.summary_es: El *Evening star* informó que el Dr. Francisco Henríquez y Carvajal rechazó las afirmaciones de que Estados Unidos ejerciera un protectorado sobre la República Dominicana, declarando que no existía ningún tratado similar a la Enmienda Platt. Henríquez explicó que la convención de 1907 se limitaba estrictamente a la administración aduanera para el pago de la deuda y que, como afirmó el presidente Roosevelt, no confería autoridad para una intervención militar. Sostuvo que el acuerdo era temporal y que expiraría de manera natural una vez que la deuda externa quedara totalmente saldada.

records.summary_en: The *Milwaukee leader* reported sharp criticisms of the U.S. military occupation in Haiti and Santo Domingo, citing findings by Judge Otto Schoenrich and Archbishop Adolfo Nouel. The article reported allegations of despotic military rule, the dissolution of legislative assemblies, arbitrary provost court trials, and the suppression of civil liberties. It also claimed that debt disbursements to native bondholders were suspended under the occupation while New York bankers acquired the depreciated securities.

El artículo dio cuenta de denuncias de un régimen militar despótico, la disolución de asambleas legislativas, juicios arbitrarios ante cortes marciales y la supresión de las libertades civiles. También afirmó que durante la ocupación se suspendieron los pagos de la deuda a los tenedores de bonos nacionales, mientras banqueros de Nueva York adquirían los títulos depreciados.

records.full_text:
OUR CARIBBEAN EMPIRE

The average citizen of the United States is blissfully ignorant of the extent to which this government has established a colonial empire in the Caribbean regions. In Nicaragua the government is practically in the hands of the United States marines. The natives complain not merely that they are ruled without their consent but that they are subject to the whims of our navy department which in this matter is responsible neither to congress nor the people. The American government is also charged with unwarranted interference in Guatemala, Costa Rica and Honduras. At a recent conference at Clark university, Judge Otto Schoenrich, a conservative citizen, born in America, who has held high judicial posts in Porto Rico and is familiar with all the Caribbean countries, read a paper reviewing the record of the American administration of the two island republics, Santo Domingo and Haiti. The first, it will be recalled, is Spanish-speaking and predominantly white; the second French-speaking and Negro. In 1916 our navy took over the government of Santo Domingo, and administers it through the marines against the wishes of the people. “Law and order” have been established. Roads have been built and a beginning has been made at popular education. The reason for our intervention was the failure of the Dominican government to live up to its agreement in the matter of its foreign debt. Foreign bondholders now get their interest regularly! Judge Schoenrich, however, charges that in accomplishing these things the United States government has maintained a censorship so rigid as to apply to every public statement “from the utterances of the chief justice to an advertisement for a servant girl.” Until recently the words, national, revolution, freedom of thought and speech could not appear in a Dominican publication. One unfortunate bookseller was originally sentenced to five years in prison for circulating a speech by the speaker of the Porto Rican house of representatives. Later his sentence was graciously commuted to banishment. Judge Schoenrich also reports serious charges of torture in connection with the administration of the provost courts.

In the neighboring republic of Haiti conditions are even more unsatisfactory. There we intervened on the nominal authority of a treaty, but the Haitian congress only ratified that treaty with 23 reservations which we ignored. In 1916 marines dispersed the congress and in 1917 dispersed a constituent assembly. Tell it not to Trotzky! Judge Schoenrich says there are three governments: the Haitian, the government of the American treaty officials, and the government of the American military. The first is impotent, the second inefficient, and the third indifferent. In the interior districts of the island the officers of the marines exercise despotic powers and the natives charge that a marine can do no wrong to a Haitian. From Haiti also come ugly stories of torture, autocratic and unjust trials of civilians by provost court, and denials of civil liberty. A few months ago armed Haitians, either bandits or revolutionists according to the point of view, actually marched on the capital city where there was vigorous fighting before they were dispersed. The Haitian debt was largely held by the people, who, lacking proper banking facilities, put their savings into national bonds. Under American occupation payment on these was suspended although it was guaranteed in the treaty. The people sold their holdings at low prices. The bonds, it is believed, are now held by New York bankers, and negotiations are under way looking to their payment at par.

It is only fair to say that such criticisms as these were vigorously attacked at the Clark university conference by defenders of the American regime. They are, however, supported by other testimony. Archbishop Nouel of Santo Domingo in a letter to the American minister (we go through the farce of maintaining a minister plenipotentiary in a country ruled by an American rear admiral) complains not only of torture, of the denial of liberty, but of a faulty system of taxation and waste in its expenditure. Emphatically the situation requires investigation. The navy department is ruling three republics without their consent primarily in the interests of their American creditors, with a blissful irresponsibility even as regards congress or the American public. Supposing that conditions in Nicaragua, Santo Domingo, and Haiti prior to our intervention were as bad as their critics assert—it is a sorry world if we can discover no way of helping to educate “backward” people without subjecting them to flagrant economic and political imperialism.

Porto Rico welcomed American annexation and her case is not on all fours with her neighbor’s. Nevertheless, our territorial rule leaves something to be desired. During the year 1917-’18 only 142,846 children out of 427,668 of school age were actually enrolled in the public schools. The total wealth of the island is in the hands of 15 per cent of the population; 14 per cent is in the hands of native Porto Ricans; 67 per cent in the hands of Americans. Wages, housing, and health conditions are wretched. The extension of this sort of thing in Mexico and the Caribbean countries is not our idea of civilizing people.—The World Tomorrow.

records.summary_en: The *Richmond times-dispatch* published a report by Military Governor Rear Admiral Thomas Snowden detailing administrative progress in Santo Domingo. Snowden reported that internal revenue collections had increased from $700,000 to approximately $3,500,000 annually and that regressive taxes were replaced with direct property taxes. He stated that the republic's floating debt was cleared, the 1908 loan was on course to be retired thirty years early by 1926, and administrative savings were funding new schools, highways, and sanitation projects.

records.summary_en: The *Dallas express* reported on Rear Admiral Thomas Snowden's official report describing the accomplishments of the U.S. military administration in Santo Domingo. Snowden stated that annual internal revenue collections rose to $3,500,000, regressive taxes were eliminated in favor of property taxes, and the $20,000,000 loan of 1908 was projected to be fully retired by 1926. He highlighted that substantial government savings were redirected toward constructing public schools, roads, harbor improvements, and sanitary facilities.

Destacó que considerables ahorros estatales se canalizaron hacia la construcción de escuelas públicas, carreteras, mejoras portuarias e instalaciones de saneamiento.

records.summary_en: The *Pine Bluff daily graphic* reported that Julio M. Cestero of the Dominican junta issued a statement asserting that Dominican citizens never sought U.S. intervention and continually demanded the return of their national sovereignty. In a concurrent release, Secretary of State Colby defended American policy, stating that military intervention in Haiti was prompted by chronic bloodshed and the 1915 lynching of President Guillaume Sam in the French legation. Colby maintained that the United States acted under the Monroe Doctrine to restore order and preempt European military intervention.
records.summary_es: El *Pine Bluff daily graphic* informó que Julio M. Cestero, de la junta dominicana, emitió una declaración afirmando que los ciudadanos dominicanos nunca solicitaron la intervención de Estados Unidos y que exigían continuamente la restitución de su soberanía nacional. En un comunicado simultáneo, el secretario de Estado Colby defendió la política estadounidense, señalando que la intervención militar en Haití fue provocada por el derramamiento de sangre crónico y el linchamiento en 1915 del presidente Guillaume Sam en la legación francesa. Colby sostuvo que Estados Unidos actuó en virtud de la Doctrina Monroe para restablecer el orden y prevenir una intervención militar europea.

records.summary_en: The *New-York tribune* reported that the State Department issued a formal denial that the National City Bank of New York received improper government favors in Haiti. The department stated it only provided routine support and had actively intervened to remove monopolistic provisions from the bank's charter when it increased its holdings in the National Bank of Haiti. Furthermore, the statement emphasized that the bank exercised no control over customs revenues, foreign loans, or exchange rates.

El departamento afirmó que únicamente prestó apoyo rutinario y que había intervenido activamente para eliminar disposiciones monopolísticas de los estatutos del banco cuando este amplió su participación en el Banco Nacional de Haití. Asimismo, la declaración enfatizó que la entidad bancaria no ejercía control alguno sobre las rentas aduaneras, los préstamos externos ni los tipos de cambio.

records.summary_en: The *Ogden standard-examiner* reported Secretary of State Colby's statement that the United States hoped to withdraw from Haiti as its mission to stabilize the republic neared completion. Colby explained that the 1915 intervention was undertaken after decades of revolutions and the mob murder of President Vilbrun Guillaume Sam in the French legation prompted French troops to land. He asserted that the United States intervened to restore order and protect foreign interests under the Monroe Doctrine before European powers could take aggressive military action.

Afirmó que Estados Unidos intervino para restablecer el orden y proteger los intereses extranjeros bajo la Doctrina Monroe antes de que las potencias europeas pudieran emprender acciones militares agresivas.

Colby confirmed that the State Department was continuing to withhold salaries from Haitian officials until they ceased obstructing the bilateral treaty. Simultaneously, Dominican representative Julio M. Cestero protested that the Dominican people never requested American occupation and consistently demanded the restoration of their freedom and sovereignty.

Colby confirmó que el Departamento de Estado seguía reteniendo los salarios de los funcionarios haitianos hasta que cesaran de obstruir el tratado bilateral. Al mismo tiempo, el representante dominicano Julio M. Cestero protestó que el pueblo dominicano jamás solicitó la ocupación estadounidense y reclamó de manera constante el restablecimiento de su libertad y soberanía.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield weekly Republican* reported that the State Department credited U.S. treaty officials with restoring public order, increasing revenues, and advancing road and telegraph construction in Haiti. The department also refuted claims of favoritism toward the National City Bank of New York, stating it received only standard commercial support abroad. The statement noted that U.S. authorities had actually required modifications to the bank's agreement to eliminate monopolistic privileges in the National Bank of Haiti.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield weekly Republican* informó que el Departamento de Estado atribuyó a los funcionarios encargados del tratado estadounidense la restauración del orden público, el incremento de las rentas fiscales y el avance en la construcción de carreteras y líneas telegráficas en Haití. El departamento también refutó las acusaciones de favoritismo hacia el National City Bank of New York, declarando que únicamente recibió el respaldo comercial habitual en el extranjero. La declaración indicó que las autoridades estadounidenses habían exigido modificaciones al convenio bancario a fin de eliminar privilegios monopolísticos en el Banco Nacional de Haití.

records.headline: After a turbulent history, during which the native Indians were exterminated
records.summary_en: The *Evening star* published a historical overview of the Dominican Republic, detailing its initial settlement by Spain, the eradication of indigenous inhabitants, and the importation of enslaved Africans. The article described how an eighteenth-century uprising abolished slavery and expelled colonizers, followed by shifts between Spanish and Haitian rule until the Dominican Republic secured independence in 1844. It observed that despite preserving Spanish language and institutions, the nation experienced frequent political coups and revolutions throughout its history.
records.summary_es: El *Evening star* publicó una reseña histórica de la República Dominicana, detallando su colonización inicial por parte de España, la desaparición de los pobladores indígenas y la importación de africanos esclavizados. El artículo describió cómo un levantamiento en el siglo XVIII abolió la esclavitud y expulsó a los colonizadores, seguido de sucesivas alternancias entre el dominio español y el haitiano hasta que la República Dominicana consolidó su independencia en 1844. Observó que, a pesar de conservar la lengua y las instituciones españolas, la nación experimentó frecuentes golpes políticos y revoluciones a lo largo de su historia.

records.summary_en: The *New-York tribune* reported on a gathering where James Weldon Johnson and former Dominican President Francisco Henriquez y Carvajal criticized U.S. military occupations in the Caribbean. Johnson characterized the occupation of Haiti as pure economic exploitation, describing native resistance fighters as patriots rather than outlaws. Henriquez y Carvajal explained that Admiral Knapp instituted military rule in 1916 after Santo Domingo rejected an imposed treaty, expressing faith that the American public would eventually repudiate the intervention.

Henríquez y Carvajal explicó que el almirante Knapp instauró el gobierno militar en 1916 después de que Santo Domingo rechazara un tratado impuesto, manifestando su confianza en que la opinión pública estadounidense finalmente repudiaría la intervención.

records.headline: The possibility that the island of Haiti might become a pawn
records.summary_en: The *Springfield weekly Republican* discussed prospective U.S. withdrawal from Santo Domingo, observing that wartime strategic concerns and foreign debt disputes had prompted military guardianship over the island of Hispaniola. Acting Secretary of State Davis noted that the occupation grew out of the 1907 convention establishing an American customs receivership and barring unauthorized debt expansion. The article observed that Dominican authorities later violated the convention by increasing public debt to finance the suppression of domestic rebellions.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield weekly Republican* analizó la proyectada retirada de Estados Unidos de Santo Domingo, observando que las preocupaciones estratégicas en tiempos de guerra y las disputas por la deuda externa habían motivado la tutela militar sobre la isla de La Española. El secretario de Estado interino Davis señaló que la ocupación derivó de la convención de 1907, la cual estableció la receptoría general de aduanas estadounidense y prohibió el aumento no autorizado de la deuda. El artículo indicó que las autoridades dominicanas violaron posteriormente dicha convención al incrementar la deuda pública para financiar la represión de rebeliones internas.

records.summary_en: The *Evening star* reported that the United States initiated steps toward withdrawing forces from Santo Domingo and establishing a native governing commission to restore self-government. The report recounted that naval officers instituted military rule in 1916 after provisional president Francisco Henriquez y Carvajal refused terms of a proposed treaty. records.headline: It is frequently said that a revolution would follow the departure
records.summary_en: The *Dearborn independent* argued that an immediate withdrawal of American marines from Haiti would quickly lead to revolution and governmental collapse. The article contrasted the French colonial period's agricultural prosperity with the nation's condition following Toussaint L'Ouverture's uprising and Jean-Jacques Dessalines's 1804 declaration of independence. It asserted that more than a century of post-independence conflict and despotic leadership had ruined the country's plantations and civil institutions.
records.summary_es: El *Dearborn independent* sostuvo que una retirada inmediata de los infantes de marina estadounidenses de Haití conduciría rápidamente a la revolución y al colapso gubernamental. El artículo contrastó la prosperidad agrícola del período colonial francés con la situación de la nación tras la sublevación de Toussaint L'Ouverture y la declaración de independencia de 1804 de Jean-Jacques Dessalines. Aseguró que más de un siglo de conflictos y caudillismos despóticos posteriores a la independencia habían arruinado las plantaciones y las instituciones civiles del país.

records.summary_en: The *Evening star* reported that President Harding, Secretary Hughes, and Secretary Denby approved a proclamation establishing procedures for withdrawing the military government from the Dominican Republic. The plan directed primary assemblies to convene within a month to choose electors, who would elect senators and deputies and nominate judges under the Dominican constitution. Delegates appointed by the military governor would then negotiate an evacuation convention to ratify military government acts, validate a $2,500,000 public works loan, and extend customs receivership duties.
records.summary_es: El *Evening star* informó que el presidente Harding, el secretario Hughes y el secretario Denby aprobaron una proclama que establecía el procedimiento para retirar el gobierno militar de la República Dominicana. El plan ordenaba convocar asambleas primarias en el plazo de un mes para designar electores, quienes elegirían a senadores y diputados y nominarían jueces conforme a la constitución dominicana. Delegados designados por el gobernador militar negociarían luego una convención de evacuación para ratificar las disposiciones del gobierno militar, convalidar un préstamo de 2 500 000 dólares para obras públicas y prorrogar las funciones de la receptoría de aduanas.

The committee proposed appointing a presidential High Commissioner with envoy extraordinary powers to direct all civilian and military U.S. officials in Haiti. It also advised issuing a new loan to discharge European debt obligations and resolve valid claims held by Haitian citizens against their government.

También aconsejó emitir un nuevo préstamo para saldar las obligaciones de deuda europea y resolver las reclamaciones legítimas de ciudadanos haitianos contra su gobierno.

records.summary_en: The *New-York tribune* reported that while a Senate committee recommended extending Cuban tariff preferences to the Dominican Republic, the Haiti-Santo Domingo Independence Society fiercely condemned the committee's preliminary report. The society denounced the findings as an imperialist endorsement of armed intervention and treaty imposition on smaller republics. It contended that maintaining military garrisons and puppet executives did lasting damage to American prestige throughout Latin America.
records.summary_es: El *New-York tribune* informó que, si bien una comisión del Senado recomendó extender a la República Dominicana las preferencias arancelarias concedidas a Cuba, la Sociedad Pro Independencia de Haití y Santo Domingo condenó enérgicamente el informe preliminar de la comisión. La sociedad denunció las conclusiones como un respaldo imperialista a la intervención armada y a la imposición de tratados a repúblicas más pequeñas. Sostuvo que el mantenimiento de guarniciones militares y gobernantes títeres causaba un perjuicio duradero al prestigio estadounidense en toda América Latina.

records.summary_en: The *Great Falls tribune* reported that a Senate committee led by Senator Medill McCormick unanimously opposed withdrawing American marines from Haiti, declaring their presence essential to preserve peace and order. McCormick stated that the committee's findings on marine atrocity allegations in Haiti would be made public around February 1, with a separate report on Santo Domingo forthcoming. He also urged the immediate appointment of a High Commissioner to unite diplomatic, treaty, and military authorities under single leadership.
records.summary_es: El *Great Falls tribune* informó que una comisión del Senado encabezada por el senador Medill McCormick se opuso por unanimidad a la retirada de los infantes de marina estadounidenses de Haití, declarando que su presencia era indispensable para mantener la paz y el orden. McCormick afirmó que las conclusiones de la comisión acerca de las denuncias de atrocidades cometidas por marines en Haití se harían públicas hacia el 1 de febrero, y que próximamente se presentaría un informe por separado sobre Santo Domingo. Asimismo, instó al pronto nombramiento de un alto comisionado para unificar la representación diplomática, las facultades derivadas del tratado y la autoridad militar bajo un solo mando.

records.summary_en: The *Birmingham age-herald* reported that Senator Medill McCormick recommended completing the Dominican North-South highway to stimulate commerce and prevent future insurrections, thereby facilitating American withdrawal. To offset revenue declines caused by the post-war trade depression, the committee advised issuing a new loan to consolidate two outstanding short-term debts. McCormick reported that outside of localized banditry in the east, the military administration had established unprecedented domestic peace while modernizing municipal sanitation, docks, and public education.
records.summary_es: El *Birmingham age-herald* informó que el senador Medill McCormick recomendó concluir la carretera Norte-Sur dominicana para estimular el comercio y prevenir futuras insurrecciones, facilitando con ello la retirada estadounidense. A fin de compensar la caída de ingresos provocada por la depresión comercial de posguerra, la comisión aconsejó emitir un nuevo préstamo para consolidar dos obligaciones pendientes a corto plazo. McCormick afirmó que, al margen de partidas aisladas de bandolerismo en el este, la administración militar había instaurado una paz interna sin precedentes a la vez que modernizaba el saneamiento municipal, los muelles y la educación pública.

records.summary_en: Horace G. Knowles said he had been compelled to leave Santo Domingo City under cover of darkness after receiving a letter from Francisco J. Peynado, former Dominican minister to the United States, advising him not to remain an hour beyond the first chance he had to leave. Knowles argued that the treatment accorded him, an American citizen, was an example of the methods of the American military government in Santo Domingo, and asked what it would stop at in the case of natives. He had remained behind to take the testimony of some fifty other witnesses at Senator McCormicks request, and went to the dock with a list of witnesses to deliver to McCormick, only to be informed that he had boarded the Argonne.

records.summary_en: The *Chicago whip* reported on continued resistance to the U.S. occupation of Haiti, mocking claims of mutual devotion between Haitians and military authorities while officials acknowledged that ending martial law would spark immediate revolt. The paper published a statement by Haitian Hague delegate Pierre Hudicourt, who traveled to Washington to formally protest the occupation before the Senate. Hudicourt condemned the invasion as an assault on national sovereignty driven by foreign commercial interests and urged the American public to demand military withdrawal.
records.summary_es: El *Chicago whip* informó sobre la continuada resistencia a la ocupación estadounidense de Haití, ridiculizando las afirmaciones de afecto mutuo entre haitianos y autoridades militares cuando los propios oficiales reconocían que el fin de la ley marcial desataría una revuelta inmediata. El periódico publicó una declaración del delegado haitiano ante La Haya, Pierre Hudicourt, quien viajó a Washington para protestar formalmente contra la ocupación ante el Senado. Hudicourt condenó la invasión como un atentado a la soberanía nacional impulsado por intereses comerciales extranjeros e instó a la opinión pública estadounidense a exigir la retirada militar.

records.summary_en: The *Milwaukee leader* asserted that the Dominican Republic was peaceful and paying foreign debts ahead of schedule when American naval forces seized Santo Domingo City in 1916. The report stated that President Jimenez resigned rather than accept American armed support against congressional impeachment proceedings. After Congress elected Francisco Henriquez y Carvajal and he rejected an American treaty identical to Haiti's, U.S. naval commanders landed marines and extinguished the constitutional Dominican government.

records.summary_en: The *Maryland women's news* published Horace G. Knowles's account of the 1916 American intervention in the Dominican Republic, alleging that President Wilson secretly deployed naval forces to seize the nation without congressional approval or a war declaration. Warships landed marines under covering guns, after which American authorities presented President Francisco Henriquez y Carvajal with a treaty subordinating national sovereignty. When Henriquez refused the terms, the American naval commander initiated full military subjugation of the republic.
records.summary_es: El *Maryland women's news* publicó el relato de Horace G. Knowles sobre la intervención estadounidense de 1916 en la República Dominicana, alegando que el presidente Wilson desplegó secretamente fuerzas navales para apoderarse de la nación sin aprobación del Congreso ni declaración de guerra. Buques de guerra desembarcaron a infantes de marina bajo el fuego de cobertura de su artillería, tras lo cual las autoridades estadounidenses presentaron al presidente Francisco Henríquez y Carvajal un tratado que subordinaba la soberanía nacional. Al rechazar Henríquez las condiciones, el comandante naval estadounidense inició el pleno sometimiento militar de la república.

records.summary_en: The *Maryland women's news* reported further disclosures by Horace G. Knowles, who claimed American representatives manufactured disorder to justify military intervention and used armed force to coerce the Dominican Congress. Knowles asserted that officials attempted to bribe the Dominican Minister of War and arrested legislators to dictate the presidency. He also pointed out that the republic had never defaulted on its 1907 loan obligations, noting that payments were running thirty-three years ahead of schedule.
records.summary_es: El *Maryland women's news* informó sobre nuevas revelaciones de Horace G. Knowles, quien afirmó que representantes estadounidenses fabricaron desórdenes para justificar la intervención militar y emplearon la fuerza armada para coaccionar al Congreso dominicano. Knowles aseveró que los funcionarios intentaron sobornar al ministro de Guerra dominicano y arrestaron a legisladores para imponer la presidencia. Señaló además que la república nunca había incurrido en mora con respecto a las obligaciones de su empréstito de 1907, destacando que los pagos se realizaban con treinta y tres años de adelanto sobre el calendario previsto.
