records.full_text:
THE AMERICAN EMPIRE

[Selected]

In none of the lands that America has guided and protected during the last generation is more interesting than the great island often called Haiti, but more correctly known as Santo Domingo—the island which lies between Cuba and Porto Rico. It is unquestionably the finest of the West Indies—a land of lofty mountains clothed with splendid forests and a rich variety of minerals; a land of spacious plateaus and fertile plains that are capable of producing the finest of sugar, tobacco and other tropical products. Santo Domingo would appear predestined by nature to be the richest and most prosperous of the West Indies. As a matter of fact it lost its early prosperity long ago, and for more than a century has been sunk in a backwardness and misery from which, under recent American guidance, it is only now beginning to emerge. The story of the turbulent past of Santo Domingo and of its new start is a story well worth telling.

As its double name suggests, the island of Santo Domingo, which has an area of some thirty thousand square miles (about half the area of New England), is divided politically into two distinct nations. The western third forms the republic of Haiti; the eastern two-thirds constitutes the Dominican Republic. Haiti is a nation of Negroes; it has only a few mulattoes and no native whites. The people speak a corrupt French and look to France for their culture. The Dominican Republic, on the other hand, is a Spanish-speaking land, much like Cuba and Porto Rico. It has a considerable white or near-white upper class, a peasantry of mixed blood (Indian, white and African) and relatively few full-blooded Negroes.

Christopher Columbus discovered Santo Domingo, and the island was the first Spanish colony in the New World. It had a fine start, for at first the whole colonizing energy of Spain flowed into that relatively small insular area. Within thirty years multitudes of colonists had covered the land with towns of stone. Even now, after four centuries of decay, Santo Domingo, the capital city, still shows those stately mansions proudly described by an early Spanish historian as “so fair and large that they may well receive any lord or noble of Spain.”

During those thirty years the blood of a million Indians paid for the ingots of gold and silver that amazed the Spanish court. But at the end of that exciting period the bloodshed ceased. Mexico and Peru were conquered, the mines of Santo Domingo became insignificant beside the mines of the mainland, and the Indian workers were dead. The restless, fortune-hunting conquistadores who had made up the bulk of the population of Santo Domingo flocked away to the more tempting Spanish Main; and depopulated Spanish Santo Domingo almost sank into oblivion.

So matters stood for perhaps a hundred years. Then, just about the time when our ancestors were settling the Atlantic seaboard of North America, the coming of the French revived the prosperity of Santo Domingo. The Spaniards had colonized only the eastern part of the island—the part now known as the Dominican Republic; they had left the western part, which is today known as Haiti, virtually uninhabited, and the deserted coasts became the haunt of the famous buccaneers. The buccaneers were mainly French, and in time France claimed the region they had occupied, introduced respectable immigrants and made it a colony known as the French part of Santo Domingo. Like the Spaniards, the French devoted themselves to agriculture, and soon showed what marvelous productiveness the island had. During the eighteenth century French Santo Domingo was by far the most flourishing colony in the West Indies. Covered with fine plantations and cultivated to the very mountain crests, the French part of Santo Domingo, though only a trifle larger than the state of Massachusetts, furnished not only France but half Europe with sugar, coffee and other tropical products.

In order to obtain the labor necessary for so many plantations the French brought in multitudes of Negro slaves, who soon vastly outnumbered the white population. When the French Revolution convulsed France and its colonies, the Negroes of French Santo Domingo took advantage of the situation, revolted and after a long struggle succeeded in expelling the whites. Then they declared their independence, and in the year 1804 set up the republic of Haiti, the old Indian name for the land. About twenty years later the eastern part of the island threw off Spanish rule and became the Dominican Republic.

But independence meant neither peace nor prosperity. Having gained their freedom, the Haitians and the Dominicans began to misuse it. Both peoples showed from the first an utter lack of capacity for orderly self-government. The “Black Republic” of Haiti quickly degenerated into an absurd burlesque of France. The government sedulously copied French political forms; and the republic was sometimes styled a kingdom, sometimes an empire. One of the rulers of Haiti especially distinguished himself by creating a whole nobility headed by four princes and fifty-nine dukes; innumerable marquises, counts and barons completed the pompous galaxy that surrounded the “imperial” throne. Meanwhile Haiti itself went to rack and ruin. An endless succession of black and mulatto “generals” at the head of tatterdemalion “armies” fought ferociously for the spoils of office and kept the land plunged in a horrid and interminable anarchy. Revolution succeeded revolution and in those senseless civil wars the fine, well-constructed towns that the French had left were destroyed and replaced by squalid shacks, and the broad plantations and shaded highroads of the countryside again became bush and forest.

In the Spanish (Dominican) Republic colonial prosperity was destroyed because the Haitians repeatedly invaded and conquered it. How the Haitians ruled their own country suggests how they ruled the Dominicans; and finally, when the Dominicans at last succeeded in expelling them, the Dominican Republic continued to flounder in the bog of misgovernment and revolution.

By the beginning of the present century things had become so bad that European intervention seemed certain. Both republics had piled up huge foreign debts that they could not pay. Some of the creditors were Americans, but most of them were Europeans, particularly Englishmen, Frenchmen and Germans.

Now, it soon became clear that whatever the United States might think about its duty in the matter, the European nations would not put up with conditions much longer. In fact, European warships were already appearing off the coast and threatening to bombard the ports unless the money that was due was paid. But if European powers seized the ports of Santo Domingo, what would become of the Monroe Doctrine, one of the corner stones of our foreign policy?

Faced with that critical situation, President Roosevelt succeeded in 1905 in getting the Dominican government to sign an agreement that permitted the United States to adjust the Dominican debt and to administer the customs for the benefit of creditors. The effects of American intervention were instantly felt.

Hitherto the goal of every revolutionist had been the nearest customhouse, because the customs were almost the only source of revenue. If a revolutionist could seize a customhouse, he could maintain an army. But when the United States took charge of the customhouses, the customs officials turned over 45 per cent of the revenue to the Dominican government for its current expenses and applied the remaining 55 per cent to paying the foreign debt. At once the customhouses ceased to be prizes for revolutionists, because an American collector with American naval forces behind him was in charge. Revolutions promptly stopped, and for nearly ten years the Dominican Republic enjoyed unprecedented peace and prosperity. The country developed rapidly; roads, harbors, schools and public buildings were constructed, and the public debt was steadily reduced.

Then came the World War. The withdrawal of American naval vessels to European waters was the signal for fresh revolutions. A series of uprisings threatened to undo all that had been accomplished. In 1916 the United States intervened with armed force. American marines landed, deposed the revolutionary government and set up a military administration headed by an American naval officer. Under American military rule the republic was completely disarmed, banditry was suppressed, and order was firmly established.

Meanwhile, across the border in Haiti, conditions had gone from bad to worse. Between 1908 and 1915 seven presidents were successively overthrown, assassinated or driven into exile. When the World War broke out, German influence in Haiti was strong, and there was danger that Germany might seize a naval base on the island. In July, 1915, after a particularly shocking massacre of political prisoners, American marines landed at Port-au-Prince. A treaty was negotiated between the United States and Haiti under which the United States assumed control of the finances and police of the republic.

Under American supervision the gendarmery was organized, public works were pushed forward, and the country was cleared of the cacos, or mountain bandits, who had terrorized the population for generations. Today both republics on the island of Santo Domingo are peacefully developing their immense natural resources under American guidance and protection.

records.summary_en: The *Evening star* detailed an agreement between Dominican leaders and American authorities to establish a provisional government preparatory to ending the military occupation. Under the arrangement, executive departments would be transferred to Dominican ministers, expenditures would follow established budgets, and American troops would concentrate into select centers while the national police preserved order. Full American evacuation was conditioned on a newly elected constitutional government ratifying executive orders and the 1918 and 1922 bond issues.

records.summary_en: Following the State Department's agreement to withdraw American military forces from San Domingo, the provisional government of the Dominican Republic will assume administrative powers from the date of its installation. It will legislate to regulate the holding of elections, reorganize provincial and municipal government and enable the Dominican people to amend the constitution as they deem appropriate, and from that date it will be alone responsible for its acts, ending seven years of American military government.
records.summary_es: Tras el acuerdo del Departamento de Estado de retirar las fuerzas militares estadounidenses de Santo Domingo, el gobierno provisional de la República Dominicana asumirá los poderes administrativos desde la fecha de su instalación. Legislará para regular la celebración de elecciones, reorganizará los gobiernos provinciales y municipales y permitirá al pueblo dominicano enmendar la constitución como lo considere apropiado, y desde esa fecha será el único responsable de sus actos, poniendo fin a siete años de gobierno militar estadounidense.

records.summary_en: The *Birmingham age-herald* commented that the planned withdrawal of American troops after seven years proved the success of the U.S. mission to stabilize the Dominican Republic and prepare it for self-government. The editorial cited extensive road construction, suppression of banditry, sanitary improvements, and fiscal reforms as permanent benefits of the occupation. It argued that the impending military evacuation refuted accusations that the United States harbored imperialistic designs in Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: El *Birmingham age-herald* comentó que la planeada retirada de las tropas estadounidenses tras siete años demostraba el éxito de la misión de Estados Unidos para estabilizar la República Dominicana y prepararla para el autogobierno. El editorial citó la extensa construcción de caminos, la supresión del bandolerismo, las mejoras sanitarias y las reformas fiscales como beneficios permanentes de la ocupación. Sostuvo que la inminente evacuación militar refutaba las acusaciones de que Estados Unidos albergaba designios imperialistas en Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: The *Alexandria gazette* reported that disagreements over a newly drafted electoral law delayed Dominican congressional elections and the scheduled withdrawal of American troops. Opponents contended the statute was overly complicated for the public, prompting efforts to amend the law to satisfy competing political factions. Special Commissioner Sumner Welles prepared to return to Santo Domingo to help mediate disputes and facilitate the transition to constitutional government.
records.summary_es: La *Alexandria gazette* informó que las discrepancias en torno a una nueva ley electoral recién redactada demoraron las elecciones legislativas dominicanas y la retirada prevista de las tropas estadounidenses. Los detractores sostenían que la ley era demasiado compleja para la ciudadanía, lo que motivó gestiones para modificarla y satisfacer a las distintas facciones políticas. El comisionado especial Sumner Welles se dispuso a regresar a Santo Domingo para mediar en las disputas y facilitar la transición hacia un gobierno constitucional.

records.summary_en: The *Washington daily news* published an editorial criticizing American assertions of non-imperialism, pointing to U.S. control across the Caribbean and Pacific, including customs administration in the Dominican Republic and marine occupation in Haiti. The piece derided official claims of purely benevolent motives while exercising regional dominance. It argued that Washington's treatment of its dependencies, particularly the curtailment of self-rule in the Philippines under General Leonard Wood, contradicted its anti-imperialist rhetoric.
records.summary_es: El *Washington daily news* publicó un editorial en el que criticaba las afirmaciones estadounidenses de no ejercer imperialismo, señalando el control de Estados Unidos en el Caribe y el Pacífico, incluida la administración de aduanas en la República Dominicana y la ocupación de la infantería de marina en Haití. El artículo ridiculizó los argumentos oficiales de motivaciones puramente benévolas mientras se ejercía el dominio regional. Sostuvo que el trato que Washington daba a sus dependencias, en particular el menoscabo de la autonomía en Filipinas bajo el general Leonard Wood, contradecía su retórica antiimperialista.

records.summary_en: The *Evening star* reported official statements declaring that the United States did not seek permanent dominion over Santo Domingo, but was actively preparing to evacuate its forces following free elections scheduled for mid-September. The statement explained that American policy in Haiti similarly aimed only to establish stability and competent self-governance following decades of revolution. U.S. authorities emphasized that they harbored no territorial ambitions on the island and would welcome the day American troops could safely withdraw.

El pronunciamiento explicaba que la política estadounidense en Haití aspiraba igualmente a restablecer la estabilidad y un gobierno autónomo competente tras décadas de revoluciones. Las autoridades de Washington hicieron hincapié en que carecían de ambiciones territoriales en la isla y celebrarían el momento en que los efectivos estadounidenses pudieran retirarse de forma segura.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield weekly Republican* published statements by Secretary of State Hughes affirming that the United States was committed to terminating its occupation of Santo Domingo and holding unsupervised elections in mid-September. Hughes maintained that American involvement in Haiti was aimed strictly at promoting stability and order after a century of chronic revolutions, disclaiming any territorial ambitions. He added that the United States maintained a consistent policy of fostering peace and responsible government across Central America and the Caribbean.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield weekly Republican* publicó declaraciones del secretario de Estado Hughes en las que ratificaba que Estados Unidos estaba comprometido a poner término a la ocupación de Santo Domingo y celebrar elecciones sin supervisión a mediados de septiembre. Hughes sostuvo que la intervención estadounidense en Haití procuraba estrictamente promover la estabilidad y el orden tras un siglo de revoluciones crónicas, descartando cualquier ambición territorial. Añadió que Estados Unidos mantenía una política invariable de fomentar la paz y gobiernos responsables en toda Centroamérica y el Caribe.

records.summary_en: The *Ventnor news* published a first-hand travel narrative praising the stabilization of Santo Domingo under the U.S. Marine Corps, highlighting administrative order and revenue collection. The author described motoring two hundred miles from Monte Cristi through Santiago to Santo Domingo City over modern mountain highways recently constructed by American military engineers. The account commended the marines for modernizing infrastructure, civilizing the region, and establishing public safety.
records.summary_es: El *Ventnor news* publicó una crónica de viaje testimonial que elogiaba la estabilización de Santo Domingo bajo el Cuerpo de Marines de Estados Unidos, destacando el orden administrativo y la recaudación fiscal. El autor describió su trayecto en automóvil de doscientas millas desde Monte Cristi pasando por Santiago hasta la ciudad de Santo Domingo a través de modernas carreteras de montaña recién construidas por ingenieros militares estadounidenses. El relato alabó a los marines por modernizar la infraestructura, pacificar la región y establecer la seguridad pública.

records.summary_en: The *Athens republique* reported on agricultural and social conditions in Haiti, noting that ninety-five percent of the population consisted of peasants who harvested coffee using primitive methods for export to Europe. The article cited the congressional inquiry's findings that rural Haitians were unfamiliar with modern tools such as plows and shovels, noting that laborers initially carried wheelbarrows on their heads during highway construction. It added that American occupation authorities were conducting agricultural education and building roads to promote economic development.
records.summary_es: El *Athens republique* informó sobre las condiciones sociales y agrícolas de Haití, señalando que el noventa y cinco por ciento de la población estaba compuesta por campesinos que cosechaban café mediante métodos rudimentarios para su exportación a Europa. El artículo citó las conclusiones de la investigación del Congreso que indicaban que los campesinos haitianos desconocían herramientas modernas como arados y palas, observando que los trabajadores inicialmente cargaban carretillas sobre la cabeza durante la construcción de carreteras. Agregó que las autoridades de ocupación estadounidenses impartían enseñanza agrícola y construían caminos para impulsar el desarrollo económico.

records.summary_en: The *Milwaukee leader* reported that Marine Corps Commandant Major General John A. Lejeune informed the Secretary of the Navy that no expeditionary combat duty was required in the Caribbean over the past year. Lejeune reported that the native gendarmerie in Haiti had successfully assumed policing duties with no banditry reported, ensuring peace and prosperity. In the Dominican Republic, he noted that the country was progressing smoothly toward self-government under the agreed bilateral evacuation plan.
records.summary_es: El *Milwaukee leader* informó que el comandante del Cuerpo de Marines, el mayor general John A. Lejeune, comunicó al secretario de la Armada que no se había requerido ninguna acción expedicionaria de combate en el Caribe durante el último año. Lejeune reportó que la gendarmería autóctona en Haití había asumido exitosamente las tareas de vigilancia sin que se registrara bandolerismo, asegurando la paz y la prosperidad. Respecto a la República Dominicana, señaló que el país avanzaba con normalidad hacia el autogobierno con arreglo al plan bilateral de evacuación pactado.

records.summary_en: The election described here was the Dominican Republic's first free election and the first held without bloodshed, after political and revolutionary factions reached an accord to support orderly, constitutional government. Washington's proposals for withdrawal require recognition of all acts of the military government, including the 1918 bond issue and the 1922 customs loan, and an assurance that the customs tariff will not be changed during the life of the 1922 loan without Washington's consent; after the convention is ratified, United States military forces will leave the republic.
records.summary_es: Las elecciones descritas fueron las primeras elecciones libres de la República Dominicana y las primeras celebradas sin derramamiento de sangre, después de que las facciones políticas y revolucionarias llegaran a un acuerdo para apoyar un gobierno ordenado y constitucional. Las propuestas de Washington para la retirada exigen el reconocimiento de todos los actos del gobierno militar, incluidas la emisión de bonos de 1918 y el empréstito aduanero de 1922, y la garantía de que el arancel de aduanas no se cambiará durante la vigencia del empréstito de 1922 sin el consentimiento de Washington; tras la ratificación de la convención, las fuerzas militares estadounidenses abandonarán la república.

El despacho manifestó su esperanza de una paz duradera, describiendo el notable potencial agrícola del país en azúcar, algodón, tabaco y frutas.

records.summary_en: The *Evening star* assessed the outlook for stability in Santo Domingo following the evacuation of American troops, noting general agreement that the nation deserved its opportunity for independent self-government. The article reviewed the background of intervention, recalling that the 1916 marine occupation followed decades of civil strife and the 1905 crisis when foreign creditors threatened naval force over unpaid debts. It described how the United States helped arrange a $20,000,000 refunding loan backed by an American receiver-general collecting customs to make monthly debt payments.
records.summary_es: El *Evening star* evaluó las perspectivas de estabilidad en Santo Domingo tras la evacuación de las tropas estadounidenses, destacando el consenso general de que la nación merecía su oportunidad de autogobierno independiente. El artículo recapituló los antecedentes de la intervención, recordando que la ocupación de los marines en 1916 siguió a decenios de contiendas civiles y a la crisis de 1905, cuando acreedores extranjeros amenazaron con recurrir a la fuerza naval por deudas impagas. Describió cómo Estados Unidos facilitó la gestión de un empréstito de refinanciamiento de 20 000 000 de dólares respaldado por un receptor general estadounidense encargado de recaudar las rentas aduaneras para efectuar pagos mensuales de la deuda.

records.summary_en: The *Perth Amboy evening news* detailed the 1905 financial convention with Santo Domingo, under which an American receiver deducted $100,000 monthly from customs duties to service a $20,000,000 loan while delivering the balance to the Dominican treasury. Although Dominican authorities promised fiscal restraint and agreed not to increase public debt without U.S. consent, recurring revolutions diverted revenues into military operations and generated massive unpaid debts. The article explained that the resulting financial collapse and threats to custom houses prompted the United States to deploy marines in 1916.
records.summary_es: El *Perth Amboy evening news* detalló la convención financiera de 1905 con Santo Domingo, según la cual un receptor estadounidense deducía 100 000 dólares mensuales de los derechos de aduana para amortizar un préstamo de 20 000 000 de dólares, transfiriendo el saldo restante a la tesorería dominicana. Aunque las autoridades dominicanas prometieron moderación presupuestaria y convinieron en no aumentar la deuda pública sin el consentimiento de Estados Unidos, sucesivas revoluciones desviaron los fondos hacia gastos bélicos y generaron deudas impagas colosales. El artículo explicaba que el colapso financiero resultante y las amenazas contra las aduanas condujeron a Estados Unidos a desplegar los marines en 1916.

records.headline: Ng, struggle of more than eight years by the people of
records.summary_en: The paper recounted a struggle of more than eight years by the people of Santo Domingo to regain the sovereignty they contended was taken from them when the United States placed the country under a large military force and set up a military government. After repeated Dominican efforts for a withdrawal, former American minister Horace G. Knowles started a campaign in 1920 to secure sovereignty for the Dominicans, and a United States Senate committee then inquired into the occupation in Santo Domingo, which was followed by an agreement for withdrawal of the forces. Sovereignty was restored and an election was held on March 15, with General Vasquez elected President, while about 1,800 marines remained in Santo Domingo and transports had begun evacuating the troops.
records.summary_es: El diario relataba una lucha de más de ocho años del pueblo de Santo Domingo por recuperar la soberanía que, según sostenía, le fue arrebatada cuando los Estados Unidos pusieron el país bajo una numerosa fuerza militar y establecieron un gobierno militar. Tras reiterados esfuerzos dominicanos por lograr la retirada, el exministro estadounidense Horace G. Knowles inició en 1920 una campaña para asegurar la soberanía de los dominicanos, y un comité del Senado de los Estados Unidos investigó luego la ocupación en Santo Domingo, lo que fue seguido de un acuerdo de retirada de las fuerzas. La soberanía fue restablecida y se celebraron elecciones el 15 de marzo, en las que resultó electo presidente el general Vásquez, mientras unos 1.800 infantes de marina permanecían aún en Santo Domingo y los transportes habían comenzado a evacuar a las tropas.

records.summary_en: The *Evening star* reported that the inauguration of General Horacio Vasquez brought a successful conclusion to over eight years of Dominican efforts to recover their national sovereignty from American military rule. The article recounted how sustained Dominican resistance and an advocacy campaign begun in 1920 by former minister Horace G. Knowles spurred a U.S. Senate investigation that culminated in an evacuation agreement. Full sovereignty was restored with the March 15 presidential election, and transports were carrying the remaining 1,800 marines back to the United States.
records.summary_es: El *Evening star* informó que la toma de posesión del general Horacio Vásquez puso un término exitoso a más de ocho años de gestiones dominicanas por recuperar su soberanía nacional frente al régimen militar estadounidense. El artículo relató cómo la sostenida resistencia dominicana y la campaña iniciada en 1920 por el exministro Horace G. Knowles impulsaron una investigación del Senado estadounidense que culminó en un acuerdo de evacuación. La plena soberanía se restableció con las elecciones presidenciales del 15 de marzo, y buques de transporte conducían a los 1 800 infantes de marina restantes de regreso a Estados Unidos.

records.full_text:
The Day in Washington

The house passed a bill to promote production and conservation of helium.

A bill for a new American embassy and consulate general in Tokio passed the house.

The senate rejected a proposal to withhold funds to maintain marines in Haiti.

A senate elections sub-committee recommended the seating of Senator Mayfield, democrat, Texas.

The senate called on Secretary Hughes for information on the Paris reparations agreement.

Heber H. Votaw, brother-in-law of the late President Harding resigned as superintendent of prisons.

The naval bill, containing a request that President Coolidge call an arms conference, passed the senate.

Members of the senate foreign relations committee and others were invited to a night dinner at the White House.

The senate ratified treaties with the Dominican republic on evacuation of American troops and refunding of the Dominican debt.

Senator Shipstead, farmer-labor, Minnesota, charged the increased prices for stocks and bonds were the result of a “stock gambling boom.”

Senator McKellar, democrat, Tennessee, presented a resolution asking President Coolidge to investigate whether England violated the arms treaty in building the battleships Rodney and Nelson.

Justice department took steps to subpoena Senator Wheeler, democrat, Montana, to appear before a grand jury here in connection with the home state indictment against him.

records.summary_en: The *Omaha morning bee* reported details of the treaty ratified by the U.S. Senate refunding the Dominican national debt of $25,000,000. The pact authorized the U.S. president to appoint a general receiver to collect all Dominican customs duties, applying proceeds to receivership expenses, interest, and sinking fund amortization before remitting any surplus to the Dominican government. Under an additional article, the Dominican Republic was prohibited from increasing its public debt without American consent until all refunding bonds were fully paid.

Conforme a un artículo adicional, se prohibía a la República Dominicana aumentar su deuda pública sin consentimiento estadounidense hasta que la totalidad de los bonos de refinanciamiento quedara saldada.

records.summary_en: The *daily worker* published a sharp critique of American policy in the Caribbean, condemning a peace society editorial that defended military intervention in Haiti and the Dominican Republic. The paper described the Haitian administration as a puppet regime upheld by American arms, asserting that a secret treaty extension planned to keep U.S. forces in Haiti until 1935. It similarly denounced the 1916 military takeover of the Dominican Republic, rejecting claims that financial collapse justified imperialist intervention on behalf of capitalist interests.

El rotativo describió al gobierno haitiano como un régimen títere sostenido por las armas estadounidenses, afirmando que una prórroga secreta de tratados contemplaba mantener tropas de Estados Unidos en Haití hasta 1935. De igual modo, denunció la toma del poder militar en la República Dominicana en 1916, rechazando el argumento de que el colapso financiero justificara una intervención imperialista en favor de intereses capitalistas.

records.summary_en: The *daily worker* criticized the $25,000,000 loan floated in the United States for the Dominican Republic, claiming that customs revenues collected by the American receiver-general served primarily to enrich Wall Street bankers. The article alleged that when Santo Domingo began retiring its debts too quickly, Secretary of State Hughes made troop withdrawal contingent on treaties that ratified military decrees, expanded receivership powers, and secured a new loan. It asserted that these treaties were secretly negotiated in 1924 prior to American military evacuation and national elections.

One treaty confirmed all the decrees issued by North Americans during the occupation of the Dominican Republic ending in 1922, and the other related to customs collections.

Un tratado confirmaba todos los decretos emitidos por los norteamericanos durante la ocupación de la República Dominicana que terminó en 1922, y el otro se refería a la recaudación de aduanas.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported on political controversy in Haiti surrounding President Borno's eligibility, his decree extending the Council of State to secure reelection, and extended American financial control under the 1915 treaty. The article also noted heavy outward migration among Haitian farmers, with tens of thousands departing for Cuba and the Dominican Republic. An estimated 150,000 natives had emigrated since the American occupation began, resulting in a local labor scarcity.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó sobre la controversia política en Haití en torno a la elegibilidad del presidente Borno, su decreto de prórroga del Consejo de Estado para asegurarse la reelección y la extensión del control financiero estadounidense bajo el tratado de 1915. El artículo también señaló una intensa emigración de agricultores haitianos, con decenas de miles partiendo hacia Cuba y la República Dominicana. Se estimaba que unos 150 000 naturales habían emigrado desde el inicio de la ocupación estadounidense, lo que provocó escasez de mano de obra local.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published an account describing the conditions of Haitian peasants under the American occupation. The report asserted that the occupation protected rural workers from forced military impressment and bandits, allowing them to farm and sell produce freely. It stated that peasants were better fed, clothed, and receiving medical treatment at free clinics, despite widespread illiteracy.

El reportaje afirmaba que la ocupación protegía a los trabajadores rurales del reclutamiento militar forzoso y de los bandoleros, permitiéndoles cultivar y vender sus productos libremente. Indicaba que los campesinos estaban mejor alimentados, mejor vestidos y recibían atención médica en dispensarios gratuitos, a pesar del analfabetismo generalizado.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported on efforts to prepare Haiti for eventual American withdrawal by training native personnel across various government departments. Haitian nationals were increasingly staffing public works, sanitary services, customs administration, and agricultural engineering, while Haitians comprised about half the commissioned officers in the gendarmerie. Concurrently, the American military presence had been reduced to an 800-man marine force.

En forma paralela, la presencia militar estadounidense se había reducido a un contingente de 800 infantes de marina.

records.summary_en: The *Pocahontas Times* recounted the history of U.S. intervention in Haiti, noting that seven revolutions between 1910 and 1915 culminated in the killing of President Sam and the landing of U.S. Marines. Under the 1916 treaty establishing a 20-year protectorate, the article stated that order and prosperity were established with minimal risk of revolution. By October, American military forces had been reduced to 800 marines supporting an armed native constabulary.
records.summary_es: El *Pocahontas Times* relató la historia de la intervención estadounidense en Haití, recordando que siete revoluciones entre 1910 y 1915 culminaron con la muerte violenta del presidente Sam y el desembarco de los marines estadounidenses. Bajo el tratado de 1916 que estableció un protectorado de 20 años, el artículo señalaba que se habían implantado el orden y la prosperidad con mínimo riesgo de revolución. Para octubre, las tropas militares estadounidenses se habían reducido a 800 marines que apoyaban a una fuerza policial nativa armada.

records.summary_en: The *New Britain Herald* reported on extensive infrastructure modernization in Haiti under President Borno, including more than 1,000 miles of paved roads, new schools, hospitals, and lighthouses. A concrete highway connecting Port-au-Prince with Santo Domingo had reached the border on the Haitian side, promising to reduce travel time between the capitals from days to hours once the Dominican section was completed. The report also highlighted telephone network expansion, tariff revisions to promote trade with the United States, and the continuing presence of 800 American marines.
records.summary_es: El *New Britain Herald* informó sobre la vasta modernización de infraestructura en Haití bajo el presidente Borno, con más de 1 000 millas de carreteras pavimentadas, nuevas escuelas, hospitales y faros. Una carretera de hormigón que comunicaba Puerto Príncipe con Santo Domingo había alcanzado la frontera del lado haitiano, prometiendo reducir el tiempo de viaje entre ambas capitales de días a horas una vez concluido el tramo dominicano. El despacho destacó asimismo la ampliación de la red telefónica, modificaciones arancelarias para estimular el comercio con Estados Unidos y la continua presencia de 800 infantes de marina estadounidenses.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported the arrival in Washington of Dr. Ángel Morales, the newly appointed Dominican Minister to the United States, and his wife. Dr. Morales, who succeeded Dr. José del Carmen Ariza, had previously served as Dominican Minister to Paris, vice president of the League of Nations, and Dominican Secretary of the Interior. records.full_text:
REPORT STATES BOSS OF HAITI FINDS ALL O. K.

By Louis R. Lautier

During the past year the American treaty officials have been directing their efforts toward increasing the productive wealth of Haiti to the ultimate end of strengthening and improving the general economic condition, Brig. Gen. John H. Russell, American High Commissioner to Haiti, declared in his fifth annual report to the Secretary of State, which was made public by the State Department Monday.

In addition, he reported, the Haitian Government and the treaty officials have continued the general governing program for the stablization of Haitian finances, the maintenance of law and order, the construction of public works, and the improvement of the public health service.

A bumper coffee crop in a period of exceptionally high and abnormal prices and the re-election

BOSS OF HAITI REPORTS EVERYTHING IS O. K.

(Continued from page 1)

of President Borno contributed to the stability and the prosperity of Haiti in 1926, General Russell stated.

Business Confidence
“Confidence among business men, which, on account of the usual sensational rumors which precede a presidential election in Haiti, had been trembling in the balance, was restored immediately upon the promulgation of the results of the election,” General Russell reports. “This fact contributed largely in making the past year the greatest in the history of the Republic from a financial and business point of view.”

As a result of the visit of President Borno to the United States in last June he returned to Haiti imbued with a stronger desire to further the progress and development of his country and to make it a republic in being as well as in name, General Russell states.

The Haitian judiciary system is in need of complete renovation. “The courts are, if such could be possible, less effective than ever and their inefficiency and incompetency more notorious,” General Russell reports. “Trials by jury are farcial.”

There has been no reduction in the United States forces in Haiti. They consist of a skeleton brigade of United States marines and a mine sweeper of 950 tons displacement. Martial law has only been exercised upon the rarest occasions, says General Russell.

The customs receipts for the past year were unprecedented. The total receipts amounted to $9,072,929.62. Of this amount the sum of $8,118,996.35 was from custom revenues.

The Public Debt
The actual debt reducing amortization was $1,384,836.90. The required reduction was only $717,218.36. The total public debt amounts to $18,849,000.

As a result of the favorable year just closed the Haitian people have been benefited materially, says General Russell. They are better fed, better clothed, and better housed than ever before.

The commerce of Haiti during the past year has been most satisfactory, it is reported. There has been a healthy growth of shipping entering the harbors of the Republic and a gradual increase in traffic across the Dominican border.

Educational Ideas
The Haitian Government believes that its educational system should be designed to furnish agricultural education to the rural and industrial education to the urban population, the American high commissioner states. He says that “the Haitian Government considers it not only essential but vital that the Haitian people be taught to use their hands.”

General Russell also states in his report:
“The efforts that have been made and are being made to foster the further increase of production in Haiti will soon show results and with the passing of an appropriate revenue law and the renovation of the Haitian judiciary, the advance toward the stabilization of government will be most marked.

“As in past years President Borno has co-operated in every way for the carrying out of the provisions of the treaty of 1915, and has made the marked improvement of last year possible.

“The treaty officials have consistently, tactfully and energetically carried out their duties and the efficient management of the respective departments under their control has largely contributed to the remarkable progress which is being made in the bringing of happiness and prosperity to the Haitian people.”

Statements Contradictory
Statements in the report of General Russell are contradictory to those made upon the floor of the Senate by Senator William H. King, Democrat, of Utah, who was recently barred by President Borno from visiting Haiti because of derogatory remarks made by the Senator concerning the Haitian president in demanding that the American forces be withdrawn from the island republic.

In a speech in the Senate on February 1 last, Senator King declared:
“First, let it be remembered that by every standard of morality and justice there was no treaty. Our forces were in possession of the country. We had destroyed the legislative branch of the government and taken possession of all governmental agencies of the country. We set up a shadow government. It was not a Haitian government. A few Haitians were put into positions, but they were named by Naval officers of the United States and they did the will of those who named them. One of them we called a President, and he was required to sign a treaty prepared by the United States.”

Senator King described the re-election of President Borno as a farce. This “shadow president,” he said, was chosen by members of an assembly which he had appointed. “The Haitian people,” he declared, “are in a condition of political servitude.”

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that Horace G. Knowles, former U.S. minister to the Dominican Republic and currently a Dominican consul, strongly condemned U.S. interventions in Nicaragua, Haiti, and Santo Domingo during a speech in Northampton. Knowles told the Hampshire County Progressive Club that these military actions constituted unauthorized acts of war undertaken by the executive government without congressional approval.

Knowles manifestó ante el Club Progresista del Condado de Hampshire que estas acciones militares constituían actos de guerra no autorizados y emprendidos por el poder ejecutivo sin el consentimiento del Congreso.

El editorial argumentó que semejante retórica contradecía las intervenciones militares activas de su gobierno, incluidos los bombardeos aéreos en Nicaragua y el mantenimiento de derechos de intervención en Cuba.

records.summary_en: Col. Charles A. Lindbergh took off from Santo Domingo at 11 a.m. on February 6 for Port-au-Prince, Haiti, on a 160-mile route flown entirely across land, as he neared the end of his goodwill flight to the Pan American conference at Havana. The night before, he had been guest of honor at a brilliant ball at the presidential palace, attended by the diplomatic body, members of the government and prominent society figures.

La noche anterior había sido el invitado de honor en un brillante baile en el palacio presidencial, al que asistieron el cuerpo diplomático, miembros del gobierno y destacadas figuras de la sociedad.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reviewed historical instances of U.S. supervision of Caribbean elections, citing American oversight of Dominican congressional elections in 1913 and presidential elections in 1914. Following the November 1916 military intervention, the country was occupied without elections until 1924, when voting was conducted under close American observation as troops prepared to depart.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* repasó los precedentes históricos de supervisión electoral estadounidense en el Caribe, citando la fiscalización de las elecciones legislativas de 1913 y las presidenciales de 1914 en la República Dominicana. Tras la intervención militar de noviembre de 1916, el país permaneció ocupado y sin elecciones hasta 1924, año en que se efectuaron votaciones bajo atenta observación estadounidense mientras las tropas preparaban su partida.

records.headline: The former vice president, who is himself a big Chicago banker
records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* criticized former Vice President Charles G. Dawes's financial mission to Santo Domingo, characterizing it as an imperialist survey designed to secure additional American loans and control. The article noted that Dominican customs had been managed by the United States for twenty-five years to service twenty million dollars in debt, while predicting growing popular resistance against foreign financial dominance across Latin America.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Worker* criticó la misión financiera del exvicepresidente Charles G. Dawes en Santo Domingo, calificándola de estudio imperialista ideado para afianzar nuevos préstamos y un mayor control estadounidense. El artículo remarcó que las aduanas dominicanas habían sido administradas por Estados Unidos durante veinticinco años para solventar una deuda de veinte millones de dólares, al tiempo que vaticinaba una creciente resistencia popular contra la hegemonía financiera extranjera en América Latina.

Destacó que la disolución del poder legislativo haitiano a manos de los infantes de marina estadounidenses había eliminado todo contrapeso representativo sobre la gestión del comisionado.

records.headline: There followed a long period of disturbed politics in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Times* summarized historical relations between the United States and the Dominican Republic, recalling President Grant's rejected annexation treaty and the 1906 financial commission that halved unjustified foreign debt. It stated that persistent revolutionary turmoil led to the 1916 U.S. military intervention and administrative reforms in finance, schooling, and transportation. The account noted that American military forces completed their withdrawal in July 1924 after restoring stability.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Times* resumió las relaciones históricas entre Estados Unidos y la República Dominicana, recordando el fallido tratado de anexión del presidente Grant y la comisión financiera de 1906 que redujo a la mitad la deuda externa injustificada. Declaró que los recurrentes conflictos revolucionarios motivaron la intervención militar estadounidense de 1916 y reformas administrativas en finanzas, educación y transportes. La reseña destacó que las fuerzas militares estadounidenses concluyeron su retirada en julio de 1924 tras restablecer la estabilidad.

records.summary_en: The *South Bend News-Times* reviewed the history of American involvement in the Dominican Republic, beginning with the failed annexation treaty under President Grant and the 1906 debt adjustment. The article recounted how political unrest caused the establishment of a U.S. military government in 1916 that initiated fiscal and infrastructural improvements. It noted that American troops eventually completed their evacuation from the republic in July 1924.

El artículo refirió cómo los disturbios políticos condujeron al establecimiento de un gobierno militar de Estados Unidos en 1916, el cual emprendió mejoras fiscales y de infraestructura. Indicó que las tropas estadounidenses completaron finalmente su evacuación de la república en julio de 1924.

records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* reported that strike movements against the Haitian administration were spreading across the country, according to dispatches from the American High Commissioner. Customs employees in Port-au-Prince stopped work and street demonstrations spread to Cap-Haïtien, prompting fears of further disorders in Aux Cayes. The High Commissioner requested that additional U.S. Marines be held in readiness to protect American lives if conditions deteriorated.
records.summary_es: El *Washington Daily News* informó que movimientos huelguísticos en contra de la administración haitiana se propagaban por todo el país, según informes del alto comisionado estadounidense. Empleados de aduanas en Puerto Príncipe suspendieron sus labores y las manifestaciones callejeras alcanzaron Cabo Haitiano, desatando temores de nuevos desórdenes en Los Cayos (Aux Cayes). El alto comisionado solicitó que se mantuvieran en alerta infantes de marina adicionales para proteger las vidas estadounidenses en caso de un empeoramiento de la situación.

records.full_text:
DOMINICAN REBELLION STARTS AS HOOVER COMMISSION DEPARTS

Haiti Commission Sails From Key West; Marines Available to Put Down Any Disorder

Departure of President Hoover's Haitian commission today from Key West coincided with reports of a rebellion in the Dominican Republic which shares the island of Santo Domingo with Haiti.

The U. S. has assumed responsibilities under the existing Dominican-American treaty which might be made the basis for intervention in the Dominican Republic if disorder persists.

President Hoover said today his reports of revolutionary conditions contained no information that there is any danger to the life or liberty of Americans at the present time.

Marines Ready
Marines are available in Haiti and a force could be dispatched to the other part of the island.

Treaty relations between the U. S. and the Dominican Republic are financial. Article I authorizes the President of the U. S. to appoint a General Receiver of Dominican Customs, and Article II says:

“The government of the U. S. will give to the General Receiver and his assistants such protection as it may find to be requisite for the performance of their duties.”

Natives Killed
The President ordered additional marines to Haiti after disorders last December, but subsequently recalled them. Several natives were killed by the marines. The Haitian Commission, headed by Cameron Forbes, former Governor General of the Philippines, is sailing on the U. S. S. Rochester.

Marines were sent to the Dominican republic in 1916 to quiet a serious uprising. They formed a military government which continued in office until 1924 when Rear Admiral Samuel S. Robinson, military governor turned the government over to the newly elected president, Horacio Vasquez, who still is in office.

Extent Unknown
Reports received by the State Department from Minister Charles B. Curtis indicated rebellion against the Vasquez governments and said Senora Vasquez had sought safety in the American Legation. First reports to the department did not define the origin or extent of the disorder.

Dominican affairs have been tranquil for 10 years. The present treaty relationship with the U. S. began in 1907. Between 1865 and 1904 domestic disorder contributed to the creation of a national debt of $32,000,000, much of which was represented by bonds held in European countries.

Roosevelt Acted
In 1905 there were rumors that several European governments contemplated vigorous action in behalf of the bondholders. President Roosevelt negotiated a treaty which was rejected by the Senate because one clause was interpreted as establishing a protectorate.

Roosevelt then negotiated an executive agreement which was put in force, and subsequently put in treaty form.

records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* reported that following the marine withdrawal, Dominican President Vásquez assumed dictatorial powers that facilitated American corporate control of over 300,000 acres of sugar plantations. The article cited Charles G. Dawes's 1928 mission to structure the Dominican budget for repayments to the National City Bank under the customs treaty. It further claimed that High Commissioner Russell in Haiti feared the Dominican rebellion would inspire Haitian peasants to revolt against President Borno's administration.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Worker* denunció que, tras la retirada de los marines, el presidente dominicano Vásquez asumió facultades dictatoriales que facilitaron el control corporativo estadounidense sobre más de 300 000 acres de plantaciones azucareras. El artículo citó la misión de Charles G. Dawes en 1928 para estructurar el presupuesto dominicano de cara a los reembolsos al National City Bank bajo el tratado aduanero. Asimismo, afirmó que el alto comisionado Russell en Haití temía que la rebelión dominicana incitara a los campesinos haitianos a alzarse contra el gobierno del presidente Borno.

records.summary_en: The *South Bend News-Times* reported that rebel chief Rafael Estrella Ureña entered Santo Domingo to negotiate with President Vásquez and U.S. Minister Charles B. Curtis following the capture of northern and eastern cities by 4,000 insurgent troops. Rebel gunfire around the central plaza and cathedral caused alarm among hotel guests, while government operations ceased. Acting as mediator, Curtis sought a constitutional compromise by appointing a new secretary of the interior who could legally succeed Vásquez.

Actuando como mediador, Curtis procuró un acuerdo constitucional mediante la designación de un nuevo secretario de Interior que pudiera suceder legítimamente a Vásquez.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that insurgent troops occupied Santo Domingo while Army Commander General Trujillo held Fort Ozama before joining peace talks at the American Legation. Rebel leaders Rafael Estrella Ureña and Desiderio Arias demanded constitutional elections on May 15 without Vásquez as a candidate. U.S. Minister Charles B. Curtis stated that Washington would not recognize a de facto regime, prompting discussions to designate Trujillo or Ángel Morales as provisional president upon Vásquez's resignation.

Los líderes rebeldes Rafael Estrella Ureña y Desiderio Arias exigieron la celebración de elecciones constitucionales el 15 de mayo sin la candidatura de Vásquez. El ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis manifestó que Washington no reconocería un régimen de facto, lo que motivó deliberaciones para designar a Trujillo o a Ángel Morales como presidente provisional tras la renuncia de Vásquez.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that Rafael Estrella Ureña assumed the provisional presidency of the Dominican Republic after negotiating with Fort Ozama commander General Rafael Trujillo. Outgoing President Horacio Vásquez requested legislative permission to travel abroad due to ill health, while Trujillo declined consideration for the presidency. U.S. Minister Charles B. Curtis, who had insisted on constitutional continuity, expressed satisfaction with the arrangement as rebel forces secured political control.

El ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis, quien había insistido en mantener la continuidad constitucional, expresó su conformidad con el acuerdo mientras las fuerzas rebeldes consolidaban el control político.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo on September 6 reports that relief agencies reaching the stricken…
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo on September 6 reports that relief agencies reaching the stricken city found the horror of Wednesday's hurricane worse rather than better: an estimated 1,500 to 2,000 persons dead, more than 5,000 injured, 30,000 homeless, and of 10,000 buildings only 400 left standing, with property damage to pass $20,000,000. There is no water fit to drink, the dead are being collected and burned in heaps and in concrete cisterns used as funeral pyres, relief planes have brought some supplies and doctors from Port-au-Prince, Havana, the United States and Porto Rico, and the president has stopped food profiteering by ordering all food sold at cost under pain of court martial, while Santiago, La Vega and Puerto Plata are reported undamaged.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Associated Press desde Santo Domingo del 6 de septiembre informa que las agencias de socorro que llegaron a la ciudad devastada encontraron el horror del huracán del miércoles peor en vez de mejor: se estima que murieron entre 1,500 y 2,000 personas, más de 5,000 resultaron heridas, 30,000 quedaron sin hogar y de 10,000 edificios solo 400 quedaron en pie, con daños materiales que pasarán de $20,000,000. No hay agua apta para beber, los muertos están siendo recogidos y quemados en montones y en cisternas de concreto usadas como piras funerarias, aviones de socorro han traído algunos suministros y médicos desde Puerto Príncipe, La Habana, los Estados Unidos y Puerto Rico, y el presidente ha detenido la especulación con los alimentos ordenando que toda la comida se venda al costo bajo pena de consejo de guerra, mientras se informa que Santiago, La Vega y Puerto Plata no sufrieron daños.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported on catastrophic devastation in Santo Domingo caused by a hurricane that demolished poorer residential districts across a 160-square-mile area. President Rafael Trujillo assumed personal command of military forces to maintain order, clear debris, and organize relief before the arrival of outside assistance. Initial relief ships from Puerto Rico and commercial cable vessels landed medical units and provided emergency tents for 2,000 homeless survivors.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* informó sobre la devastación catastrófica en Santo Domingo causada por un huracán que demolió los distritos residenciales más humildes en un área de 160 millas cuadradas. El presidente Rafael Trujillo asumió el mando personal de las fuerzas militares para mantener el orden, despejar escombros y organizar el socorro antes de la llegada de ayuda exterior. Primeros barcos de auxilio procedentes de Puerto Rico y buques de tendido de cable comercial desembarcaron brigadas médicas y proveyeron tiendas de campaña de emergencia para 2 000 damnificados sin hogar.

Swift. A 1,000-bed tent hospital was established under U.S. Navy Commander L. W. Johnson to perform surgeries and treat injured residents. records.summary_en: The *Ronan Pioneer* reviewed Latin American political changes in 1930, noting that revolutionary upheavals began in February when Dominican President Horacio Vásquez sought reelection. Vásquez was forced from office after brief skirmishes and succeeded temporarily by General Estrella Ureña. In subsequent elections held on May 16, General Rafael Trujillo was elected president, officially taking office three months later.
records.summary_es: El *Ronan Pioneer* repasó las transformaciones políticas latinoamericanas en 1930, destacando que las conmociones revolucionarias se iniciaron en febrero cuando el presidente dominicano Horacio Vásquez pretendió reelegirse. Vásquez fue forzado a renunciar tras breves escaramuzas y sucedido transitoriamente por el general Estrella Ureña. En los comicios posteriores del 16 de mayo, el general Rafael Trujillo resultó electo presidente, asumiendo oficialmente el cargo tres meses más tarde.

records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* condemned U.S. support for General Trujillo's regime in the Dominican Republic, noting heavy American capital investments and the use of U.S. currency on the island. Citing declarations from the Caribbean Red Aid, the publication alleged that Dominican authorities arbitrarily arrested workers as vagrants to condemn them to forced labor in brutal prisons. The editorial demanded that U.S. officials apply the same forced-labor import bans to Dominican sugar, cocoa, and tobacco that were imposed against Soviet imports.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Worker* condenó el respaldo estadounidense al régimen del general Trujillo en la República Dominicana, resaltando las cuantiosas inversiones de capital norteamericano y el uso de la moneda de Estados Unidos en la isla. Citando declaraciones del Socorro Rojo del Caribe, el diario denunció que las autoridades dominicanas arrestaban arbitrariamente a trabajadores bajo cargos de vagancia para destinarlos a trabajos forzados en prisiones brutales. El editorial exigió a los funcionarios de Washington aplicar al azúcar, cacao y tabaco dominicanos las mismas restricciones de importación por trabajo forzado impuestas a los productos soviéticos.

records.summary_en: The *Douglas Daily Dispatch* reported that Secretary of State Henry L. Stimson contemplated an early withdrawal of U.S. Marines from Haiti, dependent on the efficiency of the local national guard. Stimson stated that Washington aimed to establish a system similar to the Dominican Republic, where security was entrusted to native forces while an American customs receiver managed public revenue. He noted that financial adviser Sidney de la Rue and the guard would safeguard American bondholders.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Times* reported that a severe hurricane was advancing toward the Dominican Republic and Haiti after striking Puerto Rico with winds up to 100 miles per hour. The storm had caused one fatality and injured several others in San Juan before entering the passage toward Hispaniola. The report noted that this disturbance was separate from a deadly cyclone that destroyed the city of Belize.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Times* informó que un fuerte huracán avanzaba hacia la República Dominicana y Haití tras azotar a Puerto Rico con vientos de hasta 100 millas por hora. La tempestad había ocasionado una muerte y varios heridos en San Juan antes de enfilar por el canal hacia La Española. El despacho precisó que este temporal era independiente del mortífero ciclón que arrasó la ciudad de Belice.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the Dominican Republic suspended principal amortization payments on its foreign debt while maintaining interest payments, diverting customs revenues to internal operational expenses. Officials viewed the move as a breach of the 1924 treaty governing the American customs receivership, which required U.S. consent for debt modifications. The article noted that American private investments totaled nearly $70,000,000 alongside over $17,000,000 in Dominican government bonds.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que la República Dominicana suspendió los pagos de amortización del capital de su deuda externa aunque mantuvo los pagos por concepto de intereses, desviando las rentas aduaneras hacia gastos operativos internos. Funcionarios consideraron la medida como una violación del tratado de 1924 que regía la receptoría general de aduanas estadounidense, el cual exigía el consentimiento de Estados Unidos para cualquier modificación de la deuda. El artículo señaló que las inversiones privadas norteamericanas sumaban cerca de 70 000 000 de dólares, además de más de 17 000 000 de dólares en bonos del Estado dominicano.

records.full_text:
THIS IS NEWS

At least one solvent country has been discovered in these days of unbalanced budgets and record breaking deficits. At Santo Domingo the Treasury of the Dominican Republic has announced that the government of President Trujillo has rigidly maintained its budget during the first six months of 1932, and that payment on foreign and other debts has been promptly met. The administration of this Carribean country is looked upon as a model by our State Department.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported favorably on conditions in the Dominican Republic on the eve of its sixty-ninth national anniversary, noting that President Trujillo's government had strengthened internal order and foreign credit. In contrast to political instability and financial defaults across much of Latin America since 1930, the commentary noted that the Dominican Republic maintained a balanced budget and steady governance. This administrative stability was credited with bolstering public support at home and prestige abroad.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó favorablemente sobre la situación en la República Dominicana en vísperas de su sexagésimo noveno aniversario nacional, señalando que el gobierno del presidente Trujillo había fortalecido el orden interno y el crédito exterior. En contraste con la inestabilidad política y las cesaciones de pagos en gran parte de América Latina desde 1930, el comentario destacó que la República Dominicana mantenía un presupuesto equilibrado y una gobernabilidad firme. Se atribuyó a esta estabilidad administrativa el haber afianzado el respaldo popular en el país y el prestigio en el extranjero.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published a profile of Dominican President Rafael Trujillo on the republic's sixty-ninth national anniversary, recounting his rise from enlistment during the U.S. Marine Corps occupation to top commander of the Dominican Army within a decade. The article highlighted his friendly relations with the United States and his employment of American technical advisers to overhaul national finances and develop natural resources. It also commended Trujillo's programs to diversify Dominican agriculture beyond its four traditional export crops.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* publicó una semblanza del presidente dominicano Rafael Trujillo con motivo del sexagésimo noveno aniversario nacional de la república, relatando su ascenso desde que se alistó durante la ocupación del Cuerpo de Marines de Estados Unidos hasta convertirse en comandante en jefe del ejército dominicano en el lapso de una década. El artículo destacó sus relaciones cordiales con Estados Unidos y la contratación de asesores técnicos estadounidenses para sanear las finanzas nacionales y explotar los recursos naturales. Asimismo, elogió los planes de Trujillo encaminados a diversificar la agricultura dominicana más allá de sus cuatro cultivos tradicionales de exportación.

records.headline: Pulliam is returning to his job in Santo Domingo, and “on
records.summary_en: An effort to remove William E. Pulliam as collector of customs in the Dominican Republic failed, and the State Department announced that Pulliam is returning to his job in Santo Domingo and is being retained in recognition of his merit and capable work. The decision is described as a rebuke to the regime of President Rafael Trujillo, after Dominican Minister Despradel and Counselor Espaillat had represented that Pulliam was persona non grata. Pulliam served as collector from 1907 to 1913 and from 1921 to the present, and his honesty is widely praised.

Pulliam como recaudador de aduanas en la República Dominicana, y el Departamento de Estado anunció que Pulliam regresa a su puesto en Santo Domingo y es mantenido en reconocimiento a su mérito y su capaz labor. La decisión se describe como un desaire al régimen del presidente Rafael Trujillo, después de que el ministro dominicano Despradel y el consejero Espaillat representaran que Pulliam era persona non grata. Pulliam fue recaudador de 1907 a 1913 y desde 1921 hasta el presente, y su honestidad es ampliamente elogiada.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reviewed press commentary regarding the treaty providing for the withdrawal of U.S. Marines from Haiti by late 1934 and the transfer of the constabulary to native officers. Quoting the *Express*, the article suggested that Haiti could follow the example of the neighboring Dominican Republic, which was progressing under President Trujillo after overcoming years of internal conflict. Other editorials praised the marine occupation for establishing urban sanitation and internal order in Haiti.

Otros editoriales encomiaron la ocupación de los marines por haber implantado el saneamiento urbano y el orden interno en Haití.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reviewed the historical events of the 1915 U.S. intervention in Haiti under Admiral Caperton following the killing of the Haitian president. The article recounted how Caperton took control of Port-au-Prince, suppressed opposition, and urged troop deployments to secure a financial treaty desired by the State Department and the National City Bank. It described how American forces secured the election of President Dartiguenave to ensure ratification under marine guard.

Describió cómo las fuerzas estadounidenses aseguraron la elección del presidente Dartiguenave para garantizar la ratificación bajo custodia de los marines.

records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* reported that new Haitian envoy Blanchet arrived in Washington seeking tariff reductions on Haitian rum while details surfaced of a secret border arrangement between Haiti and the Dominican Republic. According to the report, Dominican President Rafael Trujillo offered on October 18 to abandon territorial claims in exchange for political concessions to bolster his regime. Soon afterward, Haitian authorities deported five exiled Dominican political opponents of Trujillo from a border town alongside a Russian laborer branded a communist.

Poco después, autoridades haitianas deportaron desde una localidad fronteriza a cinco opositores políticos dominicanos exiliados de Trujillo junto a un obrero ruso tachado de comunista.

records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó sobre una conferencia ilustrada a cargo del mayor Sawders en la que detalló ciudades del Caribe, plantaciones azucareras y monumentos históricos. Entre los temas históricos exhibidos en diapositivas a color figuraron fortificaciones coloniales, los lagos de asfalto de Trinidad y la tumba de Cristóbal Colón en Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published a profile of Dominican President Rafael Trujillo, noting his rise from private to captain in the Marine-trained constabulary and his disciplined administrative methods. The article detailed his measures eliminating government automobiles for legislators and dropping 500 redundant employees from the state payroll. Despite the depression cutting government revenues by more than half, the piece credited Trujillo and his financial adviser with balancing the national budget and maintaining civic order.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* publicó una semblanza del presidente dominicano Rafael Trujillo, destacando su ascenso de soldado raso a capitán en la guardia entrenada por los marines y sus métodos de disciplina administrativa. El artículo detalló sus medidas para suprimir los automóviles oficiales para legisladores y dar de baja a 500 empleados innecesarios de la nómina estatal. A pesar de que la depresión redujo los ingresos fiscales a más de la mitad, la nota atribuyó a Trujillo y a su consejero financiero el haber equilibrado el presupuesto nacional y preservado el orden cívico.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported on the accelerated withdrawal of U.S. Marines from Haiti, advancing their final departure two months ahead of schedule following President Roosevelt's visit to Cap-Haïtien. The article recalled the nineteen-year military occupation initiated under Woodrow Wilson in 1915 to suppress rebel factions. It observed that the departing marines left behind an efficient native constabulary, modern barracks, and improved municipal conditions in Port-au-Prince.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó sobre la acelerada retirada de los infantes de marina estadounidenses de Haití, adelantándose su salida definitiva dos meses a lo previsto tras la visita del presidente Roosevelt a Cabo Haitiano. El artículo recordó los diecinueve años de ocupación militar iniciada bajo Woodrow Wilson en 1915 para sofocar facciones rebeldes. Observó que los marines en retirada dejaban tras de sí un eficiente cuerpo policial nativo, cuarteles modernos y mejores condiciones municipales en Puerto Príncipe.

records.headline: The Foreign Bondholders Protec tive Council, headed by Reuben Clark, jr
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the Dominican government and the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council agreed to extend the maturity dates of two $10,000,000 bond issues to ease debt repayment. Under the plan, 5.5 percent bonds maturing in 1942 were extended twenty years, while 1940 bonds were extended to 1970, reestablishing the 1924 financial accord. Acting Secretary of State Phillips praised the Dominican Republic's determination to meet its debt obligations despite worldwide economic distress.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el gobierno dominicano y el Foreign Bondholders Protective Council acordaron extender las fechas de vencimiento de dos emisiones de bonos de 10.000.000 de dólares para facilitar el pago de la deuda. Conforme al plan, los bonos al 5,5 por ciento con vencimiento en 1942 se prorrogaron veinte años, mientras que los de 1940 se extendieron hasta 1970, restableciendo el acuerdo financiero de 1924. El secretario de Estado interino Phillips elogió la determinación de la República Dominicana de cumplir con sus obligaciones de deuda a pesar de la crisis económica mundial.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that ousted Cuban dictator Gerardo Machado was preparing to leave his refuge in the Dominican Republic after President Rafael Trujillo advised him to depart. Trujillo had previously granted Machado an extensive estate and extraterritorial status protected by 130 Cuban guards, but faced threats of retaliation from the Cuban government. Machado was reportedly seeking a new haven in Venezuela under President Gómez.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el derrocado dictador cubano Gerardo Machado se preparaba para abandonar su refugio en la República Dominicana luego de que el presidente Rafael Trujillo le aconsejara marcharse. Trujillo le había otorgado previamente a Machado una extensa finca y estatus extraterritorial custodiado por 130 guardias cubanos, pero enfrentaba amenazas de represalias por parte del gobierno cubano. Según trascendió, Machado buscaba un nuevo asilo en Venezuela bajo el gobierno del presidente Gómez.

The article described the settlement as a notable achievement for Davies and his client.

records.full_text:
WASHINGTON OBSERVATIONS

The happily concluded negotiations for the adjustment of the foreign dollar bonds of the tiny Dominican Republic as announced last week is a new laurel crown for the Honorable Joseph E. Davies, whose prominent place in the Washington picture dates back to the days of the Wilson administration, when “Joe” Davies was first chairman of the Federal Trade Commission. Now in the private practice of law, though boomed for a place in the Roosevelt cabinet, Mr. Davies numbers the Dominican Republic among his clients and piloted the island’s government through the tortuous channel of debt negotiations with the Foreign Bondholders’ Protective Council. Friends of Mr. Davies are in receipt of copies of his brief in these proceedings, a magnus opus of 200 pages, in which the facts and the law and the argument are skillfully intertwined.

records.summary_en: Former Cuban ruler Gerardo Machado is practically recovered from the attack of indigestion that sent him to a hospital in Santo Domingo two weeks ago and is preparing to sail for Italy. Machado fled Cuba on August 12, 1933, and lived in Canada and the United States while Cuban governments sought his return for trial. His friends denied a version that his illness in Santo Domingo was poisoning, and in the Dominican Republic he was granted refuge by President Rafael Trujillo, long a friend of Machado.
records.summary_es: El exgobernante cubano Gerardo Machado está prácticamente recuperado del ataque de indigestión que lo llevó a un hospital en Santo Domingo hace dos semanas y se prepara para zarpar hacia Italia. Machado huyó de Cuba el 12 de agosto de 1933 y vivió en Canadá y Estados Unidos mientras los gobiernos cubanos buscaban su devolución para juzgarlo. Sus amigos negaron una versión de que su enfermedad en Santo Domingo fue un envenenamiento, y en la República Dominicana recibió refugio del presidente Rafael Trujillo, amigo de Machado desde hacía tiempo.

records.summary_en: The Dominican Legation announced that the boundary dispute between the Dominican Republic and Haiti had been settled. President Trujillo Molina of the Dominican Republic and President Vincent of Haiti had conferred in Haiti recently, settling all five of the principal boundary questions, in a dispute dating back to when Haiti was French territory and Santo Domingo was under Spanish rule. After the two countries agreed in 1930 to a peaceful solution by arbitration, President Vincent paid an official visit to Santo Domingo City the previous week, when the frontier treaty was signed.
records.summary_es: La Legación Dominicana anunció que la disputa fronteriza entre la República Dominicana y Haití había quedado resuelta. El presidente Trujillo Molina, de la República Dominicana, y el presidente Vincent, de Haití, se habían reunido recientemente en Haití y resolvieron las cinco cuestiones fronterizas principales, en una disputa que se remontaba a cuando Haití era territorio francés y Santo Domingo estaba bajo dominio español. Después de que ambos países acordaron en 1930 una solución pacífica por arbitraje, el presidente Vincent realizó la semana anterior una visita oficial a la ciudad de Santo Domingo, cuando se firmó el tratado fronterizo.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Italian consular representative Amadeo Barletta was arrested in Santo Domingo on charges of conspiring against President Rafael Trujillo, though sources alleged the real motive was his refusal to sell his stake in the Dominican Tobacco Company to Trujillo's associates. Barletta's arrest resulted in the government seizure of company revenues that partially belonged to an American firm. Italian and U.S. diplomats conferred in Washington to resolve the dispute without direct Italian intervention in the republic.

La detención de Barletta derivó en la incautación estatal de ingresos de la empresa que pertenecían en parte a una firma estadounidense. Diplomáticos italianos y estadounidenses deliberaron en Washington para solucionar la controversia sin una intervención directa de Italia en la república.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that Dominican President Rafael Trujillo maintained total control over national elections, running his Dominican Party unopposed and suppressing domestic opposition with an iron hand. Meanwhile, Dominican exiles in Cuba under former Vice President Rafael Estrella Ureña were reportedly organizing an expedition against Trujillo, with some Cuban youths attempting to join their cause. Opposition actions abroad had thus far been limited to minor incidents such as the mobbing of three diplomats in Havana.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* informó que el presidente dominicano Rafael Trujillo mantenía un control absoluto sobre las elecciones nacionales, postulando a su Partido Dominicano sin oposición y reprimiendo la disidencia interna con mano de hierro. Entretanto, según se reportó, exiliados dominicanos en Cuba bajo la dirección del exvicepresidente Rafael Estrella Ureña organizaban una expedición contra Trujillo, y algunos jóvenes cubanos intentaban sumarse a su causa. Hasta entonces, las acciones opositoras en el exterior se habían limitado a incidentes menores, como la agresión a tres diplomáticos en La Habana.
