records.summary_en: *The Washington Daily News* reported that President Rafael Trujillo appointed his young son a full-fledged colonel in the army with an official salary of $400 a month and uniform. A source noted that political parties no longer existed in Santo Domingo under Trujillo's rule.

records.summary_en: *The Indianapolis Times* quoted an observer named Morales describing the fear of citizens who avoid listening to anti-Trujillo broadcasts lest neighbors report them with fatal consequences, and noting that Trujillo made his five-year-old son a full colonel. Morales stated that Trujillo, who rose from constabulary sergeant during the U.S. Marine occupation to seize power via a 1930 coup, had eliminated all other political parties and won unanimous reelection. Morales argued that while the "Old Deal" installed Trujillo, the United States' non-interventionist "Good Neighbor" policy effectively kept the dictator in power.
records.summary_es: *The Indianapolis Times* citó a un observador de apellido Morales, quien describió el temor de los ciudadanos que evitaban escuchar transmisiones radiales contrarias a Trujillo por miedo a ser delatados por sus vecinos con consecuencias fatales, e indicó que Trujillo había nombrado coronel de pleno derecho a su hijo de cinco años. Morales afirmó que Trujillo, quien ascendió desde sargento de la policía nacional durante la ocupación de los marines estadounidenses hasta tomar el poder mediante el golpe de 1930, había liquidado a todos los demás partidos políticos y ganado una reelección unánime. Morales sostuvo que si bien el «Old Deal» instaló a Trujillo, la política no intervencionista del «Buen Vecino» de Estados Unidos mantenía efectivamente al dictador en el poder.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published a statement praising President Trujillo for directing the rebuilding of Santo Domingo following its destruction, modernizing the city without incurring new debt or defaulting on bonded interest payments. The report highlighted extensive nationwide public works, including new roads, schools, hospitals, Latin America's largest suspension bridge, and a nearly completed $3,000,000 artificial port at Trujillo City. It added that despite public efforts to rename the capital in his honor, Trujillo had initially opposed the proposal.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* publicó una declaración en la que elogiaba al presidente Trujillo por dirigir la reconstrucción de Santo Domingo tras su destrucción, modernizando la urbe sin contraer nueva deuda ni suspender el pago de intereses sobre los bonos. El informe destacó amplias obras públicas en todo el territorio nacional, como nuevas carreteras, escuelas, hospitales, el puente colgante más grande de América Latina y un puerto artificial de 3.000.000 de dólares a punto de concluirse en Ciudad Trujillo. Añadió que, pese a las gestiones públicas para rebautizar la capital en su honor, Trujillo se había opuesto inicialmente a dicha propuesta.

records.summary_en: With an opening salute of 21 guns from the batteries of Ozama Fortress, the Dominican Republic inaugurated the most extensive and elaborate celebration of Washington's birthday ever held outside the United States. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that in accepting President Roosevelt's invitation to a Pan-American conference in Buenos Aires, the Dominican Republic, Colombia, and Guatemala proposed establishing an American league of nations. Dominican President Rafael Trujillo and Colombian President Alfonso López argued that an American league would serve regional purposes more effectively than the League of Nations in Geneva. Guatemala additionally proposed a mutual assistance pact providing for joint action under the Monroe Doctrine against non-American aggression.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que, al aceptar la invitación del presidente Roosevelt a la conferencia panamericana en Buenos Aires, la República Dominicana, Colombia y Guatemala propusieron la creación de una liga de naciones americanas. El mandatario dominicano Rafael Trujillo y el presidente colombiano Alfonso López sostuvieron que una liga continental respondería mejor a las necesidades de la región que la Sociedad de Naciones en Ginebra. Guatemala propuso además un pacto de asistencia mutua que contemplaba acciones conjuntas al amparo de la Doctrina Monroe frente a agresiones extracontinentales.

records.summary_en: The *Brownsville Herald* reported that Joseph E. Davies secured President Roosevelt's intervention to ease the terms of the Dominican Republic's foreign debt after the State Department objected to the proposal. In return for adjusting the debt, Davies was promised a $450,000 fee from the Dominican government, of which he had collected $250,000 while Trujillo retained the remainder. The article noted that Davies had also been expected to obtain a new loan for Trujillo, but failed to do so.

records.headline: Dominican Republic Says Haiti Incident is Closed By United Press J
records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* reported that the Dominican government declared closed the recent frontier incident in which more than 1,000 Haitians were reported killed. Dominican officials asserted that the affair was a private dispute between individuals along the border rather than an international matter, and denied dispatching troops to the frontier. The official statement reiterated the Dominican Republic's peaceful intentions.
records.summary_es: El *Washington Daily News* informó que el gobierno dominicano declaró cerrado el reciente incidente fronterizo en el que, según se reportó, murieron más de 1.000 haitianos. Las autoridades dominicanas sostuvieron que el suceso constituyó una disputa privada entre particulares a lo largo de la frontera y no un asunto internacional, desmintiendo el envío de tropas a la zona limítrofe. El comunicado oficial reiteró las intenciones pacíficas de la República Dominicana.

records.headline: TO SEE TRUJILLO While the State Department said no report has
records.summary_en: United States Minister Norweb was hastily dispatched from Havana, where he was attending an international radio conference, to Ciudad Trujillo, arriving by airplane yesterday, and was expected to confer immediately with President General Trujillo, although the State Department said no report had yet been received from him. Considerable apprehension was felt over the new threat to the peace of the hemisphere; Dominican troops were reported massing on the border, but this was denied by Dominican Minister Andres Pastoriza in Washington. Reports reaching Washington said the Haitians were massacred because they had crossed the ill-defined border to farm lands, and because they angered Dominicans by working for cheaper wages and causing them to lose their jobs.
records.summary_es: El ministro estadounidense Norweb fue enviado apresuradamente desde La Habana, donde asistía a una conferencia internacional de radio, a Ciudad Trujillo, adonde llegó en avión ayer, y se esperaba que conferenciara de inmediato con el presidente general Trujillo, aunque el Departamento de Estado dijo que aún no había recibido informe suyo. Se sentía considerable aprensión por la nueva amenaza a la paz del hemisferio; se informó de que tropas dominicanas se concentraban en la frontera, pero el ministro dominicano Andrés Pastoriza lo negó en Washington. Los informes llegados a Washington decían que los haitianos fueron masacrados porque habían cruzado la frontera mal definida para cultivar tierras, y porque irritaban a los dominicanos trabajando por salarios más bajos y haciéndoles perder sus empleos.

Dominican officials had previously claimed minimal casualties, attributing the friction to Dominican resentment over an influx of unemployed Haitians seeking agricultural work. records.headline: Massacre Stories Assailed as Lies
records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* reported that the Dominican government had not yet accepted a mediation offer tendered by the United States, Mexico, and Cuba following the killings of Haitian nationals by Dominican soldiers and police. In a communiqué to editors, Dominican Minister Andrés Pastoriza stated that the Dominican government considered the incident closed. Pastoriza asserted that the border encounters involving illegal Haitian residents were being exploited by Trujillo's political enemies and by Haitian factions attempting to obscure domestic unrest.
records.summary_es: El *Washington Daily News* informó que el gobierno dominicano aún no había aceptado la oferta de mediación presentada por Estados Unidos, México y Cuba a raíz de la matanza de ciudadanos haitianos a manos de soldados y policías dominicanos. En un comunicado remitido a directores de periódicos, el ministro dominicano Andrés Pastoriza manifestó que su gobierno daba el asunto por concluido. Pastoriza sostuvo que los choques fronterizos protagonizados por residentes haitianos en situación irregular estaban siendo manipulados por adversarios políticos de Trujillo y por facciones haitianas empeñadas en encubrir sus propias revueltas internas.

Massacre Stories Assailed as Lies

By LOUIS JAY HEATH
United Press Staff Correspondent

Haitian and Dominican politicians and revolutionists were charged with malicious distortion of a “small incident” which took place early in October near the Dominican-Haitian border, in a formal communique issued by Dominican Minister Andres Pastoriza here today.

Haitian officials have charged that the so-called “small incident” referred to by Pastoriza consisted of “brutal killings of from 3000 to 5000 Haitian nationals by Dominican soldiers and police.” At the request of the Haitian government the United States, Mexico and Cuba have tendered their good offices to mediate the incident. To date the Dominican government has not accepted the tender and has sent special envoys to all three capitols to present the Dominican case.

The Pastoriza communique, addressed to editors, stated that the Dominican government already considered the “incident closed.”

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published an analysis attributing cross-border tensions between Haiti and the Dominican Republic to acute hunger and agricultural underproduction resulting from Haiti's dense population. records.summary_en: A Haitian Legation statement responded to Dominican reports that a large number of Dominican farmers had been killed or wounded in an attack by Haitians on a Dominican frontier community, saying it was prompted by news that seemed to have its source in an organized propaganda. The Haitian government contended that unprovoked attacks by Dominicans on Haitian citizens residing in Dominican territory were the cause of the tension, and Foreign Minister Georges Leger said at least 5,000 Haitians had been slain in wholesale massacres. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Haitian President Sténio Vincent estimated 8,000 Haitians were assassinated in the Dominican Republic, maintaining that the border dispute had already been settled by treaty two years prior. Vincent asserted that the Dominican government should have used standard diplomatic channels to repatriate undesirable foreigners, rather than resorting to violence without warning. While Vincent requested mediation from the United States, Cuba, and Mexico, President Trujillo expressed surprise at the appeal, pointing to existing bilateral accords.

Vincent aseveró que el gobierno dominicano debió recurrir a los canales diplomáticos habituales para repatriar a los extranjeros indeseables en lugar de acudir a la violencia sin previo aviso. Mientras Vincent solicitaba la mediación de Estados Unidos, Cuba y México, el presidente Trujillo expresó sorpresa ante dicha apelación señalando la vigencia de los acuerdos bilaterales.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Dominican Minister Andrés Pastoriza announced President Trujillo would not seek reelection, instead endorsing Dr. Jacinto B. Peynado for president and Dr. Manuel de Jesús Troncoso de la Concha for vice president, though Trujillo remained ready to serve if needed. The announcement came amid ongoing diplomatic friction with Haiti, which alleged that over 12,000 Haitians were massacred on Dominican soil. Dominican officials denied the accusations, attributing the reports to political enemies and citing economic strain caused by illegal Haitian migration.

El anuncio se produjo en medio de continuas fricciones diplomáticas con Haití, que alegaba la masacre de más de 12.000 haitianos en suelo dominicano. Las autoridades dominicanas rechazaron las acusaciones, atribuyendo los informes a enemigos políticos y señalando la carga económica provocada por la inmigración clandestina haitiana.

records.summary_en: The *Waterbury Democrat* reported that attorney Donald Richberg was representing President Trujillo in the diplomatic conflict over the reported massacre of roughly 8,000 Haitians. The report alleged that Trujillo's concession to conciliation was merely an evasive maneuver engineered by counsel regarding whether he had previously refused to negotiate. These diplomatic delays, including an envoy's refusal to travel to Washington, reportedly caused frustration within the U.S. State Department and the Pan-American Union.
records.summary_es: El *Waterbury Democrat* informó que el abogado Donald Richberg representaba al presidente Trujillo en el conflicto diplomático suscitado por la masacre de unos 8.000 haitianos. La crónica señalaba que la avenencia de Trujillo al proceso de conciliación fue una simple maniobra dilatoria urdida por sus asesores jurídicos en torno a su previa negativa a negociar. Estas demoras diplomáticas, incluida la negativa de un enviado a trasladarse a Washington, provocaron según los informes gran frustración en el seno del Departamento de Estado de EE. UU. y de la Unión Panamericana.

records.headline: Massacre river and chop sugar cane for wealthier Santo Domingo planters
records.summary_en: The *Times-News* reported that economic hardship and falling sugar prices exacerbated animosity toward thousands of Haitian laborers living in the Dominican Republic, culminating in nocturnal massacres where hundreds of Haitians were butchered with machetes along the Massacre River. Rather than retaliating militarily, Haitian President Sténio Vincent submitted the conflict to the Permanent Committee of Inter-American Conciliation under the 1923 Gondra Treaty. The resulting settlement required the Dominican government to pay a $750,000 indemnity, continue investigating the killings with full publicity, and cooperate to prevent future occurrences.
records.summary_es: El *Times-News* informó que las dificultades económicas y la caída del precio del azúcar avivaron la hostilidad hacia miles de braceros haitianos radicados en la República Dominicana, culminando en matanzas nocturnas donde cientos de haitianos fueron degollados a machetazos a lo largo del río Masacre. En lugar de tomar represalias militares, el presidente haitiano Sténio Vincent sometió la disputa a la Comisión Permanente de Conciliación Interamericana al amparo del Tratado Gondra de 1923. El acuerdo resultante obligó al gobierno dominicano a pagar una indemnización de 750.000 dólares, proseguir las investigaciones judiciales con amplia difusión pública y cooperar para prevenir hechos semejantes en el futuro.

records.summary_en: The *Waterbury Democrat* reported that economic distress following a drop in sugar prices led to anti-Haitian hostility in the Dominican Republic, resulting in the nighttime slaughter of hundreds of Haitian residents along the Massacre River. Haitian President Sténio Vincent avoided war by submitting the dispute to the Permanent Committee of Inter-American Conciliation under the 1923 Gondra Treaty. Under the negotiated agreement, the Dominican Republic agreed to pay a $750,000 indemnification, continue criminal investigations with publicity, and work to prevent recurrences.
records.summary_es: El *Waterbury Democrat* informó que la crisis económica provocada por el desplome de los precios del azúcar desató la hostilidad antihaitiana en la República Dominicana, desembocando en la matanza nocturna de cientos de residentes haitianos a orillas del río Masacre. El presidente de Haití, Sténio Vincent, eludió el conflicto bélico sometiendo la querella a la Comisión Permanente de Conciliación Interamericana en virtud del Tratado Gondra de 1923. Conforme al arreglo pactado, la República Dominicana convino en pagar una indemnización de 750.000 dólares, mantener las investigaciones penales bajo escrutinio público y aunar esfuerzos para evitar nuevos brotes de violencia.

Davies and Dominican President Rafael Trujillo, noting that Davies's daughter had recently stayed at the Presidential Palace in Trujillo City. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the Dominican Minister would present the Dominican decoration of Juan Pablo Duarte to Colonel H. Murray Jacoby, Charles H. Wanzer, Evan E. Young, and Louis M. Vidal at a Dominican Chamber of Commerce meeting in New York. The honors recognized their efforts to enhance trade and relations between the United States and the Dominican Republic. The paper also noted that the Minister's daughter, Señorita Matilde Pastoriza, had entered Arlington Hall Junior College in Virginia.

Young y Louis M. Vidal durante una reunión de la Cámara de Comercio Dominicana en Nueva York. Las distinciones reconocían sus gestiones para impulsar el comercio y los lazos entre Estados Unidos y la República Dominicana. El rotativo mencionó además que la hija del ministro, la señorita Matilde Pastoriza, había ingresado en el Arlington Hall Junior College de Virginia.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the Dominican Legation and German sources dismissed rumors that Germany was negotiating with Latin American nations to resettle Jewish refugees in the Dominican Republic following a meeting between Adolf Hitler and new Dominican Minister Roberto Despradel. The Dominican Legation in Washington stated it had no knowledge of any such discussions. Despradel had previously served in Washington earlier in the year helping negotiate the settlement of the Haitian-Dominican dispute under the Gondra Treaty.

La Legación dominicana en Washington declaró que no tenía constancia de tales conversaciones. Despradel había prestado servicios en Washington a principios de ese año colaborando en la resolución del diferendo domínico-haitiano en el marco del Tratado Gondra.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported on the competing diplomatic proposals heading into the Pan-American conference in Lima, Peru, noting Dominican dictator Rafael L. Trujillo's plan to create a Pan-American league of nations. Other key dynamics included Mexican President Lázaro Cárdenas's policy on foreign naturalization and Argentine Foreign Minister José María Cantilo's resistance to President Roosevelt's collective defense initiative. The U.S. delegation under Secretary of State Cordell Hull was expected to navigate these differing hemispheric positions.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* reseñó las propuestas diplomáticas contrapuestas con miras a la conferencia panamericana de Lima, Perú, señalando el plan del dictador dominicano Rafael L. Trujillo de instaurar una liga de naciones panamericana. Otros factores clave abarcaban la política sobre naturalización de extranjeros del presidente mexicano Lázaro Cárdenas y la renuencia del canciller argentino José María Cantilo a la iniciativa de defensa colectiva del presidente Roosevelt. Se esperaba que la delegación estadounidense, encabezada por el secretario de Estado Cordell Hull, sorteara estas divergencias hemisféricas.

records.headline: An Adventurers' Club story tells of Charley, who worked six months for a sugar concern at La Romana and, while on…
records.summary_en: An Adventurers' Club story tells of Charley, who worked six months for a sugar concern at La Romana and, while on vacation in Santo Domingo City, received orders transferring him to a new project at Barahona, but found every steamer tied up by a steamship strike and no road to take him there. He took a small sailing vessel for what should have been an overnight trip, but a storm blew the boat ten miles off course and disabled its steering gear, leaving him becalmed for days with forty Haitian passengers, no food and hot drinking water, as the only white man aboard, paying the captain ten dollars for protection and sleeping lashed to the rail. On the third night he woke to see two men creeping toward him with machetes in their mouths and shot both dead as the ship erupted in uproar.
records.summary_es: Un relato del Club de Aventureros cuenta la historia de Charley, que trabajó seis meses para una empresa azucarera en La Romana y, estando de vacaciones en la ciudad de Santo Domingo, recibió órdenes de traslado a un nuevo proyecto en Barahona, pero encontró todos los vapores detenidos por una huelga naviera y ningún camino que lo llevara allí. Se embarcó en un pequeño velero para lo que debía ser un viaje de una noche, pero una tormenta desvió el barco diez millas de su rumbo y averió su timón, dejándolo en calma durante días con cuarenta pasajeros haitianos, sin comida y con el agua potable caliente, siendo el único hombre blanco a bordo, pagando al capitán diez dólares por protección y durmiendo atado a la barandilla. En la tercera noche despertó y vio a dos hombres acercándose a él arrastrándose con machetes en la boca, y les disparó a ambos hasta matarlos mientras el barco estallaba en alboroto.

“They didn’t know my eyes were open,” he says, “if they

Charley got those guns out just as the natives were taking their
machetes from their mouths. He whipped up one gun and fired twice.
In an instant, two men were dead on the deck and the whole ship was
in an uproar. Dark figures came swarming toward him. The captain
was a big, powerful fellow. Charley says he was built on the style of
Harry Wills in his prime. He picked Charley up with one hand, threw
him into his cabin head first, and then, with the aid of a revolver and
his powerful physique, held that furious mob at bay.
Captain Threatens to Sink the Ship.

records.summary_en: The *Washington Times* reported that thirty-two German-Jewish refugees arriving in New York aboard the Red Star liner *Westernland* planned to establish new homes in the Dominican Republic. The article noted that the country's capital, originally named Santo Domingo, had been renamed Ciudad Trujillo by Rafael Trujillo, whose past record with immigrants was criticized. The arrival occurred as over 1,500 Jewish refugees faced potential return to Germany after Paraguay and Uruguay barred their entry.

El artículo anotó que la capital del país, originalmente llamada Santo Domingo, había sido rebautizada Ciudad Trujillo por Rafael Trujillo, cuyos antecedentes hacia la inmigración eran objeto de críticas. Su llegada se produjo mientras más de 1.500 refugiados judíos se enfrentaban a una posible repatriación a Alemania tras prohibírseles la entrada en Paraguay y Uruguay.

records.headline: Trujillo “was not going to visit Hitler.” In denying the report
records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* commented on reports that General Rafael Trujillo and his entourage were traveling to Germany, raising speculation about German interest in Samaná Bay as a potential submarine base. Although the Dominican Legation denied that Trujillo would meet Adolf Hitler, it did not deny he was traveling to Germany. The report also listed members of Señora de Trujillo's party, which included military aides, a private physician, and secretary J. M. Bonetti Burgos.

Pese a que la Legación dominicana desmintió que Trujillo fuera a entrevistarse con Adolf Hitler, no negó que viajara a territorio alemán. La crónica enumeró asimismo a los miembros de la comitiva de la señora de Trujillo, en la que figuraban edecanes militares, un médico de cabecera y el secretario J. M. Bonetti Burgos.

records.summary_en: This column reports rumours that General Trujillo himself is aboard the Santa Paula with his family's party, which travelled incognito and embarked at Cape Haitien, and that Dominican Minister Andres Pastoriza and consular officials will meet the ship at Quarantine, with Mayor LaGuardia to welcome the party to a floor of the Waldorf in New York. records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* outlined the itinerary for General Rafael Trujillo's visit to Washington, D.C., following an invitation from Marine Corps Commandant Major General Thomas Holcomb. The schedule included wreath-laying ceremonies at Mount Vernon and Arlington National Cemetery, official meetings with Secretary of State Cordell Hull and President Roosevelt, and a Senate luncheon. Trujillo was also scheduled to inspect military sites including the Navy Yard, Marine Barracks, and Fort Meade.

Trujillo, now commander in chief of the Dominican army, who arrives Thursday: luncheon at the Senate on Friday, visits that afternoon to the Navy Yard and the Marine Barracks, and dinner that night as honor guest of Marine Corps Commandant Thomas Holcomb. records.headline: Even if he is denounced as a tyrant and accused of
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* profiled General Rafael Trujillo, noting that despite being denounced as a tyrant and accused of the massacre of thousands of Haitians two years earlier, he was recognized for administrative energy and public works. Having taken power in 1930 under the slogan "God and Trujillo," he oversaw road construction, school expansion, and the rebuilding and renaming of the capital before handing the presidency to Dr. Jacinto Bienvenido Peynado. The article noted that Trujillo continued to direct Dominican governance while being celebrated by sympathetic biographers as an inspired leader.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* perfiló al general Rafael Trujillo, señalando que, a pesar de haber sido denunciado como un tirano y acusado de la matanza de miles de haitianos dos años antes, se le reconocía por su empuje administrativo y sus planes de obras públicas. Habiendo tomado el poder en 1930 bajo el lema «Dios y Trujillo», dirigió la construcción de caminos, la expansión de escuelas y la reedificación y cambio de nombre de la capital antes de traspasar la presidencia formalmente al Dr. Jacinto Bienvenido Peynado. El artículo consignaba que Trujillo seguía conduciendo las riendas del gobierno dominicano mientras biógrafos afines lo ensalzaban como un líder providencial.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that General Rafael Trujillo hosted a lavish reception at the New York World's Fair aboard his yacht *Ramfis*, formerly owned by American millionaire Julius Fleischmann, before the vessel steamed toward Washington. The article noted Trujillo's fondness for military attire and listed dozens of high foreign orders and medals bestowed upon him across Europe and the Americas. Observers commented that Trujillo possessed more decorations than nearly any other anticipated foreign visitor.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el general Rafael Trujillo ofreció una suntuosa recepción en la Feria Mundial de Nueva York a bordo de su yate *Ramfis*, perteneciente con anterioridad al magnate estadounidense Julius Fleischmann, antes de que el buque zarpase hacia Washington. La nota hizo hincapié en la predilección de Trujillo por las galas militares y enumeró decenas de condecoraciones y medallas extranjeras que le habían sido otorgadas en Europa y América. Los observadores comentaron que Trujillo ostentaba más preseas que casi cualquier otro visitante distinguido del exterior.

records.summary_en: At a brief Washington press conference, General Trujillo, flanked by Minister Pastoriza and Señor Aguilar, described his trip as a goodwill visit to improve relations between the Dominican Republic and the United States before going to the State Department. He said he intended to spend July in the United States inquiring into its agriculture, industry and cultural centers, and that he had received no overtures from the German government.
records.summary_es: En una breve conferencia de prensa en Washington, el general Trujillo, acompañado por el ministro Pastoriza y el señor Aguilar, describió su viaje como una visita de buena voluntad para mejorar las relaciones entre la República Dominicana y Estados Unidos antes de dirigirse al Departamento de Estado. Dijo que pensaba pasar julio en Estados Unidos investigando su agricultura, industria y centros culturales, y que no había recibido propuestas del gobierno alemán.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the Dominican Chamber of Commerce in the United States defended General Rafael Trujillo against criticism from the Committee for Dominican Democracy regarding his White House visit with President Roosevelt. The chamber praised Trujillo's public welfare and development achievements in the Dominican Republic. Meanwhile, Trujillo visited troops at Fort George G. Meade, while a reception scheduled at the Pan American Union was canceled out of respect for the late Secretary of the Navy Claude A. Swanson.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que la Cámara de Comercio Dominicana en Estados Unidos salió en defensa del general Rafael Trujillo ante los cuestionamientos formulados por el Committee for Dominican Democracy con motivo de su visita a la Casa Blanca para reunirse con el presidente Roosevelt. Dicha corporación comercial ensalzó las obras de bienestar social y de fomento material alcanzadas por Trujillo en la República Dominicana. Entretanto, Trujillo visitó a las tropas en Fort George G. Meade, al tiempo que una recepción programada en la Unión Panamericana fue cancelada en señal de duelo por el fenecido secretario de Marina Claude A. Swanson.

records.headline: Fish is quoted as having said at a dinner to Trujillo
records.summary_en: Columnist Raymond Clapper in the *Washington Daily News* criticized Representative Hamilton Fish for praising General Trujillo's regime as a "golden age" during a New York dinner. Clapper cited first-hand reporting by Quentin Reynolds of *Collier's*, who investigated the border atrocities and observed victims mutilated by Dominican forces. Clapper maintained that any prosperity Trujillo claimed was purchased through the murder of thousands of obscure Haitian peasants.
records.summary_es: El columnista Raymond Clapper, en *The Washington Daily News*, censuró al congresista Hamilton Fish por alabar el régimen del general Trujillo calificándolo de «era dorada» durante un banquete en Nueva York. Clapper citó testimonios directos de Quentin Reynolds de *Collier's*, quien investigó las atrocidades en la frontera y constató las mutilaciones de víctimas infligidas por tropas dominicanas. Clapper aseveró que cualquier prosperidad exhibida por Trujillo se pagó con la sangre y el exterminio de miles de humildes campesinos haitianos.

A new and modern hotel was to be built at Trujillo City, and the harbor had been dredged from 14 feet to 35 feet, so cruise ships would now include Trujillo City as a port of call. On his refugee plans, 500 families would be admitted, would not have to pay the $500 Dominican immigration fee because they would be considered refugees working on colonization plans being worked out with the Committee for Refugees in New York, and he would be personally responsible for their upkeep and education for two years.

records.headline: Priateness of endorsing home-grown dictators while condemning the Eu ropean variety
records.summary_en: The *Gazette* contrasted the lavish military honors previously accorded to Latin American dictators like Trujillo with the restrained, informal reception given to visiting Haitian President Sténio Vincent in Washington. Despite Vincent being the sitting president of a nation of 2.6 million, he received no 21-gun salute, fanfare, or military parade, meeting only Undersecretary of State Sumner Welles and a small delegation at the station. Critics questioned the appropriateness of celebrating authoritarian figures while giving a chilly welcome to the head of a neighboring constitutional republic.
records.summary_es: El *Gazette* contrastó los fastuosos honores militares dispensados con anterioridad a dictadores latinoamericanos como Trujillo con el austero e informal recibimiento ofrecido en Washington al mandatario haitiano Sténio Vincent. A pesar de que Vincent ejercía la presidencia en funciones de un país de 2,6 millones de habitantes, no se le rindieron salvas de 21 cañonazos, fanfarrias ni desfiles de tropas, siendo recibido en la estación ferroviaria únicamente por el subsecretario de Estado Sumner Welles y una reducida comitiva. Quienes criticaron la actitud oficial cuestionaron la idoneidad de exaltar a mandatarios autócratas mientras se brindaba una fría acogida al gobernante de una vecina república constitucional.

records.full_text:
Dominicans to Admit
100,000 Refugees

By the Associated Press.

CIUDAD TRUJILLO, Jan. 31.—A contract signed here between the Dominican government and the Dominican Republic Settlement Association provides for the immediate admisison of some 500 European political refugee families and aims at the establishment of 100,000 refugees over a period of years.

Most of the first group are German Jewish refugees, but the contract does not specify nationalities.

The settlement association will pay for establishing them and is to be reimbursed by income from their lands once they have regained their financial feet.

records.headline: Norweb will sail this afternoon from New York on the Coamo
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that newly appointed U.S. Ambassador to Peru R. Henry Norweb and his wife departed New York aboard the *Coamo* for Ciudad Trujillo. Norweb traveled to present his letters of recall as Minister to the Dominican Republic before returning to the United States and sailing for Peru.

records.headline: Welles to the Dominican Republic as his special representative to prepare
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* recounted the diplomatic career of Undersecretary of State Sumner Welles, noting his mission under President Harding to arrange the withdrawal of U.S. Marines from the Dominican Republic. Welles also returned to Santo Domingo alongside Charles G. Dawes to examine Dominican national finances. These Caribbean experiences helped Welles formulate the non-interventionist diplomatic approach later known as the "Good Neighbor" policy.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* rememoró la trayectoria diplomática del subsecretario de Estado Sumner Welles, recordando la encomienda asumida bajo la presidencia de Harding para organizar la retirada de los marines estadounidenses de la República Dominicana. Welles también volvió a Santo Domingo junto a Charles G. Dawes para examinar las finanzas públicas de la nación caribeña. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Dominican Minister Andrés Pastoriza issued invitations for a lecture on the colonial architecture of Santo Domingo, presented by Professor Domingo Caíno de Cancio at the Pan American Union. Dr. Caíno de Cancio, an art and Spanish literature professor at Catholic University, was scheduled to speak in Spanish. The lecture featured prints of Dominican architecture that had recently won a prize at the Corcoran Gallery of Art.

El Dr. Caíno de Cancio, catedrático de arte y literatura española de la Universidad Católica, disertaría en idioma español. La disertación incluyó grabados de arquitectura dominicana que habían sido galardonados recientemente en la Corcoran Gallery of Art.

records.headline: The State Department announced yesterday that the United States had agreed
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the State Department agreed to terminate the U.S. customs receivership in the Dominican Republic, restoring duty collections of roughly $4,000,000 annually to Dominican authorities. In exchange, the Dominican Republic granted the United States a first lien on its total revenues, estimated at $12,000,000, to guarantee the servicing of $15,400,000 in external debt. The treaty was negotiated in Ciudad Trujillo by U.S. Ambassador Hugh Wilson and Dominican Foreign Minister Arturo Despradel, ending the 1924 convention.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el Departamento de Estado acordó extinguir la receptoría aduanera estadounidense en la República Dominicana, devolviendo a las autoridades dominicanas la recaudación de tributos, estimada en unos 4.000.000 de dólares anuales. Como contraparte, la República Dominicana concedió a Estados Unidos un gravamen preferente sobre la totalidad de sus rentas fiscales, calculadas en 12.000.000 de dólares, para afianzar el servicio de 15.400.000 dólares de deuda externa. El tratado fue pactado en Ciudad Trujillo por el embajador estadounidense Hugh Wilson y el canciller dominicano Arturo Despradel, poniendo término a la convención de 1924.

records.summary_en: The *Daily Alaska Empire* reported that several New York creditors, including Louis Sherry, Cartier, Annin Flag Company, and an art gallery, sought payment from General Rafael Trujillo for services and goods provided during the previous year's World's Fair reception. Although creditors hired a lawyer and dispatched a U.S. Marshal to his hotel, Trujillo was shielded from legal action because he held diplomatic immunity as an Ambassador Extraordinary. As a result, creditors were unable to collect the debts or seize his yacht *Ramfis*, docked at the Washington Navy Yard.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Alaska Empire* informó que diversos acreedores neoyorquinos, entre ellos Louis Sherry, Cartier, la Annin Flag Company y una galería de arte, procuraban el cobro de deudas al general Rafael Trujillo por concepto de bienes y atenciones brindados durante la recepción de la Feria Mundial del año anterior. Si bien los acreedores contrataron a un letrado y comisionaron a un alguacil federal (U.S. Marshal) a su hotel, Trujillo quedó a salvo de acciones judiciales en virtud de su inmunidad diplomática como embajador extraordinario. Por consiguiente, los demandantes no pudieron cobrar los créditos ni embargar su yate *Ramfis*, atracado en el Astillero Naval de Washington.

records.headline: Wilson recently negotiated a new customs treaty with the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Secretary of State Cordell Hull commended diplomat Hugh R. Wilson for completing confidential assignments, which included negotiating a new customs treaty with the Dominican Republic. The treaty was understood to be ready for submission to the U.S. Senate for ratification. Wilson had previously served as Ambassador to Germany and held various diplomatic posts before focusing on wartime issues in Europe and Latin America.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el secretario de Estado Cordell Hull felicitó al diplomático Hugh R. Wilson por la culminación de misiones reservadas, entre las cuales figuró la negociación de un nuevo tratado de aduanas con la República Dominicana. Se daba por hecho que el instrumento internacional estaba listo para ser sometido al Senado de EE. UU. para su debida ratificación. Wilson se había desempeñado previamente como embajador en Alemania y ocupado diversos cargos diplomáticos antes de volcarse a asuntos bélicos en Europa y América Latina.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that diplomatic representatives across the Americas accepted invitations to the Pan-American Aviation Day ball at the Mayflower Hotel. A special invitation was extended to General Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic, who was staying in New York. The event featured decorations provided by Latin American embassies and participation from Cuban aviators.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que representantes del cuerpo diplomático de las Américas acogieron las invitaciones al baile del Día de la Aviación Panamericana en el Mayflower Hotel. Se cursó una invitación de honor al general Rafael Trujillo, de la República Dominicana, quien residía temporalmente en Nueva York. La velada contó con ornamentaciones suministradas por embajadas hispanoamericanas y con la presencia de aviadores cubanos.

records.summary_en: The *West Virginia Digest* profiled newly elected Haitian President Élie Lescot, outlining his earlier service as Haiti's Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary to Ciudad Trujillo. In that post, Lescot helped negotiate the settlement of the border dispute between Haiti and the Dominican Republic, earning the Dominican decoration of Juan Pablo Duarte. He subsequently served as a delegate to the Buenos Aires peace conference before becoming Haitian Minister to the United States in 1937.
records.summary_es: El *West Virginia Digest* perfiló la biografía del recién electo mandatario haitiano Élie Lescot, reseñando su desempeño diplomático anterior como enviado extraordinario y ministro plenipotenciario de Haití en Ciudad Trujillo. En aquella misión, Lescot facilitó las gestiones conciliatorias del pleito limítrofe entre Haití y la República Dominicana, lo que le valió la condecoración dominicana de la Orden de Juan Pablo Duarte. Con posterioridad asistió como delegado a la conferencia de paz de Buenos Aires antes de asumir como ministro plenipotenciario de Haití ante los Estados Unidos en 1937.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* assessed the military vulnerabilities of Hispaniola, noting that the island's extensive coastline could offer bases to enemy forces threatening U.S. naval installations at Guantanamo Bay and Puerto Rico. While the Dominican Republic possessed a larger army than Haiti, it lacked airplanes, anti-aircraft weaponry, and artillery capable of resisting naval or aerial invasion. The article highlighted substantial pro-Axis sentiment in Santo Domingo, with British diplomats estimating that 75 percent of the populace favored Germany, though American observers believed sympathies were evenly divided.

UU. en Guantánamo y Puerto Rico. El reportaje puso de relieve un arraigado sentir favorable al Eje en Santo Domingo, calculando los diplomáticos británicos que un 75 por ciento simpatizaba con Alemania, mientras que observadores estadounidenses estimaban dividida la opinión pública.

yard into the fog-shrouded waters

records.full_text:
Delegates Arriving
For Inter-American
Economic Parley

Welles to Be Keynoter
At Conference Here
Opening Tuesday

By HAROLD B. ROGERS.

As distinguished delegations of finance ministers, heads of central banks, and technical experts from the other American republics continued to arrive over the week-end, plans were being put into final shape for the first Inter-American Conference on Systems of Economic and Financial Control, to open Tuesday at the Pan American Union.

Under the agenda for the conference, which was authorized by the January meeting of Foreign Affairs Ministers at Rio de Janeiro, two different committees will be set up among the delegates. One will consider “international transactions” the other “domestic transactions,” as protection against Axis influence.

The first and last sessions of the conference will be public meetings, but the intervening technical sessions, under present plans probably will be behind closed doors, unless other public sessions “are agreed upon and so ordered by the delegates.” The conference may last about 10 days.

Republics Each Have One Vote.

Each of the 21 republics will have but one vote, regardless of the size of their various delegations.

“Proposals, reports, and projects,” it is provided in the agenda, “shall be considered approved when they have obtained the affirmative vote of an absolute majority of the countries represented at the respective meeting.”

The conference is only one of the several new inter-American developments which have grown out of the second World War to help the American republics present a more united front to the aggressor nations of Germany, Japan and Italy.

Authorized specifically by the Rio Conference of Foreign Ministers, this new gathering is operating under sponsorship of the Inter-American Financial and Economic Advisory Committee. This committee was set up in 1939 and has been regularly functioning since the outbreak of the second World War. At its headquarters in the Pan American Union, this committee, headed by Undersecretary of State Welles, has been holding regularly scheduled meetings and has prepared a comprehensive background of data, which according to experts, should provide much material of value for the forthcoming meeting.

Welles to Be “Keynoter.”

Mr. Welles, who will deliver the opening “keynote” address to the conference, and Dr. Leo S. Rowe, director general of the Pan American Union, who will welcome the delegates, will be followed by a spokesman for the Latin American group. This spokesman will be selected at a preliminary meeting of the delegates tomorrow. There was no official indication today as to who this spokesman may be.

Problems to be considered by the conference, involving the severance of commercial and financial ties between the Western Hemisphere and the Axis powers, are considered by officials to be virtually parallel to the vital issues of breaking diplomatic relations with the Axis, which absorbed major public attention at the Rio conference.

By the terms of two financial and economic resolutions at Rio, it was explained last night by one official, economic intercourse between the American republics and the Axis powers is to be cut; and transactions by nationals of Axis states, likely to benefit members of the tripartite pact (Germany, Italy and Japan) are to be placed under rigid control and supervision.

Other inter-American measures have been adopted to meet economic problems arising out of the war. The Inter-American Development Commission has set up national commissions in each of the Latin-American countries and is especially interested in the development of new industries in each country for which there may be markets in the other republics.

Commission’s Duties.

The Inter-American Maritime Technical Commission, created only a few months ago, is designed primarily to supervise the operation of the immobilized vessels taken over in ports of the American republics. The Office of Co-ordinator of Inter-American Affairs and the Board of Economic Warfare have wide authority and operate extensively in Latin-American affairs.

Over all the American representatives in these agencies, the State Department has exercised a guiding hand, though allowing to some far-reaching autonomy, within the limits of the general international policies laid down by the administration. The Inter-American Defense Board recommends defense measures.

The new program of international solidarity in the economic sphere aimed at by the Rio conference, according to Dr. Rowe, “was nothing short of pooling the resources of the American continent for the winning of the war, and at the same time adopting measures to protect the economic and financial structure of all the republics. The motive that guided the (Rio) delegates,” he added, “was not the selfish interest of any individual state, but the safety and welfare of the entire Western World.”

Many foreign delegations already have arrived and established headquarters. Some are in hotels, others are understood to be established in connection with their embarries or legations. Some of the delegates are ambassadors or ministers.

Brazilian Group Arrives.

Among the first to arrive recently was the group from Brazil. This delegation is headed by Francisco Alves dos Santos, jr., director of exchange, Bank of Brazil. With his technical adviser, Achilles Moreaux of the Bank of Brazil, and other experts he is at the Shoreham Hotel.

Delegates from the other republics, according to the official list, are as follows: Argentina, Eduardo Gagneaux, assistant general manager, Central Bank of Argentina; Bolivia, Humberto Cuenca, general manager, Central Bank of Bolivia; Chile, Pedro Enrique Alfonso, former Minister of Finance; Colombia, Alberto Bayon, chief, Office of Exchange and Import Control; Costa Rica, Paul Gurdian, former Minister of Foreign Affairs and former Minister of Finance; Cuba, Ramiro Guerra Sanchez, representative of Cuba on the Inter-American Financial and Economic Advisory Committee; Dominican Republic, Harry E. Henneman, speci[illegible] representative of the Ministry of Finance and Commerce; Ecuador, Eduardo Icaza, president, Central Bank; El Salvador, Carlos Adalberto Alfaro, charge d’affairs of El Salvador here; Guatemala, Luis Beltranena, dean, School of Economic Scieinces, University of Guatemala; Haiti, Abel La Croix, Minister of Finance; Honduras, Julian R. Caceres, Minister of Honduras here; Mexico, Eduardo Villaseñor, director, Bank of Mexico; Nicaragua, Leon De Bayle, Minister of Nicaragua here; Panama, Ricardo Marciacq, comptroller general of the Republic; Paraguay, Harmodio Gonzalez, manager, Bank of the Republic; Peru, Manuel Gallagher; Uruguay, Roberto E. MacEachen, Minister of Uruguay to Cuba; Venezuela, Diogenes Escalante, Ambasador of Venezuela here.

Ten of the Central American and Caribbean countries have declared war on the Axis, and all other Latin American republics have broken diplomatic relations with the Axis except Argentina and Chile.

The United States delegate will be Edward H. Foley, general counsel of the Treasury Department. He will be assisted by advisers from both the Treasury and State Departments and by L. Werner Knoke, vice president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Captain Maurice Marshall Berck, an Army surgeon attached to Walter Reed Hospital, died from severe burns sustained in an apartment fire at the Brighton Hotel. Firefighters found him unconscious on the floor of the ablaze room, and the cause of the fire remained undetermined.

Berck, prestigioso facultativo torácico neoyorquino que contrajo nupcias con Flor de Oro Trujillo en marzo de 1942, acababa de regresar a Washington tras visitar a su cónyuge en Nueva York. records.summary_en: The *Daily Monitor Leader* reported that President Roosevelt nominated incumbent ministers across the Caribbean and Central America to become ambassadors, including Avra M. Warren in the Dominican Republic and John Campbell White in Haiti. Under the White House plan, the elevated envoys would continue receiving their ministerial salaries of $10,000 instead of the usual $17,500 ambassadorial pay. Other diplomats nominated for ambassadorial rank included Boaz Long, Robert M. Scotten, and James B. Stewart.

Otros representantes nominados comprendieron a Boaz Long, Robert M. Scotten y James B. Stewart.

records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* reported on the diplomatic elevation of missions between the United States and seven Caribbean and Central American nations, including the Dominican Republic and Haiti, from legations to full embassies. Under reciprocal agreements, the respective ministers were elevated to ambassadors, leaving Canada as the only Western Hemisphere mission remaining at ministerial rank. Latin American diplomats gathered in Washington to celebrate the confirmations and exchange congratulations.
records.summary_es: *The Washington Daily News* reseñó el acto solemne de jerarquización institucional por el cual las misiones mutuas entre Estados Unidos y siete repúblicas centroamericanas y antillanas —entre ellas la República Dominicana y Haití— fueron elevadas de legaciones a embajadas de primera clase. Conforme a convenios de reciprocidad, los respectivos ministros pasaron a ser embajadores extraordinarios, quedando Canadá como la única sede diplomática continental que conservaba rango de legación. Los dignatarios hispanoamericanos se congregaron en Washington para festejar las acreditaciones e intercambiar salutaciones de estilo.

Miss Trujillo, whose husband Captain Maurice Berck died in an accident four months prior, expressed her desire to study international law, pursue diplomacy, and observe American women's customs to introduce them to her home country. She noted that she was fluent in Portuguese, German, French, and English in addition to Spanish.

Añadió que dominaba a la perfección el portugués, alemán, francés e inglés, además de su castellano natal.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Pan-American Union Director General Dr. Leo S. Rowe hosted a luncheon honoring the new Dominican Ambassador, Dr. Anselmo Copello, following his formal reception by President Roosevelt. Copello succeeded Dr. Jesús María Troncoso, who had served as minister and subsequently as the republic's first ambassador after the legation was elevated in May 1943. Distinguished guests included Attorney General Francis Biddle, Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr., and several Pan-American Union and State Department officials.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* dio cuenta de un almuerzo servido por el director general de la Unión Panamericana, Dr. Leo S. Rowe, en agasajo al nuevo embajador dominicano Dr. Anselmo Copello, con posterioridad a la ceremonia oficial de recepción de credenciales por el mandatario Roosevelt. Copello sustituía al Dr. Jesús María Troncoso, quien había ejercido como ministro y más tarde como primer embajador formal de la república tras la jerarquización de la legación en mayo de 1943. Entre los convidados de honor asistieron el fiscal general Francis Biddle, el subsecretario de Estado Adolf A. Berle, Jr., y altos funcionarios de la Unión Panamericana y del Departamento de Estado.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Dominican Ambassador Anselmo Copello addressed the Political Study Club at the Washington Club in commemoration of Dominican independence. Copello highlighted Santo Domingo's historic significance as Columbus's first New World landing site and described plans by American nations to construct a monumental Columbus memorial lighthouse. He added that the remains of Columbus, currently resting in the Cathedral of Santo Domingo, would eventually be transferred to the lighthouse.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el embajador dominicano Anselmo Copello disertó ante el Political Study Club en el Washington Club con motivo de las efemérides patrias dominicanas. Subrayó que las cenizas del Gran Almirante, depositadas en la Catedral de Santo Domingo, serían trasladadas solemnemente a dicho mausoleo una vez finalizado.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Dominican Ambassador Anselmo Copello would deliver the principal address at a musical celebration in the Hall of the Americas commemorating Dominican independence, with music performed by the Army Air Forces band. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Dominican Secretary of Foreign Affairs Dr. Manuel Arturo Peña Batlle arrived in Washington for his first official visit since assuming the foreign affairs portfolio. A series of informal entertainments was arranged for him, while his wife and family remained at home in Ciudad Trujillo. The paper noted that his visit coincided with the Washington stay of the wife of Haitian President Élie Lescot.

Se coordinó un programa de agasajos en su honor, permaneciendo su señora esposa y familia en su residencia de Ciudad Trujillo. La gacetilla acotó que la estancia del canciller coincidió con la presencia en la capital de la esposa del mandatario haitiano Élie Lescot.

records.headline: Ambassador to the United States from the Do minican Republic, died
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Don Anselmo Copello, Dominican Ambassador to the United States, died at age 65 in Doctors Hospital following pneumonia and a heart attack. Copello, who served as president of the Dominican Republic's principal tobacco company, had never held formal government office prior to his ambassadorial appointment in November 1943. He was survived by his wife, Señora de Copello, and five children residing in Washington.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó sobre la muerte de don Anselmo Copello, embajador de la República Dominicana ante los Estados Unidos, acaecida a los 65 años de edad en el Doctors Hospital como desenlace de una neumonía agravada por un paro cardíaco. Copello, quien ejercía como titular de la principal tabacalera del territorio quisqueyano, no había ocupado dignidades gubernamentales con antelación a su designación diplomática en noviembre de 1943. Le sobrevivieron su viuda, la señora de Copello, y sus cinco hijos residentes en Washington.

records.headline: Don Anselmo Copello
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published tributes mourning the death of Dominican Ambassador Anselmo Copello, praising his distinction as a diplomat and cooperative spirit on matters of mutual concern. Copello, head of the Dominican Republic's main tobacco company based in Santiago, had returned to Washington only days before his death following three months of official business in his home country. Minister Counselor Dr. J. R. Rodríguez was designated to direct embassy affairs until a successor was appointed.

Copello, directivo de la compañía tabacalera radicada en Santiago de los Caballeros, había retornado a Washington escasos días antes de su partida terrenal luego de permanecer tres meses atendiendo gestiones de Estado en su patria. El ministro consejero Dr. J. R. Rodríguez quedó a cargo de los despachos de la misión hasta la designación de un sucesor titular.

records.full_text:
Don Anselmo Copello
Funeral Arranged
For Tomorrow

Members of the diplomatic corps and high Government officials will attend funeral services for Don Anselmo Copello, Ambassador from the Dominican Republic, at 11 a.m tomorrow at the Sacred Heart Church, Sixteenth street and Park road N.W. After temporary burial in Arlington Cemetery, the body will be taken to the Dominican Republic.

The Ambassador, who was 65, died yesterday in Doctors Hospital of a heart attack which followed pneumonia. He had been ill two days.

His work was praised in the following statement made yesterday by Secretary of State Stettinius:

“I have been greatly grieved to learn of the death of the distinguished Ambassador of the Dominican Republic. His excellency Anselmo Copella. In my association with him in dealing with the problems of mutual interest, I have come to know his outstanding qualities as a diplomat and as a friend.

“He has represented his country with distinction and has always evinced a most helpful spirit of cooperation in dealing with matters of common concern. The Dominican people will rightly mourn the passing of a gifted statesman and his many friends in this country will sincerely share their sorrow.”

Senor Copello returned to Washington Monday from the Dominican Republic, where he had been on official business for three months. He was accompanied by his only son, Jeronimo.

Before his appointment as Ambassador to this country in November, 1943, Senor Copello had never served as a government official except for several honorary posts. His credentials were received by President Roosevelt on December 20, 1943. He succeeded Dr. J. M. Troncoso, now Secretary of the Treasury of the Dominican Republic.

President of the principal tobacco company of the Dominican Republic, Senor Copello’s home was in Santiago.

Besides his widow, Senora de Copello, and his son, he is survived by four daughters, Adelina, Argentina, Ileana and Margarita. The family lives at the Embassy, 4530 Sixteenth street N.W.

Dr. J. R. Rodriguez, Minister Counselor, will direct the affairs of the Embassy until further arrangements are made by his government.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the Office of Price Administration filed a lawsuit seeking $80,870.25 in triple damages against V. M. Hinojosa, Dominican consul in Kansas City and president of the Pan-American Trading Company. The complaint charged that the firm sold imported Mexican ponderosa pine lumber at prices exceeding established ceiling limits and with incorrect grading. Hinojosa contested the suit, asserting that the lumber was bought in Mexico and sold border f.o.b. beyond U.S. price jurisdiction.

Hinojosa, cónsul dominicano en Kansas City y director de la Pan-American Trading Company. El libelo acusatorio imputaba que la firma comercializaba maderas de pino ponderosa importadas de México alterando las clasificaciones oficiales e infringiendo los topes de precios tarifarios fijados por ley. Hinojosa rechazó la acusación aduciendo que el cargamento maderero fue negociado en México y vendido con cláusula FOB fronteriza al margen de la jurisdicción estadounidense.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dominican Ambassador Emilio Garcia Godoy decorated Admiral Byrd and Maj. Banks with the Order of Christopher Columbus at the Dominican Embassy. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Ambassador L. B. Pearson of Canada, chairman of the United Nations interim commission on food and agriculture, announced the receipt of membership acceptances from eighteen countries, including the Dominican Republic and Haiti. Twenty ratifications are required to bring the agreement into effect. Pearson noted that Poland's acceptance had been received in October from its government-in-exile in London.

Se requerían veinte ratificaciones constitutivas para dotar de vigencia legal al tratado fundacional. Pearson aclaró que la anuencia de Polonia había sido remitida en el mes de octubre por su gobierno legítimo en el exilio con sede en Londres.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dr. L. S. Rowe of the Pan American Union hosted a luncheon at the Pan American Annex honoring Dominican Ambassador Emilio Garcia Godoy and Panamanian Ambassador Samuel Lewis. The event was attended by high-ranking officials including Secretary of Commerce Henry A. Wallace and State Department director Avra M. Warren. Other diplomatic guests included Dominican Minister Counselor J. R. Rodriguez and U.S. Ambassador to Panama J. Henry Norweb.

Rowe, de la Unión Panamericana, en el anexo de dicha entidad, en honor del embajador dominicano Emilio García Godoy y del embajador panameño Samuel Lewis. El encuentro congregó a notables figuras gubernamentales, entre las cuales figuraban el secretario de Comercio Henry A. Wallace y el director del Departamento de Estado Avra M. Warren. Entre los demás concurrentes figuraron el ministro consejero dominicano J. R. Rodríguez y el embajador estadounidense en Panamá J. Henry Norweb.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on U.S. wartime cooperation and mutual aid programs established across Latin America. Cooperative health programs to control malaria were launched in eighteen nations, including the Dominican Republic and Haiti, to sustain the production of vital war materials. The article emphasized that these initiatives, along with agricultural and technical assistance, were mutually beneficial cooperative efforts rather than unilateral handouts.

El informe recalcó que estos planes, junto al respaldo técnico y agrícola, obedecían a esquemas bilaterales equitativos de beneficio común y no a dádivas discrecionales unilaterales.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dr. Sevilla of Nicaragua was scheduled to fly to the Dominican Republic to present his credentials to President Rafael Trujillo as the Nicaraguan Minister in Ciudad Trujillo. Sevilla was staying at the Roosevelt Hotel in Washington alongside legal adviser Leopoldo Arguello Gil before departing. The report also covered social and diplomatic activities involving Cuban and Venezuelan embassy officials.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* comunicó que el Dr. Sevilla, representante de Nicaragua, tenía proyectado viajar por vía aérea a la República Dominicana a fin de hacer entrega de sus credenciales al presidente Rafael Trujillo como ministro nicaragüense en Ciudad Trujillo. Previo a su despegue, Sevilla se alojaba en el Roosevelt Hotel de Washington junto a su consultor jurídico Leopoldo Argüello Gil. La nota también pasó revista a reuniones de carácter social protagonizadas por diplomáticos adscritos a las embajadas de Cuba y Venezuela.

Morgan, who performed numerous charitable operations for the underprivileged in the Dominican Republic without accepting payment. Dr. Morgan commended the Dominican government for its cooperation and health advancements, noting the presence of government hospitals in Trujillo City and Santiago prior to the construction of Morgan Hospital. records.summary_en: The Midland Journal reported on upcoming celebrations marking the 450th anniversary of the founding of Santo Domingo, featuring a historic pageant and an address by President Rafael Trujillo. The article noted that the capital was rebuilt along modern lines following a devastating hurricane in 1930 and subsequently renamed Ciudad Trujillo by its citizens despite Trujillo's objections. It also praised the republic's fertile agriculture and highlighted its strong standing in Washington following its early war declarations against Japan and Germany in December 1941.
records.summary_es: El *Midland Journal* informó sobre los preparativos para conmemorar el 450.º aniversario de la fundación de la ciudad de Santo Domingo, programa que comprendería una representación alegórica de valor histórico y el discurso del mandatario Rafael Trujillo. El artículo consignó que la capital había renacido bajo directrices modernas luego del desolador huracán de 1930, siendo rebautizada como Ciudad Trujillo por voluntad popular no obstante la renuencia inicial de Trujillo. Destacó asimismo la fecunda fertilidad agrícola nacional y el sólido predicamento de que gozaba el régimen en Washington tras su pronta declaración de guerra a Japón y Alemania en diciembre de 1941.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on an interview with President Rafael Trujillo in which he announced plans to encourage a two- or three-party system with free elections during the 450th anniversary of Santo Domingo. Trujillo denied operating as a dictator, asserting that his critics had private motives, and pledged to grant amnesty to all political refugees to allow their safe return. He stated that the nation had achieved stability ahead of the presidential election scheduled for May 16, 1947.

Trujillo negó tachaduras de autócrata sosteniendo que sus detractores obedecían a móviles inconfesables, y prometió conceder indulto y amnistía general a los refugiados políticos para garantizar su retorno al terruño. Afirmó enfáticamente que el país gozaba de sosiego institucional ante las elecciones presidenciales convocadas para el 16 de mayo de 1947.

records.summary_en: The Springfield Weekly Republican reported on the extensive modernization of the Dominican Republic under President Rafael Trujillo over a sixteen-year span achieved without foreign loans. Improvements included a twenty percent decrease in illiteracy, hundreds of newly built schools, seventy new bridges, and irrigation projects reclaiming 85,000 acres. The article noted that the rebuilt capital, renamed Ciudad Trujillo by citizens, was growing into a major Caribbean tourist destination.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* reportó las profundas transformaciones de progreso material logradas por la República Dominicana bajo el mandato de dieciséis años del presidente Rafael Trujillo, realizadas sin necesidad de préstamos extranjeros. Los adelantos abarcaban una reducción del veinte por ciento en el analfabetismo, centenares de escuelas recién levantadas, setenta puentes nuevos e infraestructuras de regadío que recuperaron 85.000 acres de tierra. El informe agregaba que la reconstruida capital, rebautizada Ciudad Trujillo por la población, se afianzaba como un emporio turístico caribeño de primer orden.

records.headline: Eye witness reports received today frem Matanzas on the North Coast
records.summary_en: Eyewitness reports from Matanzas, on the north coast, said a tidal wave from Sunday's earthquake swept as much as a mile inland, catching even a party fleeing by automobile, and left only eight of the town's 300 houses standing. Residents had taken refuge in trees and high places, and reports from Matanzas and Nagua said frightened inhabitants in the forests were suffering from hunger, with authorities considering dropping food from airplanes, as wrecked communications made the damage across more than 11 towns hard to assess.
records.summary_es: Testimonios desde Matanzas, en la costa norte, decían que un maremoto provocado por el terremoto del domingo penetró hasta una milla tierra adentro, alcanzó incluso a un grupo que huía en automóvil y dejó en pie solo ocho de las 300 casas del pueblo. Los vecinos se habían refugiado en árboles y lugares altos, y los informes de Matanzas y Nagua decían que habitantes asustados en los bosques padecían hambre, mientras las autoridades consideraban lanzar alimentos desde aviones y las comunicaciones destruidas dificultaban evaluar los daños en más de 11 pueblos.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that President Rafael Trujillo directed relief operations across the Dominican Republic following a severe earthquake, deploying the military, police, and Red Cross to stricken communities including Matanzas, Nagua, Moca, and San Francisco de Macoris. Santiago suffered extensive building damage and one death, while another casualty occurred in San Francisco de Macoris. Neighboring Haiti reported minor effects in Port-au-Prince but significant destruction across northern border towns.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el mandatario Rafael Trujillo encabezó personalmente las labores de rescate en toda la República Dominicana a raíz del feroz terremoto, comisionando tropas del ejército, agentes policiales y brigadas de la Cruz Roja a las poblaciones más flageladas, entre ellas Matanzas, Nagua, Moca y San Francisco de Macorís. En Santiago se verificaron serios derrumbes y una víctima fatal, registrándose otro muerto en San Francisco de Macorís. En el colindante territorio de Haití se sintieron efectos menores en Puerto Príncipe, pero se reportaron considerables averías en los distritos de la frontera norte.

records.summary_en: The Washington Daily News reported rising casualties from the Dominican earthquake and tidal wave, with twenty bodies recovered at Bajio Cabrera, six at Arroyo Delgado, two in Puerto Plata, and one in Moca. An estimated twenty thousand people out of a population of one hundred thousand in the disaster zone were left homeless. Relief operations mobilized swiftly, including U.S. Navy flying boats carrying medical personnel and supplies from San Juan alongside Dominican aircraft from Ciudad Trujillo.
records.summary_es: *The Washington Daily News* dio cuenta del incremento de víctimas mortales provocado por el sismo y maremoto en República Dominicana, informando del rescate de veinte cadáveres en Bajío Cabrera, seis en Arroyo Delgado, dos en Puerto Plata y uno en Moca. Se calculaba que unas veinte mil personas, de los cien mil pobladores radicados en la zona del cataclismo, habían quedado a la intemperie sin hogar. Las operaciones de socorro se articularon con premura, sumándose hidroaviones de la Armada estadounidense con médicos y pertrechos desde San Juan de Puerto Rico a los aparatos dominicanos despachados desde Ciudad Trujillo.

records.summary_en: The Daily Alaska Empire reported that a strong earthquake shook the Dominican Republic, causing widespread panic but no casualties or significant damage. The tremor was identified as the strongest in thirteen days amidst an ongoing series of quakes across the country. Other brief dispatches covered a hunting fatality in Alaska and mechanical delays in German rocket testing in New Mexico.

El temblor fue catalogado como el más violento de las dos últimas semanas en medio del enjambre sísmico que azotaba a la nación. Otras gacetillas del despacho reseñaron un mortal accidente de cacería en Alaska e inconvenientes mecánicos en el ensayo con cohetes alemanes en Nuevo México.

records.headline: A dispatch from Bunnell, Florida, reports that a deputy sheriff shot and killed a 20-year-old Dominican, an adopted…
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Bunnell, Florida, reports that a deputy sheriff shot and killed a 20-year-old Dominican, an adopted nephew of President Rafael Trujillo, mistaking him for a colored American insisting upon his civil rights, as the young man, on terminal leave from the United States Army after two years of service, was driving from New York to Miami on Friday night. Dominican Consul Jose M. Noel hurried to Florida on Saturday night under direct orders of President Trujillo to determine why the young man was killed, and Sheriff Henry Wells said the shooting was done by Deputy Miller Teeter.

records.headline: Young Trujillo was shot and killed on Saturday night near Bunnell, Florida, after he and his companion Louis Henry…
records.summary_en: Young Trujillo was shot and killed on Saturday night near Bunnell, Florida, after he and his companion Louis Henry Todd were refused service at a cafe because they were thought to be American Negroes and argued that they should be served. Deputy Sheriff Tetter testified at the inquest that Trujillo, seated in his car, drew a pistol and was shot through the chest when he refused to put it away; the dead youth, generally called Trujillo but named Seijas, was the adopted son of Anibal Trujillo, brother of President Trujillo, and was on terminal leave from the United States Army on his way home.
records.summary_es: El joven Trujillo fue muerto a tiros el sábado por la noche cerca de Bunnell, Florida, después de que a él y a su compañero Louis Henry Todd se les negara el servicio en un café porque se les creyó negros estadounidenses y de que discutieran que debían ser atendidos. El alguacil adjunto Tetter declaró en la pesquisa que Trujillo, sentado en su automóvil, sacó una pistola y recibió un tiro en el pecho cuando se negó a guardarla; el joven fallecido, llamado generalmente Trujillo pero de nombre Seijas, era hijo adoptivo de Aníbal Trujillo, hermano del presidente Trujillo, y estaba con licencia terminal del Ejército de los Estados Unidos de camino a su hogar.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on an escalating banana trade war in Haiti between the Standard Fruit Company and independent exporters following the overthrow of President Elie Lescot. President Dumarsais Estime's administration reportedly prepared to revoke the export license of Habanex due to its owner's family ties to Lescot. Meanwhile, independent shippers accused Standard Fruit of aggressive price competition that threatened to price American importers out of the market.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó sobre la encarnizada pugna por el negocio bananero en Haití entre la Standard Fruit Company y firmas exportadoras autónomas a raíz del derrocamiento del presidente Élie Lescot. Trascendió que la administración del presidente Dumarsais Estimé se disponía a revocar los permisos comerciales de la compañía Habanex a causa del parentesco de su titular con Lescot. Paralelamente, los consignatarios independientes acusaban a la Standard Fruit de prácticas de competencia desleal en precios destinadas a expulsar a los importadores norteamericanos de plaza.

records.headline: On August 4th Protestant leaders from eight nations, gathered in England
records.summary_en: The East Hartford Gazette reviewed major news highlights of late 1946, noting that the Dominican Republic suffered severe losses from a violent earthquake and tidal wave in August. The retrospective also cited international incidents including the desertion of the steamship *American Farmer* and the Yugoslav shootdown of two American airplanes. Additional domestic events covered labor strikes, price controls, and the anniversary of the U.S. Army Air Forces.
records.summary_es: El *East Hartford Gazette* presentó una recopilación de los sucesos más descollantes de finales de 1946, destacando que la República Dominicana sufrió desastrosas pérdidas a consecuencia del terremoto y maremoto registrados en agosto. La síntesis informativa rememoró también episodios internacionales como el abandono del vapor *American Farmer* y el derribo por fuerzas yugoslavas de dos aeronaves militares estadounidenses. En el ámbito interno, recapituló jornadas de huelga obrera, controversias por los controles de precios y el aniversario de las Fuerzas Aéreas del Ejército norteamericano.

records.summary_en: The Key West Citizen reported that Haiti's application for an Export-Import Bank loan remained pending amid growing criticism from local Communists over past American occupation debts. Concurrently, Haitian President Dumarsais Estime moved toward closer ties with Argentina, with President Juan Domingo Peron reportedly extending credit and diplomatic overtures. The report also referenced the neighboring Dominican Republic under President Rafael Trujillo sharing the island of Hispaniola.
records.summary_es: El *Key West Citizen* reportó que la petición formulada por Haití para un empréstito ante el Export-Import Bank permanecía irresuelta, en medio del creciente clamor opositor comunista derivado de las deudas financieras acarreadas de la pasada ocupación militar estadounidense. A la par, el gobernante haitiano Dumarsais Estimé procuraba estrechar lazos con Argentina, país cuyo mandatario Juan Domingo Perón le había extendido ofertas crediticias y diplomáticas. La nota aludió además a la condición de vecindad que unía a Haití con la República Dominicana de Rafael Trujillo en el suelo compartido de La Española.

records.summary_en: The Chronicle-Star Combined with the Moss Point Advertiser reported on political and economic tensions in Haiti as the government awaited an Export-Import Bank loan from the United States. Local factions criticized long-standing American financial controls dating to the 1922 occupation, while Argentina sought commercial influence by offering loans and exchanging ambassadors. The account highlighted geopolitical dynamics involving Haitian President Dumarsais Estime and Dominican President Rafael Trujillo on Hispaniola.
records.summary_es: El *Chronicle-Star Combined with the Moss Point Advertiser* reseñó las tensiones políticas y financieras que sacudían a Haití mientras el ejecutivo esperaba el desembolso de un préstamo del Export-Import Bank de Estados Unidos. Diversos sectores locales impugnaban las ataduras fiscales estadounidenses que pervivían desde la ocupación de 1922, mientras la Argentina procuraba ganar ascendiente mercantil brindando créditos e intercambiando embajadores. La crónica puntualizó los equilibrios de poder que vinculaban en La Española al mandatario haitiano Dumarsais Estimé y al presidente dominicano Rafael Trujillo.
