records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Brazil, Venezuela, and Haiti were moving aggressively to purge communist influence in hopes of securing financial favor from the United States. In Haiti, President Dumarsais Estime dissolved the Communist Party by decree after Washington withheld a $20,000,000 loan needed for debt retirement and agricultural development. Similar anti-communist actions were noted in Brazil under President Dutra and Venezuela under President Betancourt.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que Brasil, Venezuela y Haití emprendían severas purgas anticomunistas con miras a captar auxilios y beneficios crediticios de los Estados Unidos. En Haití, el gobernante Dumarsais Estimé ilegalizó el Partido Comunista mediante decreto luego de que Washington suspendiera una partida financiera de 20.000.000 de dólares vital para redimir deuda y financiar planes agrarios. Represalias ideológicas similares fueron adoptadas en el Brasil presidido por Dutra y en la Venezuela del presidente Betancourt.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dominican Ambassador Julio Ortega Frier claimed an invasion expedition comprising two landing craft and a corvette had sailed from Cuba, accompanied by at least seven aircraft. Plane Hunt
(Continued From First Page.)

A search started, and airports along both Florida coasts were checked without success, as were other Gulf areas. Meanwhile no Washington agency could be found that would admit ordering the alert.

Then, yesterday afternoon, the State Department acknowledged it had heard the rumor and said it had relayed it to the Customs Bureau and other agencies for investigation.

The statement disclosed that the State Department has had in effect for months a general alert, based on “general rumors of revolutionary plotting,” to make sure that “United States territory would not be used for conspiracy.”

Rumor Involves 7 Planes.

The statement, issued by Press Officer Reginald Mitchell, said the State Department has been receiving “rumors” and “fragmentary reports” of impending trouble in the Caribbean area but has declined to comment because of their unsubstantial nature. The statement continued:

“One such rumor was to the effect that there were seven combat planes at an airfield in Florida ready to depart for a Caribbean destination. The department Friday immediately communicated this rumor to the Customs Bureau and other United States Government agencies concerned and requested that an investigation be made and that these alleged planes be prevented from leaving the United States.

“The department has been informed that the Customs Bureau promptly notified its Florida headquarters office at Tampa which in turn alerted its subordinate customs offices at Miami, Jacksonville, West Palm Beach and elsewhere in Florida. The department has received no further information in this particular matter.

“The department heard general rumors of revolutionary plotting in the Caribbean area as long ago as January of this year and in an effort to make sure that United States territory would not be used for conspiracy alerted the appropriate law enforcement agencies, which since that date have kept a scrupulous watch.”

Easy Flight for Fighters.

At least some of the rumors were based on reports in Haitian and Dominican newspapers.

The P38 Lightning and the P51 Mustang, Army fighter planes extensively used in the war, would easily be able to fly from Florida to the Dominican Republic. The shortest airline distance is a little over 650 miles. There are the Bahama Islands and the tip of Cuba in between.

A War Department official said some Lightnings and Mustangs have been sold as surplus and may be in the hands of civilians.

“There are plenty of young fellows in this country who know how to fly these ships,” he said.

The Dominican Ambassador, Julio Ortega Frier, told a reporter some days ago that he knew the revolutionaries had at least seven planes. He said yesterday he didn’t know where these planes were bought.

Reported Sailing.

The Ambassador said last Saturday that an army of 3,000 “Communist revolutionaries” from Cuba, Guatemala, Venezuela and Puerto Rico was poised in Cuba for an invasion. The governments concerned denied it.

Thursday night he said two landing craft and one corvette had sailed from Cuba with invasion forces, but he had no further word on this.

The Ambassador said a call to Ciudad Trujillo produced this information:

“The government has air patrols around the coast. Everything is calm in Ciudad Trujillo and not a single aircraft has been heard in the sky. Nevertheless, the government is taking all precautions.”

Haitians returning from the Dominican Republic were quoted in Port-au-Prince newspapers as saying they left because of apprehension over heavy troop movements throughout the republic, which shares the island of Haiti.

records.summary_en: A historical account traces the United States customs receivership to the Dominican resolution of March 31, 1905, known as the Modus Vivendi, which conceded to the United States the same rights over customs income as an earlier pact. It states that the Dominican-American Covenant signed February 8, 1907, gave the United States President the right to name a General Receiver of Customs to collect all Dominican customs taxes until government bonds issued to settle debts were paid and retired.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that federal customs authorities in Baltimore detained the *Patria*, a converted infantry landing craft suspected of involvement in anti-Trujillo activities. An investigation revealed the vessel was manned largely by affluent Dominican exiles and had been acquired by Cuban Cruz Alonso, though a search found no weapons or ammunition. The State Department stated the action enforced strict policy prohibiting the use of United States territory to launch civil strife in foreign nations.

Las pesquisas comprobaron que la dotación estaba formada mayoritariamente por acaudalados desterrados dominicanos y que la nave había sido adquirida por el cubano Cruz Alonso, si bien el registro ocular no arrojó hallazgo de municiones ni fusiles. El Departamento de Estado aclaró que la retención obedecía a la estricta política neutral de proscribir la utilización del suelo estadounidense para fraguar expediciones bélicas contra Estados soberanos.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star published a letter from Dominican exile Persio C. Franco criticizing former Secretary of State Cordell Hull for congratulating President Rafael Trujillo on paying off the Dominican foreign debt. Franco condemned Hull's praise as inappropriate, accusing Trujillo of seizing power through treason in 1930 and maintaining control through terror and murder. Franco appealed to democratic nations to support the Dominican people in reclaiming their freedom rather than endorsing the dictatorship.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Cuban political leaders sharply condemned President Ramon Grau San Martin following the Cuban army's suppression of a 1,500-man expedition organized to invade the Dominican Republic. Senators Eduardo Chibas and Aurelio Alvarez accused Grau of using the anti-Trujillo movement to destabilize Cuban politics and consolidate personal dictatorial power. Military authorities detained over 1,100 expedition members and seized four ships along with extensive stockpiles of arms and explosives.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que destacados dirigentes políticos de Cuba enjuiciaron con dureza al presidente Ramón Grau San Martín tras la desarticulación por el ejército cubano de una expedición de 1.500 combatientes aprestada para invadir la República Dominicana. Los senadores Eduardo Chibás y Aurelio Álvarez acusaron a Grau de instrumentalizar la conspiración antitrujillista para subvertir el orden interno de Cuba y afianzar prerrogativas dictatoriales propias. Las fuerzas castrenses arrestaron a más de 1.100 conjurados e incautaron cuatro embarcaciones mercantes y nutridos arsenales de pertrechos, proyectiles y dinamita.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Cuban magistrate Evelio Tabio ordered the release of nearly 1,200 participants in the aborted anti-Trujillo invasion expedition, holding only its purported leaders in custody. A captured diary published by the newspaper *Hoy* detailed training at Holguin and miserable conditions on Cayo Confites, where troops endured internal infighting, accidental drownings, and failed logistics aboard vessels including the *Aurora*, *Berta*, and *Angelita*. The collapse of the operation culminated in mass surrenders at Guinchos Cay and Antilla.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el magistrado judicial cubano Evelio Tabío dispuso la libertad de casi 1.200 integrantes de la frustrada expedición armada antitrujillista, reteniendo en presidio únicamente a los sindicados como cabecillas principales. Un diario de bitácora ocupado y divulgado por el diario *Hoy* detalló los adiestramientos castrenses en Holguín y las precarias penalidades sufridas en Cayo Confites, donde los reclutas padecieron motines internos, ahogamientos accidentales y severos descalabros de abasto a bordo de los barcos *Aurora*, *Berta* y *Angelita*. El fracaso del complot culminó con rendiciones multitudinarias en Cayo Guinchos y la bahía de Antilla.

records.summary_en: Twenty-six alleged chiefs of a 1,007-man expeditionary force to depose President Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic were freed in Havana under bonds of $5,000 each. Special Magistrate Evelio Tabio charged them with jeopardizing the peace of the state and taking enlistments without authorization of the Cuban government. The group, mostly Dominicans and Cubans, included eight generals; the rest of the force, including three men from the United States, had been freed after surrendering on Guinchos Cay and at Antilla.

El magistrado especial Evelio Tabio los acusó de poner en peligro la paz del Estado y de realizar alistamientos sin autorización del gobierno cubano. El grupo, en su mayoría dominicanos y cubanos, incluía ocho generales; el resto de la fuerza, incluidos tres hombres de Estados Unidos, había sido liberado tras rendirse en Cayo Guinchos y en Antilla.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Manolo Castro, head of the Cuban Sports Commission, pleaded not guilty in federal court in Jacksonville to charges of illegally exporting weapons and explosives intended for an uprising against Dominican President Rafael Trujillo. Castro alleged that Trujillo's personal hostility was behind his indictment. Co-defendants Chester L. Miller and Percy H. Cyr also pleaded not guilty, while Hollis B. Smith entered a guilty plea to purchasing the munitions.

Castro alegó que su encausamiento respondía al encono personal que Trujillo le profesaba. Los coacusados Chester L. Miller y Percy H. Cyr sostuvieron igualmente su no culpabilidad, mientras que Hollis B. Smith admitió formalmente los cargos de adquisición ilícita de armas.

Venezuelan authorities highlighted imports of 10,000 rifles and 800 machine guns as exceeding legitimate Dominican defense requirements. While asserting a right to sever diplomatic ties, the Venezuelan government affirmed it would not initiate hostilities unless compelled to defend its sovereignty.

La cancillería venezolana remarcó que las compras de 10.000 fusiles y 800 ametralladoras desbordaban con creces las urgencias ordinarias de defensa de la nación caribeña. Pese a arrogarse la prerrogativa de quebrar los tratos bilaterales, el régimen de Caracas aseguró que no desencadenaría hostilidades salvo que se viera forzado a salvaguardar su territorio nacional.

records.headline: DIPLOMATIC NOTES FOR DREW PEARSON A plot by the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: A White Paper circulated by the Venezuelan Embassy charged that the Dominican Republic was plotting to send an armed invasion against Venezuela, accusing dictator Trujillo of harboring Venezuelan enemies and purchasing arms for them in Brazil. As proof it attached a photostat of an intercepted letter from Trujillo's private secretary to Dominican foreign offices around the world, instructing them to attend to exiled Venezuelans, enemies of Caracas, and to tell them they would find in the Dominican Republic refuge, hospitality and protection, personal as well as political. The White Paper added that the Venezuelan government had concrete proof the Dominican Republic had long sponsored an armed movement against Venezuela.
records.summary_es: Un Libro Blanco distribuido por la Embajada de Venezuela acusó a la República Dominicana de tramar el envío de una invasión armada contra Venezuela, señalando al dictador Trujillo de albergar a enemigos venezolanos y comprar armas para ellos en Brasil. Como prueba adjuntaba una fotocopia de una carta interceptada del secretario privado de Trujillo a las oficinas dominicanas en el exterior, con instrucciones de atender a los venezolanos exiliados, enemigos de Caracas, y decirles que en la República Dominicana encontrarían refugio, hospitalidad y protección, tanto personal como política. El Libro Blanco añadía que el gobierno venezolano tenía pruebas concretas de que la República Dominicana auspiciaba desde hacía tiempo un movimiento armado contra Venezuela.

records.summary_en: The Atlanta Daily World reported that Brooklyn Dodgers first baseman Jackie Robinson reported to spring training in Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, where he was greeted enthusiastically as a baseball hero. Local spectators and schoolchildren cheered his appearance in the dugout, batting practice, and drills at first base. Robinson arrived fifteen pounds overweight but aimed to improve upon his .297 batting average from the previous season.

La afición deportiva y nutridos grupos de escolares lo ovacionaron con fervor en la caseta de jugadores, durante sus turnos al bate y en los entrenamientos en la primera almohadilla. Aunque Robinson se presentó al terreno con quince libras de sobrepeso, aspiraba a superar su promedio ofensivo de .297 bateado en la temporada anterior.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the Costa Rican government appealed to Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic for military assistance against insurgent forces led by Jose Figueres. Rebel troops sabotaged electrical installations at Brazil and launched surprise assaults at Quepos, threatening the advance toward Cartago. The armed conflict arose following the disputed presidential election of Otilio Ulate, which the government-controlled Congress had annulled in favor of Rafael Calderon Guardia.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el gobierno constitucional de Costa Rica recabó socorro de armas a Nicaragua y a la República Dominicana con el propósito de combatir a las columnas rebeldes acaudilladas por José Figueres. Los destacamentos insurrectos sabotearon redes de energía en la localidad de Brasil y acometieron asaltos sorpresivos en Quepos, poniendo en jaque el avance hacia Cartago. La contienda intestina estalló a raíz de los controvertidos sufragios presidenciales que ungieron a Otilio Ulate, los cuales fueron anulados por el Congreso oficialista para beneficiar al candidato Rafael Calderón Guardia.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star analyzed strategic vulnerabilities in Caribbean defenses, warning of potential submarine threats to the Panama Canal and regional bases. The analysis noted ongoing armed conflict in Costa Rica, where government forces reportedly received backing from Dominicans, Nicaraguans, and Hondurans against rebels supporting Otilio Ulate. The author cautioned that a communist victory would leave American defense lines bordered by hostile regimes, with the unsympathetic Dominican government positioned centrally in the region.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* examinó las vulnerabilidades operativas en el dispositivo de seguridad caribeño, previniendo acerca de posibles amenazas submarinas contra el canal de Panamá y las bases tácticas comarcanas. El redactor alertó de que una victoria de cuño comunista dejaría el cordón defensivo estadounidense flanqueado por regímenes antagonistas, con el desconfiado gobierno dominicano afianzado en el corazón del espacio antillano.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported regional political developments across Latin America, noting that Dominican President Rafael Trujillo alleged conspiracies against his regime originating in Cuba, Venezuela, and Central America. Trujillo was engaged in an intense war of nerves with Venezuela amid escalating mutual suspicions. The summary also noted constitutional maneuvering by Juan Peron in Argentina and military conspiracy arrests in Chile.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* reseñó los episodios políticos de la coyuntura regional latinoamericana, indicando que el presidente dominicano Rafael Trujillo denunció la urdimbre de confabulaciones golpistas contra su mandato orquestadas en Cuba, Venezuela y Centroamérica. Trujillo sostenía una aguda guerra de nervios con Venezuela al compás de crecientes recelos mutuos. La síntesis informativa dio cuenta además de las reformas institucionales promovidas por Juan Perón en Argentina y del apresamiento de conspiradores castrenses en Chile.

records.summary_en: The Ohio Daily-Express reported that captured correspondence revealed former Haitian diplomat Col. Astrel Roland conspired with Dominican President Rafael Trujillo and Interior Minister Alvarez Paulino to orchestrate an invasion of Haiti. A Belgian woman named Lady Verbracken, operating as an ethnologist, gathered Haitian military intelligence and coordinated strategy meetings in New York with Dominican officials. Following his dismissal from the diplomatic service in January, Roland launched subversive radio broadcasts targeting the Haitian government.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the Organization of American States referred the dispute between Haiti and the Dominican Republic over Col. Astrel Roland's subversive broadcasts to a peace commission, which advised direct bilateral negotiations. Haitian diplomats stated the broadcasts caused widespread unrest that necessitated declaring a state of siege to maintain public order. While Dominican authorities defended the broadcasts under free speech on a private station, Haitian officials contended the station was controlled by President Trujillo's brother.

El cuerpo diplomático haitiano adujo que las emisiones agitaron graves conmociones que forzaron a la promulgación del estado de sitio para restablecer la paz pública. Si bien las autoridades dominicanas escudaron las transmisiones amparándose en la libre expresión ejercida en una emisora particular, los voceros haitianos arguyeron que la referida estación estaba supeditada al hermano del gobernante Trujillo.

records.summary_en: The Key West Citizen published an editorial describing President Rafael Trujillo's dictatorial grip on the Dominican Republic, asserting that citizens lived in fear of enforced disappearances and state repression. The article portrayed Trujillo traveling in armored convoys out of fear for his safety and enriching himself openly with national public revenues. It observed that these oppressive conditions inspired foreign volunteers, including Americans, to join a recent anti-Trujillo invasion attempt that ended as a poorly planned fiasco.
records.summary_es: El *Key West Citizen* publicó una pieza editorial que retrataba el férreo control dictatorial impuesto por el mandatario Rafael Trujillo sobre la República Dominicana, aseverando que la ciudadanía vivía bajo el pavor permanente de las desapariciones forzosas y la violencia punitiva del Estado. La nota describía a Trujillo desplazándose en comitivas acorazadas por temor a su vida y lucrándose descaradamente del erario público. Hizo notar que ese opresivo clima motivó a brigadistas extranjeros, incluidos ciudadanos estadounidenses, a enrolarse en una reciente incursión armada contra Trujillo que zozobró convertida en un auténtico fiasco táctico.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the Dominican government established a domestic munitions factory in San Cristobal to manufacture rifles and machine guns with the assistance of European technical advisers. The Dominican Information Center stated that President Rafael Trujillo initiated domestic arms production after the U.S. State Department denied purchases of American war surplus arms following the 1947 Cayo Confites invasion attempt. Plans called for expanding the factory to produce ammunition, heavy artillery, and aircraft engines.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el gobierno dominicano instaló en San Cristóbal una fábrica nacional de armamentos destinada a la manufactura de fusiles y ametralladoras bajo el asesoramiento de técnicos europeos. El Centro de Información Dominicano comunicó que el mandatario Rafael Trujillo dispuso la industria armamentística local luego de que el Departamento de Estado de EE. UU. vetara la adquisición de pertrechos militares excedentes tras la intentona expedicionaria de Cayo Confites en 1947. Los planes contemplaban ampliar las instalaciones fabriles para la elaboración de municiones, artillería pesada y propulsores para la aviación militar.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on regional political polarization pitting Cuba, Guatemala, and Costa Rica against the authoritarian regimes of Rafael Trujillo in the Dominican Republic and Anastasio Somoza in Nicaragua. While the United States maintained a policy of non-intervention, diplomats debated proposals by Panama's Ricardo J. Alfaro urging the Organization of American States to deny recognition to regimes seizing power through coups. Observers emphasized that enduring democratic stability in the Caribbean would require addressing deep-seated socioeconomic grievances.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó sobre la polarización política regional que enfrentaba a Cuba, Guatemala y Costa Rica contra los regímenes autoritarios de Rafael Trujillo en la República Dominicana y Anastasio Somoza en Nicaragua. Mientras Estados Unidos mantenía una política de no intervención, los diplomáticos debatían las propuestas del panameño Ricardo J. Alfaro, quien instaba a la Organización de los Estados Americanos a negar el reconocimiento a los regímenes que tomaran el poder mediante golpes de Estado. Los observadores enfatizaron que una estabilidad democrática duradera en el Caribe requeriría abordar profundos reclamos socioeconómicos.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Secretary of State Dean Acheson cautioned against resorting to war after Dominican President Rafael Trujillo requested congressional authority to declare war on nations harboring anti-Trujillo invasion forces. Acheson stressed that established inter-American procedures existed to resolve disputes peacefully without military conflict. Trujillo's war-power request stemmed from allegations that Cuba and Guatemala were facilitating renewed revolutionary plots against his government.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el secretario de Estado Dean Acheson advirtió contra el recurso a la guerra después de que el presidente dominicano Rafael Trujillo solicitara autorización al Congreso para declarar la guerra a las naciones que albergaran fuerzas de invasión antitrujillistas. Acheson recalcó que existían procedimientos interamericanos establecidos para resolver disputas de manera pacífica y sin conflictos militares. La solicitud de poderes de guerra de Trujillo se derivaba de acusaciones de que Cuba y Guatemala facilitaban nuevos complots revolucionarios contra su gobierno.

records.full_text:
Dominican Republic
Asks New Airing of
Dispute With Cuba

By the Associated Press

A long-standing feud between Cuba and the Dominican Republic was spotlighted yesterday when the Dominican government formally asked for another airing of troubles between the two countries.

The development occurred in an exchange of notes between the Dominican government and the five-nation Inter-American Peace Committee.

The latter group was set up by the 21 hemisphere foreign ministers in 1940 to seek peaceful settlement of Inter-American disputes. The United States, Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Cuba are members.

After three weeks of discussion the committee Thursday night sent a note to the Dominican government expressing concern over special war powers granted to President Rafael Trujillo. The Dominican Republic replied that they resulted from a “profound state of emergency” in the Caribbean.

War Powers Granted.

Trujillo got from the Dominican Congress this month power to declare war on any country which he considers is harboring plotters working against him.

The move was directed to Cuba where Mr. Trupillo charged a new attempt to mount an invasion of the Dominican Republic is going on. This was strongly denied by Cuba.

The committee’s note asked Mr. Trujillo not to use force unless under armed attack in accordance with terms of the Rio mutual defense treaty.

In reply, Dominican Secretary of State Virgilio Diaz Ordonez said “no other country or government would fail to act in the same way as we are doing now.” But he added that the republic would respond to any conciliatory gesture to end the “abnormality with which we are confronted.”

His note added the government is ready to receive recommendations from the committee.

The feud between the two Caribbean nations is an old story to the committee. In 1948, the group got the two nations to agree to settle their differences through diplomatic channels. The Dominican charge then was based on an unsuccessful attempt in 1947 by various groups of exiles to create an invasion force in Cuba to overthrow Mr. Trujillo.

The following year the Dominicans went before the committee with the assertion the same group was being outfitted anew in Cuba.

A few months ago the committee issued a 14-point statement designed to calm Caribbean tension after an airborne invasion of the Dominican Republic failed.

In the meantime, it settled a flareup between the neighboring Dominican Republic and Haiti when the latter charged Mr. Trujillo was personally involved in a plot to ove-thorw the Port-au-Prince government.

Features highlighted included swimming pools, tennis courts, open-air dancing, nightly entertainment, and a gambling casino. The edition also covered congressional approval of emergency housing funds to assist victims of Midwest flooding.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dominican Ambassador Luis Francisco Thomen conferred the Order of Juan Pablo Duarte upon Dr. Murdock for his contributions to public health in the Dominican Republic. The ceremony and embassy reception coincided with sessions of the Pan American Sanitary Bureau and the World Health Organization. Guests including State Department officials and medical leaders were served traditional Dominican specialties alongside American delicacies.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el embajador dominicano Luis Francisco Thomen condecoró al Dr. Murdock con la Orden de Juan Pablo Duarte por sus aportes a la salud pública en la República Dominicana. La ceremonia y recepción en la embajada coincidieron con las sesiones de la Oficina Sanitaria Panamericana y la Organización Mundial de la Salud. A los invitados, entre quienes figuraban funcionarios del Departamento de Estado y dirigentes médicos, se les sirvieron especialidades tradicionales dominicanas junto a manjares estadounidenses.

records.summary_en: The Atlanta Daily World reported that President Rafael Trujillo resumed direct control of the Dominican government after temporarily delegating executive authority to his brother, General Hector Bienvenido Trujillo, since February. The dispatch observed that Trujillo frequently rotated titular authority between himself and his brother without public explanation. It noted that the ruling Dominican Party had nominated Hector for the presidency in upcoming May elections, despite executive decisions remaining concentrated in Rafael's hands.
records.summary_es: El *Atlanta Daily World* informó que el presidente Rafael Trujillo reasumió el control directo del gobierno dominicano tras haber delegado temporalmente el poder ejecutivo en su hermano, el general Héctor Bienvenido Trujillo, desde febrero. El despacho observaba que Trujillo alternaba con frecuencia la titularidad del mando con su hermano sin ofrecer explicaciones públicas. Señaló asimismo que el oficialista Partido Dominicano había postulado a Héctor a la presidencia para las elecciones venideras de mayo, aun cuando las decisiones ejecutivas seguían concentradas en manos de Rafael.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the United States concluded a ten-year bilateral pact with the Dominican Republic authorizing guided missile monitoring stations to close the observation gap between the Bahamas and Puerto Rico. Under the agreement, unarmed test missiles launched from Florida would fly over Dominican coastal waters rather than over the mainland. U.S. military personnel operating the tracking sites were capped at 300 individuals, expandable up to 500 under exceptional circumstances.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que Estados Unidos concertó un pacto bilateral de diez años con la República Dominicana que autorizaba estaciones de rastreo de misiles guiados para cerrar la brecha de observación entre las Bahamas y Puerto Rico. En virtud del acuerdo, los misiles de prueba desarmados lanzados desde Florida sobrevolarían aguas costeras dominicanas en lugar de territorio continental. El personal militar estadounidense que operaría los puestos de seguimiento tenía un límite máximo de 300 efectivos, ampliable hasta 500 en circunstancias excepcionales.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the Dominican Republic and the Republic of Turkey signed a friendship treaty in Washington pledging perpetual peace between the two nations. The agreement was signed at the Turkish Embassy by Dominican Ambassador Luis Francisco Thomen and Turkish Ambassador Feridun C. Erkin. The accord established a framework for future bilateral treaties addressing commerce, navigation, consular rights, intellectual property, and extradition.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que la República Dominicana y la República de Turquía firmaron un tratado de amistad en Washington comprometiéndose a una paz perpetua entre ambas naciones. El pacto estableció las bases para futuros tratados bilaterales sobre comercio, navegación, derechos consulares, propiedad intelectual y extradición.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Cuban Foreign Minister Aureliano Sanchez Arango denounced the Dominican seizure of a vessel and the subsequent 30-year hard-labor sentences imposed on its crew for alleged subversive plotting. Sanchez Arango accused the ship's captain, Brito, of acting as a Dominican spy who delivered the craft and kidnapped its crew under shifting pretenses before being convicted alongside them. Because diplomatic protests proved futile, Cuba appealed the maritime incident to the Inter-American Peace Commission.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores de Cuba, Aureliano Sánchez Arango, denunció la captura de una embarcación por parte de la República Dominicana y las posteriores condenas a 30 años de trabajos forzados impuestas a su tripulación por supuestas actividades subversivas. Sánchez Arango acusó al capitán del barco, Brito, de actuar como espía dominicano que entregó la nave y secuestró a su tripulación bajo pretextos cambiantes antes de ser condenado junto a ellos. Dado que las protestas diplomáticas resultaron infructuosas, Cuba recurrió ante la Comisión Interamericana de Paz por el incidente marítimo.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Cuban Foreign Minister Aureliano Sanchez Arango planned to present evidence to the OAS Peace Committee demonstrating that the Dominican interception of the unarmed vessel *Quetzal* constituted high-seas piracy. Sanchez Arango argued that the ship was seized near Cape San Antonio, far from Dominican territory, and threatened to take the case to the United Nations and the World Court if Cuban crewmen were not freed. Dominican Foreign Minister Virgilio Diaz Ordonez prepared to argue the Dominican case before the committee, amidst reports that Guatemalan prisoners might soon be released.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores de Cuba, Aureliano Sánchez Arango, planeaba presentar pruebas ante la Comisión de Paz de la OEA para demostrar que la interceptación dominicana del buque desarmado *Quetzal* constituía piratería en alta mar. Sánchez Arango sostuvo que el barco fue capturado cerca del cabo de San Antonio, lejos de territorio dominicano, y amenazó con llevar el caso ante las Naciones Unidas y la Corte Internacional de Justicia si los tripulantes cubanos no eran liberados. El canciller dominicano Virgilio Díaz Ordóñez se preparaba para exponer los argumentos dominicanos ante el comité, en medio de informes sobre la posible pronta liberación de prisioneros guatemaltecos.

records.summary_en: The Catholic Times published a roster of nations maintaining diplomatic representation with the Holy See, listing twenty embassies including the Dominican Republic, Haiti, Cuba, and several other Latin American republics. The article detailed twenty-four legations accredited to the Vatican, noting current vacancies and suspended missions in Eastern Europe. It also enumerated countries that had established or restored official relations with the Holy See during the reigning pontificate.
records.summary_es: El *Catholic Times* publicó una nómina de las naciones que mantenían representación diplomática ante la Santa Sede, enumerando veinte embajadas entre las que figuraban la República Dominicana, Haití, Cuba y varias otras repúblicas latinoamericanas. El artículo detalló veinticuatro legaciones acreditadas ante el Vaticano, haciendo notar las vacantes vigentes y las misiones suspendidas en Europa del Este. Asimismo, enumeró los países que habían establecido o reanudado relaciones oficiales con la Santa Sede durante el pontificado en curso.

records.summary_en: The News and Views reported on the Dominican Republic's expansion of state-sanctioned nightlife and gambling casinos aimed at attracting American tourists. Four major casinos operated in Ciudad Trujillo, Boca Chica Beach, and San Cristobal, offering roulette, dice, and lavish floor shows. The article noted that Dominican authorities rebuffed attempts by American gambling syndicates to muscle into operations, choosing instead to import gaming equipment directly from Florida and Louisiana.

Cuatro grandes casinos funcionaban en Ciudad Trujillo, la playa de Boca Chica y San Cristóbal, ofreciendo ruleta, dados y suntuosos espectáculos de variedades. El artículo señaló que las autoridades dominicanas rechazaron los intentos de sindicatos del juego estadounidenses de infiltrarse en las operaciones, optando en su lugar por importar equipos de juego directamente desde Florida y Luisiana.

Barnett were leading a two-week Caribbean tour visiting Haiti, Puerto Rico, Jamaica, the Dominican Republic, and Cuba. The group planned to travel aboard Pan American Constellation aircraft under arrangements coordinated by Chicago travel expert John L. Kooreman. The issue also noted that Florida Normal and Industrial Memorial College in St. Augustine received official regional academic accreditation.

La edición también señaló que el Florida Normal and Industrial Memorial College de St. Augustine recibió acreditación académica regional oficial.

records.full_text:
SERVICE BY KEFAUVER

For a long time, I have been wondering about that Kefauver television show. Did it really accomplish something constructive? Obviously, it made Rudolph Halley a figure in New York politics and encouraged Estes Kefauver himself to run for President on the Democratic side.

Was that all?

Apparently, it is not so. I have received a circular from the Dominican Republic Information Center which is devoted to advertising the aforesaid Republic where Christopher Columbus is buried. According to the circular, the Dominican Republic is progressive and takes advantage of every opportunity. Therefore, as Kefauver drove gambling out of the United States, the Dominican Republic made gambling the cultural tie between the United States and the other Republic. The circular says:

“Gambling-in-the-sky via slot machines will feature a four-hour plane flight by the ‘Sportsmen’s Special,’ between Miami and Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic—the ‘Monte Carlo of the Caribbean’ where four legal gambling casinos flourish, if final flight negotiations are completed this week. Three of the casinos have opened since the Kefauver Crime Investigation closed many illegal gambling places in the U.S.

“Service by the 50-passenger chartered plane ‘Lady Luck’ is scheduled to commence on or about March 7 from Miami. The plane, though owned by the (CDA) Compania Dominicana de Aviacion, a Pan-American subsidiary, would be chartered to a sponsoring promotion group to begin the week-end round-trips between Miami and the West Indies country. The Dominican Government itself is not sponsoring the project but approves of it.”

In addition to approving of the slot-machines and other devices, the Dominican Government sends me this circular through the mails. If any American sent a similar circular through the mails, he would probably go to jail. But then Americans no longer count in the United States except to pay taxes and to have their sons conscripted for United Nations police actions.

I forgot to save the envelope in which this circular came and therefore I cannot tell you whether it used a paid-for stamp or came as diplomatic mail, free of charge. I get a lot of that kind of mail, all free, the object of which is always to educate me to love some foreign country. But if anyone wants to send some mail about loving America, a paid-for stamp is essential. It is a fine point, this business of who pays to have mail delivered advocating love.

records.summary_en: A photograph showed the body of Andres Requena, 44, sprawled in a hallway of a New York City tenement, where five shots from the dark had killed him. Requena had been writing articles against Dominican Republic dictator Hector Trujillo in De Patria, a Spanish-language newspaper printed in the United States and sent to the Dominican Republic by underground methods. Police said recent articles had brought threats to the writer.

Requena escribía artículos contra el dictador de la República Dominicana, Héctor Trujillo, en De Patria, un periódico en español impreso en los Estados Unidos y enviado a la República Dominicana por vías clandestinas. La policía dijo que sus artículos recientes le habían valido amenazas.

records.headline: Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic was pick eted last night
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that seven demonstrators from New York picketed outside a Washington office building during a diplomatic reception held by General Rafael Trujillo at the nearby Mayflower Hotel. Police enforced regulations barring demonstrations within 500 feet of the hotel, and the peaceful picketers displayed placards accusing Trujillo of political murders during his presidency. Trujillo was serving as Dominican minister of finance and chief United Nations delegate, while his brother Hector B. Trujillo held the presidency.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que siete manifestantes procedentes de Nueva York montaron un piquete frente a un edificio de oficinas en Washington durante una recepción diplomática ofrecida por el general Rafael Trujillo en el cercano Hotel Mayflower. La policía aplicó la normativa que prohibía manifestaciones a menos de 500 pies del hotel, y los piqueteros pacíficos portaban pancartas acusando a Trujillo de asesinatos políticos durante su presidencia. Trujillo ejercía como ministro de Hacienda dominicano y delegado principal ante las Naciones Unidas, mientras su hermano Héctor B. Trujillo ocupaba la presidencia.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dominican army intelligence chief General Felix Hermida accused U.S. diplomat John M. Cabot of conferring with communist subversives during a Caribbean tour, prompting the Dominican Republic to reconsider deploying troops to the Korean War. Separately, the Philippine Senate ratified bilateral treaties of amity with India, Cuba, and the Dominican Republic.

Por otra parte, el Senado filipino ratificó tratados bilaterales de amistad con la India, Cuba y la República Dominicana.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dominican President Hector B. Trujillo nominated Brigadier General Manuel de Moya Alonzo to succeed Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo as Ambassador to the United Nations. The announcement stated that the generalissimo was temporarily relinquishing his diplomatic post and military command to manage a large sugar enterprise. De Moya had previously served on multiple Dominican trade and diplomatic missions across the United States and Europe.

De Moya había participado previamente en múltiples misiones comerciales y diplomáticas dominicanas por Estados Unidos y Europa.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on the impending departure of Dominican Ambassador Luis Francisco Thomen and his wife following the succession of President Hector Trujillo. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that stateless traveler Michael Patrick O'Brien arrived in Ciudad Trujillo after receiving an invitation of resettlement from the Dominican government. O'Brien had spent nearly two years wandering the globe, including ten months confined to a ferry shuttling between Hong Kong and Macao when both ports denied him entry. Although O'Brien claimed American birth and citizenship following imprisonment in Oregon, U.S. immigration authorities disputed his status.

Aunque O'Brien alegaba haber nacido en Estados Unidos y tener ciudadanía estadounidense luego de estar encarcelado en Oregón, las autoridades de inmigración de EE. UU. disputaban su condición.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the Dominican government stripped Porfirio Rubirosa of his diplomatic post as embassy counselor in Paris and revoked his diplomatic status citing scandalous personal conduct. Rubirosa's dismissal followed his naming as co-respondent in high-profile divorce litigation in London and the United States. His history of celebrity marriages included unions with Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's daughter Flor de Oro, French actress Danielle Darrieux, and American heiress Doris Duke.

La destitución de Rubirosa se produjo luego de ser señalado como codemandado en sonados litigios de divorcio en Londres y Estados Unidos. Su historial de matrimonios con celebridades incluía enlaces con la hija del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, Flor de Oro, la actriz francesa Danielle Darrieux y la heredera estadounidense Doris Duke.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on an embassy social gathering where guests were entertained with demonstrations of the Dominican Republic's national dance. The dance was demonstrated by Beatrice Rodriguez, daughter of the Dominican OAS Ambassador, and Senora Eva Finkel, accompanied by music provided by musicians visiting from New York. The article noted that the dance, originally practiced by rural peasants, was introduced to elite Dominican society twenty-four years earlier by President Rafael Trujillo.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported international reactions to Guatemalan accusations alleging a foreign conspiracy against President Jacobo Arbenz's government. The Dominican Foreign Ministry dismissed the charges as communist fabrications, denying any involvement with Guatemala or the Arbenz regime. Other accused figures, including Nicaraguan Colonel Anastasio Somoza Debayle and General Miguel Ydigoras Fuentes, ridiculed the conspiracy claims, while Panama dismissed an attache named in the Guatemalan communique.

Otras figuras señaladas, como el coronel nicaragüense Anastasio Somoza Debayle y el general Miguel Ydígoras Fuentes, ridiculizaron las denuncias de conspiración, mientras que Panamá destituyó a un agregado mencionado en el comunicado guatemalteco.

records.summary_en: The Minneapolis Spokesman quoted an American observer expressing surprise at the racial integration and lack of color prejudice observed in the Dominican Republic. Attending a diplomatic reception hosted by Argentine Ambassador General Martini for Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, the writer noted Black military officers and their wives socializing freely with senior officials and the Archbishop of Santo Domingo. The issue also reported on proposed New York state legislation barring teachers who promote racial or religious intolerance.

records.summary_en: The St. Paul Recorder published reflections from a visiting commentator highlighting the harmonious race relations and absence of color prejudice observed in the Dominican Republic. The observer described an official reception for Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo hosted by Argentine Ambassador General Martini, where Black army officers and their spouses mingled with high military figures and the Archbishop of Santo Domingo. A companion report covered a New York legislative bill seeking to dismiss public school educators who advocate racial or religious bias.

records.summary_en: The Tribune recounted a travelogue by visiting members of the Pan American Medical Association touring historic and medical sites across Ciudad Trujillo, including the Alcazar de Colon and the Cathedral of Santa Maria la Menor. The physicians met with Dominican medical colleagues at a modern hospital facility before being received at the presidential palace by President Hector Trujillo. In accepting a diploma of honor for national public health achievements, Trujillo declared that state social welfare and health initiatives were essential to safeguarding civilization against communism.

Los médicos se reunieron con colegas dominicanos en unas modernas instalaciones hospitalarias antes de ser recibidos en el palacio presidencial por el presidente Héctor Trujillo. Al aceptar un diploma de honor por los logros nacionales en salud pública, Trujillo declaró que las iniciativas estatales de bienestar social y salud eran esenciales para proteger la civilización contra el comunismo.

records.summary_en: The Catholic Times reported that the Holy See and the Dominican Republic signed a historic concordat during a ceremony in the Vatican Palace. The agreement was executed by Monsignor Domenico Tardini on behalf of the Vatican and former President General Rafael Leonidas Trujillo on behalf of the Dominican Republic. Trujillo stated that the treaty affirmed his government's dedication to the Catholic Church as the bulwark of order and Christian civilization.
records.summary_es: El *Catholic Times* informó que la Santa Sede y la República Dominicana firmaron un histórico concordato durante una ceremonia en el Palacio Apostólico del Vaticano. El convenio fue suscrito por monseñor Domenico Tardini en representación del Vaticano y por el expresidente, general Rafael Leónidas Trujillo, en nombre de la República Dominicana. Trujillo manifestó que el tratado ratificaba la devoción de su gobierno hacia la Iglesia católica como baluarte del orden y la civilización cristiana.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reviewed the history of Caribbean political conflicts, tracing how Venezuelan exiles and Romulo Betancourt helped form the Caribbean Legion to invade Rafael Trujillo's Dominican Republic. Following the collapse of those invasion attempts, legion remnants aided Jose Figueres in establishing power in Costa Rica during the 1948 revolution. Dictators Trujillo and Anastasio Somoza accused Figueres of harboring communist conspirators and reforming the legion to attack their regimes, charges Figueres dismissed as dictatorial paranoia.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* repasó la historia de los conflictos políticos del Caribe, reseñando cómo los exiliados venezolanos y Rómulo Betancourt colaboraron en la formación de la Legión del Caribe para invadir la República Dominicana de Rafael Trujillo. Tras el fracaso de aquellas intentonas de invasión, los remanentes de la legión ayudaron a José Figueres a afianzarse en el poder en Costa Rica durante la revolución de 1948. Los dictadores Trujillo y Anastasio Somoza acusaron a Figueres de cobijar a conspiradores comunistas y reorganizar la legión para atacar a sus regímenes, señalamientos que Figueres desestimó considerándolos paranoia dictatorial.

Medics Say Smoking Bad For
Heart;Whiskey No Antidote
BY EDWIN DIAMOND
CHICAGO—(I N S)—The Ameri
can Medical Association declared or.
Thursday “there seems to be direct
evidence” that smoking cigarettes
causes heart damage.
And the long-held notion that
drinking whiskey “protects” the
heart against the effects of ciga
rettes was rejected as “purely an il
lusion.”
Two articles and an editorial were
devoted to the effects of smoking
and drinking 4n the current Journal
of the AMA.
Timothy V. Hartnett, chairman
of the Tobacco Industry Research
Committee, commented:
“From time to time, reports can
be expected that may seem either
favorable or unfavorable to the use
of tobacco. It is impossible to at
tempt to evaluate each specific re
port as it appears in the scientific
or lay press. The Tobacco Industry
Research Committee is convinced
the vast majority of the American
•public agree that all questions of
tobacco in relation to human health
need much more thorough and com
plete investigation than has been
made up to now.”

records.headline: Hurricane Katie beat a path across the Dominican Republic, slamming into the south shore with 115-mile winds the…
records.summary_en: Hurricane Katie beat a path across the Dominican Republic, slamming into the south shore with 115-mile winds the night before, but the mountains of Hispaniola distorted the storm and weakened her winds to about 40 or 50 miles an hour. At noon her center was near Puerto Plata, moving northeast at about 14 miles an hour, and she was expected to regain hurricane force over the open Atlantic without threatening the United States mainland.
records.summary_es: El huracán Katie cruzó la República Dominicana, golpeando la costa sur con vientos de 115 millas por hora la noche anterior, pero las montañas de la Hispaniola desorganizaron la tormenta y debilitaron sus vientos a unas 40 o 50 millas por hora. Al mediodía su centro estaba cerca de Puerto Plata, moviéndose hacia el noreste a unas 14 millas por hora, y se esperaba que recobrara fuerza de huracán sobre el Atlántico abierto sin amenazar el territorio continental de los Estados Unidos.

records.summary_es: *Diario Las Américas* informó que el gobierno dominicano confirmó que la Feria de la Paz y Confraternidad del Mundo Libre en Ciudad Trujillo se inauguraría el 20 de diciembre. Las brigadas de construcción trabajaban sin cesar para concluir las instalaciones, las exhibiciones internacionales habían comenzado a llegar y se habilitaron hoteles adicionales para albergar a los visitantes esperados.

WASHINGTON —(UP)— A
group of Cuban businessmen left
for Toledo, Ohio, continuing their
tour of a number of United States
industrial centers in the interest
of promoting greater commerce
between the two countries.
The party is headed by Paul
M. Heilman, President of the Ame
rican Chamber of Commerce of
Cuba, and includes other members
of the chamber who have trade
connections in the United States.
Ambassador Miguel Angel Campa
gave a reception at his Embassy
in honor of the group. He invited
as his guests a large number of
Washington businessmen and in
dustrialists. many of whom have
trade connections in Cuba.

records.summary_en: As a result of accusations made by General Felix Hermida, chief of the Dominican army, about the supplying of arms to three individuals for subversive purposes, in which he accused the Cuban chief of staff, General Francisco Tabernilla, the Dominican government recalled its ambassador to Cuba, Federico Llaverias, for consultation. records.summary_en: *Diario Las Américas* reported that the Dominican government declared three days of official mourning following the death of Plinio Pina Chevalier in New York at age 70. Chevalier, an uncle to President Héctor Trujillo and Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, had served as a diplomat and cabinet minister and was credited with introducing Rafael Trujillo to politics.
records.summary_es: *Diario Las Américas* informó que el gobierno dominicano declaró tres días de duelo oficial tras el fallecimiento de Plinio Pina Chevalier en Nueva York a los 70 años de edad. Chevalier, tío del presidente Héctor Trujillo y del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, se había desempeñado como diplomático y ministro del gabinete, y se le atribuía haber iniciado a Rafael Trujillo en la política.

records.summary_en: *Diario Las Américas* reported that Cuban Senator Rivero Agüero warned that the Cuban Air Force would destroy Ciudad Trujillo if the Dominican Republic attempted an attack on Havana. Dismissing rumors of a Dominican-based invasion force, Rivero Agüero asserted that Cuba's military positions in Oriente Province were strategically positioned to repel any aggression.

records.full_text:
U. S. Government Rejects
Dominican Statements on
Murphy’s Disappearance

WASHINGTON, March 16 (UP) The United States rejected today the Dominican government explanation about the mysterious disappearance of the North American aviator Gerald L. Murphy, in the Dominican Republic.

23 years old Murphy disappeared in the Dominican Republic on December 3rd. last.

In official note, delivered by the United States Embassy in Ciudad Trujillo, the U. S. government rejected the explanation offered by the Dominican government that Murphy was assassinated by the Dominican pilot Octavio de la Maza, who later committed suicide at Ciudad Trujillo, leaving a letter in which he confessed his crime.

A copy of the note delivered in Ciudad Trujillo was handed today to the Dominican Ambassador in Washington, Dr. Joaquín Salazar.

The note urges the Dominican Government to continue “vigorously” the investigation on the disappearance of Murphy, who was said to have been the pilot who took to the Dominican Republic professor Jesús de Galíndez, who disappeared in New York on March 12, 1956. It has also been said Murphy was murdered because he talked too much.

Last January, the Dominican Government delivered to the State Department an alleged letter-confession of pilot de la Maza and other documents, all of which have been carefully examined by the FBI.

The note delivered today by the U. S. Government says:

“Upon examination of these documents and evidence, this Government has reached the conclusion that, if the handwriting samples submitted by Dominican authorities as belonging to Maza are really his, that means the suicide note was not written by de la Maza.”

Other points rejected by the State Department over the explanation are:

1. That Murphy did not know any person with political influence in the Dominican Republic. The U. S. investigation, says the Department of State, shows that Murphy had “good relations” with high Dominican officials, including the then Undersecretary of the Army, now Consul General in New York, Arturo Espaillat.

2. That Murphy’s income while in the Dominican Republic was $350 per month. The investigation shows, the note says, that the missing pilot had a capital substantially bigger than what Dominican authorities say.

“The Government of the United States is gravely concerned by the disappearance of one of its citizens in the Dominican Republic — the note says — and assumes this concern is shared by the Dominican Government.”

Murphy, as de la Maza, worked for the Dominican Air Line, and disappeared when he had announced his intention to return to the United States for good.

As soon as the contents of the note were revealed, Rep. Charles O. Porter, who has realized a personal investigation on Murphy’s disappearance, said the note shows the need of a Congress investigation of the relations of the United States with the Dominican Republic.

records.summary_en: From Ciudad Trujillo, Prince Juan Carlos de Borbon, heir apparent to the Spanish throne, arrived on his first visit to the Western Hemisphere. records.summary_en: Argentina officially protested to the Dominican Republic because ex-dictator Juan Peron and other Peronist exiles residing in Ciudad Trujillo were engaged in political activities that violated the most elemental rules of asylum. The Foreign Affairs Minister made the protest at noon, and an official note was delivered to the Dominican ambassador at Buenos Aires, following an earlier protest made to him some days before. The communique said the protests were aimed at stopping intervention in Argentine politics by exiles in Ciudad Trujillo, and the text of the note was not made public immediately.
records.summary_es: Argentina protestó oficialmente ante la República Dominicana porque el exdictador Juan Perón y otros exiliados peronistas residentes en Ciudad Trujillo se dedicaban a actividades políticas que violaban las reglas más elementales del asilo. El ministro de Relaciones Exteriores presentó la protesta al mediodía y se entregó una nota oficial al embajador dominicano en Buenos Aires, tras una protesta anterior hecha ante él días atrás. El comunicado decía que las protestas buscaban detener la intervención en la política argentina por parte de los exiliados en Ciudad Trujillo, y el texto de la nota no se hizo público de inmediato.

Frank, accused of failing to register as an agent of the Dominican Republic and of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, FBI agent Fred Woodcock testified that Frank told him he had acted as security adviser for Trujillo on a European trip in 1954 and when the dictator visited Kansas City in late 1955, and had served as attorney for a Dominican ship repair firm. Gibbs, Jr. testified that from 1954 through 1956 he headed a Dominican ship repair firm apparently controlled by Trujillo; Frank's earlier conviction on the same charge, in December 1957, was reversed last October by the Court of Appeals.

records.full_text:
Rebels Seize
Army Station
In Venezuela

By ARISTEDES MOLEON

CARACAS, Venezuela (AP) — Rebels seized control of an army regiment’s headquarters at San Cristobal near the Colombian border today in an attempt to set off nationwide revolt against President Romulo Betancourt’s government.

Betancourt ordered soldiers to San Cristobal to quell the uprising, and pledges of support came to him at once from military, political and civilian sources.

The moderate Venezuelan President announced he would use all constitutional powers to crush the rebellion, but would not suspend constitutional guarantees in this oil-rich nation.

The strong military garrison at Caracas announced its support at once for Betancourt’s government.

Leaders of the nation’s three major political parties spoke over a national radio network, appealing to their followers in San Cristobal to vigorously oppose the insurrection.

The rebels seized control of the Simon Bolivar army regiment’s headquarters at San Cristobal.

Gen. Pedro Jose Quevado, commander of the Venezuelan armed forces, urged “my companions in arms to set an example of common sense and maturity” and support the constitutional government.

The head of the Central Workers Organization, Jose Gonzalez Navarro, called for its 1,200,000 members to go on strike. He said this would be a demonstration of opposition to the “criminal” insurrection which, he declared, was counting on the support of the Dominican Republic.

The government had announced last Saturday that it had smashed a plot for an armed invasion of Venezuela from Colombia by officers who were dismissed from the army for their support of former dictator Gen. Marcos Perez Jimenez.

Venezuelan naval craft and air force planes were patrolling the coast today on the lookout for two fishing boats which the minister of defense, General Jose Lopez Henrique, said had sailed from Spain with arms for the plotters.

Betancourt, a moderate with a reputation as a social reformer, has faced a series of minor uprisings, threats and harassments since he took office early in 1959. He was elected a year after the overthrow of Perez Jimenez, now in exile in Florida.

Venezuela, a tropical country, lies on the northern hump of South America facing the Caribbean. It has about six million people, and because of the nation’s rich resources, has the highest per capita income in South America.

records.full_text:
Change For Better Hoped
U.S. Watches Trend In D.R.

WASHINGTON (AP)—Secretary of State Dean Rusk set out today on his delayed trip to join President Kennedy in Europe, signalling a belief that the assassination of Dominican dictator Rafael L. Trujillo will not result in the immediate turmoil officials had feared.

Rusk had been scheduled to leave Wednesday to back up Kennedy in his talks in Paris with French President Charles de Gaulle and later in Vienna with Soviet Premier Khrushchev. Instead he was held here to take personal charge of dealing with the Dominican situation.

That decision underscored the anxiety with which American officials were watching for clues as to which way the Caribbean country will shift.

Rusk’s plane was due in Paris at 9 a.m. Paris time Friday.

Just before takeoff, Rusk told newsmen at National Airport that there is no way of knowing at this time what kind of government will finally take over in the Dominican Republic.

U.S. authorities said information seeping out from tightly censored Ciudad Trujillo indicated the Trujillo group, under figurehead President Jouquin Balaguer, still was in control.

President Kennedy and Rusk, in telephone contact between Paris and Washington, were said to be agreed that the Dominican situation was of such top priority that Rusk could do more by setting the U.S. course as the situation clears than by speeding off to the summit talks.

Informed sources said both the President and the secretary of state had the recent Cuban invasion fiasco very much in mind and were determined to avoid any mistake on the neighboring Caribbean island. They feel the outcome will affect the whole of U.S.-Latin American affairs.

Balking Washington strategists was a scarcity of solid information. Officials said they did not yet know who engineered the assassination or who might be behind the figurehead president who continued in office, Joaquin Balaguer. They said their evidence did not point to pro-Communist Cuba or other foreign manipulators.

The only post-assassination communication from the U.S. Consulate in Ciudad Trujillo reported by late Wednesday was a brief message from Consul General Henry Dearborn saying the capital was calm and he knew of no injury to the 5,200 citizens in the country.

Some U.S. authorities foresaw a struggle for power, both within the Trujillo group and between it and the large elements of Dominican society persecuted during the dictator’s 31-year rule. A continued harsh rightwing regime without Trujillo’s personal leadership, they reasoned, would set off revolt—perhaps pro-Castro the next time.

The United States had several lures to attract Trujillo’s successors down the democratic path, a main aim of Kennedy’s “alliance for progress” Latin American program.

One is resumption of U.S. aid, cut off when Washington joined the other American Republics last year in breaking diplomatic relations and normal commercial ties with Trujillo. Another is a boost in U.S. sugar purchases. The Dominican economy has been sagging.

The United States could also take a leading role in a move by the hemisphere organization, the Organization of American States, in readmitting a progressive Dominican regime to the American family.

Washington congressional reaction was mixed.

Sen. George Smathers, D-Fla., recommended that U.S. Marines be landed in the Dominican Republic to prevent a Communist takeover.

Sens. Homer E. Capehart, R-Ind., Olin D. Johnston, D-S.C., and Allen J. Ellender, D-La., saw a Red Castroite takeover in prospect as a result of Trujillo’s death.

records.headline: This Spanish-language essay argues that the immense majority of the Dominican people accept Trujillo's tyrannical…
records.summary_en: This Spanish-language essay argues that the immense majority of the Dominican people accept Trujillo's tyrannical regime only out of an imperative need for collective survival, hate and fear it, and should be regarded as the despot's passive victims rather than held responsible for it. It says three things should not be counted against that majority: having enrolled in Trujillo's political parties, whose membership the regime tied to civil rights, having held public employment, which is service to the state and not to the regime, and having worked in a business of Trujillo or his followers, given the persecution system known as the 'lepra'.
records.summary_es: Este ensayo en español argumenta que la inmensa mayoría del pueblo dominicano acepta el régimen tiránico de Trujillo solo por una imperiosa necesidad de supervivencia colectiva, lo odia y le teme, y debe ser considerada víctima pasiva del déspota en lugar de hacérsele responsable de él. Dice que tres cosas no deben contarse en contra de esa mayoría: haberse inscrito en los partidos políticos de Trujillo, cuya militancia el régimen vinculó a los derechos civiles, haber servido un empleo público, que es servir al estado y no al régimen, y haber trabajado en una empresa de Trujillo o de sus secuaces, dado el sistema de persecución conocido como la «lepra».

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Haitian Foreign Minister René Chalmers addressed the Organization of American States, demanding a formal condemnation of the Dominican government for arming rebel invasions led by General Léon Cantave. Chalmers cited historical grievances including the 1937 border massacre, calling for an inter-American military commission to enforce Dominican non-intervention guarantees.

Chalmers invocó agravios históricos, entre ellos la masacre fronteriza de 1937, solicitando una comisión militar interamericana para hacer cumplir las garantías de no intervención dominicanas.

records.summary_en: *The Key West Citizen* reported on testimony by recalled U.S. Ambassador John Bartlow Martin regarding the recent military coup that deposed Dominican President Juan Bosch. Martin revealed to senators that top Dominican military officers tipped their hand by boycotting an embassy reception for an American admiral, prompting questions from Senator Wayne Morse about whether a U.S. naval show of force could have deterred the takeover.

records.summary_en: *The Farmville Herald* reported on findings released by the Dominican military junta alleging widespread Communist infiltration within the ousted administration of President Juan Bosch. A report prepared by Ambassador Bonilla-Atiles accused several cabinet ministers, agency directors, and congressional officials of collaborating with Marxist organizations such as the MPD and the 14th of June Movement.

records.headline: Virginia Prewett reports that ex-President Juan Bosch's forces in the Dominican Republic are for the first time…
records.summary_en: Virginia Prewett reports that ex-President Juan Bosch's forces in the Dominican Republic are for the first time acquiring partial army support through a quiet agreement with former president Joaquin Balaguer, who has a respectable army following and now swings his influence to the Bosch cause. Balaguer sent his reform party's secretary general, Nicolas Silfa, to Santo Domingo by air on October 17 to advise on supporting the constitutional cause, but Silfa was turned back from the airport because his name is blacklisted by the junta, and the new alignment comes as Brigadier General Elias Wessin y Wessin challenges a combination headed by General Antonio Imbert for control of the power apparatus in Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: Virginia Prewett informa que las fuerzas del expresidente Juan Bosch en la República Dominicana están adquiriendo por primera vez un apoyo parcial del ejército mediante un acuerdo discreto con el expresidente Joaquín Balaguer, que tiene un respetable seguimiento en el ejército y ahora inclina su influencia hacia la causa de Bosch. Balaguer envió a Santo Domingo por avión el 17 de octubre al secretario general de su partido reformista, Nicolás Silfa, para asesorar sobre el apoyo a la causa constitucional, pero Silfa fue devuelto desde el aeropuerto porque su nombre está en la lista negra de la junta, y la nueva alineación llega cuando el general de brigada Elías Wessin y Wessin desafía a una combinación encabezada por el general Antonio Imbert por el control del aparato de poder en Santo Domingo.
